chunks.title: Academy — Overview
chunks.text:
Academy (#/academy). Overview.
Description:
Academy (page title "AI Creator Academy", breadcrumb "Smart Video Academy") is SmartVideo's learning area. It has 15 tracks, 66 lessons and 77 templates. Each lesson has Learn, See and Create tabs, and you can mark lessons complete, bookmark them and copy a share link.
Summary:
Learn AI creator skills in 15 tracks, 66 lessons and 77 templates, then jump into SmartVideo studios to make things.
About:

chunks.title: Academy — Overview
chunks.text:
The Academy is a read-and-practice area, not a generator. The hub (#/academy) shows the heading "AI Creator Academy", a summary line ("15 tracks, 66 lessons and 77 templates imported from the creator academy. Learn the concept, see the real examples, then create with SmartVideo's studios."), an overall Progress bar, a "Reset progress" button, a Bookmarks list (once you bookmark something) and a grid of Tracks. Click a track card to see its Lessons and Templates side by side. Click a lesson to open it with three tabs: Learn (the concept, plus a "Read full lesson" button), See (example media and, for some lessons, a link to an app or studio) and Create (linked templates). Click a template to open an editor with tabs Create, See and Learn. Your progress (in-progress and completed lessons) and bookmarks are saved only in your browser's local storage on that device. Lessons can be shared with the "Copy link" button, which copies a URL of the form #/academy/track/<trackSlug>/lesson/<lessonId>. Track 01 (AI Video Ads & UGC) has the richest lessons (The problem, The concept, Do it, Launch it (get paid), Exercises) and 7 interactive template editors; the other 14 tracks show lessons and templates as documents. The Academy itself never generates images, video or audio; it points you to the studios that do.
Best for:

chunks.title: Academy — Overview
chunks.text:
Beginners and creators who want a structured path (ads and UGC, filmmaking, faceless channels, avatars, audio, product photos, fashion, real estate, headshots, merch, stock, tool choice, freelancing, agents) and ready-to-fill templates before using a studio.
When to use it:
- You are new to AI video/image creation and want step-by-step lessons.
- You want to learn how to turn a skill into a service or income (pricing, outreach, retainers, licensing).
- You want a fill-in template (ad brief, UGC script, batch matrix, outreach message, retainer proposal).
- You want to track which lessons you have finished and bookmark ones for later.
- You want to share a specific lesson with someone using a link.
When to use another studio:
- Use Apps (#/apps) when you want to browse and open SmartVideo's tools and studios rather than read lessons.
- Use Templates (#/templates) when you want ready-made video/ad templates to generate from, not learning templates (checklists, scripts, worksheets).
- Use Explore (#/explore) when you want to browse example outputs and styles for inspiration.
- Use Video Studio (#/video) when you want to actually generate a video clip.
- Use Cinema Studio (#/cinema) when you want to generate cinematic footage.
- Use Image Studio (#/image) when you want to generate images.
- Use Avatar Studio (#/avatar) when you want to create talking-avatar videos.

chunks.title: Academy — Overview
chunks.text: - Use Audio Studio (#/audio) when you want to generate voice, music or sound.

chunks.title: Academy — How to use
chunks.text:
Academy (#/academy). How to use.
How to use:
1. Open Academy from the side menu (#/academy). 2. Click a track card under "Tracks". 3. Click a lesson under "Lessons (N)" to open it (it is marked in-progress). 4. On the Learn tab read the content and click "Read full lesson" for the whole text. 5. Open the See tab for example media; click an example and "Try this in <Studio>" to open the matching studio. 6. Open the Create tab and click "Open template" for a linked template, then fill it in and click "Use Template" (copies it) or "Create With Smart Video". 7. Click the round check button ("Mark as completed") when done. 8. Click "Bookmark for later" (star) to save it and "Copy link" to share it. 9. Click "Back to track" or "All tracks" to continue.
Steps:
- Open Academy from the side menu (#/academy).
- Click a track card under "Tracks".
- Click a lesson under "Lessons (N)".
- On the Learn tab, read it and click "Read full lesson" for the full text.
- Open the See tab for example media and app links.
- Open the Create tab and click "Open template" on a linked template.
- Fill the template and click "Use Template" or "Create With Smart Video".
- Click the round check button to mark the lesson completed.
- Use the star ("Bookmark for later") and "Copy link" as needed.
Getting started:

chunks.title: Academy — How to use
chunks.text:
- Open #/academy and pick Track 01 (AI Video Ads & UGC) if you are new; its lessons have the fullest content.
- Open the first lesson and read The problem and The concept.
- Try the Create tab and click "Show example" in a template to see a filled-in sample.
- Mark lessons complete as you go so the Progress bar fills.
Tips:
- Click "Show example" in track 01 templates first to see what a good answer looks like.
- Use "Use Template" to copy your work before leaving a template page.
- Bookmark lessons you want to revisit; they show on the hub.
- The browser back button works between hub, track, lesson and template pages.
Best practices:
- Work through a track in lesson order.
- Read the lesson, then use the Create tab to produce something.
- Mark lessons complete only when you have finished the exercise.
- Do not rely on progress being available on other devices.

chunks.title: Academy — Features
chunks.text:
Academy (#/academy). Features.
Key features:
- 15 tracks, 66 lessons and 77 templates (counts come from the catalog).
- Overall Progress bar on the hub and a per-track "completed/total" counter.
- "Mark as completed" / "Mark as incomplete" round check button on each lesson row and on the lesson page.
- Bookmarks: "Bookmark for later" (star), "Bookmarked", "Remove bookmark"; bookmarked lessons are listed on the hub under "Bookmarks (N)".
- "Copy link" button on a lesson page that copies a share URL (button text changes to "Copied!").
- Lesson tabs: Learn, See, Create.
- Template editor tabs: Create, See, Learn.
- "Create With Smart Video" and "Use Template" buttons on templates; "Try this in <Studio>" on example media.
- "Reset progress" button on the hub.
Feature details:

chunks.title: Academy — Features
chunks.text:
- feature: Hub (all tracks) | explanation: Opening #/academy shows the "AI Creator Academy" header, the counts line, an overall Progress bar (shown as completed/total lessons, e.g. 3/66), your Bookmarks list (only if you have bookmarks) and the Tracks grid. Each track card shows "Track N", the title, a short summary and a progress bar with completed/total once the track has lessons. Click a card to open the track. A "Smart Video Academy" button in the top bar returns to the hub and "Exit" goes to the Apps page. | whyToUse: Starting point to pick a track and see how far you have got. | inputRequired: None. | restrictions: Progress and bookmarks shown are only those stored in this browser.
- feature: Track page | explanation: Shows "Track N", the track title and summary, a progress bar with "completed/total completed", an "All tracks" button, a "Lessons (N)" column and a "Templates (N)" column. Clicking a lesson opens it and marks it as in-progress (unless already completed). Each lesson row has a round status button, its number, title, one-line summary, a star (bookmark) and an arrow. Template rows show a small "SV" badge if the template's button is "Create With Smart Video", otherwise "Tpl". | whyToUse: See everything in one track and continue where you left off. | inputRequired: Pick a track. | restrictions: None known.

chunks.title: Academy — Features
chunks.text:
- feature: Lesson page: Learn tab | explanation: For the five Track 01 lessons the Learn tab shows cards titled "The problem", "The concept", "Do it", "Launch it (get paid)" and "Exercises". For other lessons it shows the lesson summary. Every lesson has a "Read full lesson" button (toggles to "Hide full lesson") that loads the full Markdown text. The header shows "Lesson N" plus an estimated time (for example "~45 minutes") when the lesson has one. | whyToUse: Read the concept and the steps before you create. | inputRequired: None. | restrictions: If the full lesson text cannot be loaded you see "Could not load content."; while loading it shows "Loading...".
- feature: Lesson page: See tab | explanation: Says "Example media referenced in this lesson." and shows a gallery of example images/videos (shows "No example media for this item." if none). Click one to open a larger view with a "Try this in <Studio>" button. Below the gallery, some lessons show "Open <app name>" (tracks 07 and 08 open an in-app studio page), "View App Source" (an external GitHub link for lessons marked existing) or the note "App for this lesson is under development." (lessons marked needed). | whyToUse: See real examples and jump to the right tool. | inputRequired: None. | restrictions: Not every lesson has media or an app link.

chunks.title: Academy — Features
chunks.text:
- feature: Lesson page: Create tab | explanation: Says "Turn this lesson into a deliverable. Open a template to build it, or launch a linked SmartVideo recipe." Each linked template is listed with an "Open template" button, and some also have a "Create With Smart Video" button that launches a linked recipe. Shows "No linked templates." if none. | whyToUse: Turn a lesson into a real deliverable. | inputRequired: None. | restrictions: Only templates linked to that lesson appear.
- feature: Progress tracking | explanation: Each lesson is either not started, in-progress (blue dot) or completed (green check). Opening a lesson from a track or the hub marks it in-progress (unless already completed). Click the round button on a lesson row or lesson page to complete it; click a completed one again (tooltip "Mark as incomplete") to clear it. Stored in the browser's localStorage under the key academy_progress. "Reset progress" on the hub clears everything at once with no confirmation. | whyToUse: Keep track of what you have finished. | inputRequired: Click the round status button. | restrictions: Saved per browser/device only, not synced to an account. Clearing site data, using private mode or switching browsers loses it.

chunks.title: Academy — Features
chunks.text:
- feature: Bookmarks | explanation: Click the star (tooltip "Bookmark for later") on a lesson row or the "Bookmark" button on a lesson page. Bookmarked lessons appear on the hub under "Bookmarks (N)" with a "Remove" button. Stored in localStorage under academy_bookmarks. | whyToUse: Save lessons to come back to. | inputRequired: Click the star. | restrictions: Browser-local only; lessons only (not templates).
- feature: Copy link (share a lesson) | explanation: On a lesson page, "Copy link" copies the current site address plus #/academy/track/<trackSlug>/lesson/<lessonId> to your clipboard and shows "Copied!" for about two seconds. Track 01 lesson IDs have no number prefix (e.g. how-ugc-works); tracks 02-15 use <trackSlug>::<NN-file-slug> (e.g. 02-ai-filmmaking::01-screenplay-and-story). | whyToUse: Send someone directly to a lesson. | inputRequired: None. | restrictions: The link only opens the lesson if the lesson ID exists; otherwise the hub opens. The person opening it does not receive your progress or bookmarks.

chunks.title: Academy — Features

The Learn tab has an "Open linked lesson" button. | whyToUse: Get a working checklist, script or proposal quickly. | inputRequired: Fill the fields (track 01) or just read/copy (others). | restrictions: What you type in template editors is not saved when you leave the page.

chunks.title: Academy — Features
chunks.text:
- feature: "Try this in <Studio>" on example media | explanation: In the See tab, open an example and click "Try this in <Studio>". If an example has no mapping the button reads "Try this in Studio" and opens the image route. | whyToUse: Recreate an example yourself. | inputRequired: Open an example image/video. | restrictions: Pre-fills the studio; you still generate there, and generation uses that studio's own rules and credits.

chunks.title: Academy — Problems and limits
chunks.text:
Academy (#/academy). Problems and limits.
Troubleshooting:
- A shared link opens the Academy hub instead of the lesson: the lesson or track ID in the link is wrong or no longer exists, or the link is missing the "/track/<trackSlug>" part. Copy the link again using "Copy link" on the lesson page, or open the track and click the lesson.
- My progress is missing on another browser or device: progress and bookmarks are stored only in that browser. Re-mark lessons on the new browser.
- My progress disappeared: you may have clicked "Reset progress", cleared site data, or are in a private window. Re-mark lessons manually.
- Full lesson shows "Could not load content.": the lesson text file could not be fetched; check your connection, reload and click "Read full lesson" again.
- Full lesson stays on "Loading...": wait a moment or reload the page.
- A lesson says "App for this lesson is under development.": that lesson's app is marked as needed in the data; use the studios directly instead.
- The studio button on a track 07 or 08 lesson does not show: it is on the lesson's See tab, not the Learn tab, and only tracks 07 (Product Shot Studio / Photo Studio) and 08 (Edit Studio, Change Dress) have it. If you want a different tool, open it from the side menu (Image, Edit, Product Shot or Brand).

chunks.title: Academy — Problems and limits
chunks.text:
- Template says "No example media for this item.": that item has no examples; use the Learn and Create tabs.
- A lesson or template editor opens blank: the item ID may be wrong; go back with "Back to track" or "All tracks".
- Copy buttons do nothing: the browser may block clipboard access; allow clipboard permission or select the text manually.
Troubleshooting steps:
- issue: Link opens the hub instead of a lesson | steps: Open the Academy and click the track, then the lesson.; Click "Copy link" on the lesson page and use that link.; Check the link looks like #/academy/track/<trackSlug>/lesson/<lessonId>.; For tracks 02-15 the lessonId contains "::", for example 02-ai-filmmaking::01-screenplay-and-story; do not remove it.
- issue: Progress or bookmarks missing | steps: Check you are on the same browser and profile where you made progress.; Check you are not in a private/incognito window and have not cleared site data.; If you clicked "Reset progress", the data cannot be restored; re-mark lessons.
- issue: Full lesson will not load | steps: Reload the page.; Open the lesson again and click "Read full lesson".; Read the Learn cards or summary meanwhile.
- issue: Template text lost | steps: Fields are not saved when you leave the page.; Click "Use Template" to copy before leaving and paste it elsewhere.
Common problems:

chunks.title: Academy — Problems and limits
chunks.text:
- problem: Shared lesson link goes to the hub | whyItHappens: The page falls back to the hub when the track or lesson ID is not found. | howToFix: Re-copy the link with "Copy link" from the lesson page.
- problem: Progress not on my other device | whyItHappens: Progress is saved in that browser's localStorage only. | howToFix: Mark lessons again on the other device.
- problem: Track titles look odd, for example "03 Faceless Ai Channels" | whyItHappens: The catalog stores those titles in that form for tracks 03-08. | howToFix: No fix needed; the track slug and summary identify the track.
- problem: Reset progress wiped everything | whyItHappens: The button has no confirmation. | howToFix: Re-mark lessons manually.
Limitations:
- Progress and bookmarks live only in your browser's local storage; the code shows no account sync.
- Template editor text is not saved.
- No search box, filters or certificates in the code.
- The Academy does not generate media.
- Only track 01 has the structured Learn cards and interactive template editors; the other tracks are document-style.
- "Reset progress" clears all progress immediately, with no confirmation.
- Some lessons say "App for this lesson is under development."
Limit details:

chunks.title: Academy — Problems and limits
chunks.text:
- limitation: Progress is per browser | impact: A different browser, device or a cleared cache shows no progress or bookmarks. | workaround: Keep using the same browser profile; there is no export in the code.
- limitation: Template inputs are not saved | impact: Leaving the template page loses what you typed. | workaround: Click "Use Template" to copy the text and paste it somewhere safe before leaving.
- limitation: No confirmation on Reset progress | impact: All completed/in-progress marks disappear at once. | workaround: Only click it if you really want to start over; you can re-mark lessons manually.
- limitation: Bookmarks apply to lessons only | impact: Templates cannot be bookmarked. | workaround: Bookmark the linked lesson.
FAQs:
- question: Does the Academy generate videos or images? | answer: No. It is a learning area. Buttons such as "Try this in <Studio>" or "Open in Studio" take you to a studio where you generate.
- question: Is my progress saved to my account? | answer: The code saves progress (academy_progress) and bookmarks (academy_bookmarks) in your browser's localStorage only. Nothing in the code syncs them to an account or other devices.
- question: How many tracks, lessons and templates are there? | answer: 15 tracks, 66 lessons and 77 templates, according to the catalog.

chunks.title: Academy — Problems and limits
chunks.text:
- question: How do I mark a lesson complete? | answer: Click the round check button next to the lesson title (on the lesson page or the track list). Click it again to mark it incomplete.
- question: How do I share a lesson? | answer: Open the lesson and click "Copy link". The link looks like #/academy/track/<trackSlug>/lesson/<lessonId> after your site address.
- question: How do I reset everything? | answer: On the hub, click "Reset progress". It clears all lesson progress immediately. It does not clear bookmarks.
- question: What does "Use Template" do? | answer: It copies the template text to your clipboard and briefly shows "Copied!".
- question: What does "Create With Smart Video" do? | answer: On track 01 templates it opens a brief dialog with "Copy brief" and "Open in Studio". In the Create tab of a lesson it launches the linked SmartVideo recipe directly. It only appears on templates that have a recipe linked.
- question: Which track should I start with? | answer: Track 01, AI Video Ads & UGC, has the most structured lessons and interactive templates. Pick any track that matches your goal.
- question: Can I bookmark templates? | answer: No, only lessons have a bookmark star.

chunks.title: Academy — Workflows and use cases
chunks.text:
Academy (#/academy). Workflows and use cases.
Example workflows:
- title: Learn UGC ads then build a brief | steps: Open #/academy and click "AI Video Ads & UGC".; Click lesson "How AI UGC Actually Works" and read The problem and The concept.; Open the Create tab and click "Open template" on "Ad Brief Checklist".; Click "Show example" to see a sample, then clear it and fill your own fields.; Click "Create With Smart Video", review the brief, then "Copy brief" or "Open in Studio".; Go back and click the round check button to mark the lesson completed.
- title: Save and share a lesson | steps: Open a track and click a lesson.; Click "Bookmark for later".; Click "Copy link" (it shows "Copied!") and paste the link to a teammate.; Later, find the lesson under "Bookmarks (N)" on the hub.
- title: Try an example in a studio | steps: Open a lesson and go to the See tab.; Click an example image or video to enlarge it.; Click "Try this in <Studio>".; Review the pre-filled prompt in the studio and generate there.
Use cases:

chunks.title: Academy — Workflows and use cases
chunks.text:
- title: Start earning with UGC ads | description: Follow track 01 from concept to pricing. | steps: Open the AI Video Ads & UGC track.; Work through the five lessons in order.; Use the UGC Script Template and Batch Matrix Template.; Use the Outreach Template and Retainer Proposal Template to pitch clients. | expectedOutput: Filled templates you copied out, and five lessons marked completed.
- title: Pick the right AI tool | description: Use the AI Tools Mastery track as a buyer's guide. | steps: Open the track 13-ai-tools-mastery.; Read the first lesson on image models.; Open the related studio from the side menu. | expectedOutput: A clear choice of tool for your goal.
- title: Plan a short film | description: Use the AI Filmmaking track for story and shots. | steps: Open AI Filmmaking.; Read screenplay, storyboard and camera lessons.; Open the track's templates and click "Use Template". | expectedOutput: A copied template and a plan to take into Cinema Studio.
Related studios:
- studio: video | relationship: Tracks 01, 03, 12, 13 and 15 map "Try this in Studio" to Video Studio. | whenToMove: When you want to generate a clip from a lesson example. | why: It generates the video you learned about.

chunks.title: AI VFX Studio — Overview
chunks.text:
AI VFX Studio (#/ai-vfx). Overview.
Description:
AI VFX Studio turns one still image into a short video using a preset effect: a camera move, an AI transformation or an explosion/element VFX. You pick an effect card, add an image, choose aspect ratio, duration, size and quality, and press Generate.
Summary:
Hollywood camera moves, explosive VFX and AI effects from a single image.
About:
AI VFX Studio is a native in-app version of the open-source AI-VFX app. The page has an input bar at the top (image box, optional prompt, image URL field, four dropdowns and a Generate button) and a gallery of effect cards underneath, grouped in three tabs: AI Effects (64 presets), Motion Controls (47 camera moves) and VFX (9 elements and destruction effects). Everything runs through the MuAPI generate_wan_ai_effects endpoint, so you need a MuAPI key. Defaults are 9:16 portrait, 5 seconds, 480p and Medium quality, which keeps first tests quick. Finished videos appear in a results grid on the page with a Download link, and are also saved to your generation history.
Best for:
Creators who want fast cinematic camera moves, explosion or elemental VFX and viral-style AI transformations from a single photo, with simple controls for aspect ratio, length and quality.
When to use it:
- You have one image and want a ready-made camera move such as Dolly In, Crash Zoom In, 360 Orbit or FPV Drone Cam.

chunks.title: AI VFX Studio — Overview
chunks.text:
- You want an element or destruction effect such as Building Explosion, Tornado, Electricity or Disintegration.
- You want a viral-style AI transformation such as Hulk Transformation, Kamehameha or Cakeify.
- You want to choose between portrait, landscape and square, and between 5 or 10 second clips.
- You want to paste an image link instead of uploading a file.
When to use another studio:
- Use Effects Studio (#/effects) when you want still-image effects (figurines, comic looks, Nano Banana, Kontext edits), the extra Video FX v2 presets, before-and-after compare, or Add to Library and Insert into Timeline buttons.
- Use Animate Studio (#/animate) when you want to describe the motion yourself and pick any image-to-video model.
- Use Video Tools (#/videotools) when you already have a video and want to upscale, translate, caption or recast it.
- Use Video Studio (#/video) for text-to-video or image-to-video with full model selection.
- Use Timeline (#/timeline) to assemble several clips into a finished edit.

chunks.title: AI VFX Studio — How to use
chunks.text:
AI VFX Studio (#/ai-vfx). How to use.
How to use:
1. Open AI VFX Studio from the side menu (#/ai-vfx). 2. Choose a tab: AI Effects, Motion Controls or VFX. 3. Click an effect card. The line above the prompt changes from Pick an effect below, add an image, then Generate. to Effect: followed by the effect name. 4. Click the dashed Add image box to upload a picture (JPEG, PNG, WebP or GIF), or paste a link in the ...or paste an image URL (https://) field. 5. Optional: type the subject in the prompt box. 6. Set Aspect (9:16 Portrait, 16:9 Landscape, 1:1 Square), Duration (5s or 10s), Size (480p or 720p) and Quality (Medium or High). 7. Press Generate. The button shows Generating... and a card shows Rendering with the effect name. 8. When the toast says Video ready, play the result and press Download.
Steps:
- Open #/ai-vfx and pick a tab.
- Click an effect card.
- Add an image by upload or https link.
- Optionally describe the subject.
- Choose Aspect, Duration, Size and Quality.
- Press Generate and wait for Video ready.
- Press Download on the result card.
Getting started:
- Keep the defaults (9:16, 5s, 480p, Medium) for your first test; they render fastest.
- Try a Motion Controls move like Dolly In on a clear product or portrait photo.
- Once you like the effect, switch Size to 720p and Quality to High for a final render.
Tips:

chunks.title: AI VFX Studio — How to use
chunks.text:
- Test with defaults first, then upgrade to 720p and High for the keeper.
- Use sharp, well-lit images with a clear subject.
- Match the subject to the effect: car for Car Explosion, person for transformations.
- Keep prompts to a few words naming the subject.
Best practices:
- Pick Aspect first so you do not need to re-render for a different platform.
- Download clips you like right away.
- Use short prompts and one effect per render.

- Four dropdowns: Aspect, Duration, Size, Quality.
- Generate button with live Rendering message and a results grid with Download links.
- Results saved to your generation history.

chunks.text:
- feature: Prompt box | explanation: Placeholder text: Optional: describe the subject (e.g. a red sports car). The text is passed into the effect's built-in prompt template. | whyToUse: Name your subject so the effect is applied to the right thing. | inputRequired: Optional. | restrictions: Keep it short and about the subject; it is not a free-form scene description.
- feature: Results grid | explanation: While rendering, a card says Rendering and the effect name. When ready a video card appears with playback controls, the effect name and a Download link. New results appear first. | whyToUse: Preview and download without leaving the page. | inputRequired: A finished generation. | restrictions: The results grid only holds this visit's results; older ones are in your generation history. There are no Add to Library, Timeline, Compare or Publish buttons on this page.
Modes:
- AI Effects
- Motion Controls
- VFX
Mode details:
- mode: AI Effects | description: Creative AI transformations and character or scene effects (64 presets). | useCase: Viral clips, character transformations, fun reveals.
- mode: Motion Controls | description: Camera movements applied to your image (47 presets). | useCase: Cinematic push-ins, orbits, crane moves and lens looks.

chunks.title: AI VFX Studio — Features
chunks.text:
- mode: VFX | description: Elements and destruction effects (9 presets). | useCase: Explosions, tornado, electricity, levitation and decay.
Models:
AI VFX Studio has no model picker. All three tabs call the MuAPI generate_wan_ai_effects endpoint (a Wan-based effects service) through the shared MuAPI client. The AI Effects list comes from the ai-video-effects model definition, Motion Controls from motion-controls and VFX from the vfx model, so every card shown is a name the API accepts. The catalog file describes ai-video-effects as an AI video effects pipeline, motion-controls as motion parameter control for image-to-video, and vfx as visual effects processing. No price, speed or quality numbers for these models appear in the catalog, description or comparison files, so none are stated.

chunks.title: AI VFX Studio — Problems and limits
chunks.text:
AI VFX Studio (#/ai-vfx). Problems and limits.
Troubleshooting:
- Toast says Select an effect first: click one of the effect cards, then press Generate.
- Toast says Add an image (upload or https URL) first: upload a picture or paste an https link and wait for the thumbnail to appear in the box.
- Toast says Image URL must start with http(s)://: paste a full link beginning with https://.
- Settings window opens when you upload or generate: add your MuAPI key and try again.
- Toast says Upload failed or shows an upload error: check the file is JPEG, PNG, WebP or GIF and 10 MB or smaller, then retry.
- Toast says No video URL returned: the service finished without a video. Try again, or choose another effect or image.
- Generation failed toast (shown for about 6 seconds): read the message, retry, or reduce to the defaults (5s, 480p, Medium).
- Image is blank or the preview does not load from a pasted URL: the link may block hotlinking. Download the image and upload it instead.
- An effect card shows no thumbnail: the picture is missing but the effect still works.
Troubleshooting steps:
- issue: Nothing happens when I press Generate | steps: Check the line above the prompt shows Effect: and a name.; Confirm a thumbnail appears in the image box.; Wait: while busy the button reads Generating... and is disabled.

chunks.title: AI VFX Studio — Problems and limits
chunks.text:
- issue: Upload keeps failing | steps: Use JPEG, PNG, WebP or GIF.; Keep the file at 10 MB or less.; Make sure your MuAPI key is saved.; Try pasting an image URL instead.
- issue: The effect does not look right | steps: Use a clear, well-composed image with an obvious subject.; Add a short prompt naming the subject.; Switch Quality to High and Size to 720p.; Try a different effect in the same tab.
Common problems:
- problem: Output looks low resolution | whyItHappens: Default Size is 480p. | howToFix: Change Size to 720p and Quality to High.
- problem: Portrait video when I wanted landscape | whyItHappens: Default Aspect is 9:16 Portrait. | howToFix: Change Aspect to 16:9 Landscape before pressing Generate.
- problem: Effect ignores my prompt | whyItHappens: The prompt is dropped into the effect's template and is only meant to describe the subject. | howToFix: Reword the prompt as a short noun phrase, like a red sports car.
Limitations:
- Single image input only; no video or multi-image input.
- Preset effects only; no custom effect creation.
- Duration options are only 5s and 10s; resolution options only 480p and 720p.
- No compare, library, timeline or social-publish buttons on this page.
- Requires a MuAPI key; uploads follow MuAPI limits (10 MB for images).

chunks.title: AI VFX Studio — Problems and limits
chunks.text:
- Duplicate-looking names exist across studios (for example Flying also appears in Effects Studio's Video FX v2 tab); each studio uses its own list.
Limit details:
- limitation: Only 480p or 720p | impact: Output is not full HD. | workaround: Use Upscale tools in Video Tools (#/videotools) to enlarge the finished clip.
- limitation: One image at a time | impact: You cannot blend several images into one effect. | workaround: Use Animate Studio with a reference-style model, or Video Studio.
- limitation: No library or timeline buttons | impact: You must download the clip to reuse it elsewhere. | workaround: Use Download, then upload into Timeline or Video Tools. Your history also keeps the generation.
FAQs:
- question: How many effects are there? | answer: The tabs show AI Effects 64, Motion Controls 47 and VFX 9, so 120 presets. The upstream project text mentions 80+ effects, but the numbers on the tab buttons in this app are the ones to trust.
- question: Can I make a 10 second video? | answer: Yes. Set Duration to 10s. The default is 5s.

chunks.title: AI VFX Studio — Problems and limits
chunks.text:
- question: What is the difference between this and Effects Studio? | answer: AI VFX Studio focuses on video-from-one-image with Aspect, Duration, Size and Quality controls and includes the VFX tab. Effects Studio also has still-image effect tabs, Video FX v2, compare, library, timeline and Advanced settings, but fixes video at 720p and 5 seconds.
- question: Do I need a prompt? | answer: No. It is optional and is only used to describe the subject.
- question: Which image formats work? | answer: The uploader accepts JPEG, PNG, WebP and GIF. You can also paste an https image link.
- question: How long does it take? | answer: The upstream README says typically 1 to 3 minutes. The page itself shows Rendering until the service replies; actual times vary by effect, duration and quality.
- question: Where are my videos kept? | answer: The results grid shows videos from this visit with a Download link, and each one is saved to your generation history.

chunks.title: Animate Studio — Overview
chunks.text:
Animate Studio (#/animate). Overview.
Description:
Animate Studio turns a single still image or product shot into a 3 to 12 second video with AI motion. You add an image, optionally describe the motion, choose duration and resolution, and press Animate. By default it uses Seedance Lite; you can switch to Choose a model to pick any image-to-video model.
Summary:
Turn any image or product shot into a 3-12s video with AI motion.
About:

chunks.title: Animate Studio — Overview
chunks.text:
Animate Studio is a simple image-to-video page. The source can be an uploaded image or a photoshoot you made earlier in Photo Studio. You write a Motion Prompt (or tap one of five suggestion chips such as Slow pan across the scene with subtle motion), pick a Duration (3, 5, 10 or 12 seconds) and a Resolution (480p, 720p or 1080p), and press Animate. In the default mode the studio calls the Seedance Lite image-to-video model with your prompt, duration and resolution. If you want another model, press the Model button so it reads Choose a model, pick from the MuAPI Model (I2V) list and optionally open extra controls (Negative Prompt, Seed, Steps, Guidance Scale, Denoise Strength, CFG Scale, Thumbnail URL, Prompt Extend). The finished video plays in a result card with a Download button, is saved to your generation history, and (when a brand exists) appears under Animation History. A Use My Brand row lets you connect brand details through a personalization window. Storyboard Studio can also send a frame and its motion prompt straight to this page.
Best for:
Anyone who wants to bring a photo, product shot, poster or generated image to life with a short camera move or ambient motion, and wants control over the motion prompt, length and model.
When to use it:
- You have one image (product shot, portrait, artwork, storyboard frame) and want a short moving clip.

chunks.title: Animate Studio — Overview
chunks.text:
- You want to describe the motion yourself, for example slow pan, zoom in with focus pull, or floating dust particles.
- You want to compare different image-to-video models on the same image.
- You want to animate a photoshoot created in Photo Studio.
- You are continuing from Storyboard Studio and want to animate a frame.
When to use another studio:
- Use Effects Studio (#/effects) or AI VFX Studio (#/ai-vfx) when you want a named preset effect (Dolly In, Cakeify, Building Explosion) rather than a free-form prompt.
- Use Video Studio (#/video) for text-to-video, start and end frame control, reference video and the full set of video model options.
- Use Lip Sync Studio (#/lipsync) or Avatar Studio (#/avatar) when the image should talk.
- Use Video Tools (#/videotools) to upscale, caption, translate or recast a finished clip.
- Use Storyboard Studio (#/storyboard) to plan several frames first, then send frames here.
- Use Image Studio (#/image) if you still need to create the image.

chunks.title: Animate Studio — How to use
chunks.text:
Animate Studio (#/animate). How to use.
How to use:
1. Open Animate Studio from the side menu (#/animate). 2. Choose a source tab: Upload image or From Photo Studio. 3. Upload your image (or choose a photoshoot under Select a photoshoot...). 4. In Motion Prompt, type how the image should move, or click one of the five suggestion chips. 5. Choose Duration (3, 5, 10 or 12) and Resolution (480p, 720p or 1080p). 6. Leave the Model button on Seedance Lite (default), or press it to switch to Choose a model and pick one from MuAPI Model (I2V); optionally fill the advanced fields. 7. Press Animate. The button reads Animating... and an overlay says Animating image.... 8. When the toast says Animation complete, watch the result card and press Download.
Steps:
- Open #/animate.
- Pick Upload image or From Photo Studio and add your source.
- Write a Motion Prompt or tap a suggestion chip.
- Set Duration and Resolution.
- Optionally press the Model button to Choose a model.
- Press Animate.
- Download the result.
Getting started:
- Upload a clean image with an obvious subject.
- Tap the first suggestion chip and press Animate at 5s and 480p for a fast first test.
- If you like it, rerun at 720p or 1080p, or try another model.
- Make sure your MuAPI key is saved in settings.
Tips:
- Describe only one motion at a time.
- Start at 480p to save time; upscale later if needed.

chunks.title: Animate Studio — How to use
chunks.text:
- Use clean, high contrast images with a clear subject.
- Add a Negative Prompt such as distortion or flicker when using Choose a model.
Best practices:
- Test with the default model first, then compare one or two others.
- Keep the same image and prompt when comparing models.
- Download the clip you like straight away.

Animate Studio (#/animate). Features.
Key features:

- Optional advanced fields when choosing a model: Negative Prompt, Seed, Steps, Guidance Scale, Denoise Strength, CFG Scale, Thumbnail URL, Prompt Extend.
- Use My Brand / Connect Personalization row for brand details.
- Result card with video player, details line and Download button.
- Animation History grid of the latest 8 animations for your brand.
- Hand-off from Storyboard Studio of frame image, motion prompt and duration.

After you choose it a small preview appears under the picker. | whyToUse: The normal way to start. | inputRequired: One image. | restrictions: Images only (videos and documents are not accepted here). The MuAPI image limit is 10 MB.

chunks.title: Animate Studio — Problems and limits
chunks.text:
Animate Studio (#/animate). Problems and limits.
Troubleshooting:
- Toast says Please upload an image first: add an image on the Upload image tab, or pick a photoshoot, before pressing Animate.
- From Photo Studio shows No photoshoots found. Create one in Photo Studio first.: make a photoshoot in Photo Studio or switch to Upload image.
- Animation returned no video: the service finished without output. Retry, shorten the duration, or try another model.
- Error toast after Animate (shows the error text): read the message; common causes are a missing MuAPI key, unsupported duration or resolution for the chosen model, or a service problem. Retry with 5s and 480p.
- My model choice seems ignored: press the Model button so it reads Choose a model, then select an entry in MuAPI Model (I2V). If left on Select a model... the default Seedance Lite is used.
- Chosen advanced values have no effect: not every model supports Seed, Steps, Guidance, Denoise or CFG. Leave them empty to use model defaults.
- Animation History is empty: it only records when a brand exists in this browser; your result card and generation history still show the video.
- Prompt box looks empty although a chip is highlighted: click the chip to fill the text, or type your own. Empty is fine in default mode.
- Upload fails or the image is rejected: use a JPEG, PNG or WebP under 10 MB.
Troubleshooting steps:

chunks.title: Animate Studio — Problems and limits
chunks.text:
- issue: Animate fails right away | steps: Check an image is shown in the preview.; Make sure your MuAPI key is saved in settings.; Switch the Model button back to Seedance Lite (default).; Use 5s and 480p and try again.
- issue: Motion is too subtle or wrong | steps: Be specific: say what moves and how (camera pans left, steam rises).; Try a different suggestion chip.; Try Choose a model with a higher end model.; Use a longer duration for slower moves.
- issue: Result is low resolution | steps: Change Resolution to 720p or 1080p.; If a model errors, drop to 720p.; Use Video Tools to upscale afterwards.
Common problems:
- problem: The subject distorts or morphs | whyItHappens: Large motions on complex images are hard for image-to-video models. | howToFix: Use a gentler prompt (subtle camera move), a shorter duration or a different model.
- problem: Prompt is not followed | whyItHappens: Some models weigh the image more than the text. | howToFix: Simplify the prompt to one motion, add Negative Prompt, or try another model.
- problem: Clip is shorter than expected | whyItHappens: The chosen model may cap duration. | howToFix: Pick a different model or shorter setting; join clips in Timeline.
Limitations:
- Image input only (no video input); one image at a time.
- Duration choices are limited to 3, 5, 10 and 12 seconds.

chunks.title: Animate Studio — Problems and limits
chunks.text:
- Models that need first and last frames, reference videos or audio cannot be fully used from this page.
- Animation History only shows when a brand exists and shows the latest 8.
- Resolution and duration support depends on the model; the page does not filter options by model.
Limit details:
- limitation: Options are not filtered per model | impact: A model may not support 1080p or 12 seconds and could reject or change the request. | workaround: Use 5s and 480p/720p if you see an error, then increase gradually.
- limitation: Choose a model without picking one | impact: The studio silently falls back to Seedance Lite. | workaround: Pick an entry from MuAPI Model (I2V) before pressing Animate.
- limitation: Reference-style models | impact: Models named Reference, First Last Frame or Omni Reference need extra inputs that Animate does not collect. | workaround: Use Video Studio (#/video) for those models.
FAQs:
- question: What model does Animate use by default? | answer: Seedance Lite (model id seedance-lite-i2v). The Model button reads Seedance Lite (default) until you switch it.
- question: How long can the video be? | answer: You can choose 3, 5, 10 or 12 seconds. Default is 5.
- question: Which resolutions are available? | answer: 480p (default), 720p and 1080p. Whether a specific model supports each is not checked by the page.

chunks.title: Animate Studio — Problems and limits
chunks.text:
- question: Do I have to write a prompt? | answer: No. In the default mode an empty prompt uses Slow pan across the scene with subtle motion. A specific prompt usually gives better control.
- question: Can I animate a video? | answer: No. Animate takes images only. For video, use Video Tools or Video Studio.
- question: Where do my animations go? | answer: You get a result card with Download, an entry in your generation history, and (when a brand exists) an Animation History entry.
- question: Why is Animation History empty? | answer: It is tied to a brand saved in this browser. Without one, history is not shown there.
- question: What is Use My Brand? | answer: A button that opens a personalization window to connect your business name, colours, logos and reference frames.

chunks.title: Animate Studio — Workflows and use cases
chunks.text:
Animate Studio (#/animate). Workflows and use cases.
Example workflows:
- title: Quick product animation | steps: Open Upload image and add a product photo.; Click Zoom into the subject with gentle focus pull.; Keep 5 seconds and 480p.; Press Animate and watch the result.; If happy, rerun at 1080p and Download.
- title: Compare two models | steps: Upload your image and write one motion prompt.; Run once with Seedance Lite (default).; Press the Model button to Choose a model and select another entry.; Press Animate again and compare both clips in your generation history.
- title: Animate a branded photoshoot | steps: Create a photoshoot in Photo Studio.; In Animate pick From Photo Studio.; Choose Select a photoshoot... entry.; Pick Particle dust floating in light beams.; Press Animate and Download.
Use cases:

- studio: video | relationship: Full video generation with every model option. | whenToMove: When you need start and end frames, reference clips or audio. | why: Animate is deliberately simple.

chunks.title: Animate Studio — Glossary
chunks.text: Glossary: Image-to-video (I2V): AI that creates a short video from one still image. | Motion Prompt: A sentence describing how the image should move. | Seedance Lite: ByteDance's lightweight image-to-video model, used by default. | Seed: A number that makes a result repeatable; -1 means random. | Negative Prompt: What to avoid in the result. | Guidance Scale: How strictly the model follows the prompt. | Denoise Strength: How much the result may change from the source. | CFG Scale: Another strength setting for following the prompt; exact effect depends on the model. | Prompt Extend: An option that lets the model expand your prompt automatically, where supported. | Photoshoot: A branded image set created in Photo Studio.

chunks.title: Apps — Overview
chunks.text:
Apps (#/apps). Overview.
Description:
The Apps hub is the home screen of the app: a searchable grid of every creative tool, grouped as Image apps, Video apps, Agents apps and My Work.
Summary:
Searchable grid of all 26 tools. Pick one to open it.
About:
Apps (route #/apps) is a hub page titled "Every creative tool, one place" with the line "Studios, effects, editors and AI apps. Pick one and start creating." and a badge reading "Explore apps". It shows three step cards: "1 Choose an app" (Image, video, cinema, audio and more, each studio is tuned for one job), "2 Create" (Describe what you want, pick a model and press Generate) and "3 Keep it" (Results land in your Library, ready to edit, render or publish). Below that is a "Search apps..." box and the app cards. The cards are built from the side menu itself, so the hub and the left menu list the same tools. There are 26 cards in four sections. Clicking the logo at the top left of the header also goes to the Apps hub (its label is "All apps"). The retired Chat, Assist and Training pages now redirect here.
Best for:
Finding out what tools exist, jumping to the right studio when you are not sure where to start, and getting back to a tool you used recently.
When to use it:
- You are new and want to see every tool in one place.
- You know what you want to make (an image, a video, a voiceover) but not which studio does it.

chunks.title: Apps — Overview
chunks.text:
- You want to reopen a tool you used recently (the Recently Used row).
- The side menu feels long and you want to search by name or description.
When to use another studio:
- If you want ready-made starting points with your own photo or video, use Templates (#/templates).
- If you want inspiration and sample prompts, use Explore (#/explore).
- If you want your finished files, use Library (#/library) or Content (#/content-library).

chunks.title: Apps — How to use
chunks.text:
Apps (#/apps). How to use.
How to use:
1. Open Apps from the first item in the left side menu (or click the logo at the top left). 2. Optionally type in "Search apps..." to narrow the list. 3. Click a card (or focus it and press Enter or Space) to open that app. 4. Use the left side menu or the logo to come back.
Steps:
- Open Apps from the left side menu or click the logo at the top left.
- Scan the four sections or type in "Search apps...".
- Click the card for the tool you want.
- To return, click the logo again or use the side menu.
Getting started:
- New to the app: start with Image Studio (describe a picture, press Generate) or Templates if you want a guided start.
- Add your MuAPI key first so generation works (see the API keys help topic).
Tips:
- Use the search box instead of scrolling.
- Check the card badges for quick hints, e.g. "200+ effects" on Effects Studio.
- Cards work with the keyboard: Tab to a card and press Enter.
Best practices:
- Start from the output you want (image, video, audio) and pick that section.
- Open Library after generating to find your results.

chunks.title: Audio Studio — Overview
chunks.text:
Audio Studio (#/audio). Overview.
Description:
Audio Studio generates music, speech (text-to-speech) and sound effects from a text prompt, using a model you pick from a list. Results play on a waveform player with a Download Audio button.
Summary:
Generate music, speech and sound effects.
About:
Audio Studio is one form for several kinds of audio. You choose a model (for example Suno for songs, MiniMax, ElevenLabs, Gemini or Fish Audio for speech, Lyria or MiniMax Music for music, Suno Generate Sounds or MM Audio for sound effects), type a prompt, set the controls the model offers, and click 'Generate Audio'. The form changes with the model: music models show a Style list, speech models show a Voice list, and many newer models show their own controls (voice, lyrics, tempo, reference audio, and so on) built from the model's options. Generated tracks appear in a waveform player with play, mute, volume, a Download Audio button and an Audio Editor panel, and are kept in a history grid. You can also drag an audio file onto the page to use as a reference input for models that accept audio.
Best for:
Creators who need background music, a voice-over, a song, or sound effects for videos, and beginners who want to try several audio models from one place.
When to use it:
- You need background music or a full song for a video.

chunks.title: Audio Studio — Overview
chunks.text:
- You need a narration or voice-over from written text (text-to-speech).
- You need sound effects or ambience.
- You want to clone a voice, extend, remix or add vocals/instrumentals to an existing track using the Suno or MiniMax tools.
- You need an audio file to feed into Lip Sync Studio or Avatar Studio.
When to use another studio:
- Use Lip Sync Studio (#/lipsync) to make a portrait or video speak your audio.
- Use Avatar Studio (#/avatar) to make a talking avatar video from your audio.
- Use Video Studio (#/video) to generate video; some video models can create their own audio.
- Use Timeline Studio (#/timeline) or Render Studio (#/render) to place your audio on a video timeline and export.
- Use Video Agent (#/video-agent) when you want a whole video with narration made automatically.

chunks.title: Audio Studio — How to use
chunks.text:
Audio Studio (#/audio). How to use.
How to use:
1. Open Audio Studio from the side menu (#/audio). 2. Use the model picker at the top to choose a model: a music model for songs, a speech model for narration, or a sound-effects model for effects. 3. Type your text in the 'Prompt' box ('Describe the music or speech you want to generate...'). For speech, write the exact words to be spoken. 4. Set the controls that appear: Style (music), Duration (15s/30s/60s/120s), Voice (MiniMax speech), and any model-specific options. 5. For models that need audio, upload an 'Upload audio track' file or drop an audio file on the page. 6. Optionally open Advanced to change Speed for speech. If you want a particular tone or emotion, describe it in the prompt. 7. Click 'Generate Audio'. The button shows 'Generating...' with a loading overlay. 8. When the toast 'Audio generated successfully!' appears, press Play on the waveform, then click 'Download Audio'. 9. Use the Audio Editor (Trim, End, Fade In, Fade Out) if you want, or pick an earlier result from the history grid.
Steps:
- Pick an audio model.
- Write a prompt (description for music or the words to speak for speech).
- Set style, duration, voice or other options.
- Upload reference audio if the model asks for it.
- Click Generate Audio.
- Play the result and click Download Audio.
Getting started:

chunks.title: Audio Studio — How to use
chunks.text:
- For speech: keep Minimax Speech Turbo, type a sentence, choose a Voice and click Generate Audio.
- For a song: choose Suno Create Music, describe the song, pick a Style and click Generate Audio.
- For sound effects: choose Suno Generate Sounds and describe the sound, for example 'A car passing by'.
Tips:
- Be specific with music genres and moods.
- Use SSML tags for advanced speech control (where the chosen speech model supports them).
- Combine multiple sound effects for ambience.
- Write numbers and acronyms the way you want them spoken.
- Download your favorite results; history is only stored in this browser.
Best practices:
- Test with a short prompt and duration first.
- Put genre, mood, tempo and instruments in the prompt for music.
- Use separate generations for narration and music and mix them in a timeline.
- Use a stricter, shorter script for clearer speech.

chunks.title: Audio Studio — Features
chunks.text:
Audio Studio (#/audio). Features.
Key features:
- Model picker with search and provider filter covering music, speech, voice cloning and sound-effect models.
- Prompt box: 'Describe the music or speech you want to generate...'.
- Style list for music models: Pop, Rock, Electronic, Classical, Jazz, Hip Hop, Ambient.
- Duration buttons: 15s, 30s, 60s, 120s.
- Voice list for MiniMax speech models: Female 1, Male Qingse.
- Tone list (Neutral, Cheerful, Serious, Excited, Calm, Empathetic, Warm, Authoritative): shown only for a model whose settings include a tone field. No current model has one.
- Emotion list (None, Happy, Sad, Angry, Surprised, Fearful, Disgusted, Neutral): shown only for a model whose settings include an emotion field. No current model has one.
- Speed slider (0.5x to 2.0x) for speech models. A Pitch slider appears only for a model whose settings include a pitch field; for speech models without one, the studio shows a hint to describe the delivery in the prompt.
- Model-specific controls built from each model's options: toggles, dropdowns, sliders, audio uploaders.
- Reference attachments: upload an audio track (or drop an audio file on the page).
- Waveform player with Play, Mute, Volume, time display and 'Download Audio'.
- Audio Editor with Trim and End sliders, Fade In, Fade Out, Apply Edits and Reset.

chunks.title: Audio Studio — Features
chunks.text:
- History grid of your last 30 results and recovery of jobs still running after a page reload.
- Thumbnail button (square cover art), more-tools menu (GTM Boost, Recipes, Monetize, Prompts) and Personalize.
Feature details:
- feature: Model selector | explanation: Pick the audio model at the top of the page. The default is the first model in the list, Minimax Speech Turbo. Your last selected model and form values are remembered in this browser. | whyToUse: Different models are built for songs, speech, sound effects or voice cloning. | inputRequired: None. | restrictions: Switching model clears model-specific options (they reset).
- feature: Prompt | explanation: The text for the model: a description of the music, or the actual words to speak for speech models. | whyToUse: It is the main instruction for generation. | inputRequired: Required for models that use a prompt. If empty: 'Please enter a prompt for this model.' | restrictions: Some models limit length: ElevenLabs v4 up to 2,000 characters, Lyria models up to 2,000 characters, Suno Generate Sounds up to 500 characters. The box is hidden for voice-clone models that take no prompt.

chunks.title: Audio Studio — Features
chunks.text:
- feature: Style (music) | explanation: A dropdown with 'Select a style' plus Pop, Rock, Electronic, Classical, Jazz, Hip Hop, Ambient. Shown for music models and models flagged as supporting styles. | whyToUse: Quickly steer the genre. | inputRequired: Optional. | restrictions: Only visible for music-type or style-supporting models.
- feature: Duration | explanation: Buttons 15s, 30s, 60s and 120s (30s is the default). The value is sent for music and other non-speech models. | whyToUse: Choose how long the track should be. | inputRequired: Optional. | restrictions: Some models decide length themselves; for example Lyria 3 is described as producing clips up to 30 seconds. The button row is always visible but is not sent for MiniMax speech models.

chunks.title: Audio Studio — Features
chunks.text:
- feature: Voice and Speed (speech) | explanation: For MiniMax speech models (type tts) you get a Voice list (Female 1, Male Qingse) and a Speed slider from 0.5x to 2.0x. Some speech models, such as ElevenLabs Turbo 2.5, show their own Speed setting in the model options instead. | whyToUse: Adjust how a narrator sounds. | inputRequired: Optional (defaults: Female 1, 1.0x). | restrictions: Tone, Emotion and Pitch controls appear only for a model that has those fields, and are then sent. None of the current models do, so speech models show a hint instead: describe the delivery in your prompt (for example 'in a warm, slow, cheerful voice').
- feature: Model-specific controls | explanation: Newer models show their own options right under the prompt, for example ElevenLabs 'Voice' (voice_daniel, voice_liam), Suno 'Loop', 'Sound Tempo' and 'Sound Key', Suno vocal gender and style weight, MiniMax Music lyrics and instrumental toggle, and Gemini TTS speakers/scene settings. | whyToUse: Get the most out of that particular model. | inputRequired: Depends on the model. | restrictions: Options and limits come from each model; read the small help text under each control.

chunks.title: Audio Studio — Features
chunks.text:
- feature: Audio upload and drag and drop | explanation: Models that need audio (for example Suno Add Vocals, Add Instrumental, Voice Cloning, Mashup) show an 'Upload audio track' area ('MP3, WAV, M4A up to 20MB'). Mashup shows up to 2 tracks. You can also use the attachment toolbar or drop an audio file anywhere on the page ('Drop audio to use as input'). | whyToUse: Remix, extend, clone or add vocals to existing audio. | inputRequired: Only for models that need audio. | restrictions: Own check: files over 20MB are rejected with 'Audio file exceeds 20MB limit.' The shared upload adapter may apply a stricter limit and show its own message. Dropping a non-audio file shows 'Drop an audio file (mp3, wav, m4a…)'.
- feature: Waveform player and Audio Editor | explanation: After generation you see a waveform with Play, Mute, Volume and 'Download Audio'. Below it the Audio Editor offers Trim and End sliders (percent), Fade In, Fade Out, Apply Edits and Reset. | whyToUse: Preview and make quick edits. | inputRequired: A finished track. | restrictions: Applying edits shows the toast 'Audio edits applied (trim/fade simulation)', which indicates the editor is a simple preview-style tool; use Timeline Studio or Workbench for real editing.

chunks.title: Audio Studio — Features
chunks.text:
- feature: History and job recovery | explanation: Results are added to a history grid (up to 30). If you reload while a job runs, the studio recovers it and shows 'Recovered a generation that finished while you were away'. | whyToUse: Do not lose long jobs. | inputRequired: None. | restrictions: Stored locally in this browser.
Modes:
- Music (songs and instrumentals)
- Speech / text-to-speech
- Voice cloning

Mode details:
- mode: Music | description: Generates songs or instrumentals from a description, with optional Style and Duration. | useCase: Background music, jingles, songs.
- mode: Speech | description: Turns your text into spoken audio with a chosen voice. | useCase: Voice-overs and narration.
- mode: Voice cloning | description: Models Minimax Voice Clone and Suno Voice Cloning create a voice from an audio sample. | useCase: Reusing a consistent voice.
- mode: Sound effects | description: Suno Generate Sounds and MM Audio V2 create effects and ambience from a description. | useCase: Foley, impacts, ambience.

- name: Style | description: Genre choice for music models. | required: false | whenToUse: When you want a clear genre. | restrictions: Shown for music models only.

chunks.text:
- name: Speed | description: Slider 0.5x to 2.0x in 0.1 steps, default 1.0x, for speech models. | required: false | whenToUse: Speech. | restrictions: Sent to the speech model. Tone, Emotion and Pitch are not offered unless the selected model has such a field.

chunks.title: Audio Studio — Problems and limits
chunks.text:
Audio Studio (#/audio). Problems and limits.
Troubleshooting:
- Toast 'Please enter a prompt for this model.': type something in the Prompt box before clicking Generate Audio.
- Sign-in window appears on Generate: sign in (and add credits) and click Generate Audio again.
- Toast 'Audio file exceeds 20MB limit.': use a smaller audio file or compress it.
- Toast 'Drop an audio file (mp3, wav, m4a…)': you dropped a file that is not audio.
- Upload shows an error toast: the upload service rejected the file; check type and size and retry.
- Toast 'Failed to generate audio' or another error: try again, shorten the prompt, or choose another model.
- Style list is missing: only music models show Style; pick a music model.
- Voice list is missing: only MiniMax speech models show the Voice list; other speech models have their own voice option under the prompt.
- I can't find Tone, Emotion or Pitch: they only appear for a model that has those settings, and no current model does. Describe the delivery in the prompt instead.
- Page reloaded while generating: wait; the studio shows 'Recovered a generation that finished while you were away' when the job completes.
Troubleshooting steps:
- issue: Generate Audio does nothing | steps: Check that the Prompt box is not empty.; Check you are signed in.; Click Generate Audio again.

chunks.title: Audio Studio — Problems and limits
chunks.text:
- issue: Reference audio will not upload | steps: Check the file is MP3, WAV or M4A.; Check it is under 20MB (and under 10MB if the shared uploader complains).; Retry or use the attachment toolbar Audio button.
- issue: Speech sounds wrong | steps: Check the prompt contains exactly the text to be spoken.; Try a different Voice.; Change Speed under Advanced.; Try another speech model such as Minimax Speech HD or Eleven v4.
- issue: Music does not match the genre | steps: Pick a Style.; Add genre, mood, tempo and instruments to the prompt.; Try Suno Create Music or MiniMax Music 3.0.
Common problems:
- problem: My model has different controls than another model | whyItHappens: The form is built from each model's options. | howToFix: Read the control labels and help text for your model.
- problem: A model needs an audio upload but I only have text | whyItHappens: Edit tools like Add Vocals, Add Instrumental, Voice Cloning and Mashup need an input track. | howToFix: Generate a track first with Suno Create Music, download it, then upload it.
- problem: My settings were remembered from last time | whyItHappens: The studio saves your model, prompt and options in this browser. | howToFix: Change them in the form or clear the prompt.
Limitations:

chunks.title: Audio Studio — Problems and limits
chunks.text:
- Tone, Emotion and Pitch controls are not offered for the current models, because none has a matching setting. Describe the delivery in the prompt instead.
- Duration choices are fixed to 15, 30, 60 and 120 seconds; individual models may produce shorter or fixed-length results.
- The Audio Editor is a basic preview tool; applying edits shows a 'simulation' toast.
- Reference audio uploads are limited to 20MB by this studio and possibly less by the shared upload service.
- History is stored in this browser only.
- Generation requires sign-in and credits; otherwise you are asked to sign in.
Limit details:
- limitation: No tone, emotion or pitch controls | impact: You cannot dial in tone, emotion or pitch with a control; the studio shows a hint instead. | workaround: Put the desired delivery in the prompt text (for example 'in a calm, warm voice'), or choose a model with its own expressive settings (for example Eleven v4 or Gemini TTS).
- limitation: Fixed duration buttons | impact: You cannot enter an exact length such as 45 seconds. | workaround: Generate the nearest length and trim in the Audio Editor or Timeline Studio.
- limitation: Basic editor | impact: Trim and fade are simple. | workaround: Download and edit in Timeline Studio (#/timeline) or Workbench (#/workbench).
FAQs:

chunks.title: Audio Studio — Problems and limits
chunks.text:
- question: Can Audio Studio make songs with lyrics? | answer: Yes, with models such as Suno Create Music and MiniMax Music 3.0 (which has a lyrics option). Describe the song or enter lyrics where the model provides a lyrics field.
- question: Which model is the default? | answer: The first in the list, Minimax Speech Turbo, unless the studio restored a previously used model.
- question: How long can the audio be? | answer: The Duration buttons offer 15s, 30s, 60s and 120s, but each model decides what it can really produce; for example Lyria 3 is described as clips up to 30 seconds.
- question: Can I clone a voice? | answer: Yes, with Minimax Voice Clone or Suno Voice Cloning by uploading an audio sample. Make sure you have permission to use the voice.
- question: Is there a Tone, Emotion or Pitch control? | answer: Only for a model that has those settings, and none of the current models do, so the studio shows a hint instead. Describe the delivery in your prompt, or use a model with expressive settings such as Eleven v4 or Gemini TTS.
- question: Where do I use the audio I make? | answer: Download it, then upload it to Lip Sync Studio, Avatar Studio, Timeline Studio or Render Studio.

chunks.title: Audio Studio — Workflows and use cases
chunks.text:
Audio Studio (#/audio). Workflows and use cases.
Example workflows:

- title: Background music | steps: Choose Suno Create Music.; Write 'calm lo-fi beat with soft piano' as the prompt.; Pick Style: Ambient or Electronic.; Choose Duration 60s.; Click Generate Audio and download.

- title: Short jingle | description: A 15 to 30 second music clip for intros. | steps: Choose a music model.; Describe mood and instruments.; Pick Duration 15s or 30s.; Generate. | expectedOutput: A short music clip.

chunks.title: Audio Studio — Glossary
chunks.text: Glossary: TTS: Text-to-speech: turning written text into spoken audio. | Voice cloning: Making a synthetic voice that resembles a sample you provide. | Style: A genre choice for music. | Duration: How long the generated audio should be. | Waveform: A picture of the sound over time shown in the player. | Trim / Fade: Cutting the start or end of a track, or fading volume in or out.

chunks.title: Avatar Studio — Overview
chunks.text:
Avatar Studio (#/avatar). Overview.
Description:
Avatar Studio creates talking avatar and lip sync videos. You pick a model, upload a source video or image and an audio file, and click Generate Avatar Video.
Summary:
Create talking avatars and lip sync videos.
About:
Avatar Studio is a single-form studio for talking-avatar and lip sync models. You choose a model from the model button at the top, upload a 'Source Video/Image', upload 'Audio (for lip sync)', open Advanced for any model-specific options, and click 'Generate Avatar Video'. The result plays on the page with Download Video, Publish to Social and Add AI Captions buttons. The form adapts to the model: the audio uploader, prompt box and Native Audio toggle only show when the selected model supports them. This studio does not design avatars (no hair, clothes or expression controls) and has no saved avatar library; it animates the image or video that you supply.
Best for:
Beginners who want a quick talking avatar or lip sync video from an image or video plus a voice recording, using one simple form.
When to use it:
- You have a face image or a video and an audio track and want a talking avatar video.
- You want to try the Kling Avatar, Infinite Talk, Wan 2.2 Speech to Video, LTX, VEED, Creatify or LatentSync models from one place.
- You want a talking spokesperson clip you can caption and publish to social.

chunks.title: Avatar Studio — Overview
chunks.text:
When to use another studio:
- Use Lip Sync Studio (#/lipsync) when you want a clear Portrait Image vs Video mode toggle, a resolution picker, history sidebar and the larger image-mode and video-mode model groups.
- Use Audio Studio (#/audio) to create the speech, music or sound effects that you upload here.
- Use Character Studio (#/character) or Influencer Studio (#/influencer) to design a consistent character or virtual influencer first.
- Use Video Studio (#/video) to generate new footage from a prompt instead of animating a supplied face.

chunks.title: Avatar Studio — How to use
chunks.text:
Avatar Studio (#/avatar). How to use.
How to use:
1. Open Avatar Studio from the side menu (#/avatar). 2. Click the model button at the top and choose a model. 3. Under 'Source Video/Image', upload your image or video (or browse Pexels). 4. If shown, upload your voice file under 'Audio (for lip sync)'. 5. If a 'Prompt (optional)' box appears, describe the animation you want. 6. If a 'Native Audio' toggle appears, switch it on only if you want the model's own audio. 7. Optionally open Advanced for extra options or click '🖼 Thumbnail' for a custom thumbnail. 8. Click 'Generate Avatar Video'. The button shows 'Generating...'. 9. When the video appears, click 'Download Video', 'Publish to Social' or '💬 Add AI Captions'.
Steps:
- Choose a model with the model button.
- Upload the source video or image.
- Upload the audio file.
- Fill the prompt if the box is shown.
- Click Generate Avatar Video.
- Download, publish or caption the result.
Getting started:
- Keep the default model for a first test.
- Use a clear front-facing face image.
- Use a short, clean voice recording.
- Click Generate Avatar Video and review the result before trying other models.
Tips:
- Use concise, clear scripts for best avatar performance.
- Photo avatars work best with well-lit, front-facing photos.
- Preview the result before publishing.

chunks.title: Avatar Studio — How to use
chunks.text:
- Keep the audio clean and free of background music for better lip matching.
Best practices:
- Test with a short audio clip first.
- Download the video immediately after it is generated.
- Create voice tracks in Audio Studio for consistent results.

chunks.title: Avatar Studio — Features
chunks.text:
Avatar Studio (#/avatar). Features.
Key features:
- Model selector button at the top with a searchable list of avatar and lip sync models.
- 'Source Video/Image' upload (also browse stock media from Pexels).
- 'Audio (for lip sync)' upload (shown only for models that use audio).
- 'Prompt (optional)' box with placeholder 'Describe the animation you want...' (shown only for models that accept a prompt).
- 'Native Audio' toggle (shown only for models that support it).
- Advanced panel for model-specific options, and a Thumbnail button for a custom thumbnail.
- Result card with video player, 'Download Video', 'Publish to Social' and '💬 Add AI Captions'.
- More-tools menu: GTM Boost, Recipes, Monetize, Prompts; Personalize trigger.
- Example gallery of sample avatar assets at the bottom of the page.
Feature details:
- feature: Model selector | explanation: The button at the top shows the current model name and provider. Click it to open the list and choose another model. The form updates to match the model. | whyToUse: Different models offer different quality tiers (for example Kling Avatar Standard vs Pro). | inputRequired: None. | restrictions: The default model is the first in the list, LTX LipSync.

chunks.title: Avatar Studio — Features
chunks.text:
- feature: Source Video/Image upload | explanation: The media that will be animated or re-synced. You can upload a file or browse stock videos and images from Pexels. | whyToUse: Every listed model needs source media. | inputRequired: One image or video. | restrictions: If you click Generate without it the studio shows 'Upload a source video or image first'. Shared MuAPI upload limits: images 10MB, video 50MB.
- feature: Audio (for lip sync) | explanation: Upload the voice or audio that the avatar should speak. It is shown when the selected model uses audio (all current models in the list do). | whyToUse: The audio drives the mouth movement. | inputRequired: An audio file (audio/*). | restrictions: Audio uploads fail with 'Audio upload failed: ...' if rejected. The shared upload limit for audio is 10MB. The studio does not stop you from clicking Generate without audio, so upload it before generating.
- feature: Prompt (optional) | explanation: A text box to describe the animation. It only appears for models that accept a prompt. | whyToUse: To steer the performance on models that support it. | inputRequired: If the box is shown and empty, Generate shows 'Please enter a prompt for this avatar model.' | restrictions: None of the currently listed standard models show the prompt box; it appears only if a model supports a prompt.

chunks.title: Avatar Studio — Features
chunks.text:
- feature: Native Audio toggle | explanation: Appears only for models whose inputs include native audio. It is off by default. | whyToUse: Lets a supporting model generate its own audio. | inputRequired: None. | restrictions: Hidden on models that do not support it.
- feature: Advanced options | explanation: Model-specific extra controls are built automatically from the model's options (video_url, audio_url and prompt are excluded because they have their own fields). | whyToUse: Fine-tune options a particular model exposes. | inputRequired: None. | restrictions: Most listed models expose few or no extra options, so the panel may be empty.
- feature: Result actions | explanation: After generation the video plays in a card with 'Download Video', 'Publish to Social' and '💬 Add AI Captions'. | whyToUse: Save, share or caption the result. | inputRequired: A completed generation. | restrictions: Success toast: 'Avatar generated successfully!'.
Modes:
- Image + audio -> talking avatar video
- Video + audio -> lip-synced video
Mode details:
- mode: Image-driven talking avatar | description: Models such as Kling Avatar, Infinite Talk Image to Video and WAN 2.2 Speech to Video animate a still image from audio. | useCase: Talking spokesperson from a single photo.

chunks.title: Avatar Studio — Features
chunks.text:
- mode: Video lip sync | description: Models such as VEED LipSync, Creatify LipSync, LatentSync and InfiniteTalk Video to Video re-sync an existing video to audio. | useCase: Dubbing or replacing speech in a clip.
Models:
Avatar Studio lists the models in avatarModels (src/lib/models.js), in this order: LTX LipSync (default; described as real-time lip sync from audio), LTX 19B LipSync (high-quality lip sync with 19B model), VEED LipSync, Creatify LipSync (for marketing videos), LatentSync (advanced latent space lip synchronization), Kling Avatar v2 Pro (professional AI avatar generation), Kling Avatar v2 Standard, Kling Avatar v1 Pro, Kling Avatar v1 Standard, WAN 2.2 Speech to Video (animate image from audio speech), InfiniteTalk Image to Video (create talking video from still image), InfiniteTalk Video to Video (lip sync video to video), and FLUX 3 Avatar (which has prompt, image, audio, video and native audio inputs). All except FLUX 3 Avatar are flagged as needing a video/image source and audio, with no prompt. The code does not rank them for price, speed or quality; the comparison data file has no avatar or lip sync entries. Kling Standard vs Pro are described as standard vs premium/professional tiers. For a larger, categorized lip sync model list with resolution options, see Lip Sync Studio.
