chunks.title: Avatar Studio — Problems and limits
chunks.text:
Avatar Studio (#/avatar). Problems and limits.
Troubleshooting:
- Toast 'Upload a source video or image first': upload media under 'Source Video/Image', then click Generate again.
- Toast 'Please enter a prompt for this avatar model.': the selected model shows a prompt box that must be filled.
- Toast 'Audio upload failed: ...': check the audio file type and size and try again; sign in if asked.
- Alert 'Please sign in and add api credits.': sign in and add credits, then retry.
- Toast 'Error: ...' after Generate: read the message, check your files, and try again or choose another model.
- Audio section is missing: the selected model does not use audio; pick a model that does.
- Native Audio toggle is missing: it only appears for models that support it.
- Result mouth does not match: use a clearer front-facing image, cleaner audio, or switch model (for example Kling Avatar Pro).
Troubleshooting steps:
- issue: Generate shows an error toast | steps: Read the exact text.; Upload any missing source or fill the prompt.; Sign in or add credits if asked.; Click Generate Avatar Video again.
- issue: Video is generated but the avatar is not speaking | steps: Check that you uploaded an audio file.; Use clean speech.; Try a different model.; Generate again.

chunks.title: Avatar Studio — Problems and limits
chunks.text:
- issue: Upload will not finish | steps: Check file size limits (image 10MB, video 50MB, audio 10MB).; Use common formats such as JPG/PNG, MP4, MP3/WAV.; Retry.
Common problems:
- problem: I cannot see the audio upload or prompt box | whyItHappens: The form shows only what the selected model needs. | howToFix: Choose a different model from the model button.
- problem: Where do I choose resolution? | whyItHappens: Avatar Studio has no dedicated resolution button. | howToFix: Open Advanced to see any options the model exposes, or use Lip Sync Studio (#/lipsync) which has a resolution picker.
- problem: Generation seems stuck | whyItHappens: Video models can take a while. | howToFix: Wait for 'Generating...' to finish. If it errors, retry with a shorter audio clip.
Limitations:
- No avatar design tools: no hair, clothing, skin, background or expression controls.
- No saved avatar library or voice library; you supply the source and audio each time.
- No language or accent selection; the audio you upload determines the speech.
- No in-page video trimming or timeline editing.
- Needs a signed-in account with credits to generate.
- Upload size limits follow the shared MuAPI limits (image 10MB, video 50MB, audio 10MB).
Limit details:

chunks.title: Avatar Studio — Problems and limits
chunks.text:
- limitation: You must bring your own audio | impact: Text cannot be typed to be spoken here. | workaround: Generate speech in Audio Studio (#/audio) and upload it.
- limitation: No avatar customization | impact: You cannot change how the avatar looks inside this studio. | workaround: Create or edit the face image in Character Studio (#/character) or Image Studio (#/image) first.
- limitation: Generate is not blocked when audio is missing | impact: You may spend a generation without audio and get an unsuitable result. | workaround: Always upload audio before clicking Generate Avatar Video.
FAQs:
- question: What is the difference between Avatar Studio and Lip Sync Studio? | answer: Both use talking-avatar and lip sync models. Lip Sync Studio has a Portrait Image / Video mode toggle, a resolution picker and a history panel; Avatar Studio is a simpler single form with a model button, Advanced options and a result card.
- question: Can I design my own avatar here? | answer: No. Avatar Studio animates the image or video you upload. It has no hair, clothing or expression controls.
- question: Do I need audio? | answer: Yes, for lip sync. Upload it under 'Audio (for lip sync)'. The form does not stop you if it is missing, but the result will not be useful.

chunks.title: Avatar Studio — Problems and limits
chunks.text:
- question: Which model should I start with? | answer: The default model (LTX LipSync) is a fine first test. Kling Avatar models are described as Standard and Pro tiers for talking avatars.
- question: Can I add subtitles? | answer: Yes. After the video appears click '💬 Add AI Captions'.

chunks.title: Brand Studio — Overview
chunks.text:
Brand Studio (#/brand). Overview.
Description:
Brand Studio turns a website URL into a saved Brand DNA (name, tagline, tone, colors, logo) and gives you linked tools to make on-brand campaigns, edit campaign assets, generate branded product photos and animate them.
Summary:
Paste any website URL - get your Brand DNA, on-brand campaigns, product photos and videos
About:
Brand Studio (#/brand, Image group of the side menu) is a home page for five connected brand tools. You paste your website address and click Analyze; the app reads the site and builds a Brand DNA record saved in your browser. From the Brand DNA editor (#/brand-dna) you can review and edit the identity, then open Campaigns (#/campaign) to generate concepts and platform-specific creatives, the Asset Editor (#/asset-edit) to compose a headline/body/CTA graphic, Photo Studio (#/photo-studio, also reachable as #/brand-photo-studio) to generate product photos across categories and styles, or Animate (#/animate) to bring branded assets to life. Only Brand Studio appears in the side menu; the sub-tools are reached from its Brand tools cards and from buttons on the Brand DNA page. Brand data is stored locally in your browser.
Best for:
Marketers, founders, agencies and e-commerce sellers who want on-brand social, ad and product visuals generated from their own website without designing from scratch.
When to use it:

chunks.title: Brand Studio — Overview
chunks.text:
- You want the app to learn your brand from your website URL.
- You want campaign concepts (4 ideas) and creatives sized for Instagram, LinkedIn, Facebook, X, web banners, email headers and YouTube thumbnails.
- You want batches of product photos in several settings and styles from one product image.
- You want to lay out a simple headline + body + call-to-action graphic on a colored or image background.
- You want to keep your brand name, tone, colors and key messages in one place.
When to use another studio:
- Use Product Shot Studio (#/commercial) for a quick single product image or a UGC-style ad video without brand analysis.
- Use Image Studio (#/image) for free-form images from text.
- Use Edit Studio (#/edit) to retouch or change an existing image.
- Use Find My Brand (#/find-my-brand) if you are looking for brand discovery or naming help rather than analysing an existing site.
- Use Website Builder (#/website-builder) to build a site rather than analyse one.
- Use Animate Studio (#/animate) directly when you already have an image to animate.
- Use Video Studio (#/video) or Cinema Studio (#/cinema) for full video production.

chunks.title: Brand Studio — How to use
chunks.text:
Brand Studio (#/brand). How to use.
How to use:
1. Open Brand Studio from the side menu (#/brand). 2. Type your website address into the box (placeholder 'https://your-website.com') and click Analyze. 3. Wait for 'Extracting brand DNA...'; the Brand DNA page opens. 4. Review the fields, fix anything wrong, then click Save. 5. Click Campaigns, pick a Campaign Goal, optionally add a direction, click Generate Concepts, click Select on a concept, choose platform chips and click Generate Assets. 6. Click Asset Editor to write a headline/body/CTA and click Save Asset. 7. Click Photo Studio, upload a product image, pick Resolution, Category and Style, then click Generate Product Photos. 8. Use Download on results or Animate to bring them to life.
Steps:
- Open #/brand and paste your website URL.
- Click Analyze and wait for the Brand DNA page.
- Edit fields and click Save.
- Use Campaigns for concepts and platform assets.
- Use Asset Editor for text-on-image graphics.
- Use Photo Studio for product photos.
- Use Animate for motion.
Getting started:
- Use a public website address that starts with http:// or https://.
- Sign in and connect your API key (a dialog appears otherwise).
- Check the analysed Brand DNA and click Save before moving on.
Tips:
- Analyze your homepage URL.
- Fix the Brand DNA before generating campaigns.

chunks.title: Brand Studio — How to use
chunks.text:
- Start Photo Studio with one category and one style to save time.
- Use 1k while testing, 4k for finals.
Best practices:
- Click Save after editing the Brand DNA.
- Keep Key Messages short and specific.
- Review every generated headline before publishing.

chunks.title: Brand Studio — Features
chunks.text:
Brand Studio (#/brand). Features.
Key features:
- Analyze: paste a website URL, get Brand DNA (name, industry, tagline, value proposition, tone, personality, audience, key messages, colors, fonts, logo, screenshot, imagery and layout style).
- Recent Brands list (up to 6 cards).
- Brand DNA editor with editable fields, chip lists and color pickers, saved locally.
- Campaign Studio: 6 goals, 4 AI concepts, 8 platforms, concurrent asset generation with per-platform status.
- Asset Editor: simple canvas for headline, body, CTA, alignment, colors and a background image.
- Photo Studio: 8 categories x 5 styles, multi-select, 1k/2k/4k, optional Direct MuAPI mode with advanced controls.
- Animate shortcut for branded creative.
- Personalize button on the Brand DNA page (when a screenshot exists) and on photo results.
Feature details:

chunks.title: Brand Studio — Features
chunks.text: - feature: Analyze (website to Brand DNA) | explanation: A URL box (placeholder 'https://your-website.com') and an Analyze button (enabled once you type). While running the button reads 'Extracting...' and a loading overlay says 'Extracting brand DNA...'. On success the Brand DNA is saved and the Brand DNA page opens. The app asks a backend to read the page (title, text, colors, fonts, logo candidates, screenshot), then uses AI to describe the brand from the text and, if a screenshot exists, the visuals. | whyToUse: Starts everything; the other tools use this record. | inputRequired: A website URL starting with http:// or https://. | restrictions: Invalid input shows 'Please enter a valid website URL (e.g. https://example.com)'. An API key/sign-in dialog appears if no key is connected. If the page cannot be read, the AI guesses from the domain name (see limitations).

chunks.title: Brand Studio — Features
chunks.text:
- feature: Brand tools grid | explanation: Five cards under 'Brand tools': Brand DNA ('Review and edit your brand identity'), Campaigns ('Create on-brand campaigns'), Asset Editor ('Edit campaign assets'), Photo Studio ('Create branded photos') and Animate ('Animate branded creative assets'). | whyToUse: Jump into any tool. | inputRequired: None. | restrictions: Brand DNA, Campaigns and Asset Editor open the brand you came from. If none is given they open the brand you used last, then your first saved brand. 'Brand not found' only appears when you have no saved brands or the link points at a brand that no longer exists.
- feature: Recent Brands | explanation: Up to six cards titled 'Recent Brands' showing brand name (or 'Untitled Brand') and industry (or 'No industry'). Clicking one opens its Brand DNA page. | whyToUse: Return to an analysed brand. | inputRequired: At least one analysed brand. | restrictions: Stored in your browser (up to 50 brands).

chunks.title: Brand Studio — Features
chunks.text: - feature: Brand DNA editor | explanation: Shows brand name and industry, website screenshot and logo, then editable fields: Brand Name, Industry, Tagline, Value Proposition, Target Audience, Imagery Style, Layout Style; chip editors for Tone of Voice, Brand Personality and Key Messages (type then Add or press Enter; click x to remove); and Primary and Secondary color pickers. Buttons: Campaigns, Asset Editor, Photo Studio, Animate and Save (shows 'Saved!' for a moment). | whyToUse: Correct anything the AI got wrong before generating assets. | inputRequired: None. | restrictions: Edits are not saved until you click Save. Only the first primary and first secondary color can be changed; fonts, logo and screenshot are shown/kept but not editable. A second 'Photo Studio' button opens the brand-photo-studio route (same page).

chunks.title: Brand Studio — Features
chunks.text: - feature: Campaign Studio | explanation: Pick a Campaign Goal (Product Launch, Lead Generation, Brand Awareness, Engagement, Thought Leadership, Sales), optionally type 'Optional direction or theme...', then click Generate Concepts to get 4 on-brand concepts each with title, key message, CTA and Tone Notes. Click Select on one, choose platform chips (Instagram Feed, Instagram Story, LinkedIn, Facebook Ad, X / Twitter, Web Banner, Email Header, YouTube Thumbnail) and click Generate Assets. Up to three platforms run at once and each row shows running, done or error. Each asset card shows the image, platform, format, headline, body and CTA. | whyToUse: Fast multi-platform campaign creatives with matching copy. | inputRequired: A goal; a selected concept; at least one platform. | restrictions: Copy is trimmed to per-platform word limits (for example Instagram Feed: headline 8, body 30, CTA 3 words). Images are 2k PNG and use your brand logo as a reference when available. 'Back to Brand' returns to the Brand DNA page.

chunks.title: Brand Studio — Features
chunks.text: - feature: Asset Editor | explanation: A left-hand 'Canvas Controls' panel with Headline (default 'Your Headline Here'), Body (default 'Your body copy goes here. Keep it short and impactful.'), CTA (default 'Shop Now'), Alignment (Left, Center, Right), Background Color (default #111111), Text Color, and Upload Background. A 16:9 live preview updates as you type. Save Asset stores it (toast 'Asset saved'); Upload Background shows 'Background image loaded'. | whyToUse: Quick text-on-image graphics without a design tool. | inputRequired: None; all fields have defaults. | restrictions: There is no Download/export button, no font choice and no font-size control in the panel. The background image is shown at reduced opacity.

chunks.title: Brand Studio — Features
chunks.text: - feature: Photo Studio | explanation: Upload a product image (images only), optionally choose a brand from a dropdown (first option: No brand logo), type an optional Direction ('Describe the look, mood, or specific details...'), pick Resolution (1k, 2k default, 4k), then multi-select Category (Studio White, Marble Clean, Urban Street, Golden Hour, Restaurant Plated, Scandi Living, Dark Techy, Nature Organic) and Style (Clean, Dramatic, Flat Lay, Lifestyle, Macro). Generate Product Photos makes one image for every category-and-style pair (2 categories x 3 styles = 6 images), two at a time. Each result shows Download, Personalize and an 'Animate' link. | whyToUse: Many product visuals from one photo. | inputRequired: A product image plus at least one Category and one Style. | restrictions: Output is 1:1 PNG. Toasts: 'Please upload a product image first', 'Please select at least one category and style', 'Generated N photos', 'N photo(s) failed'. The brand dropdown controls which logo is used and which brand the photo is saved under; choosing 'No brand logo' uses no logo. Each result's 'Animate →' button sends that photo to Animate Studio.

chunks.title: Brand Studio — Features
chunks.text:
- feature: Photo Studio: Generation Mode (Brand API / Direct MuAPI) | explanation: A toggle button labelled Brand API (default) or Direct MuAPI. Brand API uses the brand photo recipe with the Nano Banana 2 edit model, your product image and your brand logo. Direct MuAPI shows 'MuAPI Model (I2I)' (a list of image-edit models) and advanced fields: Negative Prompt, Seed, Steps, Guidance Scale, Denoise Strength, CFG Scale, Style, Strength and Prompt Extend. | whyToUse: Power users who want a specific model or tuning. | inputRequired: Choose a model in Direct mode. | restrictions: If Direct MuAPI is on but no model is selected the studio falls back to the Brand API route. In Direct mode the text sent is your Direction only; the Category/Style wording is not added.
Modes:
- Brand API (default, Photo Studio)
- Direct MuAPI (Photo Studio)
- Campaign concepts and assets
- Canvas composition (no AI)
Mode details:
- mode: Brand API | description: Photo Studio uses a preset brand-photo recipe on the Nano Banana 2 edit model with your product and logo. | useCase: Fast on-brand product photos.
- mode: Direct MuAPI | description: You choose an image-edit model and tune its settings. | useCase: Experimentation.
- mode: Campaign generation | description: AI writes 4 concepts, then per-platform copy and an image. | useCase: Social/ad campaigns.
Models:

chunks.title: Brand Studio — Features
chunks.text: Image generation in Photo Studio (Brand API mode) and Campaign Studio uses 'nano-banana-2-edit' (catalog description: 'Nano Banana 2 image editing and guided transformation.'), at 1k/2k/4k in Photo Studio and 2k in Campaigns, PNG output. Brand analysis and campaign/copy writing use the app's text and vision AI calls; the specific language model is not named in the code. Direct MuAPI mode lists any image-edit models in the app's image-to-image and video-to-video catalogs that accept multiple images and a prompt. No prices, speeds or quality rankings are given in the files read.

chunks.title: Brand Studio — Problems and limits
chunks.text:
Brand Studio (#/brand). Problems and limits.
Troubleshooting:
- Analyze button is greyed out: type a URL first.
- 'Please enter a valid website URL (e.g. https://example.com)': include http:// or https://.
- A sign-in/key dialog appears on Analyze: connect your API key and click Analyze again.
- Error text in red under the form after Analyze: the site could not be analysed; try the home page URL or retry.
- 'Brand not found - The brand you are looking for does not exist.' on Brand DNA, Campaign or Asset Editor: this only happens when you have no saved brand (the page has nothing to open) or the link is for a brand that was deleted. Click 'Back to Brand Studio', then run Analyze to create a brand, or pick one under Recent Brands.
- Photo Studio toast 'Please upload a product image first': upload an image (video is not accepted).
- Toast 'Please select at least one category and style': choose at least one of each.
- 'N photo(s) failed' or 'N platform(s) failed': retry; failed items show an error card/row.
- Asset Editor background does not stick after Save: the image may be too large for browser storage; use a smaller file.
Troubleshooting steps:
- issue: Analysis returns generic or wrong brand info | steps: Try the exact homepage URL.; Open the Brand DNA page and correct each field.; Click Save.

chunks.title: Brand Studio — Problems and limits
chunks.text:
- issue: Brand not found on sub-tools | steps: Click Back to Brand Studio.; If you have no brands yet, paste your website address and click Analyze to create one.; Otherwise pick the brand under Recent Brands, then open the tool from the Brand DNA page buttons.
- issue: Campaign assets fail for some platforms | steps: Look at the status rows (running/done/error).; Read the red error text.; Run Generate Assets again with only the failed platforms selected.
- issue: Photo Studio makes too many images | steps: Remember each selected Category is combined with each selected Style.; Deselect extras before clicking Generate Product Photos.
Common problems:
- problem: Colors are wrong | whyItHappens: Colors are extracted from the site and screenshot. | howToFix: Change Primary/Secondary pickers on the Brand DNA page and Save.
- problem: Logo missing in results | whyItHappens: No logo was found on the site. | howToFix: Photo Studio and Campaigns use the brand logo only when one was detected.
- problem: Text Color seems unchanged in the Asset Editor | whyItHappens: Headline and body in the preview use fixed light text styling. | howToFix: Choose a darker Background Color or use a darker background image.
Limitations:
- Brand data (brands, assets, photoshoots) lives in your browser's local storage; limits: 50 brands, 200 campaigns, 500 assets, 200 photoshoots, about 4MB total.

chunks.title: Brand Studio — Problems and limits
chunks.text:
- If the website cannot be read, the AI infers the brand from the domain name and may be wrong.
- Asset Editor has no export/download.
- Photo Studio output is square (1:1).
- Campaign assets are generated one set per run; there is no editing of generated copy in place.
- Only Brand Studio is in the side menu; other tools are reached from within it.
Limit details:
- limitation: Browser-only storage | impact: Clearing site data or switching browser/device loses your brands. | workaround: Re-run Analyze on your site; keep a note of edits.
- limitation: Analysis may be a guess when the site cannot be scraped | impact: Colors, logo and text may be generic. | workaround: Edit the Brand DNA fields and Save.
- limitation: Asset Editor cannot export | impact: You cannot download the graphic from this tool. | workaround: Screenshot the preview, or use Campaign Studio's Generate Assets which saves images to history.
FAQs:
- question: Does Brand Studio need my website? | answer: Yes, to create a Brand DNA you paste a website URL. Photo Studio can be used with only a product image.
- question: Where is my brand saved? | answer: In your browser's local storage on this device.
- question: What goals can I choose for campaigns? | answer: Product Launch, Lead Generation, Brand Awareness, Engagement, Thought Leadership, Sales.

chunks.text:
- question: Which platforms are supported? | answer: Instagram Feed, Instagram Story, LinkedIn, Facebook Ad, X / Twitter, Web Banner, Email Header, YouTube Thumbnail.

- question: What is the difference between Photo Studio and brand-photo-studio? | answer: They open the same Photo Studio page.

chunks.title: Brand Studio — Workflows and use cases
chunks.text:
Brand Studio (#/brand). Workflows and use cases.

chunks.title: Character Studio — Overview
chunks.text:
Character Studio (#/character). Overview.
Description:
Character Studio turns one clear reference face photo plus a text description into a new image of the same person in a new outfit, scene or mood. It offers two face-preserving image models and five one-click expression presets.
Summary:
Consistent characters with face ID preservation
About:
Character Studio (#/character, in the Image group of the side menu) is a single-image generator built around a reference face. You upload one clear face photo or short video clip (or pick a stock photo from Pexels), choose either Flux PuLID or Subject Reference as the model, describe the new look in the Character Description box, and click Generate Character. The result appears below the form with Download, Generate Again and Publish to Social buttons. Five Expression Presets (Happy, Sad, Angry, Surprised, Neutral) append expression wording to your description. A Saved Characters list and an Example Gallery sit lower on the page. The studio works on one image at a time and has no training step, no multi-photo reference and no seed lock.
Best for:
Creators, marketers and storytellers who already have a face photo (of themselves with permission, a model, or a generated portrait) and want the same face in new outfits, settings and expressions for thumbnails, social posts, ads and concept art.
When to use it:

chunks.title: Character Studio — Overview
chunks.text:
- You have one clear, front-facing face photo and want new images of that same person in different outfits, scenes or styles.
- You want a quick portrait variation (for example the same face as a cyberpunk hacker or in a 1920s style).
- You want to try an expression (Happy, Sad, Angry, Surprised, Neutral) on an existing face.
- You need a still image reference to feed into a video studio later.
When to use another studio:
- Use Image Studio (#/image) when you have no reference face and want to create an image from text alone.
- Use Edit Studio (#/edit) when you want to edit an existing photo (remove an object, change a background) rather than recreate the person.
- Use AI Influencer (#/influencer) when you want to design a character from visual attributes (gender, eye color, hair, body, rendering style) with a style preset and a history list.
- Use Avatar Studio (#/avatar) or Lip Sync Studio (#/lipsync) when you need the face to talk or move.
- Use Cinema Studio (#/cinema) or Video Studio (#/video) when you need the character in moving video.
- Use Upscale Suite (#/upscale) when the finished portrait needs more resolution.

chunks.title: Character Studio — How to use
chunks.text:
Character Studio (#/character). How to use.
How to use:
1. Open Character Studio from the side menu (Image group) or go to #/character. 2. Under Model, leave Flux PuLID selected or open the dropdown and choose Subject Reference. 3. Under Reference Face, click the upload button and choose a clear, front-facing face photo (or use the Pexels button). 4. In Character Description, describe the outfit, scene and mood, for example 'wearing a leather jacket, standing in a neon-lit alley, cyberpunk style'. 5. Optionally click an Expression Preset (Happy, Sad, Angry, Surprised, Neutral) to add an expression. 6. Optionally open Advanced to change model options. 7. Click Generate Character. The button shows 'Generating...'. 8. When the image appears, click Download to save it, Generate Again for another variation, or Publish to Social.
Steps:
- Open Character Studio (#/character).
- Choose the model: Flux PuLID (default) or Subject Reference.
- Upload a clear face photo or video under Reference Face.
- Write the scene and outfit in Character Description.
- Optionally add an Expression Preset.
- Click Generate Character and wait for the image.
- Download, regenerate or publish the result.
Getting started:
- Have one sharp, well-lit, front-facing face photo ready (JPG/PNG/WebP under 10MB).

chunks.title: Character Studio — How to use
chunks.text:
- Make sure you are signed in with an active plan and your API key is connected, otherwise an upgrade prompt or key dialog appears when you click Generate.
- Start with a short description and Flux PuLID, then change one thing at a time.
Tips:
- Use a sharp, front-facing, evenly lit reference with no sunglasses or heavy filters.
- Describe clothes, place, lighting and mood; leave the face to the reference.
- Change one thing per run so you can see what worked.
- Generate Again is the fastest way to get more variations.
- Use Download straight away; keep originals of your references.
Best practices:
- Keep a folder of approved reference photos.
- Reuse the same reference and a similar description pattern for a consistent series.
- Use only faces you have permission to use.
- Upscale final images in Upscale Suite if you need print or large-screen size.

chunks.title: Character Studio — Features
chunks.text:
Character Studio (#/character). Features.
Key features:
- Two face-preserving models: Flux PuLID (Black Forest Labs) and Subject Reference (MiniMax).
- Reference Face upload for a photo or video, plus a Pexels stock-photo browser button.
- Character Description text box with an example placeholder.
- Five Expression Presets that add wording to your description: Happy, Sad, Angry, Surprised, Neutral.
- Model-specific Advanced controls (shown when the chosen model defines extra options such as aspect ratio).
- Action row with Thumbnail, Advanced and Personalize buttons, plus a three-dot tools menu (GTM Boost, Recipes, Monetize, Prompts).
- Saved Characters list that can reload a stored character's image and description into the form.
- Result card with Download, Generate Again and Publish to Social.
- Every successful image is saved to your generation history under the character studio.
- Example Gallery of sample characters at the bottom of the page.
Feature details:

chunks.title: Character Studio — Features
chunks.text:
- feature: Model selector (Flux PuLID / Subject Reference) | explanation: A button at the top of the form opens a dropdown with the two models. Flux PuLID is described as 'Face ID preservation with text prompt'. Subject Reference is described as 'Maintain subject consistency across images'. | whyToUse: Try Flux PuLID first for keeping a face recognisable. Try Subject Reference if you want a different look or more aspect ratio options. | inputRequired: Pick one model (Flux PuLID is the default). | restrictions: Only these two models are offered in this studio.
- feature: Reference Face | explanation: Upload a face photo or video with the upload button, or click the compass-style Pexels button (tooltip 'Browse stock photos from Pexels') to pick a stock photo. The hint text reads 'Upload a clear face photo or video'. | whyToUse: The model copies the identity from this image, so it is the most important input. | inputRequired: Required. Without it you get the toast 'Upload a reference face first'. | restrictions: Uploads use the shared upload picker: images up to 10MB and videos up to 50MB. Only one reference is used.

chunks.title: Character Studio — Features
chunks.text:
- feature: Character Description | explanation: A text box labelled Character Description. Placeholder: 'e.g. wearing a leather jacket, standing in a neon-lit alley, cyberpunk style'. Describe the scene, clothes and mood, not the face. | whyToUse: This is what changes between images while the face stays the same. | inputRequired: Optional. If left empty the studio sends 'professional portrait photo'. | restrictions: The model definitions list a prompt limit of 1500 characters.
- feature: Expression Presets | explanation: Five buttons under the form: Happy, Sad, Angry, Surprised, Neutral. Clicking one appends wording such as 'smiling, happy expression, cheerful' (or the matching phrase) to the description box, separated by a comma. Clicking several keeps adding phrases. | whyToUse: A fast way to get an expression without writing it yourself. | inputRequired: None. Click before generating. | restrictions: They only edit the text box. They have no intensity slider and clicking again does not remove the phrase; edit the text manually to remove it.

chunks.title: Character Studio — Features
chunks.text:
- feature: Advanced panel | explanation: The Advanced button in the action row reveals extra options defined for the selected model (prompt and image fields are hidden). The options differ per model. | whyToUse: Fine-tune things like aspect ratio when the model offers it. | inputRequired: Optional. | restrictions: If the model defines no extra options, the panel stays empty/hidden.
- feature: Thumbnail | explanation: The Thumbnail button opens a thumbnail panel for this studio (1:1) where you can generate or clear a custom thumbnail. The chosen thumbnail is sent with your next generation. | whyToUse: To give the generation a cover image in your history and gallery. | inputRequired: Optional. | restrictions: Does not change the generated image itself.
- feature: Personalize | explanation: Personalize lets you use contact tokens in the description. When a contact profile is selected, tokens in your text are replaced with that contact's details before generating. | whyToUse: To make personalised batches of images for specific people or leads. | inputRequired: Optional; needs a contact profile. | restrictions: Exact token names are managed by the Personalizer feature and are not listed in this studio's code.

chunks.title: Character Studio — Features
chunks.text:
- feature: Three-dot tools menu | explanation: A small menu with GTM Boost (opens a prompt-builder modal and puts the result in the description), Recipes, Monetize and Prompts (a prompt gallery that inserts a prompt). | whyToUse: Help writing prompts or ideas for selling character content. | inputRequired: None. | restrictions: Prompts inserts into the first text area on the page.
- feature: Saved Characters | explanation: A section listing characters kept in your browser storage (key character_library), showing a count such as '0 saved'. Clicking one loads its image as the reference and its description into the text box and shows the toast 'Loaded character: <name>'. | whyToUse: Quickly reuse a character you saved before. | inputRequired: None. | restrictions: In the current code nothing in the app writes new entries, so the list is normally empty ('No saved characters yet. Generate a character and save it!'). There is no Save button in this studio.
- feature: Result card | explanation: After a successful run the image appears with Download, Generate Again and Publish to Social. | whyToUse: Save the picture, re-run with the same settings for a new variation, or share it. | inputRequired: None. | restrictions: Generate Again re-clicks the main button with whatever is currently in the form.
Modes:
- Single image from reference face + description (image-to-image)
Mode details:

chunks.title: Character Studio — Features
chunks.text:
- mode: Image-to-image with face reference | description: Both models take your reference image plus text and return one new image that keeps the face. | useCase: Putting the same person in new scenes and outfits.
Models:
The studio offers exactly two models. 'Flux PuLID' (id flux-pulid, provider Black Forest Labs): catalog description 'Flux-based identity-preserving image generation from a reference face.' 'Subject Reference' (id minimax-image-01-subject-reference, provider MiniMax): catalog description 'MiniMax Image 01 subject-reference driven editing.' In the studio list they are labelled 'Face ID preservation with text prompt' and 'Maintain subject consistency across images'. The model files list per-model options such as aspect ratio, render speed, style and image count, but this studio does not state prices, speeds or quality rankings for either model, so none are given here. Model comparison data does not include these two ids.

chunks.title: Character Studio — Inputs and outputs
chunks.text:
Character Studio (#/character). Inputs and outputs.
Inputs:
- Model
- Reference Face
- Character Description
- Expression Presets
- Advanced model options
- Thumbnail

Required inputs:
- Reference Face
Optional inputs:

- Expression Presets
- Advanced model options
- Thumbnail

Input details:
- name: Reference Face | description: A photo or video of the face to keep. Upload from your device, a URL via the picker, or pick a Pexels stock photo. | required: true | whenToUse: Always. | restrictions: One reference only. Shared limits: images 10MB, videos 50MB. A clear front-facing face works best.
- name: Character Description | description: Text describing the new look, scene, clothing and style. | required: false | whenToUse: Almost always; otherwise you only get a plain portrait. | restrictions: Prompt limit of 1500 characters per the model definitions. Default if empty: 'professional portrait photo'.
- name: Model | description: Flux PuLID or Subject Reference. | required: false | whenToUse: Switch if the face does not look right with the first model. | restrictions: Only two choices.

chunks.text:

- name: Advanced options | description: Per-model extras such as aspect ratio. | required: false | whenToUse: When you need a specific shape of image. | restrictions: Depends on the model. Flux PuLID lists aspect ratios 16:9, 9:16, 1:1, 4:3, 3:4 in its definition; Subject Reference lists 16:9, 9:16, 1:1, 4:3, 3:4, 3:2, 2:3, 21:9.
Outputs:

chunks.title: Character Studio — Problems and limits
chunks.text:
Character Studio (#/character). Problems and limits.
Troubleshooting:
- Toast 'Upload a reference face first': click the upload button (or the Pexels button) and add a photo before generating.
- An upgrade prompt appears when you click Generate Character: your account does not have full access; follow the prompt to upgrade or sign in.
- A key/sign-in dialog appears: connect your API key, then click Generate Character again.
- Toast 'Error: ...' after generating: read the message; common causes are an unsupported or oversized file or a service hiccup. Try again, or switch model.
- The face does not look like the reference: use a sharper, front-facing, well-lit photo; switch between Flux PuLID and Subject Reference; keep the description about scene and clothes, not the face.
- Result looks plain: your description was empty, so 'professional portrait photo' was used. Add an outfit, place and mood.
- Expression text is contradictory: you clicked several Expression Presets; delete the extra phrases from the description box.
- Saved Characters says '0 saved': nothing has been stored in your browser's character library; this is expected.
- Upload rejected for size: images must be 10MB or smaller and videos 50MB or smaller; compress or resize the file.
Troubleshooting steps:

chunks.title: Character Studio — Problems and limits
chunks.text:
- issue: Nothing happens or I get an upgrade prompt when I click Generate Character | steps: Check you are signed in.; Complete the upgrade prompt if shown.; If a key dialog appears, connect your key, then click Generate Character again.
- issue: The generated face is not the same person | steps: Replace the reference with a close-up, front-facing, evenly lit photo.; Remove face details (hair colour, eye colour) from the description unless you want them changed.; Open the Model dropdown and try the other model.; Click Generate Again for a new variation.
- issue: I want a different image shape | steps: Click Advanced.; Look for an aspect ratio option for the selected model.; If none appears, switch to Subject Reference, which lists more ratios, or crop later in Edit Studio.
- issue: The reference upload fails | steps: Check the file is an image (or video) and within 10MB (image) or 50MB (video).; Try the Pexels button to pick a stock photo instead.; Retry the upload.
Common problems:
- problem: Face drifts between generations | whyItHappens: Only one reference is used and there is no seed lock. | howToFix: Use the same strong reference every time and keep descriptions short and consistent.
- problem: Description ignored | whyItHappens: Very long or conflicting prompts, or stacked Expression Presets. | howToFix: Shorten to one scene, one outfit, one mood.

chunks.title: Character Studio — Problems and limits
chunks.text:
- problem: Generate button stays disabled | whyItHappens: A generation is still running ('Generating...'). | howToFix: Wait for it to finish; the button returns to 'Generate Character'.
Limitations:
- One reference image or video only; no multi-angle references.
- No training step, no seed lock and no saved-character 'anchor' in this studio.
- Expression Presets have no intensity slider and only edit text.
- No pose, age, gender or outfit-reference controls beyond the text description.
- Saved Characters list is read-only in practice; there is no Save button.
- Requires sign-in/plan access and a connected API key to generate.
- Results depend on reference photo quality; side-on, blurry or hidden faces give weaker likeness.
Limit details:
- limitation: Only one reference face | impact: Likeness can drift for unusual angles or expressions. | workaround: Pick the clearest front-facing photo; try the other model.
- limitation: No built-in way to save a character | impact: You must re-upload the reference each session unless a character was added to the library elsewhere. | workaround: Keep your reference photo and favourite description in your own files; reuse them.
- limitation: Expression Presets cannot be toggled off | impact: Clicking several adds conflicting phrases (for example happy and angry). | workaround: Edit the description text box manually to remove a phrase.

chunks.title: Character Studio — Problems and limits
chunks.text:
- limitation: Output is a still image | impact: No motion or voice. | workaround: Send the result to Animate, Video, Avatar or Lip Sync studios.
FAQs:
- question: How many photos do I need? | answer: One. The studio accepts a single Reference Face photo or video. The in-app help text elsewhere mentions several photos and a training step, but the Character Studio form itself has only one upload and no training step.
- question: Which model should I pick? | answer: Start with Flux PuLID (the default, 'Face ID preservation with text prompt'). If the likeness is weak, try Subject Reference ('Maintain subject consistency across images').
- question: What happens if I leave the description empty? | answer: The studio sends 'professional portrait photo'.
- question: Do Expression Presets change the face? | answer: They only add words to the description (for example 'smiling, happy expression, cheerful'). The model decides how strongly to apply them.
- question: Can I save my character? | answer: There is a Saved Characters list read from your browser storage, but this studio has no Save button, so it is normally empty.
- question: Where are my images stored? | answer: Each successful image is added to your generation history, and you can download it from the result card.

chunks.title: Character Studio — Problems and limits
chunks.text:
- question: Can I use any face photo? | answer: Only use faces you have the right to use. The studio does not check permissions for you.
- question: Can I make the character talk or move? | answer: Not here. Download the image and use Avatar, Lip Sync, Animate or Video studios.

chunks.title: Cinema Templates — Overview
chunks.text:
Cinema Templates (#/cinema-template). Overview.
Description:
Cinema Templates is a library of 46 ready-made cinematic templates (short films, trailers, brand films, ad films, genre scenes, a movie poster and more). You pick one, fill in a few simple fields, optionally add a start image, and the studio builds a full cinematic prompt and generates the video or image.
Summary:
Ready-made cinematic templates: pick one, add your media and generate.
About:

chunks.title: Cinema Templates — Overview
chunks.text:
Cinema Templates (page title 'CINEMATIC TEMPLATES', banner 'Cinema Template Studio') opens on a grid of template cards with filters for Favorites, Recent and My Templates. Opening a card shows a create screen with a Quick Mode and an Advanced mode, a Video Intent panel, the template's own fields, a model picker, Media Sources for a start image or source video, an AI Enhancer switch, a Generate button and an Output panel with editable tabs (Enhanced Prompt, Scene Beats, Voiceover, Negative Prompt). Video templates also show a Scene Timeline that is auto-built from the template, and some have a Scene Builder where you can add scenes or open the Storyboard. The studio assembles and enriches the prompt for you, then routes the run by the media you attached: text only goes to text-to-video, an image goes to image-to-video, a video goes to video-to-video. Results open in a preview with Open in new tab, Download, Publish to Social, a scrubber, Regenerate / Extend and a history strip.
Best for:
Beginners and small-business owners who want a polished cinematic result (brand film, ad, trailer, restaurant promo, real estate tour, and so on) without writing a technical prompt.
When to use it:
- You know the kind of video you want (trailer, brand film, ad film, testimonial, founder story, documentary-style, genre scene) and want a template to structure it.

chunks.title: Cinema Templates — Overview
chunks.text:
- You want the studio to expand a few answers into a full cinematic prompt, scene beats, voiceover and negative prompt.
- You want industry-flavoured templates such as Restaurant/Cafe Cinematic Film, Real Estate Cinematic Property, Automotive Cinematic Promo, Fitness Transformation Video, Fashion & Lifestyle Film, Event Recap Film or Local Business Cinematic Promo.
- You want a movie poster image from a title, genre and tagline.
- You already planned frames in Storyboard Studio and want to continue with them ('Send to video studio').
When to use another studio:
- Use Cinema Studio (#/cinema) when you want to choose camera body, lens, focal length, aperture, movement and film look yourself.
- Use Video Studio (#/video) when you just want a prompt bar with a model picker and workflows like Edit video, Extend uploaded video or Motion transfer.
- Use Storyboard Studio (#/storyboard) when you want to plan frames first.
- Use Templates (#/templates) for the broader template library (image and non-cinematic video templates).

chunks.title: Cinema Templates — How to use
chunks.text:
Cinema Templates (#/cinema-template). How to use.
How to use:
1. Open Cinema Templates (#/cinema-template). 2. Browse the grid (or use Favorites, Recent, My Templates) and click a template card. 3. Choose 'Quick Mode' for the essentials or 'Advanced' for more fields. 4. Optionally set the Video Intent panel (Video Type, Aspect Ratio, Tone, Style Preset, Lighting Preset, Color Grade, Target Audience, CTA, Subject, Premise). 5. Fill the template fields under 'Basic Information' (and 'Brand Context' if shown). 6. Under 'Media Sources' add a start image (needed for most cinematic templates) or a source video. 7. Check the model (model picker) and leave AI Enhancer on. 8. Optionally edit the Enhanced Prompt, Scene Beats, Voiceover or Negative Prompt tabs in the Output panel and adjust the Scene Timeline. 9. Click Generate. 10. On the preview screen use Download, Open in new tab, Publish to Social, Regenerate or Extend. Use the Save button to keep the project.
Steps:
- Open Cinema Templates and pick a template card.
- Choose Quick Mode or Advanced.
- Fill in the required fields.
- Add a start image under Media Sources if the template needs one.
- Review the Enhanced Prompt in the Output panel.
- Click Generate and wait.
- Download, share, regenerate or extend the result.
Getting started:
- Start with Brand Film, Ad Film or Social Cinematic Reel in Quick Mode.

chunks.title: Cinema Templates — How to use
chunks.text:
- Have one clear image ready (a product, a place or a person) to use as the start frame.
- Leave the AI Enhancer on for your first try.
- You need to be signed in with a working API key; the header shows 'No API key' until one is detected, and Generate opens a sign-in box if there is none.
Tips:
- Use Favorites (the heart on a card) for your go-to templates.
- Write a clear one-paragraph story or brand story; the enhancer builds on it.
- Check the Enhanced Prompt tab before generating to avoid wasted runs.
- Pick Tone and Lighting Preset in Video Intent for a quick look change.
- Use a high-quality, well-lit start image.
Best practices:
- Start in Quick Mode, then move to Advanced.
- Keep the prompt below the model's limit; watch the length counter warning.
- Generate scenes individually for longer stories.

Templates are grouped by category such as Cinematic Films, Business & Brand, Commercial & Ads, Social Media, Documentary, Personal Story, Industry Specific, Narrative & Story, Film Genres, Scene Construction and Movie Poster & Promo. Advanced adds extra fields (for example a Cinematic Short Film adds Main Character, Setting/Location, Central Conflict, Visual Style). Switching mode resets the form to that mode's defaults. | whyToUse: Start simple; go Advanced when you want more control. | inputRequired: Required fields are marked by the template. | restrictions: If a required field is empty Generate shows 'Please fill in required fields: ...' with the field names.

chunks.title: Cinema Templates — Features
chunks.text: - feature: Video Intent panel | explanation: A shared set of creative choices: Video Type (commercial, brand film, trailer, social reel, testimonial, documentary, short film, explainer), Aspect Ratio (16:9, 9:16, 1:1, 4:5), Tone (dramatic, cinematic, upbeat, luxury, gritty, minimal, emotional, humorous), Style Preset (None, Photorealistic, Cinematic, Noir, Anime, Watercolor, Oil Painting, Cyberpunk, Fantasy, Documentary), Lighting Preset (None, Golden Hour, Neon, Studio, Dramatic, Soft, Volumetric, High Key, Low Key), Color Grade (None, Warm, Cool, Desaturated, Vibrant, Monochrome, Sepia, Teal & Orange), plus Target Audience, CTA, Subject and Premise. The note 'Video intent is saved automatically' appears. The same intent is shared with Storyboard Studio. Reset clears it ('Video intent reset'). | whyToUse: Set the creative direction once and reuse it. | inputRequired: Optional. | restrictions: Fields you typed yourself are not overwritten by the panel.

- feature: AI Enhancer | explanation: A switch (default on) that keeps the simple template flow but auto-detects the niche, expands the prompt cinematically, applies scene logic and cleans up in the background. If enhancement fails you see 'AI enhancement failed, using raw prompt' and generation continues with the plain prompt. | whyToUse: Better prompts with no extra effort. | inputRequired: None. | restrictions: Very long prompts trigger a warning: 'Prompt is N characters - this may exceed model limits. Consider shortening.'
- feature: Editable Output tabs | explanation: Under Output you can read and edit the generated Enhanced Prompt, Scene Beats, Voiceover and Negative Prompt. Edits to the Enhanced Prompt are used when you generate; a reset button restores the built prompt. | whyToUse: Fine-tune wording before spending credits. | inputRequired: None. | restrictions: If the prompt box is empty you get 'Please enter a prompt or description before generating.'

chunks.title: Cinema Templates — Features
chunks.text: - feature: Media Sources and routing | explanation: For video templates a start/reference image field and a source video field are shown. A badge shows which path Generate will take. Image attached means image-to-video (or image-to-image for the poster), a video attached means video-to-video, nothing attached means text-to-video. Most cinematic templates are image-to-video templates and treat the start image as required. | whyToUse: Use your own picture or footage as the base. | inputRequired: An image when the route is image-driven ('Please upload an image before generating.'); a video when you chose video-to-video ('Please upload a video before generating.'). | restrictions: If you add an end frame but the chosen model has no end-frame input, a warning says the end frame is not used and suggests a model with start and end frames such as Seedance 2.5.

chunks.title: Cinema Templates — Features

- feature: Scene Timeline and Scene Builder | explanation: Video templates auto-pick scenes and list them in a Scene Timeline; 'Refresh' re-picks them ('Scene timeline refreshed'). Templates with a scene builder show '+ Add Scene' and a 'Storyboard' button that opens Storyboard Studio inside this screen. You can edit scene number, beat/description and shots, and move or remove scenes. | whyToUse: Shape the story structure. | inputRequired: None. | restrictions: Errors show as 'Failed to add scene', 'Failed to remove scene' or 'Failed to move scene'.

chunks.title: Cinema Templates — Problems and limits
chunks.text:
Cinema Templates (#/cinema-template). Problems and limits.
Troubleshooting:
- 'Please fill in required fields: ...': fill in each field listed before pressing Generate.
- 'Please upload an image before generating.': attach a start image under Media Sources.
- 'Please upload a video before generating.': you are on a video-to-video route; attach a source video or remove the video/model choice.
- 'Please enter a prompt or description before generating.': the Enhanced Prompt is empty; fill the template fields or type in the Enhanced Prompt tab.
- 'AI enhancement failed, using raw prompt': the enhancer could not run; generation continues with the basic prompt, which you can edit.
- 'Prompt is N characters - this may exceed model limits. Consider shortening.': trim the prompt in the Output panel.
- A red error box appears under Generate with a Retry link: click Retry (up to 2 retries) or change the model; the box disappears after about 5 seconds.
- 'Generation cancelled.': you or the app cancelled the run; click Generate again.
- Warning about the end frame not used: choose a model that has start and end frames, for example Seedance 2.5.
- 'Only Seedance 2.0 videos can be extended.': use a Seedance 2.0 model, or use Video Studio's 'Extend uploaded video'.
- Header shows 'No API key': sign in and add credits; Generate also opens a sign-in box.
Troubleshooting steps:

chunks.title: Cinema Templates — Problems and limits
chunks.text:
- issue: Generate shows a toast and nothing happens | steps: Read the toast text.; Fill missing fields or add the image/video it asks for.; Click Generate again.
- issue: Result failed | steps: Click Retry in the red box (up to 2 times).; If it still fails choose a different model in the picker.; Shorten the prompt in the Enhanced Prompt tab.
- issue: I cannot find my earlier work | steps: Open the browse grid and click 'Recent' or 'My Templates'.; Use the history strip below the Output panel.; Use Save to keep a project explicitly.
- issue: Storyboard not applied | steps: In Storyboard Studio click 'Send to video studio'.; Look for the 'Storyboard Loaded' banner; if missing, send it again.
Common problems:
- problem: My model choice changed | whyItHappens: Attaching media changes the route (text, image or video) and the picker switches to a model that fits that route unless you picked one yourself. | howToFix: Pick the model after attaching media.
- problem: My typed prompt edits disappeared | whyItHappens: Changing fields or switching mode rebuilds the prompt (mode switch resets inputs). | howToFix: Edit the Enhanced Prompt last, just before Generate.
- problem: Aspect ratio different from the template | whyItHappens: Your explicit choice wins, and it is then snapped to a ratio the model supports. | howToFix: Pick a model that supports your ratio.
Limitations:

chunks.title: Cinema Templates — Problems and limits
chunks.text:
- Most cinematic video templates need a start image.
- Extend only works for Seedance 2.0 results.
- Template duration ranges (for example 60-180s, default 90 for Cinematic Short Film) describe the intended story length; the actual clip length depends on the model.
- Very long prompts may exceed model limits (a warning is shown).
- Retry after a failed generation is offered up to 2 times.
- You need an API key and credits.
Limit details:
- limitation: Start image requirement | impact: Generate says 'Please upload an image before generating.' if no image is attached. | workaround: Upload a picture or pick a text-to-video-capable route/model.
- limitation: Clip length versus template duration | impact: A 90-second template does not guarantee a 90-second clip. | workaround: Generate scenes separately and assemble in Render or Timeline.
- limitation: End frame support | impact: The end frame is ignored on models without an end-frame input. | workaround: Choose a model with start and end frames such as Seedance 2.5.
FAQs:
- question: How many templates are there? | answer: 46 cinematic templates: 45 video templates and 1 image template (Movie Poster). The browse header shows the live count.
- question: Do I need a picture? | answer: Most cinematic video templates are image-to-video, so yes, add a start image under Media Sources. The route badge shows what Generate will do.

chunks.title: Cinema Templates — Problems and limits
chunks.text:
- question: What is the difference between Quick Mode and Advanced? | answer: Quick Mode asks only the essentials. Advanced shows extra fields for more control.
- question: What does the AI Enhancer do? | answer: It detects the niche, expands the prompt cinematically, applies scene logic and cleans up the text. It is on by default and you can switch it off.
- question: Can I edit the prompt before generating? | answer: Yes. Use the Output tabs (Enhanced Prompt, Scene Beats, Voiceover, Negative Prompt).
- question: Where are my saved projects? | answer: Click Save to store a project ('Project saved!'). Templates you used appear under Recent, and hearted templates under Favorites.
- question: Can I extend a result? | answer: Only Seedance 2.0 videos can be extended from the preview.
- question: How is this different from Cinema Studio? | answer: Cinema Templates gives guided formats with forms and auto-built prompts. Cinema Studio gives manual camera, lens and film-look controls.
- question: Can I turn a storyboard into a template video? | answer: Yes. In Storyboard Studio click 'Send to video studio'; this studio opens with a 'Storyboard Loaded' banner.

chunks.title: Cinema Studio — Overview
chunks.text:
Cinema Studio (#/cinema). Overview.
Description:
Cinema Studio makes cinematic video shots (or still images) by combining your scene description with real camera, lens, focal length, aperture, camera movement and film look settings.
Summary:
Cinematic shots with real camera, lens and movement controls.
About:
Cinema Studio is a prompt bar plus a set of cinematography controls. You describe your scene, choose a camera body, lens, focal length and aperture (from the summary card or the camera overlay), then choose a camera movement and film look (in the Quick camera builder). When you press the generate button the studio writes all of those choices into one long cinematic prompt and sends it to the video model you picked. You can start from text only (text-to-video), from a start-frame image (image-to-video), or from a start and end frame (first/last-frame video). A Video / Image switch lets you render a cinematic still instead of a video. Results appear on a result screen with Regenerate, Download, Copy Prompt, Copy Link/Image, + New Shot and Publish to Social, plus a History rail.
Best for:
Creators who want film-style shots with a specific camera and lens look, and who prefer picking cinematography options from lists rather than writing technical prompt wording by hand.
When to use it:

chunks.title: Cinema Studio — Overview
chunks.text:
- You want a single cinematic shot with a chosen camera body and lens look (for example Grand Format 70mm Film with Classic Anamorphic).
- You want to control focal length (8, 14, 24, 35, 50, 85 mm) and aperture (f/1.4, f/4, f/11) through simple choices.
- You want a camera movement such as Dolly In, Crane Up, Orbit, FPV Drone or Handheld, and a film look such as Anamorphic, Teal & Orange or Moody Noir.
- You have a still image (a scene, a location, a character) that should become the first frame of a cinematic shot, optionally with an end frame.
- You want a cinematic still image rather than a video (switch to Image).
When to use another studio:
- Use Video Studio (#/video) when you want the full set of video workflows (Edit video, Extend uploaded video, Motion transfer, watermark removal) or the Extend / Upscale to 4K buttons.
- Use Cinema Templates (#/cinema-template) when you want a ready-made format such as a trailer, brand film or ad film that asks you a few questions and builds the prompt.
- Use Storyboard Studio (#/storyboard) when you want to plan several shots as frames before generating.
- Use Image Studio (#/image) when you only want pictures and need more image-specific controls.

chunks.title: Cinema Studio — How to use
chunks.text:
Cinema Studio (#/cinema). How to use.
How to use:
1. Open Cinema Studio from the side menu (#/cinema). 2. Decide Video or Image with the switch at the left of the toolbar. 3. Type your scene in the prompt box ('Describe your scene - use @ to add characters & props'). 4. Optional: attach a Start frame (and End frame) to start from pictures. 5. Click the summary card (tooltip 'Open camera settings') and choose Camera, Lens, Focal Length and Aperture. 6. Click the camera builder button (tooltip 'Quick camera builder'), choose Movement and Film Look, then press 'Use This Setup'. 7. Choose the model button, aspect ratio and resolution. 8. Optional: Advanced, Character Lock, Personalize, Thumbnail. 9. Click the generate button (tooltip 'Generate cinema shot'; the button reads 'SHOOTING...' while it works). 10. On the result screen use Regenerate, Download, Copy Prompt, Copy Link / Copy Image, + New Shot or Publish to Social.
Steps:
- Open Cinema Studio (#/cinema).
- Write the scene in the prompt box.
- Open camera settings and choose camera, lens, focal length and aperture.
- Open the Quick camera builder, choose Movement and Film Look, press 'Use This Setup'.
- Pick a model, aspect ratio and resolution.
- Press the generate button and wait for 'SHOOTING...' to finish.
- Download, copy, regenerate or publish the result.
Getting started:

chunks.title: Cinema Studio — How to use
chunks.text:
- Type a short scene such as 'A lone rider crossing a salt flat at dusk' and press generate with all defaults.
- Then open camera settings and change only the lens, so you can see the difference.
- Try the Image switch first to preview the look as a still.
Tips:
- Change one cinematography setting at a time so you can see what it does.
- Pair a wide focal length (14-24mm) with FPV Drone or Dolly In for immersive shots; use 85mm with f/1.4 for portraits.
- Anamorphic lenses and the Anamorphic film look give the classic widescreen movie feel (built-in help tip).
- Use the Image switch to test a look cheaply before making a video.
- Use @ in the prompt box to refer to characters and props where supported.
Best practices:
- Describe the subject, action and place first; let the controls handle camera language.
- Use 21:9 or 16:9 for a cinematic frame and 9:16 for social.
- Keep the prompt focused on one shot.

chunks.title: Cinema Studio — Features
chunks.text:
Cinema Studio (#/cinema). Features.
Key features:
- Cinema Prompt Builder: a collapsible card with a 'Base scene description...' box, Camera and Lens lists and a live prompt preview; the 'Use in Prompt' button copies the built prompt into the main prompt box.
- Camera settings overlay opened from the summary card (tooltip 'Open camera settings') with four columns: Camera, Lens, Focal Length, Aperture.
- Quick camera builder (tooltip 'Quick camera builder'): Camera, Lens, Focal, Aperture, Movement and Film Look lists with a Preview and a 'Use This Setup' button.
- Video / Image output switch (your choice is remembered in the browser).
- Model button with a split-pane catalog picker for 'Text to Video' and 'Image to Video' models and a search box ('Search models...').
- Aspect ratio choices 16:9, 21:9, 9:16, 1:1, 4:5 and resolution choices 1K, 2K, 4K.
- Attachment toolbar for Start frame, End frame, Image, Video and Audio references; a stock-photo button ('Select Reference Scene') for a reference scene.
- Character Lock toggle, GTM Boost in the three-dot menu, Personalize and Thumbnail buttons, and an Advanced panel.
- Result actions: ↻ Regenerate, ↓ Download, ⧉ Copy Prompt, ⧉ Copy Link / Copy Image, + New Shot, Add AI Captions, Publish to Social, and a History rail.

chunks.title: Cinema Studio — Features
chunks.text:
- Reload recovery: a generation that finished while you were away is restored with the toast 'Recovered a generation that finished while you were away'.
Feature details:
- feature: Camera and lens controls | explanation: Click the summary card to open the camera overlay. Choose a Camera (Modular 8K Digital, Full-Frame Cine Digital, Grand Format 70mm Film, Studio Digital S35, Classic 16mm Film, Premium Large Format Digital), a Lens (Creative Tilt Lens, Compact Anamorphic, Extreme Macro, 70s Cinema Prime, Classic Anamorphic, Premium Modern Prime, Warm Cinema Prime, Swirl Bokeh Portrait, Vintage Prime, Halation Diffusion, Clinical Sharp Prime), a Focal Length (8, 14, 24, 35, 50, 85) and an Aperture (f/1.4, f/4, f/11). Defaults are the first camera, the first lens, 35mm and f/1.4. | whyToUse: Each choice is turned into plain-English camera wording in the prompt (for example 'shot on a grand format 70mm film camera', 'using a classic anamorphic lens at 35mm (natural cinematic perspective)', 'aperture f/1.4, shallow depth of field, creamy bokeh'). | inputRequired: None. Defaults are filled in. | restrictions: These work by adding words to the prompt; they do not change the model's real optics, and results vary by model.

chunks.title: Cinema Studio — Features
chunks.text:
- feature: Camera movement | explanation: Set in the Quick camera builder under 'Movement'. Options as shown on screen: Static, Dolly In, Dolly Out, Crane Up, Orbit, FPV Drone, Handheld, Pan, Tilt, Dolly Zoom. Dolly Zoom adds the wording 'Hitchcock dolly zoom (vertigo effect)'. Default is Static. | whyToUse: Adds a movement phrase such as 'slow dolly in toward the subject' or 'smooth 360 orbit around the subject' to the prompt. | inputRequired: Open the Quick camera builder and press 'Use This Setup'. | restrictions: Movement is only a prompt hint; the video model may follow it loosely.
- feature: Film look | explanation: Set in the Quick camera builder under 'Film Look'. Options: Natural, Anamorphic, Teal & Orange, Moody Noir, Vintage, Neon Nights, Documentary, Golden Hour. Default is Natural. | whyToUse: One choice sets the colour and mood wording, for example 'teal and orange blockbuster grade' or 'warm golden-hour glow'. | inputRequired: Open the Quick camera builder and press 'Use This Setup'. | restrictions: Prompt wording only.

chunks.title: Cinema Studio — Features
chunks.text:
- feature: Cinema Prompt Builder | explanation: A collapsed card titled 'Cinema Prompt Builder' ('Build cinematic prompts with camera & lens metadata'). Type a base scene, choose a Camera and Lens and read the compiled prompt, then press 'Use in Prompt' to place it into the main prompt box. | whyToUse: Lets you see and edit the full cinematic wording before generating. | inputRequired: A base scene description. Until you type one it shows 'Cinematic prompt will appear here...'. | restrictions: This builder uses a fixed 35mm and f/1.4 and does not include Movement or Film Look; those are added on generate from your saved settings.
- feature: Video / Image switch | explanation: A two-button switch at the start of the toolbar. 'Video' renders a clip with the model you picked. 'Image' renders a cinematic still using the nano-banana-pro model (or nano-banana-pro-edit when you attached a start frame), at 1K, 2K or 4K. | whyToUse: Test a look cheaply as a still before spending on video. | inputRequired: Optional start frame. | restrictions: In Image mode your selected video model is not used.

chunks.title: Cinema Studio — Features
chunks.text:
- feature: Start frame and End frame | explanation: Attach a Start frame to make the studio switch to an image-to-video model. Attach both Start frame and End frame and the studio uses the 'seedance-2.5-first-last-frame' model to pin both ends of the clip. | whyToUse: Control exactly how the shot begins and ends. | inputRequired: One or two images. | restrictions: If you drop a non-image file on the start-frame area you see 'Drop an image to use as the start frame.'
- feature: Reference attachments (Image, Video, Audio) | explanation: The attachment toolbar also lets you add extra reference images, videos and audio, which are sent to the model when the model accepts them. | whyToUse: Guide the look, motion or sound. | inputRequired: Files. | restrictions: Whether a given model uses references is model dependent. Upload errors appear as a toast with the reason.
- feature: Character Lock | explanation: A toggle labelled 'Character Lock'. When on, the studio reuses a stored character reference and after a successful result saves the new result as the stored reference. | whyToUse: Keep the same character across shots. | inputRequired: A first successful generation to store the reference. | restrictions: Effect depends on the model.

chunks.title: Cinema Studio — Features
chunks.text:
- feature: Result screen | explanation: ↻ Regenerate runs again, ↓ Download saves the file, ⧉ Copy Prompt copies your prompt text, ⧉ Copy Link (videos) or ⧉ Copy Image (stills) copies the media link or image, + New Shot returns to the prompt bar, Add AI Captions captions a video, Publish to Social opens publishing. | whyToUse: Finish and share your shot. | inputRequired: A finished result. | restrictions: Copy buttons can fail with 'Could not copy the prompt' or 'Could not copy' if the browser blocks the clipboard.
Modes:
- Text-to-video
- Image-to-video (start frame)
- First/last-frame video (start + end frame)
- Image (still) mode
Mode details:
- mode: Text-to-video | description: No images attached, Video selected. Uses the text-to-video model you picked (default is the first in the list, Seedance Lite). | useCase: Create a shot from words.
- mode: Image-to-video | description: A start frame is attached. Uses the image-to-video model you picked (or the first one). | useCase: Turn a scene or location picture into a moving shot.
- mode: First/last-frame video | description: Both frames attached. Uses seedance-2.5-first-last-frame. | useCase: Controlled start and end.
- mode: Image mode | description: Still render with nano-banana-pro or nano-banana-pro-edit (when a start frame is attached). | useCase: Preview a look or make a cinematic still.
Models:

chunks.title: Cinema Studio — Features
chunks.text: Cinema Studio uses the same catalog as Video Studio. The model picker has two tabs, 'Text to Video' (115 catalog entries) and 'Image to Video' (188 entries), covering families such as Seedance (Lite, Pro, v1.5, v2.0, 2.5), Kling (v2.1 to v3.0 and O1), Google Veo (3, 3.1, 4), OpenAI Sora 2, Wan, Hunyuan, Runway, Pixverse, MiniMax Hailuo, Vidu, LTX, OVI, Grok Imagine and Flux 3 video. App descriptions are one-liners (for example Kling V3.0 Pro 'cinematic text-to-video', Seedance 2.0 'latest', Wan 2.2 Fast 'fast'). The comparison table gives only relative scores (price, speed, quality) not real prices. Special models used by the code: seedance-2.5-first-last-frame (start + end frame), nano-banana-pro and nano-banana-pro-edit (Image mode). If the chosen id is missing from the catalog the code falls back to kling-v2.6-pro-t2v or kling-v2.6-pro-i2v.

chunks.title: Cinema Studio — Problems and limits
chunks.text:
Cinema Studio (#/cinema). Problems and limits.
Troubleshooting:
- Nothing happens when I press generate: the prompt box is empty. Type a scene description.
- A sign-in window appears: you are not signed in or have no API key. Sign in and add credits, then press generate again.
- Toast 'Generation Failed: ...': the text after the colon is the reason from the service (for example 'No Data' when no video came back). Try again or pick another model.
- Toast 'Upload failed: ...': the start frame did not upload; check file type and size and try again.
- 'Drop an image to use as the start frame.': you dropped something that is not an image.
- The camera or movement did not change the shot: movement and look are only prompt words; also make sure you pressed 'Use This Setup' in the Quick camera builder.
- 'Could not copy the prompt' or 'Could not copy': your browser blocked clipboard access; allow clipboard permission or copy by hand.
- I only got an image: the Image switch is selected (it is remembered). Switch back to Video.
- Movement list shows 'Dolly Zoom': that is the dolly zoom (vertigo effect) option. Older saved projects that stored it under its previous spelling still load with the same camera move.
Troubleshooting steps:

chunks.title: Cinema Studio — Problems and limits
chunks.text:
- issue: Generation fails with a toast | steps: Read the text after 'Generation Failed:'.; Click generate again.; If it repeats, choose a different model in the model picker.; Try a smaller or simpler prompt.
- issue: My start frame is ignored | steps: Check the camera builder shows 'Reference Scene - Loaded'.; Make sure Video mode is selected.; If you also attached an end frame, the studio uses the first/last-frame model.
- issue: Wrong output type (image instead of video) | steps: Look at the Video / Image switch at the left of the toolbar.; Select Video.; Generate again.
- issue: Interrupted by page reload | steps: Return to Cinema Studio.; A finished job is recovered automatically with a toast.; Check the History rail.
Common problems:
- problem: Result does not look like the chosen lens | whyItHappens: The lens is a text hint only. | howToFix: Repeat the look in your scene description and try another model.
- problem: Model switched after attaching a frame | whyItHappens: Attaching a start frame switches to the first image-to-video model. | howToFix: Re-pick the model afterwards.
- problem: Resolution changed by itself | whyItHappens: On model change the resolution takes the model's first listed value unless you set it yourself. | howToFix: Pick the resolution after choosing the model.
Limitations:

chunks.title: Cinema Studio — Problems and limits
chunks.text:
- Camera, lens, focal length, aperture, movement and look are added as words to the prompt; they are not physical settings.
- Clip duration is taken from the selected model's first listed duration unless the Advanced options set it; there is no dedicated duration button on the main toolbar.
- Cinema Studio only runs text-to-video, image-to-video, first/last-frame video and stills; it has no extend, edit or motion-transfer tools (use Video Studio).
- Empty prompt: nothing happens and no message is displayed.
- You need an API key and credits.
Limit details:
- limitation: Prompt-based camera controls | impact: Two models can render the same camera wording differently. | workaround: Try another model or add detail to your scene description.
- limitation: Fixed clip length | impact: You cannot pick a duration on the toolbar. | workaround: Open Advanced to see whether the model offers a duration control, or use Video Studio where Duration is a button.
- limitation: No extend or edit tools | impact: You cannot continue or edit a finished clip here. | workaround: Download the clip and use Video Studio.
FAQs:
- question: Does Cinema Studio make video or images? | answer: Both. The Video / Image switch decides. Video uses the model you pick; Image uses nano-banana-pro.

chunks.title: Cinema Studio — Problems and limits
chunks.text:
- question: What is the Dolly Zoom movement? | answer: It is the Hitchcock dolly zoom (vertigo effect) option in the movement list: the camera moves while the framing zoom changes the opposite way, so the background seems to stretch.
- question: Where do I set movement and film look? | answer: In the Quick camera builder (camera icon button). Choose Movement and Film Look, then press 'Use This Setup'. The summary card then shows your movement and look.
- question: Can I set the video length? | answer: There is no duration button on the main toolbar. The studio uses the model's first listed duration; check the Advanced panel for extra controls.
- question: Can I use my own picture? | answer: Yes. Attach a Start frame (and optionally an End frame), or use the stock-photo button for a reference scene.
- question: How do I keep the same character? | answer: Switch on Character Lock. After a successful result the studio stores it as the character reference.
- question: What is the difference from Video Studio? | answer: Cinema Studio adds camera, lens, movement and film-look controls. Video Studio has more video workflows (edit, extend, motion transfer, watermark removal) and a per-model duration button.
- question: Does it remember my work? | answer: A History rail lists results from this session, and a job that finished while you were away is recovered on return.

chunks.title: Cinema Studio — Workflows and use cases
chunks.text:

Example workflows:
- title: Moody noir street shot | steps: Prompt: 'A detective lights a cigarette under a flickering streetlamp in the rain'.; Camera settings: Studio Digital S35, Vintage Prime, 35mm, f/1.4.; Quick camera builder: Movement Dolly In, Film Look Moody Noir, press 'Use This Setup'.; Aspect ratio 21:9, generate.

- title: Controlled start and end | steps: Attach a Start frame and an End frame.; Describe the transition in the prompt.; Generate (uses first/last-frame model).

- title: Product hero shot | description: A product with macro lens and shallow depth of field. | steps: Attach product photo as Start frame.; Lens Extreme Macro, aperture f/1.4, Movement Orbit. | expectedOutput: An orbiting close-up clip.
Related studios:
- studio: video | relationship: Video Studio is the general video generator. | whenToMove: When you need edit, extend, motion transfer or a duration button. | why: It has more workflows.

chunks.title: Cinema Studio — Glossary
chunks.text: Glossary: Focal length: How wide or tight the view is. Small numbers are wide, large numbers are zoomed in. | Aperture: How open the lens is. f/1.4 blurs the background, f/11 keeps everything sharp. | Anamorphic: A widescreen lens style with stretched flares. | Dolly: The camera moves toward or away from the subject on a track. | Crane: The camera rises or lowers. | Orbit: The camera circles the subject. | FPV Drone: A fast, immersive drone-style fly-through. | Dolly zoom: The vertigo effect: the camera moves one way while the zoom goes the other. | Film look: A colour and mood style like Teal & Orange or Moody Noir. | Start / End frame: The first and last picture of a clip.
