chunks.title: Product Shot Studio — Overview
chunks.text:
Product Shot Studio (#/commercial). Overview.
Description:
Product Shot Studio turns one product photo into a studio-quality product image in a scene you choose, and also has an Ad video mode that makes a short UGC-style ad from a product image and a script.
Summary:
Studio-quality product photos from a single image
About:
Product Shot Studio (route #/commercial, Image group of the side menu; the internal studio id is 'commercial') has two modes switched by a toggle at the top of the form: 'Product shot' and 'Ad video'. In Product shot mode you upload a product image or video, pick a Model (Product Shot or Product Photography), choose one of nine Scene Presets and one of four Output Formats, and click Generate Product Shot. In Ad video mode you upload a product image, write an ad script, optionally add an avatar and reference images, pick a video format preset, aspect ratio, resolution and duration, and click Generate Ad Video. Results show Download, Generate Again and Publish to Social. The studio is deliberately focused: it has no template rails or example galleries.
Best for:
Online sellers, small brands, agencies and marketers who have a plain product photo and want catalog, social or ad-ready imagery or a short UGC-style ad video without a photo shoot.
When to use it:

chunks.title: Product Shot Studio — Overview
chunks.text:
- You have a clean photo of a product and want it placed in a studio, marble, outdoor, kitchen, neon, wooden, gradient, beach or office scene.
- You need the same product in different output shapes (banner 16:9, square 1:1, story 9:16, billboard 21:9).
- You want a short UGC, tutorial, unboxing, product review or TV-spot style ad video from a product image and a script.
- You want quick variations for A/B testing.
When to use another studio:
- Use Brand Studio (#/brand) when you want a whole set of branded product photos by category and style (Photo Studio inside Brand Studio) or full campaign creatives with copy.
- Use Image Studio (#/image) when you want to create an image from text without a product photo.
- Use Edit Studio (#/edit) when you need to remove a background, erase an object or retouch an existing photo.
- Use Video Studio (#/video) or Animate Studio (#/animate) when you want to turn a finished product shot into motion with full control.
- Use Upscale Suite (#/upscale) when a finished shot needs more resolution.
- Use Avatar Studio (#/avatar) when you need a talking presenter rather than a product ad.

chunks.title: Product Shot Studio — How to use
chunks.text:
Product Shot Studio (#/commercial). How to use.
How to use:
1. Open Product Shot Studio from the side menu or go to #/commercial. 2. Make sure the toggle at the top says Product shot. 3. Under Model choose Product Shot (default) or Product Photography. 4. Under Product Media upload your product image or video (or use the Pexels button). 5. Under Scene Preset click the backdrop you want, for example 'Luxury marble surface'. 6. Under Output Format click Ad Banner (16:9), Social Post (1:1), Story (9:16) or Billboard (21:9). 7. Click Generate Product Shot. The button shows 'Generating...'. 8. When the image appears use Download, Generate Again or Publish to Social. For an ad video: switch the toggle to Ad video, upload a product image, type your script (use @image1 for the product and @image2 for an avatar), optionally pick an avatar and references, choose format, aspect ratio, resolution and duration, then click Generate Ad Video (button shows 'Making your ad...').
Steps:
- Open #/commercial.
- Choose Product shot or Ad video with the toggle.
- Upload the product image (or video in Product shot mode).
- Pick Model, Scene Preset and Output Format (Product shot mode) or write a script and pick ad settings (Ad video mode).
- Click Generate Product Shot or Generate Ad Video.
- Download, regenerate or publish the result.
Getting started:

chunks.title: Product Shot Studio — How to use
chunks.text:
- Take a sharp photo of the product on a plain background, with the whole product visible.
- Sign in with an active plan and connect your API key (an upgrade prompt or key dialog appears otherwise).
- Start with Product Shot + Studio white background, then try other scenes.
Tips:
- Use a plain, well-lit product photo.
- Try several scenes and compare.
- For ads, keep the script short and name @image1.
- Use 720p while testing, 1080p for the final.
Best practices:
- Keep product photos consistent in angle and lighting.
- Check the product's label and logo in every result before publishing.
- Upscale finals in Upscale Suite if needed.

chunks.title: Product Shot Studio — Features
chunks.text:
Product Shot Studio (#/commercial). Features.
Key features:
- Two modes: 'Product shot' and 'Ad video'.
- Two product models: Product Shot (default) and Product Photography, both from MuAPI.
- Nine Scene Presets and four Output Formats with aspect ratios.
- Upload an image or video, or browse Pexels stock photos for a test image.
- Ad video: script with @image1 / @image2 references, avatar presets, extra reference images, six video format presets, five aspect ratios, 720p/1080p, durations 4-15 seconds.
- Result card with Download, Generate Again and Publish to Social.
- Saved to generation history under the commercial studio.
- Three-dot tools menu with Recipes, Monetize and Prompts.
Feature details:
- feature: Mode toggle: Product shot / Ad video | explanation: A two-button toggle at the top of the form. Product shot hides the ad controls; Ad video hides Model, Scene Preset and Output Format and shows the script box and ad controls. The main button changes between 'Generate Product Shot' and 'Generate Ad Video'. | whyToUse: Pick Product shot for still images and Ad video for a short promo clip. | inputRequired: None. | restrictions: Ad video needs an image, not a video, as the product.

chunks.title: Product Shot Studio — Features
chunks.text:
- feature: Model (Product Shot / Product Photography) | explanation: A dropdown labelled Model with two MuAPI models. 'Product Shot' (id ai-product-shot) is described as 'Quick AI product shot generation for e-commerce catalogs.' 'Product Photography' (id ai-product-photography) is described as 'AI product photography generation with professional lighting.' | whyToUse: Product Shot for fast catalog images; Product Photography when you want the format/aspect ratio applied and a lighting-focused result. | inputRequired: Defaults to Product Shot. | restrictions: Only these two models.

A Pexels button (tooltip 'Browse stock photos from Pexels') lets you pick a stock photo. | whyToUse: The product is the star of every result. | inputRequired: Required. Toast 'Upload a product image or video first' in Product shot mode. | restrictions: Shared upload limits: images 10MB, videos 50MB.

The chosen text becomes: '<scene>, professional product photography, commercial quality'. | whyToUse: One click to set the backdrop and mood. | inputRequired: Defaults to 'Studio white background'. | restrictions: Preset-only: there is no free-text scene box in this studio (a prompt chosen from the Prompts gallery is appended as extra text).

The product image is @image1; an optional avatar is @image2. | whyToUse: Tells the video model what to say and show. | inputRequired: Script required. | restrictions: Validation: 'Please enter an ad script.'

- feature: Three-dot tools menu | explanation: Recipes, Monetize and Prompts. Choosing a prompt from the gallery silently stores it and adds it to the end of your scene text on the next product shot. | whyToUse: Extra prompt ideas and business ideas. | inputRequired: None. | restrictions: The chosen prompt is not shown anywhere on screen after you pick it.
Modes:

- Ad video (short video)
Mode details:

- mode: Ad video | description: Sends the product image, optional avatar and references, a format preset and your script to a Seedance 2 omni-reference video route. | useCase: UGC-style, tutorial, unboxing, review or TV-spot ads (4-15 seconds).

chunks.title: Product Shot Studio — Problems and limits
chunks.text:
Product Shot Studio (#/commercial). Problems and limits.
Troubleshooting:
- Toast 'Upload a product image or video first': add a file under Product Media before clicking Generate Product Shot.
- Toast 'Please enter an ad script.': type a script in the Ad video box.
- Toast 'Please upload a product image.': Ad video mode needs the product image uploaded.
- Toast 'Ad video needs a product image, not a video.': replace the video with a still image.
- Toast 'Upload failed: ...' when adding an avatar or references: check size/type and try again.
- Toast 'No video URL returned by API' or 'Marketing generation failed': the ad service returned nothing; try again, shorten the script or lower the resolution/duration.
- Toast 'Error: ...' on a product shot: read the message, then retry or switch the Model.
- Output shape is not what I chose: use the Product Photography model, which receives the aspect ratio.
- An upgrade prompt or key dialog appears: finish sign-in/upgrade or connect your key, then click Generate again.
Troubleshooting steps:

chunks.title: Content — Overview
chunks.text:
Content (#/content-library). Overview.
Description:
Content is your saved-content shelf: generations you saved from a studio or Library, files you uploaded, PDFs and stock media from Pexels. Its side-menu label is "Content" and its route is #/content-library.
Summary:
Your saved content: saved generations, uploads, PDFs and stock media.
About:
Content (route #/content-library, shown in the menu as "Content") is headed "Content" with the line "Your saved content — generations you saved, uploads, PDFs and stock media". Filter tabs are All, Saved, Images, Videos, Audio and PDFs. There is a search box ("Search saved content..."), a "Browse Stock Media" button (Pexels), and an upload button (upload picker, up to 10 images, videos accepted). A status line shows the count, for example "3 items in saved". Empty state: "Nothing saved yet - Use Save to Content on any result in a studio or in your Library, or upload files here." Saved generations are kept in your browser (local storage), so saving always works; uploads and stock-media entries go to the cloud content library when the deployment has it configured, otherwise they are kept in the browser too.
Best for:
Keeping and reusing the files you care about: favourites, reference uploads, PDFs and licensed stock clips/photos.
When to use it:
- You want a short list of keepers apart from your full history.

chunks.title: Content — Overview
chunks.text:
- You want to upload PDFs or videos to reuse.
- You want free stock photos or videos from Pexels.
When to use another studio:
- For everything you have ever generated, use Library (#/library).
- To generate new content, open a studio from Apps (#/apps).

How to use:
1. Open Content from the left side menu (My Work group). 2. To add items, press Save on a result in a studio or Library, press Browse Stock Media, or use the upload button. 3. Use the tabs All, Saved, Images, Videos, Audio or PDFs and the search box to find items. 4. Click an item to preview and Download. 5. Hover and use the delete button to remove it.
Steps:

Tips:

Best practices:

chunks.title: Director — Overview
chunks.text:
Director (#/director). Overview.
Description:
Director is a chat-and-agents workspace where you load a video and ask AI agents to summarize it, find highlights, add subtitles, dub it, cut shorts, fix color and more. It has 48 agents backed by VideoDB, OpenAI and FFmpeg.
Summary:
AI agentic editor with 48 agents that analyse and edit an existing video through chat.
About:
Director (also labelled DIRECTOR - AI Agentic Editor - REASONING ENGINE on the page) works on a video you already have. You open it with a video loaded (normally by going to Director from the Render studio), then either click one of the 48 agent cards, click a Quick Action, or type a command such as 'Summarize this video'. Director matches your words to an agent, shows processing steps and a progress bar, and returns a result (a summary, highlights, scenes, subtitles, a dubbed or processed video, a timeline and so on) in the RESULT panel. Most agents run as jobs on the backend using VideoDB and OpenAI keys; a few (B-roll, shorts, color correction, upscaling, stabilization, speed, reverse) use FFmpeg-based actions. You need your own VideoDB and OpenAI keys saved in Settings, and an active plan.
Best for:
People who already have a video and want AI help understanding, cutting, captioning, translating or enhancing it, rather than generating new footage from scratch.
When to use it:

chunks.title: Director — Overview
chunks.text:
- You want a summary, scene list or highlights of an existing video.
- You want subtitles or an SRT file for a video.
- You want to dub or translate a video into another language.
- You want short vertical clips for TikTok, Reels or Shorts cut from a longer video.
- You want to find moments by what is said (keyword search) or what is seen (visual search).
- You want quick fixes: color correction, stabilization, speed change, reverse or upscale.
- You want a voiceover, a meme, a trailer narration or other creative remix built on your video.
When to use another studio:
- Use Video (#/video) when you want to generate brand-new AI video from text or an image.
- Use Timeline (#/timeline) when you want manual multi-track editing and export.
- Use Workbench (#/workbench) when you want to arrange generated clips, images and audio with motion cards.
- Use Video Agent (#/video-agent) when you want coded motion graphics from a prompt.
- Use Videotools (#/videotools) when you want a single quick tool such as a one-off edit on a clip.
- Use Lipsync (#/lipsync) or Avatar (#/avatar) when you need a talking presenter or lip-synced speech.
- Use Render (#/render) to prepare and export a finished video; Director's back arrow returns you there.

chunks.title: Director — How to use
chunks.text:
Director (#/director). How to use.
How to use:
1. Open Director with a video loaded: from the Render studio click through to Director so your video appears in the player (Director reads the video address from the page link). 2. Check Settings: add your VideoDB key and your OpenAI key. 3. Pick what to do: click an agent card in AI AGENTS, click a button under QUICK ACTIONS, or type a command in the box that says 'Type your command (e.g., 'Summarize this video')' and click Send. 4. If a small form appears (for example Text to synthesize or Video A URL), fill it in and click Run. 5. Watch the PROCESSING panel and the Progress bar; click Cancel to stop. 6. Read the result in the chat and in the RESULT panel; use the Download link or the video player. 7. Run more agents or click Clear Chat to start over. 8. Click the back arrow to return to Render.
Steps:
- Open Director from the Render studio so a video is loaded.
- Save your VideoDB and OpenAI keys in Settings.
- Click an agent card, a Quick Action, or type a command and click Send.
- Fill in any extra-input form and click Run.
- Follow progress in the PROCESSING panel; Cancel if needed.
- Review the result in RESULT, download it if offered.
- Use the back arrow to return to Render.
Getting started:
- Start with Summarize or Detect Scenes to see how Director responds.

chunks.title: Director — How to use
chunks.text:
- Make sure a video is showing in the player before running agents.
- Keep your VideoDB and OpenAI keys in Settings; most agents need them.
- Use the category filter to narrow the 48 agents.
Tips:
- Use the category drop-down to find agents quickly.
- Include a number in speed commands.
- Name the language in dubbing commands.
- Run Detect Scenes or Summarize first to understand a long video.
Best practices:
- Start from the Render studio so your video is loaded.
- Keep keys current in Settings.
- Run one agent at a time and review the RESULT before the next.
- Use shorter videos for faster jobs.

chunks.title: Director — Features
chunks.text:
Director (#/director). Features.
Key features:
- 48 AI agents in ten categories: Analysis, Search, Extract, Translate, Accessibility, Enhance, Audio, Edit, Create and Social.
- AI CHAT with a command box: type a request and Director picks the matching agent by keywords.
- AI AGENTS panel with a category filter (All Categories plus each category).
- QUICK ACTIONS: Summarize, Extract Highlights, Detect Scenes, Add Subtitles, Dub Video, Add B-Roll, Browse B-Roll from Pexels, Voiceover, Create Shorts, Color Correction, Stabilize.
- Live PROCESSING panel with step names and a Progress percentage bar, plus a Cancel button.
- ACTIVE AGENTS list and RECENT ACTIONS history in the left panel.
- RESULT panel that shows summaries, counts, playable video or audio, and a Download link.
- Inline mini-forms for agents that need extra input (for example voice text, two video URLs or a collection id).
- Chat history is remembered in your browser; Clear Chat resets it.
- Automatic retry for network errors, 429 and 5xx responses (up to 3 attempts).
Feature details:

chunks.title: Director — Features
chunks.text:
- feature: Command box (AI CHAT) | explanation: Type a request in the box with placeholder 'Type your command (e.g., 'Summarize this video')' and click Send or press Enter. Director looks for keywords in your sentence (for example summarize, subtitle, dub, highlight, scene, shorts, color, stabilize, speed, reverse, thumbnail, trailer, meme, slack) and runs the first matching agent. | whyToUse: The quickest way to run an agent in plain language. | inputRequired: A sentence containing a keyword for the agent you want. | restrictions: If no agent matches, Director replies 'I couldn't match that to a specific agent. Try one of these or use a keyword:' and shows suggestion chips. Only one job runs at a time.
- feature: AI AGENTS panel | explanation: A grid of 48 agent cards. Clicking a card runs that agent using its description as the command. The drop-down 'All Categories' filters the grid by category. | whyToUse: Browse what is possible and run an agent without typing. | inputRequired: A loaded video. | restrictions: Without a video, clicking a card says 'Please open Director with a video URL (from the Render studio) before running <agent>.' and a 'No video loaded' notice appears.

chunks.title: Director — Features
chunks.text:
- feature: QUICK ACTIONS | explanation: Ready-made buttons that send a command for you: Summarize ('summarize this video'), Extract Highlights, Detect Scenes, Add Subtitles, Dub Video (sends 'dub to Spanish'), Add B-Roll, Voiceover, Create Shorts (TikTok/Reels/Shorts), Color Correction, Stabilize. | whyToUse: One-click common jobs. | inputRequired: A loaded video. | restrictions: Dub Video defaults to Spanish; type your own command (for example 'dub to French') to choose another language.
- feature: Browse B-Roll from Pexels | explanation: Opens a Pexels stock-footage browser titled 'Browse B-Roll'. Selecting a clip adds it as B-roll and shows the photographer attribution chip. | whyToUse: Find free stock footage to overlay. | inputRequired: None. | restrictions: Attribution to the Pexels photographer is shown with the selection.
- feature: Processing panel and Cancel | explanation: While a job runs, the PROCESSING panel shows the agent name, step lines (for example 'Analyzing video content...', 'Generating summary...') and a Progress percentage. A Cancel button appears in the header. | whyToUse: See what is happening and stop a job you no longer want. | inputRequired: None. | restrictions: Cancel stops waiting for the job and shows 'Job cancelled'. Jobs time out after 10 minutes: 'Job timed out after 10 minutes'.

chunks.title: Director — Features
chunks.text:
- feature: Extra-input forms | explanation: Some agents ask for more information in a small form in the chat with Run and Cancel buttons. Voice Cloning asks for 'Text to synthesize'. Gen AI Audio Overlays and AI Voiceovers ask for 'Audio description / script'. Comparison Agent asks for 'Video A URL' and 'Video B URL'. Content Compiler, Compilation Builder and Montage Builder ask for 'VideoDB Collection ID' (default 'default'). | whyToUse: Provides the data those agents cannot get from the loaded video. | inputRequired: The fields shown. | restrictions: Empty required fields show 'Please provide a value for "<field>".' Press Enter to run or Escape to cancel.
- feature: RESULT panel | explanation: Shows what the agent produced: summary text, counts such as scenes, highlights, matches or shorts, SRT size, a playable video or audio player, and a Download link. | whyToUse: Read or download the output. | inputRequired: None. | restrictions: Which fields appear depends on the agent; before any run it says 'Run an agent to see results here.'
- feature: Clear Chat and Back | explanation: Clear Chat wipes the saved conversation and restores the greeting. The back arrow in the header returns to the Render studio with your video. | whyToUse: Start fresh, or go back to finishing your video. | inputRequired: None. | restrictions: Chat history is stored in this browser only.
Modes:

chunks.title: Director — Features
chunks.text:
- Backend job agents (VideoDB + OpenAI)
- FFmpeg actions
- VideoDB timeline compile
Mode details:
- mode: Backend job agents (VideoDB + OpenAI) | description: The request is submitted as a job and polled every 1.5 seconds until it completes, fails or is cancelled (10 minute limit). Used by summaries, highlights, scene detection, subtitles, dubbing, search, text-to-movie, storyboarding, memes, trailers, voiceover and cloning, ad films, lyric video, profanity remover, sales assistant, comparison, Slack, intro/outro, brand elements, dynamic ads and more. | useCase: Analysis and creative AI tasks.
- mode: FFmpeg actions | description: Returns results directly without job polling. Used by B-Roll Adder, Social Media Clip (create shorts), Color Correction, Video Enhancer (upscale), Video Stabilize, Speed Control and Reverse Video. | useCase: Fast technical fixes.
- mode: VideoDB timeline compile | description: Content Compiler, Compilation Builder and Montage Builder search your VideoDB collection semantically for your prompt and compile the matches into a timeline. | useCase: Building a compilation from many stored videos. If nothing matches you get 'No matching moments found in the collection.'
Models:

chunks.title: Director — Features
chunks.text: Director does not use a single selectable model. Its agents call a backend that combines VideoDB (video indexing, scene and visual search, subtitles, dubbing, timeline compile) with OpenAI (reasoning, scripting, summaries) and FFmpeg for technical edits; the Voice Cloning and some audio agents may also use a MuAPI key if present. The specific model names behind each agent are chosen on the backend and could not be confirmed from the front-end code. Speed Control uses the number in your command as the speed factor and defaults to 1.5 if none is given.

Add your VideoDB key in Settings.' or 'Missing API key. Add your VideoDB + OpenAI keys in Settings to use <agent>.'

chunks.title: Director — Problems and limits
chunks.text:
Director (#/director). Problems and limits.
Troubleshooting:
- 'No video loaded' or 'Please open Director with a video URL...': go back to the Render studio and open Director from there with your video.
- 'Missing API key. Add your VideoDB + OpenAI keys in Settings...': open Settings and save both keys, then run again.
- 'This feature requires an active subscription...': check your plan under Settings.
- 'I couldn't match that to a specific agent': click one of the suggestion chips or an agent card instead.
- '<Agent> failed: ...': read the message, check your keys and connection, and retry; the app already retries network, 429 and 5xx errors up to 3 times.
- 'Job timed out after 10 minutes': the video may be too long; try a shorter video or another agent.
- 'Video Agent job submission failed' or 'Poll failed': the backend may be unreachable; wait and retry.
- Buttons are greyed out: a job is still running; wait or click Cancel.
Troubleshooting steps:
- issue: Agents will not run | steps: Check the player: if it says 'No video loaded', return to Render and reopen Director with a video.; Open Settings and confirm your VideoDB key and OpenAI key are saved.; Confirm your plan is active.; Click the agent card again.
- issue: A job seems stuck | steps: Watch the Progress bar in the PROCESSING panel.; Click Cancel to stop waiting.; Retry with a shorter video or a smaller task.

chunks.title: Director — Problems and limits
chunks.text:
- issue: Compilation agents find nothing | steps: Make sure the VideoDB Collection ID is correct (default is 'default').; Describe the moments you want in clearer words.; Check that the collection has indexed videos in VideoDB.
Common problems:
- problem: Dub Video always dubs to Spanish | whyItHappens: The Quick Action sends the fixed command 'dub to Spanish'. | howToFix: Type your own command such as 'dub to French' in the command box.
- problem: Speed Control used 1.5x | whyItHappens: Speed is read from your command text and defaults to 1.5 when no number is found. | howToFix: Include the number, for example 'speed 2'.
- problem: Old chat reappears | whyItHappens: Chat history is saved in your browser. | howToFix: Click Clear Chat.
Limitations:
- Needs a video loaded from the Render studio; Director has no upload box of its own.
- Needs your own VideoDB and OpenAI keys and an active plan.
- Only one agent job runs at a time.
- Jobs stop waiting after 10 minutes.
- Agent choice from typed text is keyword-based, so unusual wording may not match.
- Chat history is saved only in this browser.
- Does not generate new video footage from a text prompt in the way the video studios do (Text to Movie and similar agents build on VideoDB assets and scripts).
Limit details:

chunks.title: Director — Problems and limits
chunks.text:
- limitation: No video loaded | impact: Agent cards will not run and show 'No video loaded'. | workaround: Go to the Render studio, load a video, then open Director from there.
- limitation: Keyword matching | impact: A sentence without a recognised keyword gets 'I couldn't match that to a specific agent'. | workaround: Click an agent card or use words like summarize, subtitle, dub, highlight, shorts, color or stabilize.
- limitation: Plan required | impact: Without an active plan you see 'This feature requires an active subscription. Please check your plan in Settings.' | workaround: Check or upgrade your plan.
FAQs:
- question: How many agents does Director have? | answer: 48, shown in the AI AGENTS panel and in the header line 'AI Agentic Editor - 48 Agents'.
- question: Do I need API keys? | answer: Yes. Most agents need your VideoDB key and your OpenAI key saved in Settings.
- question: Can I upload a video inside Director? | answer: No upload control was found. Director reads the video from the page link, normally set when you open it from the Render studio.
- question: Where is my chat saved? | answer: In your browser's local storage on this device. Clear Chat removes it.
- question: Can I cancel a running agent? | answer: Yes, click Cancel in the header while a job runs.

chunks.title: Director — Problems and limits
chunks.text: - question: Can Director add stock footage? | answer: Yes. Use Add B-Roll, or Browse B-Roll from Pexels to pick a clip yourself; Pexels attribution is shown.

chunks.title: Director — Workflows and use cases
chunks.text:
Director (#/director). Workflows and use cases.
Example workflows:
- title: Summarize and caption a video | steps: From the Render studio open Director with your video.; Click the Summarize Quick Action and read the summary in RESULT.; Click Add Subtitles and wait for the SRT result.; Click the back arrow to return to Render.
- title: Turn a long video into shorts | steps: Open Director with the video loaded.; Click Create Shorts.; Check the result count in RESULT and play or download the clips.
- title: Dub into another language | steps: Type 'dub to French' in the command box and click Send.; Follow the PROCESSING steps (extract audio, transcribe, translate, synthesize, mix).; Play or download the dubbed video.
Use cases:

- title: Accessibility captions | description: Add subtitles for viewers who watch without sound. | steps: Click Add Subtitles.; Wait for the SRT to be generated.; Download the result. | expectedOutput: Subtitles (SRT) for your video.

chunks.title: Director — Glossary
chunks.text: Glossary: Agent: A specialised AI helper that does one video task, such as subtitles or highlights. | VideoDB: A video-as-data service Director uses to index, search and process videos. | Collection: A group of videos stored in your VideoDB account. | B-roll: Extra cutaway footage laid over the main video. | SRT: A common subtitle file format. | Job: A background task that Director starts and checks on until it finishes.

chunks.title: Edit Studio — Overview
chunks.text:
Edit Studio (#/edit). Overview.
Description:
Edit Studio is a gallery of 16 focused AI photo-editing tools. You pick a tool, upload a photo, adjust a few settings and click Apply Edit to get a before/after result.
Summary:
16 AI photo tools: remove objects and backgrounds, extend, reframe, effects, face swap and more.
About:
Edit Studio opens on a grid of 16 tool cards. Clicking a card opens that tool's own mini-studio with a 'Source image' upload, any extra inputs the tool needs (a mask, an outfit photo, a face photo, a logo), an optional prompt, a Settings panel and an 'Apply Edit' button. A Preview panel on the right shows your photo, then a Before / After comparison slider with Download, Generate Again and 'Use result as new source' buttons. Five of the tools (AI Edit, Upscale, Product Shot, Photo Effects, Character & Reference) have a Model dropdown so you can choose between several AI models; the screen adapts to the model (prompt box, number of extra reference images, settings). Edit Studio works on images only in the current code; the upload picker does not accept video.
Best for:
Beginners who want to fix or change a photo with a single clear tool, without writing long prompts: removing something from a picture, cutting out a background, putting a product in a scene, trying an outfit, adding a logo, or giving a photo a one-click look.
When to use it:

chunks.title: Edit Studio — Overview
chunks.text:
- You have a photo and want one specific change (remove an object, remove the background, extend it, change the aspect ratio).
- You want a one-click look such as 3D figurine, cyberpunk or 1980s (Photo Effects).
- You want to describe a change in plain words and apply it to a photo (AI Edit).
- You want a product photo placed in a new scene (Product Shot).
- You want to swap a face, change an outfit, colorize an old black-and-white photo or add a watermark.
- You want to compare the original and edited photo side by side.
When to use another studio:
- Use Image Studio (#/image) when you want to create a new picture from a text prompt, or do free-form image-to-image with many models.
- Use Upscale Suite (#/upscale) when you only want a larger, sharper copy of an image with a dedicated method picker.
- Use Character Studio (#/character) when you need one character kept consistent across many images and scenes.
- Use Commercial Studio (#/commercial) for ad-style product and commercial content.
- Use Video Tools (#/videotools) or Video Studio (#/video) when you are working with video clips; Edit Studio does not accept video uploads.

chunks.title: Edit Studio — How to use
chunks.text:
Edit Studio (#/edit). How to use.
How to use:
1. Open Edit Studio from the side menu (Edit). 2. Click the card of the tool you want, for example Remove Background. 3. Under 'Source image' click the upload button (or the Pexels button) and add your photo; it shows in Preview and the hint changes to 'Image ready'. 4. If the tool shows an extra panel (mask painter, 'Outfit image', 'New face photo', 'Watermark / logo image'), fill it in. 5. If a Model dropdown is shown, choose a model; read the note under it. 6. If a Prompt or 'Scene description' box is shown, type what you want. 7. Adjust anything in the Settings panel. 8. Click Apply Edit. 9. Use the Compare slider, or the Before and After buttons, to check the result. 10. Click Download to save, Generate Again to retry, or 'Use result as new source' to keep editing the result with another tool.
Steps:
- Choose a tool card (or use 'Switch tool' later).
- Upload the Source image.
- Add any extra image or mask the tool needs.
- Choose a Model if the dropdown is shown.
- Fill the Prompt or Settings if shown.
- Click Apply Edit and wait for the preview.
- Compare Before and After, then Download.
Getting started:
- Try Remove Background first: it needs only a photo and no settings.
- Then try AI Edit with a simple instruction such as 'make the sky a sunset'.

chunks.title: Edit Studio — How to use
chunks.text:
- Use 'Use result as new source' to chain two edits, for example Remove Background then Product Shot.
Tips:
- Use a larger brush for Remove Object so the AI sees surrounding context.
- Remove Background works best when the subject clearly stands out from the background.
- Use a clear, front-facing, well-lit face for Face Swap.
- Use a transparent PNG for the watermark.
- Write short, specific instructions in AI Edit, one change at a time.
- Use the Compare slider before you download.
Best practices:
- Start from the highest-quality source image you have.
- Chain small edits with 'Use result as new source' rather than one huge instruction.
- Keep each upload under 10MB.
- Download results you want to keep.

chunks.title: Edit Studio — Features
chunks.text:
Edit Studio (#/edit). Features.
Key features:
- 16 tool cards: Remove Object, Remove Background, Extend Image, AI Edit, Reframe, Change Dress, Enhance Skin, Colorize, Add Watermark, Upscale, Face Swap, Product Shot, Ghibli Style, Photo Effects, Change Angle, Character & Reference.
- Each tool has a one-line how-to under its title and its own thumbnail.
- 'Switch tool' dropdown to jump between tools without going back, and '← All tools' to return to the grid.
- Deep links: opening /?tool=<slug>#/edit (for example tool=remove-object) opens that tool straight away.
- Model dropdown on five tools, grouped by maker, with a short note about the selected model.
- Built-in mask painter for Remove Object (Brush, Erase, Clear, Brush size).
- Before / After preview with Compare slider, Before and After buttons.
- Result actions: Download, Generate Again, 'Use result as new source' (chain edits).
- 'This session' strip of earlier results (appears once you have 2 or more results).
- Pexels stock photo browser as a source (button titled 'Browse stock photos from Pexels').
- Cancel button while an edit is running.
Feature details:

chunks.title: Edit Studio — Features
chunks.text:
- feature: Remove Object | explanation: Upload a photo, then paint over what you want gone using the mask painter (hint: 'Paint over everything you want removed.'). Tools: Brush, Erase, Clear and a Brush size slider (default 48). You can instead upload a ready-made mask under 'Mask image (optional)': white means remove, black means keep. | whyToUse: Clean up photobombers, wires, text or clutter. | inputRequired: Source image plus either a painted mask or an uploaded mask. | restrictions: Without a mask you see 'Paint over the object you want removed (or upload a mask).' Paint a bit beyond the object so the AI has context.
- feature: Remove Background | explanation: Upload a photo and get a clean cut-out with a transparent background. | whyToUse: Product shots, profile pictures, stickers. | inputRequired: Source image only. | restrictions: No settings. Works best when the subject is clearly separated from the background.
- feature: Extend Image | explanation: AI paints in more scene around the edges of your photo (outpainting). | whyToUse: Widen a crop or add space around a subject. | inputRequired: Source image only. | restrictions: No prompt or settings are shown for this tool.

chunks.title: Edit Studio — Features
chunks.text:
- feature: AI Edit | explanation: Instruction-based editing: upload a photo and describe the change, for example 'make it night time'. Prompt placeholder: 'Describe the edit...'. Has Aspect Ratio (1:1, 16:9, 9:16, 4:3, 3:4, 2:3, 3:2, 21:9; default 1:1) and Quality (basic or high; default basic) for the default model, and a Model dropdown with 30 editors. | whyToUse: The most flexible tool: change colors, add or remove things, change the time of day or style. | inputRequired: Source image and a prompt. | restrictions: Prompt is required: 'Describe the edit you want.' Some models accept extra reference images (up to 14 for Nano Banana 2 Edit).
- feature: Reframe | explanation: Pick a new aspect ratio and AI fills the new space. Settings: Aspect Ratio (16:9, 9:16, 1:1, 4:3, 3:4; default 1:1), Render Speed (Turbo, Balanced, Quality; default Balanced), Style (Auto, General, Realistic, Design; default Auto), Variations (1 to 4). | whyToUse: Turn a landscape photo into a vertical one or the reverse. | inputRequired: Source image. | restrictions: No prompt.
- feature: Change Dress | explanation: Upload a photo of a person and a photo of the outfit to put on them. | whyToUse: Virtual try-on. | inputRequired: Source image and 'Outfit image' (a clear photo of the clothing item). | restrictions: If the outfit is missing: 'Upload the outfit image.'

chunks.title: Edit Studio — Features
chunks.text:
- feature: Enhance Skin | explanation: Natural, professional skin retouching for a portrait. | whyToUse: Portrait cleanup. | inputRequired: Source image of a portrait. | restrictions: No settings.
- feature: Colorize | explanation: Adds color to a black-and-white photo. | whyToUse: Bring old photos to life. | inputRequired: Source image. | restrictions: No settings.
- feature: Add Watermark | explanation: Overlay your logo on a photo. Settings: Position (top-left, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-right, center; default bottom-right), Opacity (0-100%, default 70%), Size (5-100%, default 20%). | whyToUse: Brand or protect photos. | inputRequired: Source image and 'Watermark / logo image' (a PNG with a transparent background works best). | restrictions: If the logo is missing: 'Upload the watermark / logo image.'
- feature: Upscale (inside Edit Studio) | explanation: Sharpens and increases resolution. Model dropdown: AI Image Upscaler (quick, clean, good default), Topaz Image Upscale (choose factor 1, 2, 4 or 8; default 2) and Seedvr2 Image Upscale (resolution 2k, 4k or 8k; default 4k). | whyToUse: Quick resolution boost without leaving Edit Studio. | inputRequired: Source image. | restrictions: The 'Upscale Suite' (#/upscale) is the dedicated studio for this.

chunks.title: Edit Studio — Features
chunks.text:
- feature: Face Swap | explanation: Upload the photo to change, then a clear photo of the new face. Setting: Target Face Index (0 to 10, default 0) chooses which face in a group photo is replaced. | whyToUse: Replace one person's face with another. | inputRequired: Source image and 'New face photo' (front-facing, well-lit works best). | restrictions: If missing: 'Upload the new face photo.' Use only photos you have the right to use.
- feature: Product Shot | explanation: Upload a product photo and describe the scene to place it in (field label 'Scene description', placeholder 'Describe the product scene...'). Models: AI Product Shot (places your product in a scene you describe) and AI Product Photography (turns a product photo into a polished studio or lifestyle shot). | whyToUse: E-commerce and ad visuals. | inputRequired: Source image and a scene description. | restrictions: If empty: 'Describe the product scene.'
- feature: Ghibli Style | explanation: Redraws any photo in a hand-painted anime style. | whyToUse: Fun stylization. | inputRequired: Source image. | restrictions: No settings.

chunks.title: Edit Studio — Features
chunks.text:
- feature: Photo Effects | explanation: One-click looks chosen from a grid of presets. Three models: Image Effects (18 looks, default Angel Figurine; includes Acrylic Ornaments, American Comic Style, Cyberpunk, Felt 3D Polaroid, Glass Ball, Plastic Bubble Figure and more), Nano Banana Effects (17 looks, default 3D Figurine; includes 16bit Game Character, decade looks 1920s to 1980s, Action Figure, landmark and famous-art looks; also an Aspect Ratio setting with Auto default) and Flux Kontext Effects (13 edits, default Age Progression; includes Background Change, Cartoonify, Hair Change, Expression Change, Time of Day, Weather Effect, and a prompt box). | whyToUse: Quick creative looks without writing prompts. | inputRequired: Source image and a preset (a default is preselected). | restrictions: The list of presets depends on the model.
- feature: Change Angle | explanation: Re-shoot a photo from a new camera angle using the Qwen Camera Angle model: rotate left/right (-90 to 90), move forward (0 to 10), vertical angle (-1 to 1), a wide-angle lens switch and output width/height (256 to 1536, default 1024). | whyToUse: See the subject from another side or closer. | inputRequired: Source image (the model can take up to 3 images). | restrictions: Large rotations may look less natural.

chunks.title: Edit Studio — Features
chunks.text:
- feature: Character & Reference | explanation: Upload a person, product or style as the 'Reference image', then describe a new scene (placeholder: 'Describe the new scene, e.g. "standing on a beach at sunset"...'). Models: Ideogram Character, Minimax Image 01 Subject Reference, Midjourney v7 Omni Reference (weight sets strength), Midjourney v7 Style Reference, Vidu Q2 Reference To Image (combines up to 7 reference images). | whyToUse: Keep the same person, product or style in new scenes. | inputRequired: Reference image and a scene prompt. | restrictions: If empty: 'Describe the scene you want the reference placed in.'
Modes:
- Single-tool edit with before/after preview
- Chained edits (Use result as new source)
- Model-switching within multi-model tools
Mode details:
- mode: Gallery view | description: The grid of 16 tool cards (each shows 'Open studio ->' on hover). | useCase: Browse and choose a tool.
- mode: Tool studio view | description: Inputs on the left, Preview on the right. | useCase: Do the edit.
- mode: Compare / Before / After | description: Toggle buttons above the preview. Compare shows a draggable divider labelled BEFORE and AFTER. | useCase: Judge exactly what changed.
Models:

chunks.title: Edit Studio — Problems and limits
chunks.text:
Edit Studio (#/edit). Problems and limits.
Troubleshooting:
- 'Upload a source image first.': you clicked Apply Edit before adding a photo. Upload one in the Source image panel.
- 'Paint over the object you want removed (or upload a mask).': in Remove Object, paint on the photo with Brush or upload a mask.
- 'Describe the edit you want.' / 'Describe the product scene.' / 'Describe the scene you want the reference placed in.': the selected model needs a prompt. Type one and apply again.
- 'Upload the outfit image.' / 'Upload the new face photo.' / 'Upload the watermark / logo image.': the tool needs its second image. Upload it in the extra panel.
- 'Could not read the painted mask. Try painting again.': click Clear in the mask painter and paint again.
- 'Edit completed, but no result image was returned. Please try again.': the model finished without an image. Click Generate Again or choose another model.
- A red message appears over the preview after Apply Edit: it shows the error text from the AI service. Read it, adjust the input or model and try again.
- A sign-in / API key dialog opens when you click Apply Edit: complete it; the edit then restarts automatically.
- Nothing seems to happen: check the progress area below Apply Edit; use Cancel to stop and retry.

chunks.title: Edit Studio — Problems and limits
chunks.text:
- I do not see the Model dropdown: only AI Edit, Upscale, Product Shot, Photo Effects and Character & Reference have one.
- My painted mask is gone: the mask painter resets when you change tool or source image. Paint it again.
Troubleshooting steps:
- issue: Object removal leaves traces | steps: Click Clear in the mask painter.; Increase Brush size and paint a little beyond the object edges.; Click Apply Edit again, or click 'Use result as new source' and run Remove Object a second time.
- issue: Edit changed more than I wanted | steps: Switch to a model noted for leaving the rest of the photo alone, such as Flux Kontext Dev or SeedEdit v3.; Make the prompt more specific about the one thing to change.; Try Generate Again.
- issue: Upload will not start | steps: Check the image is under 10MB and is a normal image file.; Try the Pexels button as a test to confirm the rest of the studio works.; Reload the page and try again.
- issue: Result is not what the tool says it does | steps: Confirm you opened the right tool (see the title above the form).; Use the 'Switch tool' dropdown if needed.; Check the second image slot is filled with the right picture.
Common problems:
- problem: Apply Edit shows a validation message in red | whyItHappens: A required input is missing. | howToFix: Read the message: it names the missing item (source image, mask, outfit, face, logo or prompt).

chunks.title: Edit Studio — Problems and limits
chunks.text:
- problem: Face Swap changes the wrong face | whyItHappens: The photo has several faces. | howToFix: Change Target Face Index (0 to 10) in Settings and try again.
- problem: Watermark is too strong or too big | whyItHappens: Defaults are Opacity 70% and Size 20%. | howToFix: Lower Opacity or Size and apply again.
- problem: Background removal edges look rough | whyItHappens: Subject and background are too similar. | howToFix: Use a photo with clearer separation or clean up with Remove Object.
Limitations:
- Images only: the upload picker does not accept video or documents.
- There are no separate Inpaint or Relight tools; the 16 tools are the ones listed.
- Each upload is limited to 10MB.
- Edits are applied one at a time; the progress bar is an estimate that moves up to about 90% until the result arrives.
- The 'This session' history is not saved if you refresh the page (the results themselves are registered in your generation history).
- An API key must be present; otherwise a sign-in dialog opens.
Limit details:
- limitation: No video editing | impact: Uploading an MP4 is not possible in this studio. | workaround: Use Video Tools (#/videotools), Video Studio (#/video) or the Timeline editor for video.

chunks.title: Edit Studio — Problems and limits
chunks.text:
- limitation: Remove Object needs a mask | impact: Clicking Apply Edit without painting or uploading a mask shows an error. | workaround: Paint over the object with the Brush, or upload a white-on-black mask.
- limitation: Result quality depends on the model | impact: Different models change different amounts of the photo. | workaround: Try another model in the Model dropdown or use Generate Again.
FAQs:
- question: Can Edit Studio edit videos? | answer: No. In the current studio the upload accepts images only. For video use Video Tools or Video Studio.
- question: How many tools are there? | answer: 16: Remove Object, Remove Background, Extend Image, AI Edit, Reframe, Change Dress, Enhance Skin, Colorize, Add Watermark, Upscale, Face Swap, Product Shot, Ghibli Style, Photo Effects, Change Angle and Character & Reference.
- question: How do I switch tools without losing my photo? | answer: Use the 'Switch tool' dropdown at the top of the tool screen; your uploaded source image stays loaded.
- question: How do I apply a second edit to the result? | answer: Click 'Use result as new source', then open another tool.

chunks.title: Edit Studio — Problems and limits
chunks.text:
- question: What is the difference between Upscale here and Upscale Suite? | answer: Both run the same three upscalers (AI Image Upscaler, Topaz, SeedVR2). Edit Studio shows each model's own settings (Topaz factor 1/2/4/8, SeedVR2 resolution 2k/4k/8k). Upscale Suite is a dedicated page with its own method picker.
- question: Which model should I use for AI Edit? | answer: The default Seedream 5.0 Edit is described as a good default. Nano Banana Edit is a fast everyday editor, GPT Image 1.5 Edit is best at text and logos, and Flux Kontext Dev is good at leaving the rest of the photo untouched.
- question: How do I link directly to one tool? | answer: Open the studio with ?tool=<slug> before the #/edit part, for example tool=remove-background, remove-object, extend-image, ai-edit, reframe, change-dress, enhance-skin, colorize, add-watermark, upscale, face-swap, product-shot, ghibli-style, photo-effects, change-angle or character-reference.
- question: Why is there a Cancel button? | answer: It appears while an edit runs so you can stop waiting and start again.

chunks.title: Edit Studio — Workflows and use cases
chunks.text:
Edit Studio (#/edit). Workflows and use cases.
Example workflows:
- title: Clean product cut-out then place it in a scene | steps: Open Remove Background and upload the product photo; click Apply Edit.; Click 'Use result as new source'.; Use 'Switch tool' to open Product Shot.; Type a scene such as 'on a marble counter with soft morning light' and click Apply Edit.; Click Download.
- title: Remove a person from a travel photo | steps: Open Remove Object and upload the photo.; Paint over the person with Brush (use a larger Brush size).; Click Apply Edit and use Compare to check the result.; Click Download.
- title: Turn a landscape photo into a vertical story | steps: Open Reframe and upload the photo.; Set Aspect Ratio to 9:16 and Render Speed to Quality.; Click Apply Edit, then Download.
- title: Add your logo to photos | steps: Open Add Watermark and upload the photo.; Upload a transparent PNG as the 'Watermark / logo image'.; Set Position, Opacity and Size, then click Apply Edit.
Use cases:
- title: E-commerce product images | description: Remove backgrounds and place products in lifestyle scenes. | steps: Remove Background; Product Shot with a scene description; Download | expectedOutput: A polished product image.

chunks.title: Edit Studio — Workflows and use cases
chunks.text:
- title: Photo restoration and fun | description: Colorize old photos, retouch skin or apply a Ghibli or figurine look. | steps: Open Colorize, Enhance Skin, Ghibli Style or Photo Effects; Upload the photo; Apply Edit | expectedOutput: A transformed copy of your photo.
- title: Virtual try-on | description: Show a person in a different outfit. | steps: Open Change Dress; Upload the person and the outfit image; Apply Edit | expectedOutput: The person wearing the new outfit.
Related studios:
- studio: image | relationship: Create or transform images with a prompt | whenToMove: When you want a brand-new image or free-form image-to-image with many models. | why: Image Studio has the full model picker and prompt bar.

- studio: videotools | relationship: Video editing tools | whenToMove: When your media is a video. | why: Edit Studio does not take video.

chunks.title: Edit Studio — Glossary
chunks.text: Glossary: Mask: A black-and-white image that marks the area to change; white is the area to remove or change. | Outpainting: AI drawing new content beyond the original edges (Extend Image). | Reframe: Changing the aspect ratio and letting AI fill the new area. | Source image: The photo you are editing. | Reference image: A photo the AI should keep a person, product or style from. | Before / After: The original photo and the edited result shown for comparison. | Model: The AI engine that performs the edit.

chunks.title: Effects Studio — Overview
chunks.text:
Effects Studio (#/effects). Overview.
Description:
Effects Studio applies ready-made visual and motion effects to a photo or video. You pick an effect from a catalogue of about 200 presets in six tabs, upload your media, and press Generate. A second mode called Motion graphics (also known as Vibe Motion) creates animated graphics from a text description.
Summary:
Pick a preset effect, upload a photo or clip, and generate a styled image or an effect video.
About:

chunks.title: Effects Studio — Overview
chunks.text:
Effects Studio is a catalogue-driven studio. Instead of writing a long prompt, you choose a named effect (for example Angel Figurine, Dolly Zoom In, Cakeify or Kissing Pro), upload one image or video, optionally add a short prompt, and press Generate. The studio has six tabs: Image Effects, Nano Banana, Kontext Effects (these three output still images) and Video Effects, Motion Controls, Video FX v2 (these three output videos). Each tab shows its effect count and a thumbnail grid with a search box. After generating you can compare before and after, download, save to your library, insert into the timeline, add AI captions (videos only) or publish to social. A top toggle switches the page between Effects and Motion graphics, where you describe an animated graphic (kinetic text, charts, logo reveals) and can later remix a previous result. Generation runs through MuAPI and needs your MuAPI key plus an account with full access.
Best for:
Beginners and social creators who want a one-click transformation (figurine looks, comic styles, decade looks, camera moves, kiss/hug style clips, melt/inflate style clips) without writing prompts, and anyone who wants to quickly try many looks on the same photo.
When to use it:
- You want a named, repeatable effect applied to a photo (for example 3D Figurine, Cyberpunk, Glass Ball, 1980s Decade).

chunks.title: Effects Studio — Overview
chunks.text:
- You want to turn one photo into a short effect video (for example Cakeify, Melt It, Inflate It, Hulk Transformation).
- You want a camera move on a still (for example Dolly In, Crash Zoom In, Arc Shot, FPV Drone Cam) from the Motion Controls tab.
- You want to edit a photo with a short instruction such as 20 years older or Background Change using the Kontext Effects tab.
- You want a quick animated motion graphic (title, chart, logo reveal) from text using the Motion graphics mode.
When to use another studio:
- Use AI VFX Studio (#/ai-vfx) when you want a cleaner, single-purpose page with Aspect, Duration, Size and Quality controls for AI Effects, Motion Controls and explosion/VFX presets from one image.
- Use Animate Studio (#/animate) when you want to animate an image freely with your own motion prompt and choose any image-to-video model.
- Use Video Tools (#/videotools) when you want to upscale, translate, caption, clip, reframe or recast an existing video rather than apply a style effect.
- Use Image Studio (#/image) when you want to create an image from a text prompt rather than apply a preset effect to your own photo.
- Use Edit Studio (#/edit) when you need detailed prompt-based photo editing with many controls.
- Use Upscale Studio (#/upscale) when the only goal is a sharper, higher-resolution image.

chunks.title: Effects Studio — Overview
chunks.text: - Use Timeline (#/timeline) when you want to arrange several generated clips into a finished video.

chunks.title: Effects Studio — How to use
chunks.text:
Effects Studio (#/effects). How to use.
How to use:
1. Open Effects Studio from the side menu (#/effects). 2. Pick a tab: Image Effects, Nano Banana or Kontext Effects for still images, or Video Effects, Motion Controls or Video FX v2 for videos. 3. Use Search effects... to find a preset, then click its card; the name appears at the top right of the preview area instead of No effect selected. 4. Under Input, click the upload button (hint: Upload image or video) to add your photo, or use the compass button to browse Pexels stock photos. 5. Optional: type in the Optional prompt... box. For Kontext Effects describe the change you want. 6. Optional: press Advanced to set Guidance, Steps, Seed, Negative Prompt, Effect Strength or Denoise Strength. 7. Press Generate. The output panel shows Applying and the effect name. Images usually come back within about 90 seconds and videos within about 3 minutes before the studio gives up. 8. Review the Output. Press Compare to see before and after. 9. Use Download, Add to Library, Insert into Timeline, Add AI Captions (video only) or Publish to Social.
Steps:
- Open Effects Studio (#/effects) and choose a tab.
- Search and click an effect card so it is highlighted and named in the preview header.
- Upload an image or video, or pick a Pexels stock photo.
- Optionally write a prompt and open Advanced for fine controls.

chunks.title: Effects Studio — How to use
chunks.text:
- Press Generate and wait for the Output panel to fill.
- Compare, then download, save to library, insert into the timeline, caption or publish.
Getting started:
- Start on the Image Effects tab with a clear, well-lit, face-forward photo and try Angel Figurine or Glass Ball.
- Try the same photo on several effects and use Compare to see which you like.
- Move to Video Effects or Motion Controls to get a 5 second clip from the same photo.
- Make sure your MuAPI key is set in the settings window and your account has full access, otherwise Generate will ask you to upgrade or enter a key.
Tips:
- Use a high resolution, well lit, front-facing photo for face and portrait effects.
- Try several effects on one photo and use Compare to choose.
- For Kontext Effects, write a specific instruction instead of leaving the prompt blank.
- Use a fixed Seed in Advanced when you want to repeat a look.
- Use Search effects... with a single keyword such as kiss, zoom or dolly.
- Use Add to Library early so you do not lose a result.
Best practices:
- Choose the tab by output type first: first three for images, last three for video.
- Keep source files well under 10 MB for images and 50 MB for videos.
- Describe the subject, not the camera, in the prompt on Motion Controls.
- Generate one effect at a time; layers multiply the number of generations.

chunks.title: Effects Studio — Features
chunks.text:
Effects Studio (#/effects). Features.
Key features:
- Six effect tabs: Image Effects (18), Nano Banana (17), Kontext Effects (13), Video Effects (64), Motion Controls (47), Video FX v2 (41). The counts are shown on each tab button and come from the model lists in the code.
- Thumbnail grid of effect cards and a Search effects... box that filters by name.
- Upload an image or a video, browse stock photos from Pexels, or attach extra reference files from the toolbar next to the prompt box.
- Optional prompt box. For Kontext Effects, Video Effects and Motion Controls the studio fills in the effect name if you leave it empty.
- Advanced panel with Guidance, Steps, Seed, Negative Prompt, Effect Strength and Denoise Strength, saved in your browser, with Reset to defaults.
- Compare button for a side-by-side Input and Output view.
- Result actions: Download, Add to Library, Insert into Timeline, Add AI Captions (video results only), Publish to Social.
- Effect Layers with blend modes and opacity (experimental, see limitations).
- Motion graphics (Vibe Motion) mode with Generate and Edit (Remix) and a saved gallery of your last 30 results in this browser.
- Extras menu (three dots) with Recipes, Monetize and Prompts, plus Thumbnail and Personalize buttons.
Feature details:

chunks.text:
- feature: Advanced panel | explanation: Press Advanced to open Guidance (1 to 20, default 7.5), Steps (1 to 50, default 20), Seed (default -1 means random, with a dice button to randomise), Negative Prompt, Effect Strength (0 to 100 percent, default 100 percent) and Denoise Strength (0 to 1, default 0.70). The button changes to Less when open. Press Reset to defaults to restore everything. | whyToUse: Reproduce a result with a fixed seed, steer away from unwanted looks, or soften an effect. | inputRequired: None. Values are saved in this browser. | restrictions: The studio sends these values to the API only when they differ from defaults. Whether each specific effect honours each control is not documented, so changes may have little or no visible effect on some presets.
- feature: Compare | explanation: The Compare button (labelled Compare with a double arrow; Toggle Compare on mobile) shows your input and the output side by side after a result exists. | whyToUse: Judge how strongly the effect changed your photo. | inputRequired: A finished result. | restrictions: Only works for the most recent result.

Clicking the output preview opens a larger detail view. | whyToUse: Move the result into the rest of your workflow. | inputRequired: A finished result. | restrictions: If there is no result yet you see toasts such as No result to download, No result to save or No result to insert.

chunks.text:
- feature: Motion graphics (Vibe Motion) mode | explanation: Switch the top toggle from Effects to Motion graphics (URL parameter ?mode=motion opens it directly). Type a description such as Animated sales dashboard with glowing bar charts and rising numbers, choose an aspect ratio (16:9, 9:16 or 1:1) and a duration (5, 6, 8, 10, 12, 15, 20, 25 or 30 seconds; default 6s), then press Generate. Use the Generate / Edit toggle or Remix this generation on a result to change it, for example change background to dark navy, make bars gold, add particles. | whyToUse: Animated titles, data charts, logo reveals and kinetic typography without a source photo. | inputRequired: A text description. Edit mode also needs a source generation (Pick source). | restrictions: You can only edit results whose animation code was saved by the service. Otherwise the studio shows: This generation can't be remixed - the animation code wasn't saved server-side. Generate a new motion graphic first, then remix that result. Your gallery keeps the last 30 results in this browser only.

Mode details:

chunks.title: Effects Studio — Features
chunks.text:
- mode: Image effect (still) | description: Image Effects, Nano Banana and Kontext Effects tabs. One image in, one styled image out. | useCase: Profile pictures, figurines, comic and decade looks, quick photo edits.
- mode: Video effect (5 second clip) | description: Video Effects and Video FX v2 tabs. One image in, one short effect video out at 720p and 5 seconds. | useCase: Short-form social clips such as Cakeify, Melt It, Kissing, Hugging.

Models:

chunks.title: Effects Studio — Features
chunks.text: Effects Studio does not have a general model picker. Each tab maps to one fixed model in the code: Image Effects (id image-effects, provider MuAPI, general image effects), Nano Banana Effects (id nano-banana-effects, provider Google, creative visual effects), Flux Kontext Effects (id flux-kontext-effects, provider Black Forest Labs, instruction-style edits and stylisation), AI Video Effects (id ai-video-effects, MuAPI Wan AI effects endpoint), Motion Controls (id motion-controls, same Wan AI effects endpoint, camera-move presets) and Video Effects v2 (id video-effects, MuAPI video-effects endpoint, filters and transitions style presets). The effect names are the enum values defined for each of those models and the studio only offers names the API accepts. Motion graphics mode uses MuAPI motion-graphics and motion-graphics-edit endpoints. The catalog files give only one-line descriptions for these models and no price, speed or quality figures, so none are stated here.

In Edit mode an empty prompt shows: Describe the change you want to make., and no source shows: Pick the generation you want to edit.

chunks.title: Effects Studio — Problems and limits
chunks.text:
Effects Studio (#/effects). Problems and limits.
Troubleshooting:
- Alert says Select an effect first: click an effect card in the grid. Selecting a different tab clears your choice, so pick the effect again.
- Alert says Upload an image or video first: add a file with the upload button or Pexels before pressing Generate.
- An upgrade prompt appears when you press Generate: your account needs full access. Upgrade or sign in with an account that has access.
- A settings or key window opens when you press Generate: add your MuAPI API key, then press Generate again.
- Error toast after a long wait: the request may have timed out (about 90 seconds for images, 180 seconds for videos). Press Retry, or try a smaller image.
- Error mentioning Effect is not supported by the API: choose a preset from the grid; the Video Effects and Motion Controls tabs only accept the listed names.
- File is too large: images must be 10 MB or less and videos 50 MB or less. Compress the file.
- The result looks barely changed: try a clearer face-forward photo, raise Effect Strength to 100 percent, or pick a stronger preset.
- Add AI Captions button is missing: it only appears after a video result. Image tabs never show it.
- No effects match your search: clear the Search effects... box or check you are on the right tab; each tab has its own list.

chunks.title: Effects Studio — Problems and limits
chunks.text:
- Motion graphics Remix fails with This generation can't be remixed: generate a new motion graphic first, then remix that new result.
- Thumbnail in a card is blank: card thumbnails fall back to an icon when an image file is missing. The effect still works.
Troubleshooting steps:
- issue: Generate does nothing or asks me to upgrade | steps: Check that you are signed in with an account that has full access.; If a settings window opens, enter your MuAPI key and save.; Press Generate again.
- issue: Generation fails or times out | steps: Read the red error toast; it shows the message returned by the service.; Press the Generate button again (it turns into a retry button after a failure).; Use a smaller photo (under 10 MB) and a clear subject.; On video tabs, wait up to 3 minutes; on image tabs up to 90 seconds.
- issue: I cannot find the effect I saw before | steps: Open the tab that holds it: image looks are in the first three tabs and video presets in the last three.; Type part of the name in Search effects...; Remember Video Effects (64), Video FX v2 (41) and Motion Controls (47) are separate lists.
- issue: Result is not saved in my library | steps: Press Add to Library under the Output.; Look for the toast Added to media library.; If you see Failed to add to library, press the button again.
Common problems:

chunks.title: Effects Studio — Problems and limits
chunks.text:
- problem: Face looks wrong or the effect is weak | whyItHappens: Face effects work best with a clear, well-lit, front-facing photo. Small or occluded faces give poor results. | howToFix: Use a higher resolution portrait with the face clearly visible, then retry.
- problem: Video is only 5 seconds | whyItHappens: The studio fixes video effects at 5 seconds and 720p. | howToFix: Use AI VFX Studio for a 10 second option, or join clips in Timeline.
- problem: Settings keep coming back after refresh | whyItHappens: Advanced values are saved in your browser (key effects_studio_advanced_settings). | howToFix: Open Advanced and press Reset to defaults.
- problem: Kontext Effects gives an unexpected edit | whyItHappens: With an empty prompt the studio uses only the effect name as the instruction. | howToFix: Write a specific prompt, for example make the person look 20 years older.
Limitations:
- Only the preset effects listed in each tab are available; you cannot create your own effect.
- Video tabs use a fixed 720p resolution and 5 second duration; there is no duration or resolution control in Effects Studio. Use AI VFX Studio for 10 second or 480p options.
- One source file at a time.
- Uploads are limited by MuAPI to 10 MB for images and 50 MB for videos.
- Generation can time out: about 90 seconds for image tabs and about 180 seconds for video tabs.

chunks.title: Effects Studio — Problems and limits
chunks.text:
- Effect Layers and the per-slider animate toggles are experimental and do not behave like a layer or keyframe editor (see notConfirmed).
- Motion graphics can only be remixed if the service saved the animation code.
Limit details:
- limitation: Fixed clip length and size on video tabs | impact: You always get a 5 second 720p clip. | workaround: Use AI VFX Studio for 10 second clips, or extend and edit the clip in Video Tools or Timeline.
- limitation: Generation timeout | impact: If the effect takes longer than about 90 seconds (images) or 180 seconds (videos) the studio cancels and shows an error. | workaround: Press Retry (the Generate button changes to a retry state after a failure), try a smaller or simpler photo, or try again later.
- limitation: Upload size | impact: Files over the MuAPI limit are rejected with: This file is too large for MuAPI (images 10 MB, videos 50 MB, other 10 MB). | workaround: Compress or trim the file before uploading.
- limitation: The count is 200 presets, not more | impact: The six tabs add up to 200 presets (18 + 17 + 13 + 64 + 47 + 41), which is what the header and Apps card now say (200+). | workaround: Trust the counts shown on the tab buttons.
FAQs:

chunks.title: Effects Studio — Problems and limits
chunks.text:
- question: How many effects does Effects Studio have? | answer: The tabs list 200 presets: Image Effects 18, Nano Banana 17, Kontext Effects 13, Video Effects 64, Motion Controls 47 and Video FX v2 41.
- question: Do I need to write a prompt? | answer: No. The prompt is optional. For Kontext Effects, Video Effects and Motion Controls the studio sends the effect name if you leave it empty. A short prompt usually gives better, more specific results.
- question: Can I choose the video length or resolution? | answer: Not in Effects Studio. Video tabs use 720p and 5 seconds. AI VFX Studio lets you pick 5s or 10s and 480p or 720p.
- question: Can I upload a video? | answer: The upload picker accepts videos (up to 50 MB), but the effect tabs are described as image-to-effect tools and the code sends your upload as the source image. Use a photo for reliable results.
- question: Where do my results go? | answer: Each finished result is saved to your generation history. Press Add to Library to keep it as an asset, Insert into Timeline to edit it, or Download to save a file.
- question: What is Motion graphics mode? | answer: It is a second mode on the same page (toggle at the top, or ?mode=motion in the URL) that generates animated graphics from a text description, with durations from 5 to 30 seconds and aspect ratios 16:9, 9:16 and 1:1. You can remix a previous result.

chunks.title: Effects Studio — Problems and limits
chunks.text: - question: Why does Generate ask for a key or an upgrade? | answer: Generation uses MuAPI, so you need a MuAPI key saved in settings, and your account must have full access.

chunks.title: Effects Studio — Glossary
chunks.text: Glossary: Effect: A named preset (for example Cakeify or Dolly In) that tells the AI what transformation to apply. | Prompt: Optional short text that adds detail to the effect. | Seed: A number that makes a result repeatable. -1 means random. | Guidance: How strictly the AI follows your prompt, from 1 (creative) to 20 (strict). | Steps: How many refinement passes the AI makes. More steps can look better but are slower. | Denoise Strength: How much the output may change from your source. 0 preserves, 1 fully regenerates. | Effect Strength: How strongly the effect is applied, from 0 to 100 percent. | Negative Prompt: Things you want the AI to avoid, such as blurry or watermark. | Kontext: Flux Kontext, an instruction-following image editing model family from Black Forest Labs. | Nano Banana: Google's image model family used for the Nano Banana tab. | Vibe Motion: The name of the Motion graphics mode that generates animated graphics from text. | MuAPI: The service that runs the generation. Your MuAPI key is needed.

Find My Brand (#/find-my-brand). Overview.
Description:
A free brand discovery tool. Paste a business website and SmartVideo reads the page it already has and shows the logo, photos, products and branding found on it, ready to review.
Summary:
Free: paste a website and pull its logo, photos and branding.
About:
Find My Brand (#/find-my-brand, not in the side menu) is a simple page with the label 'SmartVideo - Free Discovery', the title Find My Brand and a button '✦ Find My Brand'. It opens the shared personalization modal in anonymous mode and opens it automatically when you arrive. In the modal you paste your website (placeholder https://yourbusiness.com), or search for a business instead, and the tool surfaces the logos, photos, products and branding already on the page for you to review and arrange. Per the page text, nothing is generated, nothing is charged and nothing is saved.
Best for:
Business owners, freelancers and agencies who want to quickly see and collect the real brand assets on a website, without signing in or paying.
When to use it:
- You want your business logo, photos and products pulled from your own site.
- You are about to make a video or page for a business and want its real assets.
- You want to try the discovery step for free before using other studios.
