chunks.title: Image Studio — Overview
chunks.text:
Image Studio (#/image). Overview.
Description:
Image Studio is where you create AI images from a text description, or transform photos you upload. One prompt bar handles both text-to-image and image-to-image, with a model picker, aspect ratio, resolution and advanced options.
Summary:
Generate images from text or reference photos with 80+ AI models.
About:
Image Studio is a single prompt bar with a model button, an aspect-ratio button, an optional resolution (quality) button and a Generate button. With no reference image it works as text-to-image: you type a description and the chosen model draws it. When you add a reference image (upload, stock photo, sketch or an attachment) the studio switches into image-to-image mode and lists the editing models instead, so you can restyle, edit or combine photos. The model list is large: the code bundles 84 text-to-image models and 92 image-to-image models from makers such as Google (Nano Banana), Black Forest Labs (Flux), ByteDance (Seedream), OpenAI (GPT Image), Midjourney, Ideogram, Alibaba (Qwen, Wan), Hunyuan, Kling, Leonardo, Grok and more. Results appear on a canvas with Regenerate, Download, New and Publish to Social buttons, and every result is added to a History strip on the right side. The studio header reads 'Generate images with 20+ AI models', which is older marketing text; the real list is much longer.
Best for:

chunks.title: Image Studio — Overview
chunks.text:
Beginners and creators who want a fast way to make social posts, product visuals, concept art, thumbnails or illustrations from a sentence, and anyone who wants to try many different image models in one place.
When to use it:
- You want a brand-new image from a written description (text-to-image).
- You want to restyle, transform or combine photos you already have using a prompt (image-to-image).
- You want to compare how different AI models draw the same prompt.
- You want a quick sketch-to-image: draw a rough reference with the Draw button and let a model follow it.
- You want an image to use later as a start frame in Video Studio.
When to use another studio:
- Use Edit Studio (#/edit) when you need a focused photo tool such as Remove Object, Remove Background, Extend Image, Reframe, Change Dress, Face Swap or Add Watermark rather than a free-form prompt.
- Use Upscale Suite (#/upscale) when the picture is already good and you only need more resolution and sharpness.
- Use Video Studio (#/video) when you want the image to move as a video clip.
- Use Character Studio (#/character) when you need the same character to stay consistent across many images.
- Use Commercial Studio (#/commercial) when you want ad-style product and commercial content.
- Use Brand Studio (#/brand) when you need images that follow a saved brand identity.

chunks.title: Image Studio — How to use
chunks.text:
Image Studio (#/image). How to use.
How to use:
1. Open Image Studio from the side menu (Image). 2. Click the model button (it shows 'Nano Banana' by default) and choose a model, or keep the default. 3. Type your idea in the prompt box that says 'Describe the image you want to create'. 4. Optional: click the Aspect Ratio button to choose a shape, and the Resolution button if it appears. 5. Optional: click Advanced for Style Preset, Batch Count and model-specific options, or Tools for Quick Starters and the Prompt Enhancer. 6. Optional: add a reference image with the picker button at the left of the prompt bar (the box then says 'Describe how to transform this image (optional)') and pick an image-to-image model. 7. Click Generate. 8. When the picture appears, click Download to save it, Regenerate to try again, + New to start over, or Publish to Social to share it.
Steps:
- Open Image Studio (#/image).
- Pick a model with the model button.
- Write a prompt (or add a reference image for image-to-image).
- Choose Aspect Ratio and, if shown, Resolution.
- Open Advanced for extra options if you want them.
- Click Generate and wait for the canvas to show your image.
- Download, Regenerate, start a + New image, or Publish to Social.
Getting started:
- Leave the model on the default and type a simple, specific sentence such as 'a red fox in a snowy forest, soft morning light'.

chunks.title: Image Studio — How to use
chunks.text:
- Click Generate. Use Regenerate to see another take.
- Open Tools and try a Quick Starter or the Prompt Enhancer if you are unsure what to write.
- Once you like the result, change the Aspect Ratio to match where you will post it and generate again.
Tips:
- Be specific: subject, setting, lighting, style, camera angle.
- Pick the aspect ratio before you generate; it is part of the request.
- Change one thing at a time (model, prompt, ratio) when comparing results.
- Use Regenerate for another variation with the same settings.
- Use Quick Starters and the Prompt Enhancer if you get stuck.
- For editing photos, also try Edit Studio's focused tools.
Best practices:
- Draft with a fast model, then switch to a higher-quality model for the final image.
- Keep reference images under 10MB and clearly lit.
- Re-check the model button after adding or clearing a reference image.
- Download results you want to keep; History lives in your browser.

chunks.title: Image Studio — Features
chunks.text:
Image Studio (#/image). Features.
Key features:
- One prompt bar for text-to-image and image-to-image (the studio switches mode when you add a reference image).
- Model button with a searchable, provider-grouped picker; the studio remembers your last text-to-image model and aspect ratio between visits.
- Aspect Ratio button with the ratios each model supports (for the default Nano Banana model: 1:1, 3:4, 4:3, 9:16, 16:9, 3:2, 2:3, 5:4, 4:5, 21:9).
- Resolution (quality) button that appears only for models that have resolution or quality options (for example 1k/2k/4k, low/medium/high, or basic/high).
- Advanced panel with a Style Preset list (None, Photorealistic, Anime, Cinematic, Oil Painting, Watercolor, Digital Art, Concept Art, Cyberpunk), Batch Count 1-4, Reference Strength 0-100 (image-to-image only) and model-specific controls.
- Tools panel with Quick Starters and a Prompt Enhancer (enhancement tags, Copy, Use in Generator).
- Reference images: upload, paste, browse Pexels stock photos, attach via the attachment toolbar, or sketch with the Draw button.
- Multi-image image-to-image for models that accept several reference images.
- Special model extras: an Effect menu for models that take a named effect, and a 'Swap face image' slot for face-swap models.

chunks.title: Image Studio — Features
chunks.text:
- Prompt helpers: Prompts (prompt gallery), Recipes, GTM Boost, Monetize and Personalize ({{token}} replacement from a selected contact).
- Thumbnail button to generate a custom thumbnail for the studio.
- Result canvas with Regenerate, Download, New and Publish to Social, plus a History strip with per-image download and delete.
- Pending-job recovery: if you reload while an image is generating, a finished result is recovered with the message 'Recovered a generation that finished while you were away'.
- An examples gallery below the prompt bar, with a 'Show all ... image prompts' button.
Feature details:
- feature: Text-to-image | explanation: Type what you want in the prompt box and click Generate. The default model is Nano Banana (or the last text-to-image model you used). | whyToUse: Fastest way to create something from nothing. | inputRequired: A prompt. Without one you see 'Please enter a prompt to generate an image.' | restrictions: Each model has its own aspect ratios, resolutions and extra options. Your plan and API key must be active.

chunks.title: Image Studio — Features
chunks.text: - feature: Image-to-image (reference images) | explanation: Add a reference image with the picker button at the left of the prompt bar, the Pexels button, the attachment toolbar or the Draw button. The studio switches to image-to-image mode, the placeholder changes to 'Describe how to transform this image (optional)', and the model list switches to image-to-image models. | whyToUse: Restyle a photo, change a scene, apply an effect, combine several photos, or follow a sketch. | inputRequired: At least one reference image. The prompt is optional in this mode. Without an image you see 'Please upload a reference image first.' | restrictions: Images up to 10MB each (the shared upload limit). The number of images depends on the model; the picker shows 'Add up to N images' when a model takes several. When you add an image the studio keeps your model if it already accepts images, otherwise it switches to the matching editing version (for example Nano Banana becomes Nano Banana Edit) or a general editing model such as Seedream 5.0 Edit. You can always change it with the model button.

chunks.title: Image Studio — Features
chunks.text:
- feature: Model picker | explanation: The model button (shows the current model name and provider logo) opens a split-pane picker with a provider sidebar, search and category tabs. Choosing a model resets the aspect ratio to that model's first option and shows or hides the Resolution button and advanced controls to match. | whyToUse: Different models are better at different things: speed, photorealism, text inside images, anime, editing accuracy. | inputRequired: None. | restrictions: If you pick from the All tab while a reference image is loaded, the studio keeps image-to-image mode when that model family has an image-to-image variant.
- feature: Aspect Ratio and Resolution | explanation: The Aspect Ratio button lists the ratios the current model supports. The Resolution button (labelled with a value such as 1k, 2k, 4k, low, medium, high, basic or high) only appears for models that expose a resolution or quality field. | whyToUse: Match the picture to where it will be used (9:16 for stories, 16:9 for banners, 1:1 for posts) and trade quality for speed. | inputRequired: None. | restrictions: Available values differ by model. For example GPT Image 1.5 offers 1:1, 2:3, 3:2 and quality low/medium/high; Nano Banana Pro offers resolution 1k/2k/4k.

chunks.title: Image Studio — Features
chunks.text:
- feature: Advanced panel | explanation: Click Advanced (the label changes to Less) to open a panel built from the selected model's own inputs plus Style Preset, Batch Count and, in image-to-image mode, Reference Strength. Depending on the model it can also include controls such as negative prompt, seed, steps, guidance scale, width and height, or LoRA fields. | whyToUse: Fine control, repeatable results (seed), or excluding unwanted elements. | inputRequired: None; everything is optional. | restrictions: Only the controls the selected model supports are shown. Style Preset is sent as a style field if the model has one, otherwise it is appended to your prompt as ', <style> style'. Batch Count only applies when set above 1.
- feature: Tools panel (Quick Starters and Prompt Enhancer) | explanation: The Tools button opens Quick Tools. Quick Starters are one-click prompt starters. The Prompt Enhancer lets you type a base prompt under 'Enter base prompt...', click Enhancement Tags to add them, then Copy or 'Use in Generator'. | whyToUse: Helps beginners write richer prompts. | inputRequired: None. | restrictions: Opening Tools also opens the Advanced panel.

chunks.title: Image Studio — Features
chunks.text:
- feature: Draw (sketch a reference) | explanation: The Draw button opens a sketch pad ('Sketch a reference for the model to follow'). When you finish you can add the sketch as a reference ('Sketch added as reference') or send it to Video Studio as a start frame. | whyToUse: Control composition by drawing rough shapes. | inputRequired: A drawing (optionally on top of the first reference image). | restrictions: If the upload fails you see 'Sketch upload failed: ...'.
- feature: Effect menu and Swap face image | explanation: Some models take a named effect preset; for those an Effect button appears and lists the options. Face-swap models (for example AI Image Face Swap) show a 'Swap face image' slot where you upload the face to put into your reference photo. | whyToUse: One-click looks and face replacement. | inputRequired: For face swap: both the reference image and the swap face image. Otherwise: 'Please upload a swap face image first.' | restrictions: These controls are hidden for models that do not support them.

chunks.title: Image Studio — Features
chunks.text:
- feature: Result canvas, History and Publish | explanation: After generation the image fills the canvas. Regenerate runs the same settings again, Download saves the file, + New clears the prompt and returns to text-to-image with the first model, and Publish to Social opens the social publishing dialog. The History strip on the right keeps thumbnails you can click to restore, download or delete. | whyToUse: Iterate quickly and share. | inputRequired: A finished generation. | restrictions: History is kept in your browser; it is also saved so the Library (#/library) can show it.
Modes:
- Text-to-image
- Image-to-image (single reference)
- Image-to-image (multiple references)
- Sketch-to-image (via Draw)
Mode details:
- mode: Text-to-image | description: Default mode with no reference image. Uses the text-to-image model list. | useCase: Create from scratch: posters, concept art, product mockups, thumbnails.
- mode: Image-to-image | description: Starts automatically when you add a reference image. Uses the image-to-image model list (editors, restylers, effects, tools such as background remover or face swap). | useCase: Restyle a photo, change the setting, apply an effect or keep a subject while changing the scene. Removing the reference image (clear it in the picker) returns you to text-to-image with the first model.

chunks.title: Image Studio — Features
chunks.text:
- mode: Sketch-to-image | description: Use Draw to make a rough sketch; it is added as a reference image. | useCase: Control layout and composition by drawing.
Models:

chunks.title: Image Studio — Features
chunks.text: The studio bundles 84 text-to-image models and 92 image-to-image models (src/lib/models.js; the public catalog lists the same families). Text-to-image families include: Google (Nano Banana, Nano Banana Pro, Nano Banana 2, 2.1 and Lite, Imagen 4, Imagen 4 Fast, Imagen 4 Ultra), Black Forest Labs (Flux Dev, Flux Schnell, Flux Kontext Pro/Max/Dev, Flux 2 Dev/Flex/Pro, Flux 2 Klein 4B/9B and Turbo, Flux Krea Dev, Flux Pulid, Flux Redux), ByteDance (Seedream v3, v4, v4.5, 5.0, 5.0 Pro and Flash), OpenAI (GPT-4o text-to-image, GPT Image 1.5), Midjourney (v7, v8, Niji), Ideogram (v3, v4), Alibaba (Qwen Image, Qwen Image 2.0 and Pro, Qwen 3, Wan 2.1 / 2.5 / 2.6 / 2.7), Tencent Hunyuan Image 2.1 and 3.0, Kling O1 and O3 Image, Leonardo (Phoenix 1.0, Lucid Origin), Reve, Grok Imagine, Vidu Q2, HiDream I1, SDXL, Krea 2 Turbo, Meta Muse Image, and MuAPI models such as AI Anime Generator, Chroma Image, Perfect Pony XL, Neta Lumina and Z Image. Several have LoRA variants. Image-to-image families include editors (Flux Kontext, Flux 2 edit, Nano Banana edit, Seedream edit, GPT-4o/GPT Image edit, Qwen Image Edit, Wan image edit, Kling edit, Grok, Reve, Midjourney v7 image-to-image and reference models) and specialist tools (AI Image Upscaler, AI Image Face Swap, AI Dress Change, AI Background Remover, AI Product Shot, AI Product Photography, AI Skin Enhancer, AI Color Photo, AI Ghibli Style, AI

chunks.title: Image Studio — Features
chunks.text: Image Extension, AI Object Eraser, Image Effects, Ideogram Character, Topaz and SeedVR2 upscale, Add Image Watermark). Short catalog descriptions: Nano Banana is 'fast and playful'; Flux Dev is 'high-quality with full parameter control'; Flux Schnell is 'ultra-fast ... for rapid prototyping'; Flux 2 Pro is 'professional-grade ... for production use'; Midjourney v7 is 'stylised'; Ideogram v3 has 'render speed and style controls'; Google Imagen 4 is 'high-fidelity'; Hunyuan Image 2.1 is 'cinematic-quality'; Seedream 5.0 is 'high-fidelity'; SDXL gives 'full width and height control'; Flux Pulid is 'identity-preserving from a reference face'; AI Anime Generator is 'specialised anime and illustration'. The file src/lib/modelComparisonData.js has rough relative figures (price and speed are relative units, quality is 1-5) for a few text-to-image models: Nano Banana price 1, speed 3, quality 4; Flux Schnell 2, 2, 4; Flux Dev 3, 4, 5; SDXL 1, 3, 3; Seedream 5.0 4, 5, 5; Midjourney V7 5, 6, 5; Google Imagen 4 4, 5, 5; Ideogram V3 3, 4, 5. These are relative estimates, not real prices or seconds. No real credit costs are stated in the studio code.

chunks.title: Image Studio — Inputs and outputs
chunks.text:
Image Studio (#/image). Inputs and outputs.
Inputs:
- Prompt
- Model
- Aspect Ratio
- Resolution / quality
- Reference image(s)
- Swap face image
- Effect
- Style Preset
- Batch Count
- Reference Strength
- Advanced model options
- Sketch (Draw)
Required inputs:
- Prompt (text-to-image mode)
- At least one reference image (image-to-image mode)
- Swap face image (only for face-swap models)
Optional inputs:
- Prompt (in image-to-image mode)
- Aspect Ratio
- Resolution / quality
- Style Preset
- Batch Count
- Reference Strength
- Negative prompt and other model-specific advanced options
- Effect
- Custom thumbnail
Input details:
- name: Prompt | description: Plain-language description of the image. Placeholder: 'Describe the image you want to create'. In image-to-image mode: 'Describe how to transform this image (optional)'. With several reference images: 'N images selected - describe the transformation (optional)'. | required: true | whenToUse: Always in text-to-image; optional in image-to-image. | restrictions: {{token}} placeholders inserted with Personalize are replaced with the selected contact's details at generation time. No character limit is stated in the code.

chunks.title: Image Studio — Inputs and outputs
chunks.text:
- name: Model | description: The AI model that draws the image. Default is the first text-to-image model, Nano Banana, unless you used another one last time. | required: true | whenToUse: Change it when you need a different look, more speed, better text rendering or an editing model. | restrictions: Text-to-image and image-to-image use different model lists.
- name: Aspect Ratio | description: Shape of the output, such as 1:1, 16:9 or 9:16. | required: false | whenToUse: Before generating, to fit the destination. | restrictions: Only the ratios the current model supports are listed; changing model resets it to that model's first ratio.
- name: Resolution / quality | description: Appears as a button next to Aspect Ratio for models with a resolution or quality field. | required: false | whenToUse: Use higher values for final output, lower for drafts. | restrictions: Hidden when the model has no such option.

chunks.title: Image Studio — Inputs and outputs
chunks.text:
- name: Reference image(s) | description: Photos that the model should transform or follow. Added through the picker (upload, history, paste, URL), the Pexels stock browser, the attachment toolbar or the Draw sketch pad. | required: false | whenToUse: For image-to-image. | restrictions: Images up to 10MB. JPG, PNG, WebP, GIF, SVG, AVIF, HEIC and BMP are accepted by the picker. Number of images depends on the model. Video and audio attachments are not accepted in this studio's attachment toolbar.
- name: Swap face image | description: The face photo to put into the reference image, shown only for face-swap models. | required: true | whenToUse: Only with models such as AI Image Face Swap. | restrictions: Upload failures show 'Upload failed: ...'.
- name: Style Preset | description: None, Photorealistic, Anime, Cinematic, Oil Painting, Watercolor, Digital Art, Concept Art or Cyberpunk, found in the Advanced panel. | required: false | whenToUse: Quick way to steer the look. | restrictions: For models without a style field it simply adds the style words to your prompt.
- name: Batch Count | description: Number from 1 to 4 in the Advanced panel (text-to-image mode only). | required: false | whenToUse: When you want more than one result per run. | restrictions: The studio displays the single URL returned by the API; how extra images are delivered is not confirmed in code.

chunks.title: Image Studio — Inputs and outputs
chunks.text:
- name: Reference Strength | description: Slider 0-100 in steps of 5, default 50, shown only in image-to-image mode. | required: false | whenToUse: Higher keeps closer to the reference; lower gives the model more freedom (typical meaning). | restrictions: It is only sent when it differs from 50, and only some models may use it.
Outputs:
- A generated image shown on the result canvas
- Download of the image file (named like muapi-<id>.jpg)
- Entries in the History strip and in the Library
- Optional Publish to Social hand-off

chunks.title: Image Studio — Problems and limits
chunks.text:
Image Studio (#/image). Problems and limits.
Troubleshooting:
- Message 'Please enter a prompt to generate an image.': you are in text-to-image mode with an empty prompt. Type a description and click Generate again.
- Message 'Please upload a reference image first.': you are in image-to-image mode with no image. Add a reference image, or clear the picker to go back to text-to-image.
- Message 'Please upload a swap face image first.': a face-swap model is selected. Upload the face in the 'Swap face image' slot or pick a different model.
- The Generate button briefly shows 'Error: ...' and returns to 'Generate': the request failed; the first 40 characters of the error are shown. Try again, or switch model or reduce options.
- An upgrade or plan prompt appears when you click Generate: your account does not have full access yet. Upgrade or sign in, then try again.
- A sign-in / API key dialog opens when you click Generate: no API key is stored. Complete the dialog; Generate then runs automatically.
- The result does not look like my original model: adding a reference image switches the studio to an editing model. Open the model button and choose the image-to-image model you want.
- The Resolution button is missing: the selected model has no resolution or quality option. Choose a model that has one (for example Nano Banana Pro or Seedream 5.0).

chunks.title: Image Studio — Problems and limits
chunks.text:
- I reloaded the page while it was generating: when the job finishes you should see 'Recovered a generation that finished while you were away' and the image appears in History.
- 'Attachment upload failed: ...' or 'Sketch upload failed: ...' toasts: the file did not upload. Check the file size (10MB max) and your connection and try again.
- The result looks different from my style choice: Style Preset is added to the prompt for models without a style field, so its effect is subtle. Put the style directly in your prompt.
Troubleshooting steps:
- issue: Generate does nothing or shows an upgrade prompt | steps: Make sure you are signed in.; If an upgrade prompt appears, your account does not have full access; follow the prompt.; Click Generate again after finishing any sign-in or API key dialog.
- issue: Image-to-image gives an unexpected result | steps: Look at the model button to see which editing model is selected.; Pick a different editing or restyling model from the image-to-image list if needed.; Write what to change in the prompt and lower or raise Reference Strength in Advanced.; Click Regenerate.
- issue: Image looks wrong shape or too small | steps: Click the Aspect Ratio button and pick the ratio you need.; If the Resolution button is shown, choose a higher value.; Generate again, then use Upscale Suite if you need more pixels.

chunks.title: Image Studio — Problems and limits
chunks.text:
- issue: Generation takes very long or fails | steps: Wait for the 'Generating...' state to finish; a progress overlay is shown.; If you see 'Error: ...', try a faster model such as Flux Schnell or Nano Banana.; Simplify the prompt and lower Batch Count to 1.
Common problems:
- problem: The image does not match the prompt | whyItHappens: The prompt is vague or the chosen model interprets it differently. | howToFix: Add subject, setting, lighting, style and camera angle; try another model; use Quick Starters or the Prompt Enhancer.
- problem: Model button shows a different model than I picked earlier | whyItHappens: Adding a reference image switches to an image-to-image model (your model's editing version where one exists), and clearing it switches back to the first text-to-image model (Nano Banana). | howToFix: Re-select your model after adding or clearing a reference image.
- problem: Text inside the image is garbled | whyItHappens: Not every model renders text well. | howToFix: Try models described as strong with text such as Ideogram or GPT Image models, and keep the text short and in quotes.
- problem: Cannot find the Resolution option | whyItHappens: Only some models have it. | howToFix: Switch to a model with 1k/2k/4k or quality levels.
Limitations:
- A valid sign-in/plan (entitlement) and an API key are required before generating.

chunks.title: Image Studio — Problems and limits
chunks.text:
- Uploaded reference images are limited to 10MB each.
- The model list is long and every model has different ratios, resolutions and options, so some controls appear or disappear when you change model.
- After you add a reference image the studio switches to an image-to-image model for you (your model's own editing version, or a general editing model); you can change it with the model button.
- The studio shows one result at a time on the canvas.
- No built-in Variations, Upscale, Edit or Favorite buttons on the result canvas; use Upscale Suite and Edit Studio for those.
- Generation can take a while; the Generate button shows 'Generating...' and a progress overlay appears.
Limit details:
- limitation: Reference image too large | impact: The upload is refused or fails. | workaround: Resize or compress the image to under 10MB and upload again.
- limitation: The model changes when you add a reference image | impact: Text-to-image models cannot use a reference, so the studio switches to an image-to-image editing model. The result can look different from what your original model would make. | workaround: Open the model button after adding the image and pick the image-to-image model you prefer.

chunks.title: Image Studio — Problems and limits
chunks.text:
- limitation: Model-specific options | impact: A setting you used with one model (for example Resolution) is not available on another. | workaround: Check the Advanced panel and the Resolution button after every model change.
- limitation: Result actions are minimal | impact: You cannot upscale or inpaint directly from the canvas. | workaround: Download the image and use Upscale Suite (#/upscale) or Edit Studio (#/edit); you can also use the Library (#/library) 'use in studio' flow.
FAQs:
- question: Which model should I start with? | answer: Start with the default, Nano Banana, which the catalog describes as fast and playful. For production-style quality try models like Flux 2 Pro, Seedream 5.0 or Google Imagen 4; for very quick drafts try Flux Schnell.
- question: How do I turn a photo into something else? | answer: Add it with the picker button, then check the model button: the studio switches to an image-to-image model for you (your model's editing version, or a general editing model). Describe the change in the prompt.
- question: Does Image Studio remember my settings? | answer: It remembers your last text-to-image model and aspect ratio in your browser. Reference images and prompts are not remembered; + New clears them.

chunks.title: Image Studio — Problems and limits
chunks.text:
- question: Where are my images saved? | answer: Each result is added to the History strip on the right and saved for the Library. Use Download to save a file to your device.
- question: What file size can I upload as a reference? | answer: Up to 10MB per image.
- question: Can I use several reference images? | answer: Yes, with models that accept more than one. The picker then says 'Add up to N images', and the prompt placeholder shows how many are selected.
- question: Do I have to type a prompt in image-to-image mode? | answer: No, it is optional there, but a short instruction usually gives better control. In text-to-image mode a prompt is required.
- question: What are the Text to Image and Image to Image pages? | answer: #/text-to-image and #/image-to-image are information pages that list example models and prompts. Their buttons ('Start Creating Free', 'Get Started Free', 'Try this') send you to Image Studio and can pre-fill a prompt. They do not pre-select a model.
- question: How do I make my image bigger or sharper? | answer: Use Upscale Suite (#/upscale), or Edit Studio's Upscale tool (#/edit).

chunks.title: Image Studio — Workflows and use cases
chunks.text:
Image Studio (#/image). Workflows and use cases.
Example workflows:
- title: Make a social post image from text | steps: Open #/image and keep the default model.; Type: 'flat-lay of a coffee cup and notebook on a wooden desk, soft window light, minimal'.; Click the Aspect Ratio button and choose 4:5 (or 1:1).; Click Generate.; If you like it, click Download; otherwise click Regenerate.; Optionally click Publish to Social.
- title: Restyle your own photo | steps: Click the picker button at the left of the prompt bar and upload a photo (10MB max).; Check the model button: the studio picks an editing model for you; change it if you want a different one.; Type 'turn this into a watercolor painting, soft pastel colors'.; Open Advanced and adjust Reference Strength if needed.; Click Generate, then Download.
- title: Sketch to finished image | steps: Click Draw and sketch the layout (for example a horizon, a tree and a house).; Finish the sketch so it is added as a reference ('Sketch added as reference').; Pick an image-to-image model, describe the scene in the prompt, and click Generate.
- title: Build an image prompt with the Prompt Enhancer | steps: Click Tools.; In 'Enter base prompt...' type a basic idea.; Click a few Enhancement Tags.; Click 'Use in Generator', then Generate.
Use cases:

chunks.title: Image Studio — Workflows and use cases
chunks.text:
- title: Marketing and social visuals | description: Create eye-catching posts, banners and story images from a sentence. | steps: Write the prompt; Choose the ratio for the platform; Generate; Download or Publish to Social | expectedOutput: A ready-to-post image in your chosen shape.
- title: Concept art and illustration | description: Explore characters, scenes and moods quickly across different models. | steps: Pick an art-focused model; Set Style Preset in Advanced; Generate several times with Regenerate | expectedOutput: A set of concept images in History to compare.
- title: Photo transformation | description: Change the style or setting of an existing photo. | steps: Upload the photo; Choose an image-to-image model; Describe the change; Generate | expectedOutput: A transformed version of your photo.
Related studios:
- studio: edit | relationship: Focused photo-editing tools | whenToMove: When you want Remove Object, Remove Background, Extend Image, Reframe, Face Swap, Change Dress or similar. | why: Each tool has the right inputs (mask painting, second image) built in.
- studio: upscale | relationship: Increase resolution | whenToMove: When the image content is right but it needs more pixels. | why: It runs dedicated upscaling models.

chunks.title: Image Studio — Workflows and use cases
chunks.text:
- studio: video | relationship: Animate the image | whenToMove: When you want motion. The Draw button can send a sketch to Video Studio as a start frame. | why: Video Studio turns images and prompts into clips.
- studio: character | relationship: Consistent characters | whenToMove: When you need the same person across many images. | why: Character Studio is built for that.
- studio: library | relationship: Saved results | whenToMove: When you want to find past generations. | why: Generations are saved there.

chunks.title: Image Studio — Glossary
chunks.text: Glossary: Prompt: The text you write to tell the AI what to draw. | Text-to-image: Making an image from words only. | Image-to-image: Making a new image from a reference image, usually with a prompt. | Aspect ratio: The width-to-height shape of the picture, such as 16:9. | Resolution: How many pixels the image has; some models offer 1k, 2k or 4k. | Negative prompt: Words describing what you do not want in the image (available on models that support it). | Seed: A number that makes a result repeatable on models that support it. | Reference Strength: How closely image-to-image output follows your reference. | LoRA: A small add-on that gives a model a particular style or subject (offered by some models). | History: The thumbnail strip of your past results in this studio.

chunks.title: AI Influencer — Overview
chunks.text:
AI Influencer (#/influencer). Overview.
Description:
AI Influencer Studio lets you design a consistent-looking AI character by picking visual attributes (face, body, style), a style preset and an output format, then generates a portrait from your reference photo. It is reachable at #/influencer but is not shown in the side menu.
Summary:
Design a consistent AI influencer and their content
About:
AI Influencer Studio (route #/influencer; the page title is 'AI Influencer Studio' and the app's route list calls it 'AI Influencer' in the Image category) is an image-to-image character builder. You upload a reference photo (or video, or a Pexels stock photo), then build the character with a 'Visual Attributes' panel split into Face, Body and Style tabs, each with picture-card options (character type, gender, ethnicity/origin, eye color and type, mouth, ears, horns, skin conditions, skin material and pattern, body type, arms and legs, hair, accessories and rendering style). Shuffle randomises all attributes and Reset clears them. You also choose one of 20 Style Presets and one of four Output Formats, optionally add instructions, and click Generate Content. Results appear in a 3:4 preview with a Save button and a History strip of your last 50 images. It makes still images only: there is no voice, script or video in this studio.
Best for:

chunks.title: AI Influencer — Overview
chunks.text:
Creators and brands who want to invent a stylised virtual influencer or character look (realistic, anime, cartoon or 2D) and produce social-ready portraits, and who like building a character from picture options rather than writing long prompts.
When to use it:
- You want to design a character by choosing options (gender, eye color, hair, body type, rendering style) instead of writing a prompt.
- You want a style preset such as Quiet luxury, Y2K Posters or Tokyo Streetstyle on your portrait.
- You want output sized for Instagram Post, Story / Reel, YouTube Thumb or Pinterest Pin.
- You want to randomise ideas quickly with Shuffle.
- You want a running history of the characters you generated.
When to use another studio:
- Use Character Studio (#/character) when you must keep a real person's face recognisable; it has face-preserving models (Flux PuLID, Subject Reference) and expression presets.
- Use Image Studio (#/image) for general text-to-image generation with many models.
- Use Avatar Studio (#/avatar) or Lip Sync Studio (#/lipsync) to make your influencer talk.
- Use Audio Studio (#/audio) for voices and music.
- Use Video Studio (#/video), Animate Studio (#/animate) or Cinema Studio (#/cinema) for moving content.
- Use Product Shot Studio (#/commercial) when the product, not the person, is the subject.

chunks.title: AI Influencer — How to use
chunks.text:
AI Influencer (#/influencer). How to use.
How to use:
1. Go to #/influencer (it is not in the side menu). 2. Under Your Photo, click the upload button and add a reference photo (or use the Pexels button). 3. In Visual Attributes, switch between the Face, Body and Style tabs and click the picture cards you want; click Shuffle for random choices or Reset to clear them. 4. Under Style Preset pick a look such as Realistic or Quiet luxury. 5. Under Output Format pick Instagram Post (1:1), Story / Reel (9:16), YouTube Thumb (16:9) or Pinterest Pin (2:3). 6. Optionally open Advanced to set Style Intensity or turn on the seed lock. 7. Optionally type extra instructions in 'Additional instructions (optional)'. 8. Click Generate Content (or the Generate button above the preview). 9. Click Save to download, or use the History strip to review past results.
Steps:
- Open #/influencer.
- Upload a reference photo.
- Pick attributes in Face, Body and Style tabs (or Shuffle/Reset).
- Choose a Style Preset and Output Format.
- Optionally adjust Style Intensity and Seed lock under Advanced.
- Add optional instructions.
- Click Generate Content and Save the result.
Getting started:
- Upload a sharp photo of the person or look you want to base the character on.
- Click Reset if you do not want any attribute wording sent, otherwise review the default selections.

chunks.title: AI Influencer — How to use
chunks.text:
- Sign in with an active plan and connect your API key.
Tips:
- Click Reset first if you want full control.
- Keep choices consistent with each other.
- Use Shuffle for inspiration, then fine-tune.
- Use the same reference photo and preset for a consistent series.
Best practices:
- Save images you like; history is browser-only.
- Use only photos you have the right to use.
- Check generated images before publishing as a real person's likeness.

chunks.title: AI Influencer — Features
chunks.text:
AI Influencer (#/influencer). Features.
Key features:
- Reference upload for a photo or video, plus a Pexels stock-photo button.
- Visual Attributes with Face, Body and Style tabs and about 20 sub-categories of picture options.
- Shuffle (randomise) and Reset (clear) buttons.
- 20 Style Presets, default Realistic.
- 4 Output Formats: Instagram Post (1:1), Story / Reel (9:16), YouTube Thumb (16:9), Pinterest Pin (2:3), plus quick ratio buttons 3:4, 1:1, 9:16, 16:9 above the preview.
- Style Intensity slider (0-100%, default 70%) and Seed lock toggle in the Advanced panel.
- Optional 'Additional instructions' text box.
- Model selector listing the app's image-to-image models.
- History strip of up to 50 generated characters with download and delete.
- Thumbnail, Personalize, GTM Boost, Recipes, Monetize and Prompts helpers.
- Example Gallery at the bottom.
Feature details:
- feature: Your Photo (reference upload) | explanation: An upload button with hint 'Upload reference photo or video' and a Pexels button (tooltip 'Browse stock photos from Pexels'; after picking, the hint reads 'Media from Pexels'). | whyToUse: The generated character is built from this image. | inputRequired: Required. Without it: toast 'Upload a photo first'. | restrictions: Shared upload limits: images 10MB, videos 50MB.

chunks.title: AI Influencer — Features
chunks.text:
- feature: Visual Attributes (Face / Body / Style tabs) | explanation: Picture cards you click to choose one option per sub-category. Face: Character Type (Human, Elf, Alien, Amphibian, Reptile, Mantis, Bee, Octopus, Crocodile, Iguana, Lizard, Beetle, Ant), Gender, Ethnicity / Origin, Eye Color, Eye Type, Eye Features, Mouth & Teeth, Ears, Horns, Skin Conditions. Body: Face Skin Material, Skin Pattern, Body Type, Left/Right Arm, Left/Right Leg. Style: Hair / Head Growth, Accessories & Markings, Rendering Style (Hyper-Realistic, Anime, Cartoon, 2D Illustration). A tag bar below shows the chosen options ('show more' / 'hide'). | whyToUse: Build a detailed character without writing a prompt. | inputRequired: Optional, but every sub-category starts with its first option selected (for example Human, Female, African, Blue eyes, Normal arms and legs, Bald), and those are sent to the model unless you change or Reset them. | restrictions: One option per sub-category. Some options (for example 'no left arm', 'no ears') are literal descriptions.
- feature: Shuffle and Reset | explanation: Shuffle picks a random option in every sub-category. Reset clears every choice so no attribute wording is sent. | whyToUse: Shuffle for ideas; Reset to rely on your photo and text only. | inputRequired: None. | restrictions: Shuffle changes all sub-categories at once.

chunks.title: AI Influencer — Features
chunks.text:
- feature: Style Preset | explanation: Twenty chips: Realistic, DigitalCam, Quiet luxury, FashionShow, 90s Grain, Sunset beach, Amalfi Summer, Bimbocore, Vintage PhotoBooth, Gorpcore, Indie sleaze, Fairycore, Avant-garde, Y2K Posters, Grunge, Coquette core, Tokyo Streetstyle, 2049, Night rider, Glazed doll skin makeup. The preset name is added to the prompt as 'Style preset: <name>'. | whyToUse: One-click overall look. | inputRequired: Defaults to Realistic. | restrictions: Choose one.
- feature: Output Format | explanation: Instagram Post (1:1), Story / Reel (9:16), YouTube Thumb (16:9), Pinterest Pin (2:3). Quick ratio buttons 3:4, 1:1, 9:16 and 16:9 above the preview change the aspect ratio sent. | whyToUse: Match the platform. | inputRequired: Defaults to Instagram Post (1:1). | restrictions: The 3:4 button is the only way to choose 3:4; 2:3 comes from the Pinterest Pin preset.
- feature: Style Intensity and Seed lock (Advanced) | explanation: Style Intensity is a 0-100% slider in steps of 5, default 70%, sent as 0.0-1.0. Seed lock is a switch ('Toggle seed lock'); when on, a fixed random number shown as '#<number>' is sent as the seed. | whyToUse: Intensity to strengthen or soften the style; seed lock to repeat a look. | inputRequired: Optional. | restrictions: Whether the chosen model honours these settings depends on the model; see notConfirmed.

chunks.title: AI Influencer — Features
chunks.text:
- feature: Additional instructions | explanation: Text box with placeholder 'Additional instructions (optional)'. If empty, 'Fashion editorial photo, professional quality' is used. | whyToUse: Add pose, outfit, setting or mood. | inputRequired: Optional. | restrictions: Contact tokens are replaced if a contact profile is selected (Personalize).
- feature: History strip | explanation: A side strip labelled 'Generated - N characters' showing up to 50 thumbnails. Hover for Download and Delete; clicking a thumbnail shows it with Download and Generate Again. | whyToUse: Compare and re-download earlier results. | inputRequired: None. | restrictions: Stored in your browser only (key influencer_history).
- feature: Result preview and Save | explanation: A 3:4 preview area shows the newest image with a Save button that downloads it. Generate and Generate Content buttons both start a run. | whyToUse: See and keep results. | inputRequired: None. | restrictions: The preview shows a placeholder until the first result.
Modes:
- Image-to-image character portrait
Mode details:
- mode: Image-to-image | description: Your photo plus a prompt built from attributes, style preset and instructions goes to the selected model. | useCase: Creating a stylised influencer or character portrait.
Models:

chunks.title: AI Influencer — Features
chunks.text: The studio starts with an internal model id 'higgsfield-soul-image-to-image' labelled 'Influencer Image' and also shows the app's full list of image-to-image models in a model selector. That default id does not appear in the model catalog, descriptions or comparison files read, so its provider, price, speed and quality cannot be stated. The built prompt asks for an 'Ultra-realistic professional portrait photograph of an AI influencer character, 8k resolution, cinematic lighting, sharp detail' followed by your chosen attributes and style preset; choosing Anime, Cartoon or 2D Illustration under Rendering Style adds that wording. No per-model prices or rankings are given in the files read.

chunks.title: AI Influencer — Problems and limits
chunks.text:
AI Influencer (#/influencer). Problems and limits.
Troubleshooting:
- Toast 'Upload a photo first': add a reference photo before clicking Generate Content.
- An upgrade prompt appears: your account needs full access; follow the prompt.
- A key dialog appears: connect your API key, then click Generate again.
- Toast 'Error: ...': read the message and retry; try another model from the model selector if it persists.
- The character has unwanted features: those come from default attribute picks; click Reset and select only what you want.
- Output has the wrong shape: choose another Output Format or the ratio buttons (3:4, 1:1, 9:16, 16:9) above the preview.
- I cannot find the studio in the menu: open #/influencer directly.
- History is empty: it only records images generated on this browser.
- Style looks weak: raise Style Intensity under Advanced, or pick a different Style Preset.
Troubleshooting steps:
- issue: Generate Content does nothing | steps: Check that a photo is uploaded.; Complete any upgrade/key dialog.; Click Generate Content again.
- issue: The result ignores my attributes | steps: Check the tag bar shows your choices.; Avoid contradictory options (for example Human character type with Tentacles hair).; Shorten extra instructions.
- issue: Same look every time or too random | steps: Turn Seed lock on for repeatability.; Turn it off for variety.
Common problems:

chunks.title: AI Influencer — Problems and limits
chunks.text:
- problem: Unexpected eyes, hair or skin | whyItHappens: Default first options are sent. | howToFix: Use Reset.
- problem: Rendering style not what I wanted | whyItHappens: Rendering Style default is Hyper-Realistic. | howToFix: Select Anime, Cartoon or 2D Illustration on the Style tab.
- problem: Image cropped | whyItHappens: Chosen ratio differs from the preview 3:4 box. | howToFix: Download the image; the file uses your chosen ratio.
Limitations:
- Image only: no voice, script, camera or video.
- One reference image only.
- Attribute defaults are applied automatically unless you click Reset.
- Seed and intensity may not be honoured by every model.
- History is stored in this browser only.
- No batch generation; one image per click.
- Not shown in the side menu.
Limit details:
- limitation: Default attributes are always sent | impact: Your result may include features you did not choose (for example 'female', 'african heritage', 'striking blue eyes'). | workaround: Click Reset, then choose only the attributes you want.
- limitation: No voice or video | impact: Cannot make a talking influencer here. | workaround: Download and use Avatar, Lip Sync, Audio or Video studios.
- limitation: Browser-only history | impact: History disappears if you clear site data. | workaround: Click Save on images you want to keep.
FAQs:

chunks.title: AI Influencer — Problems and limits
chunks.text:
- question: Is AI Influencer Studio the same as Character Studio? | answer: No. Character Studio focuses on keeping a real face with two face-preserving models and expression presets. AI Influencer Studio focuses on building a stylised character from attribute options and style presets.
- question: Why is it not in the side menu? | answer: It is reachable at #/influencer; the menu does not list it.
- question: Can it clone a voice or make videos? | answer: No. This studio only generates images.
- question: How many images does History keep? | answer: Up to 50, stored in your browser.
- question: What does Shuffle do? | answer: Randomly selects an option in every attribute group.
- question: What does Reset do? | answer: Clears all attribute choices.
- question: What are the default settings? | answer: Style Preset Realistic, Instagram Post (1:1), Style Intensity 70%, Seed lock off.
- question: Does the seed lock guarantee identical results? | answer: No. It sends a fixed seed, but whether a model repeats results depends on the model.

chunks.title: Lead Finder — Overview
chunks.text:
Lead Finder (#/leadfinder). Overview.
Description:
Find local businesses that may need video: search a niche and location, review scored prospects, pull their logos and photos from their website, and save leads with a pipeline stage.
Summary:
Search local businesses by niche and location and save them as leads.
About:
Lead Finder (#/leadfinder, not listed in the side menu) is an entry page for the Personalization and Lead Finder modal. Its hero reads 'Find local businesses that need video' and has two buttons: Find businesses (opens the modal at the Find business step) and Find My Brand (free, pastes a website to pull its branding). Below is a Saved leads list showing each lead's name, category and location, address, website, phone, a star if starred, and a pipeline stage badge. The search uses OpenStreetMap by business type and location, and saving leads needs you to be signed in.
Best for:
Agencies and freelancers prospecting local businesses (roofers, salons, restaurants, and so on) who want a list of leads and a quick way to make a personalized demo for each.
When to use it:
- You need a list of local businesses in a niche and area.
- You want to save prospects and track them through a sales pipeline.
- You want to pull a prospect's real logo and photos from their website before making a demo video.
- You want to review saved leads in one place.
When to use another studio:

chunks.title: Lead Finder — Overview
chunks.text:
- Use Find My Brand (#/find-my-brand) when you already know the website and only want its branding, free and without signing in.
- Use Personalizer (#/personalizer) to build a personalized page for a lead.
- Use Video (#/video) or Viral (#/viral) to generate the demo video itself.
- Use Timeline Editor (#/timeline) to edit a demo video.

chunks.title: Lead Finder — How to use
chunks.text:
Lead Finder (#/leadfinder). How to use.
How to use:
1. Open Lead Finder at #/leadfinder. 2. Click Find businesses. 3. Under Find Local Business, pick a Business Type / Niche. 4. Type a Location, for example Tampa, Florida. 5. Pick a Search Radius (5 mi, 10 mi, 15 mi, 25 mi or 50 mi). 6. Click Find Businesses and review the Search Results. 7. Select a business to see its summary and use Find My Brand to pull its logo and photos from its website. 8. Save the lead (sign in if asked) and set the Lead stage. 9. Close the modal and click Refresh in Saved leads to see it listed.
Steps:
- Click Find businesses.
- Choose niche, location and radius.
- Click Find Businesses and review results.
- Select a business and run Find My Brand on its website.
- Save the lead and set its stage.
- Click Refresh on the Saved leads list.
Getting started:
- Sign in first so you can save leads.
- Start with a 10 mi radius in a city you know and the General Business niche if unsure.
- Use the Notes field to remember why a lead is interesting.
Tips:
- Search a few niches rather than one broad one.
- Star leads you want to return to.
- Update stages as you go so the list stays useful.
Best practices:
- Review each business website before pitching.
- Record context in Notes.
- Keep stage values current.

- problem: Stage did not change | whyItHappens: Not signed in, or the update failed. | howToFix: Sign in and set the Lead stage again.

- Saving and viewing leads requires sign in.

chunks.title: Library — Overview
chunks.text:
Library (#/library). Overview.
Description:
Library is where everything you generate in any studio is saved automatically, plus your uploaded files. You can filter, search, preview, download, copy prompts, save to Content, delete, or send an upload to a studio.
Summary:
Everything you generated and uploaded, in one place.
About:
Library (route #/library) is headed "Library" with the line "Everything you have generated and uploaded, in one place". The empty state says "Everything you create in any studio is saved here automatically". It shows a grid of your images, videos and audio clips with filter buttons (All, Images, Videos, Audio, Uploads) that show counts such as "Images · 4", a sort menu (Newest first, Oldest first) and a search box ("Search by prompt or model..."). History is loaded from cloud storage (Supabase) and from this browser, merged without duplicates; when a MuAPI key is saved, MuAPI's own generation history is also folded in on a best-effort basis. The Uploads view is a separate permanent Asset Library of files you uploaded in studios. The old "pexels-media" page now redirects to Library.
Best for:
Finding, previewing, downloading and reusing anything you have made or uploaded.
When to use it:
- You generated something and want to find or download it.
- You want to copy the prompt of a past result.

chunks.title: Library — Overview
chunks.text:
- You want to reuse an uploaded file in another studio without uploading again.
- You want to keep a favourite by saving it to Content.
When to use another studio:
- To keep a curated set of favourites, uploads, PDFs and stock media, use Content (#/content-library).
- To edit video on a timeline, use Timeline Editor (#/timeline).

chunks.title: Library — How to use
chunks.text:
Library (#/library). How to use.
How to use:
1. Open Library from the left side menu (My Work group). 2. Pick a filter: All, Images, Videos, Audio or Uploads. 3. Optionally sort or search. 4. Hover an item and use Download, Copy prompt, Save or Delete, or click it to preview. 5. In Uploads, hover a file and press "Use in studio" and pick a studio.
Steps:
- Open Library from the left side menu.
- Choose All, Images, Videos, Audio or Uploads.
- Search or change the sort order if needed.
- Hover an item for Download, Copy prompt, Save, Delete; or click it to preview.
- In Uploads choose "Use in studio" to reuse a file.
Getting started:
- Generate something in any studio; it appears in Library automatically.
- Use Save on favourites so they also show in Content.
Tips:
- Search by model name to compare results from the same model.
- Use Copy prompt to rebuild a good result.
- Save the best results to Content.
Best practices:
- Download important results soon after generating.
- Save keepers to Content so you can find them quickly.

- Sort: Newest first / Oldest first.

Feature details:
- feature: Filters and counts | explanation: Buttons labelled All, Images, Videos, Audio and Uploads. The first four show a count after loading, for example "Videos · 3". Uploads shows your permanent uploaded files instead of generations. | whyToUse: Narrow a long history. | inputRequired: None | restrictions: Counts cover generations only (not Uploads).
- feature: Search and sort | explanation: Type in "Search by prompt or model..." to match the prompt text, model name or template name. The sort menu offers "Newest first" and "Oldest first". | whyToUse: Find an item by what you typed or which model made it. | inputRequired: Any text | restrictions: Search matches text metadata only, not image content.

This cannot be undone."). | whyToUse: Act without opening the item. | inputRequired: None | restrictions: Delete removes it from your Library history; MuAPI history will not bring it back.

If the chosen studio is already open it receives the file; otherwise the file is queued and the studio opens. | whyToUse: Reuse a reference image or video without re-uploading. | inputRequired: None | restrictions: Only those eight studios appear in the chooser.

chunks.title: Library — Problems and limits
chunks.text:
Library (#/library). Problems and limits.
Troubleshooting:
- No generations yet: nothing has been generated in this browser/account; create something in a studio first.
- Nothing matches this filter: clear the search or choose All.
- An item is missing: it may have been deleted, or generated in another browser before it was synced; check the cloud/MuAPI history by saving your MuAPI key.
- Uploads shows "No uploaded assets yet": upload a file inside a studio first.
- Download opens a new tab instead of saving: right-click the file and choose Save.
Troubleshooting steps:
- issue: My latest generation is not in Library | steps: Wait a few seconds and reopen Library.; Switch the filter to All.; Clear the search box.; Confirm your MuAPI key is saved in Settings.
Common problems:
- problem: Deleted something by mistake | whyItHappens: Delete asks once, then removes it from your Library history. | howToFix: It cannot be undone from Library; regenerate it using the prompt if you copied it.
Limitations:
- Delete cannot be undone.
- The Uploads view needs a working asset service and key context; if it cannot load, it shows an empty list.
- Audio items cannot be opened in the detail view.
Limit details:
- limitation: Library does not edit media | impact: You cannot trim or restyle inside Library. | workaround: Send an upload to a studio with Use in studio, or open the Timeline Editor.

chunks.title: Lip Sync Studio — Overview
chunks.text:
Lip Sync Studio (#/lipsync). Overview.
Description:
Lip Sync Studio makes a still portrait talk, or re-syncs the mouth of an existing video, to an audio file you upload. You pick a model, upload your media and audio, and click Generate.
Summary:
Make a portrait talk or re-sync any video to new audio.
About:
Lip Sync Studio has two input modes. In Portrait Image mode you upload one clear face photo plus an audio file, and the studio produces a talking video of that person. In Video mode you upload an existing video plus new audio, and the studio changes the lip movement so it matches the new audio (useful for dubbing or replacing a voice-over). You choose from a list of lip sync and talking-avatar models, optionally set a resolution, optionally type a prompt for talking style, then click Generate. Finished videos play in a result canvas where you can download, regenerate, publish to social, or add AI captions, and a History panel keeps your recent results.
Best for:
Beginners and creators who want a talking-head video from a photo and a voice recording, or who want to dub or replace the speech in a short video clip without re-filming.
When to use it:
- You have a portrait photo and an audio recording (voice-over, narration, song) and want the person in the photo to appear to speak it.

chunks.title: Lip Sync Studio — Overview
chunks.text:
- You have a video of someone talking and want the mouth movement to match new or translated audio.
- You want to turn text-to-speech or a cloned voice from Audio Studio into a talking face video.
- You want a quick talking-head clip for a social post, explainer, or personalized message.
When to use another studio:
- Use Avatar Studio (#/avatar) when you want the avatar-style lip sync and talking models in a simpler single-form layout with a Source Video/Image upload and optional Native Audio toggle.
- Use Audio Studio (#/audio) when you first need to create the speech, music, or sound effects that will drive the lip sync.
- Use Video Studio (#/video) when you want to generate a brand new video from a text prompt rather than animate a photo to speak.
- Use Video Tools (#/videotools) for other video-to-video utilities that are not lip sync.
- Use Character Studio (#/character) when you first need a consistent character image to use as your portrait.

chunks.title: Lip Sync Studio — How to use
chunks.text:
Lip Sync Studio (#/lipsync). How to use.
How to use:
1. Open Lip Sync Studio from the side menu (#/lipsync). 2. Next to 'Input:' choose '🖼 Portrait Image' (photo + audio) or '🎬 Video' (existing video + audio). 3. Upload your media: click the portrait image button (Upload portrait image) or the video button (Upload source video), or browse Pexels stock media. 4. Upload an audio file with the audio button (Upload audio file). The status labels change from 'No image'/'No video'/'No audio' to a check mark with the file name. 5. Click the model button and pick a model from the 'Portrait Image' or 'Video' group. 6. If a resolution button is shown, choose a resolution. 7. Optionally type a prompt in 'Optional: describe the talking style or motion...' (only if the model shows the box). 8. Click 'Generate ✨' and wait while the button shows 'Generating...'. 9. When the video appears, press '↓ Download', '↻ Regenerate', 'Publish to Social' or '💬 Add AI Captions'. Use '+ New' to start again.
Steps:
- Choose the input mode: Portrait Image or Video.
- Upload a portrait image (Portrait Image mode) or a source video (Video mode).
- Upload the audio file that should drive the lips.
- Pick a model from the model list.
- Pick a resolution if the studio shows one.
- Optionally add a prompt describing the talking style.
- Click Generate and wait for the result.

chunks.title: Lip Sync Studio — How to use
chunks.text:
- Download, regenerate, publish or caption the result.
Getting started:
- Stay in Portrait Image mode with the default model for your first test.
- Use a clear, front-facing photo with the face well lit.
- Use a short audio clip (the built-in tips suggest keeping audio under 60 seconds).
- Leave the resolution on its default, click Generate, and judge the result before trying other models.
Tips:
- Clear, front-facing portraits work best.
- Keep audio files under 60 seconds for best results.
- Higher resolution models take longer but produce better quality.
- Use clean audio with little background noise.
- Test with a short clip before making a long one.
Best practices:
- Test your photo and audio at the default resolution first, then raise the resolution for the final render.
- Keep faces uncovered and large in frame.
- Download finished videos right away.
- Use Audio Studio to produce consistent voice tracks.

chunks.title: Lip Sync Studio — Features
chunks.text:
Lip Sync Studio (#/lipsync). Features.
Key features:
- Two input modes: Portrait Image (photo + audio -> talking video) and Video (existing video + audio -> re-synced video).
- A model picker that lists image-mode models and video-mode models in separate groups.
- Resolution picker (for models that offer one): 480p, 720p, and on some models 1080p.
- Optional prompt box: 'Optional: describe the talking style or motion...' (only shown for models that accept a prompt).
- Upload buttons for portrait image, source video and audio, with progress and a READY state; drag and drop is supported.
- Pexels stock photo and stock video browsers for portrait or video sources.
- Result canvas with Download, Regenerate, New, Publish to Social, and Add AI Captions buttons.
- History panel of recent generations (stored in your browser, up to 30 entries).
- Resumes generations that were still running if you refresh the page (banner: 'Resuming N pending generation(s)...').
- Extra tools menu with GTM Boost, Recipes, Monetize, Prompts; a Thumbnail button; and a Personalize trigger.
Feature details:

chunks.title: Lip Sync Studio — Features
chunks.text:
- feature: Portrait Image mode | explanation: Turns one face photo into a talking video driven by your audio file. This is the default mode when you open the studio. | whyToUse: You only have a photo (not a video) of the person or character. | inputRequired: A portrait image and an audio file. | restrictions: Image uploads are limited to 10MB and audio uploads to 10MB under the app's shared MuAPI upload limits (see notConfirmed for the exact audio limit).
- feature: Video mode | explanation: Takes an existing video and your audio, and changes the lip movement to match the audio. | whyToUse: Dubbing, replacing a voice-over, or fixing the mouth movement after changing the speech. | inputRequired: A source video and an audio file. | restrictions: Video uploads are limited to 50MB under the shared upload limits.
- feature: Model selector | explanation: Click the model button to open a list. The list is grouped into 'Portrait Image' and 'Video' models. Switching mode automatically selects the first model of that mode. | whyToUse: Different models differ in quality, speed and which extra options they offer. | inputRequired: None. | restrictions: You can only use models that belong to the current mode. Switch between Portrait Image and Video to see the other group.

chunks.title: Lip Sync Studio — Features
chunks.text:
- feature: Resolution picker | explanation: A resolution button appears only for models that offer a resolution choice. Infinite Talk, Wan 2.2 and Infinite Talk V2V offer 480p and 720p (default 480p). LTX 2.3 and LTX 2 19B offer 480p, 720p and 1080p (default 720p). | whyToUse: Higher resolution looks sharper but is expected to take longer. | inputRequired: None (a default is chosen for you). | restrictions: Hidden for models with no resolution option such as Sync Lipsync, LatentSync, Creatify and Veed.
- feature: Optional prompt | explanation: A text box with the placeholder 'Optional: describe the talking style or motion...'. If filled, it is sent only to models that accept a prompt. | whyToUse: To hint at the expression or style of the talking performance. | inputRequired: None. | restrictions: The box is hidden for models that do not support prompts (for example Sync Lipsync, LatentSync, Creatify, Veed).
- feature: Pending job recovery and History | explanation: Each submitted job is remembered. If you reload the page while a job is running, the studio resumes waiting for it and adds it to History when ready. History is kept in your browser, newest first. | whyToUse: Long generations do not get lost if you close or refresh the tab. | inputRequired: None. | restrictions: History keeps up to 30 entries and lives in this browser only.

chunks.title: Lip Sync Studio — Features
chunks.text:
- feature: Result actions | explanation: After a video is ready you see it in a canvas with '+ New', '↻ Regenerate', '↓ Download', 'Publish to Social' and '💬 Add AI Captions'. | whyToUse: To save, repeat, share or caption the result. | inputRequired: A finished generation. | restrictions: Regenerate reuses the current inputs and clicks Generate again.
Modes:
- Portrait Image (image + audio -> video)
- Video (video + audio -> video)
Mode details:
- mode: Portrait Image | description: Animates one still face photo so it speaks your audio. | useCase: Talking-head intros, avatars, explainers from a single photo.
- mode: Video | description: Re-syncs the mouth in an existing video to new audio. | useCase: Dubbing, translating, replacing narration.
Models:

chunks.title: Lip Sync Studio — Features
chunks.text: Models are read from the studio's model list in src/lib/models.js. Portrait Image group (first is the default, Infinite Talk): Infinite Talk, Wan 2.2 Speech to Video, LTX 2.3 Lipsync, LTX 2 19B Lipsync (these four take a prompt; Infinite Talk and Wan offer 480p/720p, the two LTX models offer 480p/720p/1080p with 720p default), Kling v1 Avatar Standard, Kling v1 Avatar Pro, Kling v2 Avatar Standard, Kling v2 Avatar Pro, and Omnihuman 1 5 (a separate output resolution of 720 or 1080 is defined in its inputs, but the studio resolution button only reads a field named 'resolution', so it may not appear). Video group (first is the default, Sync Lipsync): Sync Lipsync, LatentSync, Creatify Lipsync, Veed Lipsync, Infinite Talk V2V (prompt and 480p/720p), and Volcengine Video to Video Lip Sync (its own mode option lite/basic). Catalog descriptions: Infinite Talk animates a portrait into a talking video driven by audio; Wan 2.2 generates a talking portrait from an image and audio; LTX 2.3 is described as high-quality lipsync from portrait and audio; Sync Lipsync produces realistic lipsync from audio; LatentSync is video-to-video lipsync for high-quality audio-driven lip animation; Creatify is optimized for speed, quality and consistency; Veed generates realistic lipsync from any audio; Kling Avatar Standard vs Pro are the standard and premium tiers for talking avatars from a single image

chunks.title: Lip Sync Studio — Features
chunks.text: plus audio; Omnihuman 1.5 generates realistic talking head video from a portrait and audio. The comparison data file (price/speed/quality scores) contains no entries for lip sync models, so no price, speed or quality ranking is stated here. The public model catalog also lists FLUX 3 Lip Sync, but it has no mode category in the studio and does not appear in either group.

chunks.title: Lip Sync Studio — Inputs and outputs
chunks.text:
Lip Sync Studio (#/lipsync). Inputs and outputs.
Inputs:
- Portrait image
- Source video
- Audio file
- Model
- Resolution
- Prompt (optional)
- Thumbnail (optional)
Required inputs:

Optional inputs:

- Seed (advanced, only on models that expose it)
Input details:
- name: Portrait image | description: A photo of the face you want to animate. Upload it, or pick one from the Pexels stock photo browser ('Select Portrait Photo'). | required: true | whenToUse: Portrait Image mode only. | restrictions: Image uploads are limited to 10MB. Front-facing, clear, well-lit faces work best.
- name: Source video | description: The video whose mouth movement will be re-synced. Upload it or pick one from the Pexels stock video browser. | required: true | whenToUse: Video mode only. | restrictions: Video uploads are limited to 50MB.
- name: Audio file | description: The speech, singing or voice track that drives the lip movement. Any file the audio picker accepts (audio/*). | required: true | whenToUse: Always. Without audio the studio shows 'Please upload an audio file first.' | restrictions: The shared upload limit for audio is 10MB. Built-in tip: keep audio under 60 seconds.

chunks.title: Lip Sync Studio — Inputs and outputs
chunks.text:
- name: Model | description: Which AI model does the lip sync. Preselected to the first model of the current mode. | required: true | whenToUse: Change it if the first result is not good enough or you want a different resolution option. | restrictions: Models are split by mode.
- name: Resolution | description: Output resolution for models that offer it. | required: false | whenToUse: Choose higher for final deliverables, lower for quick tests. | restrictions: Options depend on the model (480p, 720p, 1080p).

Outputs:

- Downloadable file named like lipsync-<id>.mp4
- A History entry stored in your browser
- Optional AI-captioned preview

chunks.title: Lip Sync Studio — Problems and limits
chunks.text:
Lip Sync Studio (#/lipsync). Problems and limits.
Troubleshooting:
- Toast 'Please upload an audio file first.': upload an audio file with the audio button before clicking Generate.
- Toast 'Please upload a portrait image first.': you are in Portrait Image mode with no photo; upload one or switch to Video mode.
- Toast 'Please upload a source video first.': you are in Video mode with no video; upload one or switch to Portrait Image mode.
- Alert 'Please sign in and add api credits.' during upload: sign in and make sure your account has credits, then retry.
- Toast 'Image upload failed: ...' / 'Video upload failed: ...' / 'Audio upload failed: ...': check the file size and type, then try again or use a different file.
- Generate button shows 'Error: ...' for about 4 seconds then returns to 'Generate ✨': read the message, fix the input, and click Generate again.
- Error 'No video URL returned by API': the model finished without a usable video; try again, use another model, or a different photo/audio.
- No prompt box or resolution button visible: the selected model does not support them; pick a model that does if you need them.
- Page was refreshed during generation: a banner 'Resuming N pending generation(s)...' appears and the result is added to History when ready.

chunks.title: Lip Sync Studio — Problems and limits
chunks.text:
- Mouth does not match well: use a clear front-facing portrait, clean speech with little background noise, and try another model.
Troubleshooting steps:
- issue: Generate does nothing and a red message appears | steps: Read the toast text.; If it asks for audio, portrait image or source video, upload that file and wait for the status label to show a check mark.; Click Generate again.
- issue: Upload fails | steps: Check you are signed in and have credits.; Check the file size (image 10MB, video 50MB, audio 10MB).; Try a more common format such as JPG/PNG, MP4 and MP3/WAV.; Retry the upload.
- issue: Result looks poor | steps: Use a sharper, front-facing, well-lit photo (or a clean source video).; Use clear audio with one speaker.; Raise the resolution if a resolution button is available.; Switch to a different model and use Regenerate.
- issue: Generation is taking very long | steps: Wait; the studio polls for a long time before giving up.; Do not worry if you refresh: pending jobs are resumed.; If it fails, try a lower resolution or shorter audio.
Common problems:
- problem: I cannot find the resolution or prompt option | whyItHappens: These controls only appear for models that support them. | howToFix: Pick a model such as Infinite Talk or LTX 2.3 Lipsync, which offer resolution and a prompt.

chunks.title: Lip Sync Studio — Problems and limits
chunks.text:
- problem: The model list is different after I clicked Video | whyItHappens: The list depends on the mode, and switching mode resets the model to the first one in that group. | howToFix: Re-select the model you want after switching modes.
- problem: My earlier results disappeared | whyItHappens: History is stored in this browser only and keeps 30 entries. | howToFix: Download results you want to keep.
Limitations:
- Audio is required in both modes; a portrait or video is required depending on mode.
- Upload size limits come from the shared MuAPI limits: images 10MB, video 50MB, audio 10MB.
- You can only use models from the current mode's group.
- There is no phoneme-level timing editor, voice library, background replacement or expression sliders in this studio; you control the result with the audio, the photo, the model and an optional prompt.
- History is stored locally in your browser (up to 30 entries) and is not synced between devices.
- Generating requires being signed in with credits; otherwise you are asked to sign in or add credits.
Limit details:
- limitation: No voice library | impact: You must bring your own audio file. | workaround: Create speech or a cloned voice in Audio Studio (#/audio), download it, then upload it here.

chunks.title: Lip Sync Studio — Problems and limits
chunks.text:
- limitation: Upload size limits | impact: Large files are rejected. | workaround: Trim or compress the video to under 50MB and keep audio under 10MB.
- limitation: Model groups are tied to the mode | impact: A video-only model cannot be used with a photo. | workaround: Switch the Input toggle to the mode that contains the model you want.
FAQs:
- question: What do I need to make a portrait talk? | answer: A portrait image and an audio file, in Portrait Image mode. Then click Generate.
- question: What is the difference between Portrait Image and Video mode? | answer: Portrait Image animates a still photo to speak your audio. Video re-syncs the mouth in an existing video to your audio.
- question: Which model is the default? | answer: In Portrait Image mode the first model, Infinite Talk, is selected (480p by default). In Video mode the first model, Sync Lipsync, is selected.
- question: Can I type what the person should say? | answer: No. This studio is driven by an audio file. Create speech from text in Audio Studio first, then upload it here. The optional prompt only describes talking style or motion.
- question: How long can the audio be? | answer: The in-app tips suggest keeping audio under 60 seconds for best results. The studio itself does not show a hard duration limit.
