chunks.title: Motion Director — Overview
chunks.text:
Motion Director (#/motion-director). Overview.
Description:
Motion Director is a chat that plans a short promotional film from your prompt and your website, builds it from a library of about 150 motion shot recipes, and opens it in an editable Motion Workbench where you can adjust and export an MP4.
Summary:
Chat that plans a film from a prompt and your website using shot recipes, then lets you edit and export it.
About:
Motion Director is an AI film director for product and launch videos. You describe the film (and usually give your website address); the director captures your real web pages, proposes a storyboard built from motion shot recipes (title cards, product-page shots, camera moves, data shots, transitions, outros), builds an editable film, and lets you play it in the chat. You can then click Open in Motion Workbench to fine-tune the timeline, text, colors and music with an Edit agent, and export an MP4. It has two views on the same route family: the chat at #/motion-director and the editor (Motion Workbench) at #/motion-director/workbench. It is not listed in the side menu; you reach it by its address. It needs your own OpenAI key for the director AI and a plan that includes SmartVideo GO to start a film.
Best for:

chunks.title: Motion Director — Overview
chunks.text:
Founders, marketers and agencies who want a polished launch or promo film made from their own website pages without building a timeline by hand, and who want to edit the result afterwards.
When to use it:
- You want a promo or launch film made from your website's real pages.
- You want the AI to plan shots (storyboard) and you to approve or change it.
- You want to pick specific shot cards (templates) and have them used in order.
- You want a finished film that stays editable on a timeline, with an Edit agent to change text and styling.
- You want a vertical (9:16), square (1:1) or widescreen (16:9) film.
When to use another studio:
- Use Video Agent (#/video-agent) when you only want a quick coded animation from a prompt, such as a chart or animated title, with no website capture.
- Use Workbench (#/workbench) when you already have clips, images or audio generated in other studios and want to arrange them on a timeline.
- Use Timeline (#/timeline) when you want a general multi-track editor for footage.
- Use Video (#/video) or Cinema (#/cinema) when you want AI-generated footage rather than designed motion graphics.
- Use Brand (#/brand) or Find My Brand (#/find-my-brand) when you mainly want to discover or set up your brand look first.

chunks.title: Motion Director — How to use
chunks.text:
Motion Director (#/motion-director). How to use.
How to use:
1. Open #/motion-director (it is not in the side menu, so type the address or follow a link). 2. Make sure your OpenAI key is saved in Settings. 3. In the box labelled 'Describe your motion video' write what you want and include your website address and length, for example 'Make a 30 second launch film for https://your-product.com'. 4. Optionally choose an Aspect ratio (16:9, 9:16, 1:1), click Templates to pick shot cards, attach files, or use Use My Brand. 5. Click Generate (the button is named Send while you are answering the director). 6. Answer the director's questions, for example choose Use Ink Press, Let the director pick shots or Work it out together, and confirm each step with the buttons such as 'Looks right - next'. 7. Review the storyboard and ask for changes in the chat. 8. When the film appears, play it in the result card. 9. Click Open in Motion Workbench to edit, using the Edit agent, the library, Properties and the timeline. 10. Click Export video to render an MP4 in your browser.
Steps:
- Go to #/motion-director.
- Check that your OpenAI key is saved in Settings.
- Describe the film in 'Describe your motion video' and include your site address and length.
- Optionally set Aspect ratio, Templates, attached files or Use My Brand.
- Click Generate and answer the director's questions.

chunks.title: Motion Director — How to use
chunks.text:
- Review and adjust the storyboard in chat.
- Play the finished film, then click Open in Motion Workbench for edits.
- Click Export video to get the MP4.
Getting started:
- Have your website address ready; real pages make the best shots.
- Say how long the film should be, otherwise 20 seconds is used.
- If unsure about style, choose Use Ink Press or Work it out together.
- Use the one-click example prompts under the composer to see good phrasing.
Tips:
- Always include your website address and a length in the first message.
- Say 'you decide' when you do not mind the director choosing.
- Use Fast draft (720p) while iterating, then export at full quality.
- Use Export JSON to back up a project before big changes.
Best practices:
- Confirm the storyboard before building the film.
- Keep headlines short (about 70 characters) and captions about 90.
- Hold key moments at least a second so viewers can read them.
- Keep the tab open during export.

chunks.title: Motion Director — Features
chunks.text:
Motion Director (#/motion-director). Features.
Key features:
- Chat that turns a prompt plus your site address into a storyboard and then a film.
- Real page capture of your website for product-page shots.
- About 150 shot recipes in ten categories: opening, typography, ui-entrance, camera, data, interaction, transition, rhythm, effects, outro.
- Ink Press template: a validated paper-and-ink launch film structure the director can offer.
- 'Work it out together' guided mode: the director proposes a product check, a visual direction and a shot plan, and you confirm each step.
- Templates picker to choose shot cards by hand (up to 12) with live previews, search and categories.
- Aspect ratio choice: 16:9, 9:16 or 1:1.
- Attach images, video or audio from your computer, and connect your brand (Use My Brand).
- Open in Motion Workbench: timeline, library, properties inspector, preview, Edit agent.
- Export video to MP4 in your browser with Fast draft (720p) and Without music options.
- Undo and redo, Export JSON, Import and Reset to sample for projects.
- Interface languages English, Chinese and Russian in the editor.
Feature details:

chunks.title: Motion Director — Features
chunks.text: - feature: Describe your motion video (chat composer) | explanation: On the chat screen, titled 'Films are easier with Motion Director', type what you want in the box (label 'Describe your motion video'). The placeholder changes with the conversation stage. The send button says Generate for a new film and Send while you are answering the director. | whyToUse: This is how every film starts. Include your website address, the length (for example 'a 30 second video') and the goal. | inputRequired: A text message. A site address is strongly recommended. | restrictions: If you do not say a length, 20 seconds is used. Film length is kept between 5 and 90 seconds, with 2 to 14 scenes, each scene between 1.5 and 12 seconds. A plan is needed to start (see limitations).

chunks.title: Motion Director — Features
chunks.text:
- feature: Storyboard planning with your options | explanation: After your prompt the director may ask a question such as 'Use Ink Press? Or I can let the director pick shots from the whole library...' with buttons Use Ink Press, Let the director pick shots and Work it out together. You then see a storyboard and can tell it what to change before the film is built. | whyToUse: Lets you control the look and the shots before time is spent building. | inputRequired: Your answer in the chat or a button click. | restrictions: In the guided flow the confirm buttons read 'Looks right - next', 'Use my recommendation' and 'Looks right - write the storyboard'.
- feature: Templates picker | explanation: The Templates pill opens 'Motion Templates' where you pick shot cards. Picking a card adds it (or removes it if already chosen) and returns you to the chat box. You can open Templates again to add more; the film uses them in the order picked. Tags warn when a shot 'Shows your site's pages', 'Draws a sample screen; your site appears beside it' or is 'Slow to export'. | whyToUse: When you know which kind of shots you want. | inputRequired: None. | restrictions: Up to 12 shot cards can be picked (the storyboard holds 14 scenes and two go to title cards).

chunks.title: Motion Director — Features
chunks.text:
- feature: Aspect ratio | explanation: An Aspect ratio pill in the composer lets you choose 16:9, 9:16 or 1:1. | whyToUse: Pick vertical for TikTok/Reels/Shorts, square for feeds, widescreen for websites and YouTube. | inputRequired: None, default is set by the app. | restrictions: Only those three ratios.
- feature: Attach image / video / audio | explanation: The attach button (label 'Attach image / video / audio') adds local files from your computer; they appear as small chips you can remove with the x button and are carried into the new film. | whyToUse: To use your own screenshots, clips or music. | inputRequired: Local files. | restrictions: Files are used locally in the browser; exact size limits for this attach button were not confirmed.
- feature: Use My Brand | explanation: Connects your brand kit (business name, colors, logos, images and reference frames) through the shared personalization modal. A chip shows the Brand Kit company in use; clicking it clears it. | whyToUse: To make the film follow your brand colors and logo, especially if you have no site address. | inputRequired: A saved brand or the brand form fields. | restrictions: A site address you give in the prompt wins over the Brand Kit company.

chunks.title: Motion Director — Features
chunks.text: - feature: Open in Motion Workbench | explanation: When a film is finished you get a card with a player, a Render MP4 button and Open in Motion Workbench. The Workbench (#/motion-director/workbench) has an 'Edit agent' panel (tell it what to change in this film), the shot library, the Properties inspector, the preview and a multi-track timeline. A 'Back to chat' button returns to the chat and your film stays available as Continue editing. | whyToUse: Fine-tune text, timing, colors, music and shot order. | inputRequired: A built film. | restrictions: Keyboard shortcuts: Space play or pause, S split at the playhead, Delete or Backspace remove the selected clip, Ctrl/Cmd+D duplicate, Ctrl/Cmd+Z undo, Shift+Ctrl/Cmd+Z redo, Left and Right arrows step 1 frame (hold Shift for 10).

chunks.title: Motion Director — Features
chunks.text:
- feature: Export video | explanation: The Workbench top bar has Export video. It renders the film to MP4 inside your browser tab with the Remotion web renderer (the button tooltip says to keep the tab open). While running it shows 'Exporting N%', with a Cancel button; on success it shows 'Exported' with a way to show or download the file; on error it shows 'Export failed - Retry'. Extra options: 'Fast draft (720p)' (about a third faster) and 'Without music'. A rough time estimate is shown. | whyToUse: Get the final MP4. | inputRequired: A project with clips. | restrictions: Heavy shots and long films take longer. Some shot cards are tagged 'Slow to export'.
- feature: Project file tools | explanation: The Workbench top bar also offers Undo, Redo, Export JSON (saves the project as a .json file), Import (loads a project JSON) and Reset to sample (asks 'Replace the current project with the sample project? You can undo this.'). | whyToUse: Back up or share a project, or start over from a sample. | inputRequired: A project JSON for Import. | restrictions: Bad files show 'Import failed: not a valid project JSON'.
Modes:
- Use Ink Press
- Let the director pick shots
- Work it out together
- Named or picked shot cards
- Edit agent (in Workbench)
Mode details:

chunks.title: Motion Director — Features
chunks.text:
- mode: Use Ink Press | description: A validated launch-film template: a bold paper-and-ink title card, your real pages in product shots with caption strips, flash cuts on the beat, whoosh and impact sound design, and a launch outro. Default colors are a paper background (#f7f4ee), ink text (#1c1a17) and amber accent (#b5651d) unless brand colors are given. | useCase: The fastest path to a polished launch film.
- mode: Let the director pick shots | description: The director chooses shots from the whole library to fit your product. | useCase: When you have no strong preference.
- mode: Work it out together | description: The director reads your site and proposes a product check, a visual direction (up to three options labelled A, B, C) and a shot plan; you confirm each step before it writes the storyboard. | useCase: When you want to steer the creative direction.
- mode: Named or picked shot cards | description: You name shot cards in chat (for example deck-deal-flyin and row-embed) or pick them in Templates. | useCase: When you know exactly which effects you want.
- mode: Edit agent (in Workbench) | description: A panel where you tell the agent what to change in the film (for example make text bigger). It proposes edits to clips and text. | useCase: Quick changes without manual timeline work.
Models:

chunks.title: Motion Director — Features
chunks.text: The director runs on OpenAI models through your own OpenAI key. The server default director model is gpt-6-astra, and only gpt-6-astra, gpt-4o and gpt-4o-mini are allowed values (the default can be overridden by the environment variable MOTION_STUDIO_DIRECTOR_MODEL). The model is used to plan briefs, visual directions, shot mappings, storyboards, text edits, adapted shot code, frame-by-frame quality review and Edit agent instructions; it only chooses among catalog recipes and a fixed set of edit operations. There is no AI video model: the film is rendered from motion shot code (Remotion) and your captured pages.

chunks.title: Motion Director — Inputs and outputs
chunks.text:
Motion Director (#/motion-director). Inputs and outputs.
Inputs:
- Prompt
- Website address
- Aspect ratio
- Templates (shot cards)
- Attached media
- Brand kit (Use My Brand)

Required inputs:

Optional inputs:

Input details:
- name: Prompt | description: Your description of the film. The director also reads the first web address in it. | required: true | whenToUse: Always. | restrictions: Empty requests do nothing (the server answers 'Describe the film first').
- name: Website address | description: A URL in your prompt (for example https://your-product.com). The director captures the pages to build product-page shots. | required: false | whenToUse: Whenever you have a site. | restrictions: The capture needs the site to be reachable; if it cannot be captured the film will lean on non-site shots.
- name: OpenAI API key | description: Your own key, used by the director AI. | required: true | whenToUse: Save once in Settings. | restrictions: Without it the server responds 'Add your OpenAI API key in SmartVideo GO Settings to use the Motion Studio director.' A rejected key gives 'OpenAI rejected the API key'.

chunks.title: Motion Director — Inputs and outputs
chunks.text:
- name: Aspect ratio | description: 16:9, 9:16 or 1:1. | required: false | whenToUse: Choose before generating. | restrictions: Three options only.
- name: Templates (shot cards) | description: Specific shot recipes you want used, in the order picked. | required: false | whenToUse: When you want specific effects. | restrictions: Up to 12.
- name: Attached media | description: Images, video or audio from your computer. | required: false | whenToUse: To include your own assets. | restrictions: Size limits not confirmed.
Outputs:
- A storyboard shown in the chat
- An editable film project (tracks and clips) opened in the Motion Workbench
- A playable film in the chat result card
- An MP4 file rendered in your browser (Export video / Render MP4)
- A project JSON file (Export JSON)

chunks.title: Motion Director — Problems and limits
chunks.text:
Motion Director (#/motion-director). Problems and limits.
Troubleshooting:
- Generate shows an upgrade prompt: your account lacks the SmartVideo GO entitlement; upgrade your plan.
- Error 'Add your OpenAI API key in SmartVideo GO Settings to use the Motion Studio director.': save your OpenAI key in Settings and retry.
- Error 'OpenAI rejected the API key': replace the saved key with a valid one.
- Page shows 'Motion Director could not be loaded. Please reload the page.': reload the browser tab; if it persists check your connection.
- The film does not use my website: include a full address such as https://yoursite.com in the prompt and make sure the site is publicly reachable.
- Export fails: press Export video again (it shows 'Export failed - Retry'), keep the tab open, try Fast draft (720p) or remove slow shots.
- My film disappeared after going back to the chat: reopen it from the Continue editing tile or the Recent Projects list.
- Import failed: the file is not a valid project JSON; use a file made with Export JSON.
Troubleshooting steps:
- issue: The director will not start | steps: Check you are signed in and your plan includes SmartVideo GO.; Open Settings and confirm your OpenAI key is saved.; Make sure the message box is not empty and click Generate again.

chunks.title: Motion Director — Problems and limits
chunks.text:
- issue: Export is slow or fails | steps: Keep the browser tab open and in front.; Tick Fast draft (720p) for a faster export.; Hide or remove shots marked 'Slow to export'.; Click Export again after 'Export failed - Retry'.
- issue: I cannot find my film in the editor | steps: Go to #/motion-director and look for the Continue editing tile or Recent Projects.; Click it to reopen the Workbench with your project.; If you saved a JSON earlier, use Import.
Common problems:
- problem: The film does not look like my site | whyItHappens: No site address was given or the capture failed, so generic shots were used. | howToFix: Include your full website address and ask the director to use real page shots, or use Use My Brand for colors and logos.
- problem: I picked too many shot cards | whyItHappens: A film holds at most 14 scenes and two are title cards, so 12 shots can be picked. | howToFix: Remove some picks by clicking the x on their chips.
- problem: Changes in the Edit agent were skipped | whyItHappens: Every edit is checked; invalid edits are skipped. | howToFix: Rephrase the instruction or use the Properties inspector manually. Undo with Ctrl/Cmd+Z.
Limitations:
- Not listed in the side menu; reach it at #/motion-director.
- Starting a film requires an active plan that includes SmartVideo GO; otherwise an upgrade prompt appears.

chunks.title: Motion Director — Problems and limits
chunks.text:
- Requires your own OpenAI key; there is no fallback platform key.
- Film length is limited to 5 to 90 seconds, 2 to 14 scenes, each scene 1.5 to 12 seconds; headlines about 70 characters and captions about 90.
- At most 12 shot cards can be picked in Templates.
- MP4 export runs in your browser tab, so heavy shots and long films are slow; keep the tab open.
- The film is built from catalog shot recipes, not from AI-generated footage.
Limit details:
- limitation: Plan required | impact: Clicking Generate can open an upgrade prompt instead of starting. | workaround: Upgrade your plan to one that includes SmartVideo GO, or contact support.
- limitation: OpenAI key required | impact: The director cannot plan without your key. | workaround: Add your OpenAI API key in Settings and retry.
- limitation: Slow exports | impact: Some shot cards are tagged 'Slow to export' and long films take longer. | workaround: Tick Fast draft (720p) for a quicker preview export, choose lighter shots, or shorten the film.
- limitation: Scene and length caps | impact: Very long or very busy briefs are trimmed to the limits. | workaround: Make several shorter films.
FAQs:
- question: Where is Motion Director in the menu? | answer: It is not in the side menu. Open it at #/motion-director. The editor is at #/motion-director/workbench.

chunks.title: Motion Director — Problems and limits
chunks.text:
- question: Do I need an OpenAI key? | answer: Yes. The director uses your own OpenAI key from Settings.
- question: Do I need a paid plan? | answer: Starting a film checks for a plan that includes SmartVideo GO and shows an upgrade prompt otherwise.
- question: How long can the film be? | answer: Between 5 and 90 seconds. If you do not say a length, the composer uses 20 seconds.
- question: Is this the same as Workbench? | answer: No. Workbench (#/workbench) is a separate studio for editing your generated clips, images and audio. Motion Director has its own editor called Motion Workbench, which opens from a film made in the chat.
- question: Where is my exported MP4? | answer: Export video renders in your browser and offers the file to download. Whether it is also saved to your library from this editor was not confirmed.
- question: Can I change the text after the film is built? | answer: Yes. Use the Edit agent, or select a clip in the timeline and change its text and style in Properties.

chunks.title: Motion Director — Workflows and use cases
chunks.text:
Motion Director (#/motion-director). Workflows and use cases.
Example workflows:
- title: Launch film from my website | steps: Open #/motion-director.; Type 'Make a launch film for https://your-product.com with the Ink Press template' (one of the example prompts).; Click Generate and choose Use Ink Press if asked.; Review the storyboard and ask for tweaks.; Play the film, then click Open in Motion Workbench.; Use the Edit agent to change the headline, then click Export video.

chunks.title: Personalizer — Overview
chunks.text:
Personalizer (#/personalizer). Overview.
Description:
A drag-and-drop canvas for building personalized web pages and creatives. You place text, images, buttons, forms and videos, drop in {{tokens}} such as {{firstName}}, and preview the page as each contact would see it.
Summary:
Build a page on a canvas and personalize it per contact with tokens.
About:
Personalizer is a visual canvas editor. You add elements (Heading, Text, Image, Button, Form, Video, Spacer, Container) from the left sidebar, position them freely, and type tokens like {{firstName}} or {{company}} into text and link fields. Choose an Active Contact and the canvas shows the page with that person's details filled in; Preview Personalized refreshes it and Export HTML produces a standalone page. A Personalization hub in the sidebar holds client profiles, an asset library, AI Assist and website discovery. Content sent from other studios arrives as a Source panel with a Return button. The same personalization system (a modal with Find My Brand, Find Local Business, client profile, assets, prompt and engine sections) powers the Personalize buttons in other studios.
Best for:
Marketers, agencies and freelancers who need many personalized variants of one page or creative, each filled with a contact's or client's own name, company, logo and offer.
When to use it:

chunks.title: Personalizer — Overview
chunks.text:
- You want one landing page or creative that shows a different name, company or offer per contact.
- You want to preview how a page looks for a specific contact before sending.
- You received content from another studio and want to personalize it.
- You need a quick standalone HTML export of a designed page.
- You want to store client profiles and brand assets once and reuse them.
When to use another studio:
- Use Lead Finder (#/leadfinder) when you need to find local businesses to personalize for.
- Use Find My Brand (#/find-my-brand) when you only want to pull a business's logo, photos and branding from its website.
- Use Timeline Editor (#/timeline) when the thing to personalize is a video edit.
- Use Website Builder (#/website-builder) when you want a full website rather than one canvas page.
- Use Video Render (#/render) to export an existing video.

chunks.title: Personalizer — How to use
chunks.text:
Personalizer (#/personalizer). How to use.
How to use:
1. Open Personalizer from the Apps hub or go to #/personalizer. 2. Choose a canvas size (for example Landing Page) or type W and H and click Apply Size. 3. Click Heading, Text, Image, Button, Form or Video in the sidebar to add elements. 4. Click an element and edit it in the Properties panel (text, Source URL, Link URL, colors, fonts, position). 5. Click a token chip such as {{firstName}} to insert it into the selected element, or type the token yourself. 6. Under Personalization choose an Active Contact. 7. Click Preview Personalized to check the result. 8. Click Save Canvas to keep your work in this browser. 9. Click Export HTML to open the finished page. 10. Press Delete to remove a selected element.
Steps:
- Pick a canvas size.
- Add elements from the palette.
- Insert tokens into text or link fields.
- Choose an Active Contact.
- Click Preview Personalized.
- Click Save Canvas and then Export HTML.
Getting started:
- Start with the Landing Page preset and add a Heading containing {{firstName}}.
- Create or pick a contact in the Personalization hub so previews have data.
- Save Canvas early; storage is local to your browser.
Tips:
- Keep a few sample contacts so you can flip between them while previewing.
- Use short, clear tokens like {{company}} in headings.
- Save before you leave the page.
Best practices:

chunks.title: Personalizer — How to use
chunks.text:
- Preview with at least two different contacts.
- Export HTML as your backup copy.
- Reuse uploaded images through the Asset Library.

chunks.title: Personalizer — Features
chunks.text:
Personalizer (#/personalizer). Features.
Key features:
- Canvas with 8 element types: Heading, Text, Image, Button, Form, Video, Spacer, Container
- Canvas size presets: Blank 1280x720, Landing Page 1280x800, Email 600x800, Social Post 1080x1080, Story 1080x1920, Banner 728x90, plus custom W and H with Apply Size
- Token chips such as {{firstName}} that insert into the selected element
- Active Contact dropdown (default - None -) to preview with real contact data
- Preview Personalized and Export HTML actions
- Save Canvas and Load Canvas (stored in your browser, with an integrity check)
- Properties panel per element (position in percent, size in pixels, text, source URL, link URL, colors, fonts)
- Upload image... / Replace asset... stored in your Asset Library
- Personalization hub: client profiles, asset library, AI Assist, Discover from website
- Source panel with Return to <studio> and Dismiss Source for content sent from other studios
- Delete or Backspace removes the selected element
Feature details:

chunks.title: Personalizer — Features
chunks.text:
- feature: Element palette | explanation: Click Heading, Text, Image, Button, Form, Video, Spacer or Container in the sidebar to add that element. A toast says 'Added <name>'. New text elements start with the text 'Double-click to edit text. Use {{token}} for personalization.' | whyToUse: Builds the page layout. | inputRequired: None. | restrictions: Spacer and similar elements do not support tokens.
- feature: Canvas size | explanation: Pick a preset (Blank, Landing Page, Email, Social Post, Story, Banner) or type W and H and click Apply Size. If a field is empty it falls back to 1280 by 720. | whyToUse: Match the page to where it will be used. | inputRequired: Optional width and height in pixels. | restrictions: None stated.

chunks.title: Personalizer — Features
chunks.text: - feature: Tokens | explanation: Tokens are placeholders in double curly braces. The chips in the sidebar cover names (firstName, lastName, fullName), company (company, companyName), title, email, location, industry, companySummary, painPoint, product, service, interest, buyingSignal, tone, brandColor, logoUrl, avatarUrl, image tokens (productImageUrl, brandImageUrl, ctaImageUrl, firstFrameUrl, lastFrameUrl), social links (github, linkedin, twitter, website) and business fields (businessName, businessPhone, productService, offer, ctaHeadline, callToAction, brandDescription). Select an element and click a chip, or type the token yourself. Older labels like {{First Name}} also still work. | whyToUse: One design, many personalized results. | inputRequired: A selected element and a contact with data. | restrictions: If no element is selected you get 'Select an element first'; some element types give 'This element type does not support tokens'. Without a contact you see 'No contact selected - showing base content'.

chunks.title: Personalizer — Features
chunks.text:
- feature: Active Contact and preview | explanation: The Active Contact dropdown lists your saved profiles. Choosing one fills tokens with that contact's data. Preview Personalized refreshes the view and shows 'Preview updated'. | whyToUse: Check the result for each recipient. | inputRequired: At least one saved contact profile. | restrictions: Empty token values may stay blank or show the base text.
- feature: Export HTML | explanation: Export HTML opens the personalized page in a new window as a standalone page titled Personalized Page. | whyToUse: Share or host the page elsewhere. | inputRequired: A built canvas. | restrictions: If the browser blocks the window you see 'Popup blocked - please allow popups for this site'.
- feature: Save Canvas / Load Canvas | explanation: Save Canvas stores your elements and size in this browser and says 'Canvas saved'. Load Canvas restores it ('Canvas loaded'). The saved data has a checksum so damaged data is rejected. | whyToUse: Continue later on the same browser. | inputRequired: None. | restrictions: Saved only in this browser (local storage); not shared across devices. Messages: 'Save failed - storage may be full', 'No saved canvas found', 'Saved canvas appears corrupted', 'Saved canvas integrity check failed', 'Failed to load canvas'.

chunks.title: Personalizer — Features
chunks.text:
- feature: Properties panel | explanation: Selecting an element shows '<type> Properties' with X (%), Y (%), Width (px), Height (px), plus Text, Source URL, Link URL, Background, Color, Font Size, Font Family and Font Weight where they apply, and 'Tokens in this element' listing detected tokens. X and Y are limited to 0-95 percent and width and height to at least 40. | whyToUse: Fine tune each element. | inputRequired: A selected element. | restrictions: If nothing is selected: 'Select an element to edit its properties.'
- feature: Image upload | explanation: On an Image element, Upload image... stores the file in your Asset Library so it can be reused across studios without re-uploading (hint: 'Stored in your Asset Library - reused across studios without re-uploading.'). The button then reads Replace asset... | whyToUse: Use your own logos and photos. | inputRequired: An image file. | restrictions: If the upload fails the button shows an error message or 'Upload failed'.

chunks.title: Personalizer — Features
chunks.text:
- feature: Personalization hub | explanation: At the bottom of the sidebar. It holds client profiles ('No client profile yet. Create one to personalize every studio render.'), an asset library with categories such as Person, Logo, Product, Brand, First frame and Last frame, an AI Assist box (placeholder: describe the edit, e.g. 'remove the background and brighten the logo') and 'Discover from website', where you paste a website URL to import its images. | whyToUse: Reuse client data and brand assets everywhere. | inputRequired: Optional: client details, website URL. | restrictions: Website discovery needs sign-in ('Sign in to run website discovery'). Messages include 'Enter a website URL to discover its images.', 'The discovery service is busy - try again in a moment.', 'Discovery timed out. The site may be too slow - try again.', 'No assets found on that page.'
- feature: Source handoff from other studios | explanation: When another studio sends content here, a Source section lists the fields. Return to <studio> goes back, and Dismiss Source clears it ('Source content dismissed'). | whyToUse: Move generated content into personalization and back. | inputRequired: Content sent from another studio. | restrictions: Handoff lives only in the current tab (session storage). A bad route shows 'Invalid return route'.

chunks.title: Personalizer — Features
chunks.text:
- feature: Personalization modal in other studios | explanation: Personalize buttons in other studios open a full-screen modal. It has sections Overview, Discovered, Client Assets, Saved Assets, Preview, Business, Prompt, Output, Mode and Engine. You can pick Me, My Business or Client, save a client ('Save Client' or 'Update Client'), write a prompt and click Personalize Prompt, then generate. Output choices include Prompt, Video or Image, and Everything (prompt plus media plus assets plus CTA). Modes include Face Only, Full Presenter, Recreate For Client and Complete Personalization for video, and Keep This Design, Replace Face, Replace Person, Recreate For Client and Complete Personalization for images. The Engine section offers SmartVideo Recommended plus aspect ratio, resolution, quality and duration selectors. | whyToUse: Turn a demo or creative into a version for a specific business. | inputRequired: Business or client details and assets. | restrictions: Results show Original and Personalized side by side; failures say 'We Could Not Complete This Personalization' while keeping your inputs.
Mode details:
- mode: Canvas editor | description: Free-form page building with tokens. | useCase: Personalized landing pages and creatives.

chunks.title: Personalizer — Features
chunks.text: - mode: Personalization modal (other studios) | description: Prompt and asset personalization for generated images and videos. | useCase: Client-specific versions of demos.

chunks.title: Personalizer — Inputs and outputs
chunks.text:
Personalizer (#/personalizer). Inputs and outputs.
Inputs:
- Elements
- Tokens
- Contact profiles
- Images
- Canvas size
- Website URL (hub discovery)
Optional inputs:
- Active Contact
- Uploaded images

Input details:
- name: Active Contact | description: Which saved profile fills the tokens. | required: false | whenToUse: When previewing or exporting for one person. | restrictions: Default is - None -, which shows base content.
- name: Canvas size | description: Width and height in pixels. | required: false | whenToUse: At the start. | restrictions: Defaults to 1280 x 720.

chunks.title: Personalizer — Problems and limits
chunks.text:
Personalizer (#/personalizer). Problems and limits.
Troubleshooting:
- Select an element first: click an element on the canvas before inserting a token.
- This element type does not support tokens: use a Text, Heading, Button or similar element.
- No contact selected - showing base content: choose an Active Contact.
- Popup blocked: allow popups for this site and click Export HTML again.
- Save failed - storage may be full: free up browser storage or export your HTML.
- Saved canvas integrity check failed: the saved data was altered or damaged; rebuild and save again.
- Discovery asks you to sign in: sign in, then paste the website URL again.
Troubleshooting steps:
- issue: Tokens show as raw {{text}} | steps: Choose an Active Contact.; Check the token name matches a chip (for example firstName).; Click Preview Personalized.
- issue: Cannot load a saved canvas | steps: Click Load Canvas.; If you see No saved canvas found, it was never saved in this browser.; If corrupted, rebuild the page.
Common problems:
- problem: Preview shows no personal details | whyItHappens: No contact is selected or the profile lacks that field. | howToFix: Pick a contact and fill in the missing field.
- problem: Element cannot be moved off the edge | whyItHappens: X and Y are limited to 0-95 percent. | howToFix: Use width and height to resize instead.
Limitations:

chunks.title: Personalizer — Problems and limits
chunks.text:
- Saved canvases live in this browser only.
- Token resolution needs a contact with data.
- Website discovery needs sign-in.
- Pop-up blockers can stop Export HTML.
Limit details:
- limitation: Local-only save | impact: Clearing browser data loses the canvas. | workaround: Export HTML when finished.
- limitation: Popup blocked | impact: Export HTML window does not open. | workaround: Allow popups for this site and click again.
FAQs:
- question: What are tokens? | answer: Placeholders written like {{firstName}} that are replaced with a contact's real details when you preview or export.
- question: Where is my canvas saved? | answer: Save Canvas stores it in your browser. It is not synced to other devices.
- question: How do I delete an element? | answer: Select it and press Delete or Backspace; you will see 'Element deleted'.
- question: What canvas sizes are available? | answer: Blank 1280x720, Landing Page 1280x800, Email 600x800, Social Post 1080x1080, Story 1080x1920 and Banner 728x90, or any custom size.

chunks.title: Personalizer — Workflows and use cases
chunks.text:
Personalizer (#/personalizer). Workflows and use cases.
Example workflows:
- title: Personalized landing page | steps: Choose the Landing Page preset.; Add a Heading with 'Hi {{firstName}}'.; Add Text mentioning {{company}}.; Add a Button linking to your offer.; Pick an Active Contact and click Preview Personalized.; Click Export HTML.
- title: Brand-based personalization | steps: Open the Personalization hub.; Use Discover from website with the client's URL.; Import the logo and photos.; Drop the logo into an Image element and export.
Use cases:
- title: Cold outreach page | description: A page per prospect with their company and pain point. | steps: Create tokens for company and painPoint.; Preview each contact.; Export HTML. | expectedOutput: One HTML page per contact.
Related studios:

- studio: find-my-brand | relationship: Pulls brand assets from a website | whenToMove: You only need logos and photos. | why: It is free and needs no sign-in.

chunks.title: Video Render — Overview
chunks.text:
Video Render (#/render). Overview.
Description:
Finish and re-export a video from your library: choose a style preset, set output format, frame rate and quality, then export, queue a render, or make trailer cuts, social resizes, shorts, subtitles and more.
Summary:
Export and finish a generated video with presets and format options.
About:
Video Render (#/render, not in the side menu) edits videos made in other studios. If no video is selected it shows 'Choose a video to render' with a grid of your library videos. Once a video is loaded you pick a look preset (Luxury Brand Grade, Documentary Contrast, Film Trailer Punch or Emotional Story Tone), set Output Format, Frame Rate and Quality, and use action buttons such as Export Video, Download Frame, Queue Render, Trailer Cut, Social Resize and Remix Scene, plus AI tiles like Create Shorts, Generate Highlights, Add Subtitles and Dub / Voiceover. Exports happen in your browser. A render queue lists jobs with progress and a Download render link, and you can save drafts and templates.
Best for:
Anyone who has a generated video and wants a polished export, a trailer or short version, resized social variants or a delivery package without building a timeline.
When to use it:
- You have a video in your library and want to export it as WebM or MP4.
- You want a trailer cut, short vertical clips, highlights or subtitles.

chunks.title: Video Render — Overview
chunks.text:
- You want social formats (9:16, 1:1, 4:5, 16:9) from one video.
- You want to queue renders and download them later.
When to use another studio:
- Use Timeline Editor (#/timeline) when you need to combine several clips, music and voice-over on tracks.
- Use Video (#/video) to generate a new video first.
- Use Video Tools (#/videotools) for other quick video operations.
- Use Storyboard (#/storyboard) to plan scenes (Render has a Send to Storyboard action).

chunks.title: Video Render — How to use
chunks.text:
Video Render (#/render). How to use.
How to use:
1. Open Video Render at #/render. 2. If asked 'Choose a video to render', click a video from your library. 3. Pick a preset such as Film Trailer Punch. 4. Under Output Format choose WebM (VP9) or an MP4 option, set Frame Rate and move the Quality slider. 5. Click Export Video and wait for the progress to finish. 6. Download the result. 7. Optionally click Trailer Cut, Social Resize, Remix Scene or Publish / Deliver for more versions, or Queue Render to run it later from the queue.
Steps:
- Select a video from the library.
- Choose a preset.
- Set Output Format, Frame Rate and Quality.
- Click Export Video.
- Download the finished file or open the queue.
Getting started:
- Generate a video in Video Studio first, then open it in Render.
- Leave Quality at 82 and Frame Rate at the default for your first export.
- Try Download Frame for a quick thumbnail.
Tips:
- Use the queue for several exports.
- Download Frame makes a quick thumbnail.
- Save a template once you like a setup.
Best practices:
- Export a short test first.
- Pick the format your destination platform prefers.
- Keep the original video untouched; exports create new files.

chunks.title: Video Render — Features
chunks.text:
Video Render (#/render). Features.
Key features:
- Video picker from your library ('Choose a video to render')
- Four presets: Luxury Brand Grade, Documentary Contrast, Film Trailer Punch, Emotional Story Tone
- Output Format: WebM (VP9), MP4 (H.264), MP4 (H.265), depending on what your browser can encode
- Frame Rate: 24 FPS Cinematic, 30 FPS Standard, and 60
- Quality slider from 1 to 100, default 82
- Action buttons: Export Video, Download Frame, Queue Render, Trailer Cut, Social Resize, Remix Scene
- Quick actions: Copy Prompt, Duplicate Render, Save as Template, Send to Storyboard, Publish / Deliver
- AI tiles: Create Shorts, Generate Highlights, Add Subtitles, Dub / Voiceover, Trailer Cut, Social Resize
- Render queue with progress, Remove and Download render
- Save Draft and a Saved list of drafts and templates
Feature details:
- feature: Choosing a video | explanation: Open Render with a video id (the address carries an asset parameter) or choose one from the grid. Clicking a card loads it. Header shows the title and ID. | whyToUse: Render works on videos that already exist. | inputRequired: A video in your library. | restrictions: 'No videos in your library yet. Generate one in Video Studio, then open it in Render.' If the id is wrong: 'Video not found'.

chunks.title: Video Render — Features
chunks.text:
- feature: Presets | explanation: Clicking a preset sets the look and shows its Color Profile, Pacing and Export Profile, with a toast like 'Preset: Film Trailer Punch'. Luxury Brand Grade is measured and elegant, Documentary Contrast grounded, Film Trailer Punch aggressive and dramatic, Emotional Story Tone emotive and warm. | whyToUse: Quickly set a finishing style. | inputRequired: None. | restrictions: Presets are applied while exporting by the browser renderer; exact visual effect is not described beyond names.
- feature: Output settings | explanation: Output Format lists only the formats your browser can encode (WebM VP9, MP4 H.264, MP4 H.265). If none are detected it shows WebM (browser default). Frame Rate offers 24, 30 and 60. Quality is a slider with labels: 85 and above 'High quality master export', 60-84 'Standard quality', below 60 'Low quality draft'. | whyToUse: Control file type and size. | inputRequired: None; defaults apply. | restrictions: Some browsers cannot encode MP4 or H.265.

chunks.title: Video Render — Features
chunks.text:
- feature: Export Video | explanation: Starts the export in your browser, shows progress, validates the result and shows 'Video exported successfully'. Failures show messages such as 'Export produced no output' or 'Export failed validation: ...'. | whyToUse: Get the finished file. | inputRequired: A loaded video. | restrictions: Requires full access (see below). Without a video: 'Load a video first'.
- feature: Queue Render | explanation: Adds a job to the render queue ('Queued: ...'). The queue lists status, shows errors for failed jobs, offers Remove and, when done, a Download render link. A background processor works through the queue. Empty queue says 'No jobs in queue'. | whyToUse: Line up renders. | inputRequired: A loaded video. | restrictions: The queue works in this browser.
- feature: Download Frame | explanation: Saves the current frame as a PNG (file name ends _frame.png) and shows 'Frame downloaded'. | whyToUse: Grab a thumbnail or still. | inputRequired: A loaded video, positioned at the frame you want. | restrictions: None stated.

chunks.title: Video Render — Features
chunks.text:
- feature: Trailer Cut, Social Resize, Remix Scene | explanation: Trailer Cut builds a shorter trailer-style export ('Trailer cut exported'). Social Resize exports variants for aspect ratios 9:16 (1080x1920), 1:1 (1080x1080), 4:5 (1080x1350) and 16:9 (1920x1080) ('Social variants exported'). Remix Scene exports a remixed version ('Remix exported'). | whyToUse: Make platform-ready versions. | inputRequired: A loaded video. | restrictions: Each says '<name> produced no output' if the export fails.
- feature: Publish / Deliver | explanation: Exports a delivery package in MP4 (H.264), MP4 (H.265) and WebM (VP9). It reports 'Delivery package ready (N formats)' or that in-browser delivery is unavailable in this browser. Skipped formats are listed. | whyToUse: Get multiple formats at once. | inputRequired: A loaded video. | restrictions: Only formats your browser supports are produced.

chunks.title: Video Render — Features
chunks.text:
- feature: AI tiles | explanation: Create Shorts plans and exports vertical short clips. Generate Highlights detects standout scenes. Add Subtitles makes a subtitled video and reports the number of segments. Dub / Voiceover needs a script and makes narration. An AI Auto-Edit action also exists. Messages include 'Script is required for voiceover', 'No highlight scenes detected' and 'Could not generate short - no suitable scenes found'. | whyToUse: Fast repurposing. | inputRequired: A loaded video (and a script for voiceover). | restrictions: These call external services; if unreachable you see 'Service unavailable - please check configuration' or 'Subtitles unavailable - Director/VideoDB not reachable'.
- feature: Drafts, templates and saved items | explanation: Save Draft stores the current setup ('Draft saved'). Save as Template stores a template ('Saved as template'). Duplicate Render copies the last template ('Render duplicated') or says 'Nothing to duplicate yet - save a template first'. The Saved button toggles the saved list. Copy Prompt copies the prompt ('Prompt copied to clipboard'). Send to Storyboard sends the video to Storyboard. | whyToUse: Reuse settings and move work between studios. | inputRequired: None. | restrictions: Stored in this browser.

chunks.title: Video Render — Features
chunks.text:
- feature: Personalization overlays | explanation: If you set up personalization (logo, business name, CTA), those overlays can be drawn on exports. The export setting can disable them. | whyToUse: Brand each export. | inputRequired: Personalization data. | restrictions: Exact controls for disabling overlays were not confirmed.
Modes:
- Export Video
- Queue Render
- Trailer Cut
- Social Resize
- Remix Scene
- Create Shorts
- Generate Highlights
- Add Subtitles
- Dub / Voiceover
Mode details:
- mode: Export Video | description: Renders the current video with your settings. | useCase: Final file.
- mode: Queue Render | description: Adds the job to a queue. | useCase: Several renders in a row.
- mode: Trailer Cut | description: Builds a short trailer-style version. | useCase: Teasers.
- mode: Social Resize | description: Exports 9:16, 1:1, 4:5 and 16:9 variants. | useCase: Different platforms.
- mode: Create Shorts | description: Plans and exports short vertical clips. | useCase: Reels, Shorts, TikTok.

chunks.title: Video Render — Inputs and outputs
chunks.text:
Video Render (#/render). Inputs and outputs.
Inputs:
- Library video
- Preset
- Output Format
- Frame Rate
- Quality
- Script (for voiceover)
Required inputs:
- Library video
Optional inputs:
- Preset
- Output Format
- Frame Rate
- Quality

Input details:
- name: Library video | description: A video previously generated or saved. | required: true | whenToUse: Always. | restrictions: Must have a playable URL.
- name: Output Format | description: WebM (VP9), MP4 (H.264) or MP4 (H.265). | required: false | whenToUse: When you need a particular file type. | restrictions: Only formats your browser can encode are listed.
- name: Frame Rate | description: 24, 30 or 60 FPS. | required: false | whenToUse: Every export. | restrictions: None stated.
- name: Quality | description: Slider 1 to 100, default 82. | required: false | whenToUse: To balance size and clarity. | restrictions: 85 or higher is labelled master export.

- PNG frame
- Social aspect ratio variants

chunks.title: Video Render — Problems and limits
chunks.text:
Video Render (#/render). Problems and limits.
Troubleshooting:
- Load a video first: pick a video from the library grid.
- Video not found: the id is wrong or the video was deleted; choose another.
- Could not load video preview: the video URL may be broken or expired; reopen from the library.
- Export produced no output: try WebM, lower the Quality or try another browser.
- Export failed validation: the result file was unusable; export again.
- In-browser export for the requested formats is unavailable in this browser: switch browsers.
- Service unavailable - please check configuration: the AI service could not be reached; try again later.
- Script is required for voiceover: enter a script before using Dub / Voiceover.
Troubleshooting steps:
- issue: Export does nothing | steps: Check that a video is loaded.; If an upgrade prompt appears, complete access first.; Click Export Video again.
- issue: Exported file will not play | steps: Export as WebM (VP9).; Play it in a current browser.; Lower Quality if the file is very large.
Common problems:
- problem: MP4 option missing | whyItHappens: Your browser cannot encode MP4. | howToFix: Use WebM or another browser.
- problem: Library is empty | whyItHappens: No videos generated yet. | howToFix: Generate one in Video Studio, then open Render.

chunks.title: Video Render — Problems and limits
chunks.text:
- problem: Duplicate Render says nothing to duplicate | whyItHappens: No template saved yet. | howToFix: Click Save as Template first.
Limitations:
- Exports run in your browser and depend on which formats it can encode.
- Needs a video that already exists in your library.
- Actions require full access; otherwise an upgrade prompt appears.
- AI actions depend on external services.
Limit details:
- limitation: Browser encoding support | impact: Some formats do not appear or fail. | workaround: Use WebM, or try another browser such as current Chrome.
- limitation: Full access required | impact: Actions show an upgrade prompt. | workaround: Upgrade your plan or sign in with an account that has full access.
FAQs:
- question: What formats can I export? | answer: WebM (VP9), MP4 (H.264) and MP4 (H.265), limited to those your browser can encode.
- question: What is the default quality? | answer: The Quality slider starts at 82, labelled High quality master export from 85 upward.
- question: Which social sizes does Social Resize make? | answer: 9:16 (1080x1920), 1:1 (1080x1080), 4:5 (1080x1350) and 16:9 (1920x1080).
- question: Do I need a video first? | answer: Yes. Render edits videos made in other studios and shows your library to choose from.

chunks.title: Storyboard Studio — Overview
chunks.text:
Storyboard Studio (#/storyboard). Overview.
Description:
Storyboard Studio turns a short description into a plan of 3 to 12 shots, draws each shot as an AI image frame, and lets you edit, reorder, compare, save and export the result, or send it on to be animated or turned into a video.
Summary:
Plan scenes as AI storyboard frames, then turn them into video.
About:
Storyboard Studio has two stages. In the first stage ('Describe your storyboard') you write what you want to make, optionally customise video type, tone, total length, number of frames, audience, call to action, characters and look, and press 'Generate storyboard'. The studio plans the shots (using your OpenAI key if you have one, otherwise a built-in story-arc template) and, if 'Also generate frame images' is ticked, draws every frame. In the second stage you see the board: one card per frame with Shot, Camera, Seconds, 'What we see', 'Narration / dialogue', 'Director notes', a reference image option, a generate button and Animate / Publish actions. A toolbar offers Save, Load, Export (PDF shot sheet, CSV shot list, JSON), Add frame, Undo, Redo, Layout (Horizontal, Grid, Story), model and aspect ratio choices, 'Generate all frames', and a menu with GTM Boost, Recipes, Monetize, Prompts and Compare frames. 'Send to video studio' passes the frames to Cinema Templates.
Best for:

chunks.title: Storyboard Studio — Overview
chunks.text:
Anyone who wants to plan a video before making it: ad concepts, short films, explainers, social reels and client pitches. Also useful for keeping characters and look consistent across frames.
When to use it:
- You want to plan the shots of a video (shot type, camera move, length) before generating video.
- You want a visual shot list or PDF shot sheet to share with a client or team.
- You want consistent characters and setting across several images (use the 'Characters, setting and look' box and the previous-frame reference option).
- You want to quickly turn a one-paragraph idea into 3-12 frames with narration and director notes.
- You want to animate individual frames or pass the whole board into Cinema Templates.
When to use another studio:
- Use Video Studio (#/video) when you just want a video clip from a prompt or image without planning.
- Use Cinema Studio (#/cinema) when you want one cinematic shot with camera, lens and film-look controls.
- Use Cinema Templates (#/cinema-template) when you want a ready-made cinematic format; you can bring your storyboard there with 'Send to video studio'.
- Use Image Studio (#/image) when you only need a single image with full image controls.
- Use Animate (#/animate) to animate a single image.

chunks.title: Storyboard Studio — How to use
chunks.text:
Storyboard Studio (#/storyboard). How to use.
How to use:
1. Open Storyboard Studio from the side menu (#/storyboard). 2. In 'Describe your storyboard' type what you want to make. 3. Optional: open 'Customize (type, tone, length, frames, characters, style)' and set Video type, Tone, Total length, Frames, Audience, Call to action, 'Characters, setting and look' and the style/lighting/color grade. 4. Choose whether to keep 'Also generate frame images' ticked. 5. Click 'Generate storyboard'. 6. On the board, edit each frame's Shot, Camera, Seconds, 'What we see', 'Narration / dialogue' and 'Director notes'. 7. Pick the model and aspect ratio buttons in the toolbar. 8. Click 'Generate all frames' (or 'Generate frame' on a single card; 'Retry failed' for failures). 9. Reorder with the arrows, '+ Add frame', duplicate or delete as needed. 10. Type a Project name and click Save, then use Export (PDF shot sheet, CSV shot list, JSON). 11. Click '▶ Animate' on a frame or 'Send to video studio ▸' to continue in video.
Steps:
- Describe the story in the main box.
- Open Customize if you want to set tone, length, frames, characters and style.
- Click Generate storyboard.
- Edit frames and descriptions on the board.
- Generate or regenerate frame images.
- Save and export.
- Animate frames or send the board to Cinema Templates.
Getting started:

chunks.title: Storyboard Studio — How to use
chunks.text:
- Try: 'A 30-second launch ad for a trail-running shoe: a runner climbs a misty ridge at dawn, laces tighten, the city wakes below. End on Run further.'
- Leave everything else at default and click Generate storyboard.
- Add an OpenAI key in Settings if you want a custom AI-written story; without one the studio uses a built-in story-arc template and tells you so.
- If you are not signed in or have no key, a sign-in box appears when you try to draw images.
Tips:
- Start with 4-6 frames for a simple scene (built-in help tip).
- Describe camera angles for each shot for variety.
- Use consistent character descriptions across frames.
- Put the length in your description, like '30-second ad', and the studio sets the total length.
- Use '✨ Start from shot preset' when a description box is blank.
Best practices:
- Plan first, draw second: untick 'Also generate frame images' if you expect to edit the plan.
- Save with a clear project name and export JSON as a backup.
- Keep each 'What we see' to one clear visual.
- Check the timeline strip total against your target length.

chunks.title: Storyboard Studio — Features
chunks.text:
Storyboard Studio (#/storyboard). Features.
Key features:
- Story brief: description box plus 'Customize (type, tone, length, frames, characters, style)'.
- Automatic plan of 3 to 12 frames with shot type, camera movement, duration, visual description, narration and notes.
- Fallback template storyboard that follows a story arc (Hook, Setup, Problem, Turn, Detail, Action, Experience, Scale, Payoff) when no OpenAI key is available.
- Per-frame editing: Shot, Camera, Seconds, 'What we see', 'Narration / dialogue', 'Director notes', reference image, '✨ Start from shot preset', GTM enhance.
- Frame image generation for one frame, all frames ('Generate all frames' / 'Stop'), and 'Retry failed'.
- Toolbar: project name box, Save, Load, Export menu, '+ Add frame', Undo, Redo, Layout, model button, aspect ratio button, 'Send to video studio', Thumbnail, Personalize, and a tools menu.
- Generation settings panel: Negative prompt, Guidance scale, Steps, Seed and 'Use the previous frame as a reference'.
- Timeline strip showing the total length and each frame's shot, camera and seconds.
- Compare frames overlay (choose two frames side by side).
- Autosave after you have saved or loaded a project, and keyboard shortcuts Ctrl+S, Ctrl+Z, Ctrl+Shift+Z.
Feature details:

chunks.title: Storyboard Studio — Features
chunks.text:
- feature: Describe and generate a storyboard | explanation: Type your idea in 'What do you want your storyboard to be about?' (example placeholder: a 30-second launch ad for a trail-running shoe). Press 'Generate storyboard'. While it works the button reads 'Planning...' and placeholder cards say 'Planning shots...'. A length written in the text such as '30 second' or '2 minute' sets the total length if you have not set it yourself. | whyToUse: Fastest way to get a full shot plan. | inputRequired: A description or a title/subject. Otherwise 'Describe what you want to make first.' | restrictions: If frames already exist you are asked 'Replace the current frames with a new storyboard?'.
- feature: Customize panel | explanation: Optional fields: 'Title or subject (optional)', Video type (Commercial, Brand Film, Trailer, Social Reel, Testimonial, Documentary, Short Film, Explainer), Tone (Dramatic, Cinematic, Upbeat, Luxury, Gritty, Minimal, Emotional, Humorous), 'Total length (sec)' (minimum 6, maximum 300; default 60), 'Frames (3-12)', Audience, 'Call to action (optional)', 'Characters, setting and look (kept the same in every frame)', Visual style, Lighting and Color grade. | whyToUse: Steer the story and keep the same character and look in every frame. | inputRequired: None. | restrictions: Frames are clamped to 3-12. By default about one frame per 5 seconds of length.

chunks.title: Storyboard Studio — Features
chunks.text:
- feature: Also generate frame images | explanation: A checkbox next to the Generate button, ticked by default. When ticked and an image key is available, every frame is drawn right after planning. | whyToUse: Get pictures straight away. | inputRequired: An OpenAI key or a MuAPI key for images. | restrictions: Untick it to plan first and draw later with 'Generate all frames'.
- feature: Frame cards | explanation: Each frame has move earlier/later arrows, duplicate and delete buttons, an image area, a Shot list (Wide Shot, Medium Shot, Close-Up, Extreme Close-Up, POV, Overhead, Low Angle), a Camera list (Static, Pan Left, Pan Right, Tilt Up, Tilt Down, Dolly In, Dolly Out, Tracking, Handheld, Crane / Drone, Zoom In, Orbit), Seconds (1 to 60), 'What we see' ('Describe this shot...'), 'Narration / dialogue', 'Director notes', a reference image option, a button reading 'Generate frame' (or 'Regenerate' once there is an image) and the actions '▶ Animate' and 'Publish'. | whyToUse: Fine control over each shot. | inputRequired: A description for each frame you want drawn ('Describe this frame first.'). | restrictions: At most 40 frames in total ('That is plenty of frames. Delete some first.'). The last frame cannot be deleted.

chunks.title: Storyboard Studio — Features
chunks.text:
- feature: Start from shot preset | explanation: The button '✨ Start from shot preset' fills the description with a starter for the chosen shot type, for example Wide Shot becomes 'Establishing shot, wide angle, epic landscape, professional cinematography'. If the box already has text you are asked 'Replace this frame's description?'. | whyToUse: Overcome a blank page. | inputRequired: A shot type. | restrictions: Replaces the description.
- feature: Generate all frames / Retry failed | explanation: 'Generate all frames' draws every frame with a description, two at a time, with a progress bar and a count like '3/6 · 1 failed'. The same button becomes 'Stop'. 'Retry failed' reruns frames that failed. Finished frames are kept when you stop ('Stopped. Finished frames are kept.'). When done you see 'All frames generated' or 'N frame(s) failed. Use "Retry failed".'. | whyToUse: Draw the whole board in one go. | inputRequired: At least one frame with a description ('Describe at least one frame first.') and an API key. | restrictions: Each frame is tried up to 3 times before failing and each image has a 180-second time limit.

chunks.title: Storyboard Studio — Features
chunks.text:
- feature: Generation settings | explanation: A collapsed 'Generation settings' panel. 'Negative prompt' (example: blurry, text, watermark, extra fingers), 'Guidance scale', 'Steps' and 'Seed (-1 = random)' appear only when the selected model supports them. The checkbox 'Use the previous frame as a reference' feeds the previous frame's image into the next one to keep characters consistent. | whyToUse: Improve consistency and avoid unwanted details. | inputRequired: None. | restrictions: With an OpenAI key, frames are drawn by OpenAI and only the negative prompt applies; seed, guidance and steps apply to MuAPI models.
- feature: Save, Load and Export | explanation: Type a name in 'Project name' and press Save (Ctrl+S) or Load. Saved boards are listed under 'Saved storyboards' with an Open button. Export menu: 'PDF shot sheet', 'CSV shot list', 'JSON'. The PDF opens in a new window ('Popup blocked. Please allow popups to export PDF.' if blocked). | whyToUse: Keep and share your plan. | inputRequired: A project name; frames to export ('Nothing to export yet. Generate a storyboard first.'). | restrictions: Projects are saved in your browser. If storage is full or blocked: 'Could not save: browser storage is full or blocked. Export JSON instead.' Large images may be left out of a saved project ('Saved "name" without N large image(s). Export a PDF to keep them.').

chunks.title: Storyboard Studio — Features
chunks.text:
- feature: Layout, Undo and Redo | explanation: Layout list: Horizontal, Grid, Story. Undo and Redo buttons (Ctrl+Z, Ctrl+Shift+Z) step through your edits. | whyToUse: View the board your way and recover from mistakes. | inputRequired: None. | restrictions: Keyboard undo is ignored while you are typing in a text field.
- feature: Compare frames | explanation: In the tools menu choose '⚖ Compare frames' to open an overlay where you select two frames ('Frame 1', 'Frame 2') and view them side by side. Press Escape to close. | whyToUse: Check consistency between shots. | inputRequired: Two frames with images. | restrictions: Shows 'No image' for frames not generated yet.
- feature: Send to video studio and Animate | explanation: 'Send to video studio ▸' passes your frames to Cinema Templates, which opens with a 'Storyboard Loaded' banner. '▶ Animate' on a frame sends that frame's image, description (plus camera move) and duration to Animate (#/animate). | whyToUse: Turn the plan into video. | inputRequired: A generated image on the frame to animate ('Generate this frame first, then animate it.'). | restrictions: If browser storage is blocked: 'Could not pass the frame along (browser storage is blocked).'
Modes:
- AI-planned storyboard (needs OpenAI key)
- Template-planned storyboard (no OpenAI key)
- Build frames by hand ('or build the frames by hand')
- Per-frame image generation

chunks.title: Storyboard Studio — Features
chunks.text:
- Generate all frames
Mode details:
- mode: AI-planned storyboard | description: If you have an OpenAI key the studio asks it for a JSON plan of frames. Toast: 'Storyboard planned'. | useCase: Custom stories.
- mode: Template-planned storyboard | description: Without a key, or if the AI answer is unusable, a built-in story arc (Hook, Setup, Problem, Turn, Detail, Action, Experience, Scale, Payoff) is used. Toast: 'Storyboard planned from a template. Add an OpenAI key in Settings for a custom story.' | useCase: Quick generic structure.
- mode: Build by hand | description: Click 'or build the frames by hand' to start with an empty board and use '+ Add frame'. | useCase: Full manual control.
Models:

chunks.title: Storyboard Studio — Features
chunks.text: Frame images use text-to-image models. The model button lists the app's text-to-image catalog (84 models); the first and default model is Nano Banana. Other early entries are Flux Dev, Flux Kontext Dev T2I, an Ai Anime Generator, Wan2.1 Text To Image and Flux Kontext Pro T2I. If an OpenAI key is saved, frames are drawn by OpenAI first (sizes 1536x1024 for 16:9, 1024x1536 for 9:16 and 4:5, 1024x1024 for 1:1) and only fall back to the selected MuAPI model if OpenAI fails and a MuAPI key exists. The app's comparison table gives relative scores for some image models, for example Nano Banana price 1 speed 3 quality 4, Flux Dev price 3 speed 4 quality 5, Flux Schnell price 2 speed 2 quality 4, Seedream 5.0 price 4 speed 5 quality 5, Midjourney V7 price 5 speed 6 quality 5; these are relative numbers, not real prices. Planning text uses OpenAI only when a key is present.

chunks.title: Storyboard Studio — Inputs and outputs
chunks.text:
Storyboard Studio (#/storyboard). Inputs and outputs.
Inputs:
- Story description
- Title or subject
- Video type
- Tone
- Total length (sec)
- Frames (3-12)
- Audience
- Call to action
- Characters, setting and look
- Visual style
- Lighting
- Color grade
- Reference attachments
- Model
- Aspect ratio
- Per-frame Shot, Camera, Seconds, What we see, Narration / dialogue, Director notes
- Negative prompt, Guidance scale, Steps, Seed
- Reference image per frame
- Project name
Required inputs:
- A story description or a title/subject (to plan)
- A description for each frame you want drawn
Optional inputs:
- Everything under Customize
- Reference images
- Generation settings
- Narration and director notes
- Project name (needed only to save)
Input details:
- name: Story description | description: Plain-language idea. A phrase like '30 second' or '2 minute' sets the length. | required: true | whenToUse: Always when planning. | restrictions: Or provide a title/subject instead.
- name: Total length (sec) | description: Whole-story length. Minimum 6, maximum 300, default 60. Durations are split across frames in whole seconds. | required: false | whenToUse: Match your target video length. | restrictions: Each frame's Seconds is between 1 and 60.

chunks.title: Storyboard Studio — Inputs and outputs
chunks.text:
- name: Frames (3-12) | description: Number of frames. Default follows about one frame per 5 seconds. | required: false | whenToUse: More frames for more detail. | restrictions: Clamped to 3-12 when planning; you can add up to 40 by hand.
- name: Characters, setting and look | description: Text that is repeated in every frame prompt to keep characters and place consistent. | required: false | whenToUse: Whenever people or places repeat. | restrictions: Keep it short and specific.
- name: Aspect ratio | description: 16:9, 9:16, 1:1 or 4:5, limited to what the model supports. | required: false | whenToUse: Match the final video. | restrictions: Changing model may change the ratio to the model's first supported one.
- name: Reference image (per frame) | description: An uploaded or stock (Pexels) image attached to a frame to guide its look. | required: false | whenToUse: To match an existing look. | restrictions: MuAPI needs web URLs; inline images from OpenAI cannot be sent to it.
Outputs:
- A board of 3-12 (up to 40) frames with images, shot, camera, duration, description, narration and notes
- PDF shot sheet
- CSV shot list
- JSON file
- Saved project in the browser
- Frames passed to Animate or Cinema Templates

chunks.title: Storyboard Studio — Problems and limits
chunks.text:
Storyboard Studio (#/storyboard). Problems and limits.
Troubleshooting:
- 'Describe what you want to make first.': type a description or a title/subject before pressing Generate storyboard.
- 'Could not plan the storyboard: ...': the plan failed; the text after the colon is the reason; try again.
- 'Storyboard planned from a template. Add an OpenAI key in Settings for a custom story.': this is expected without an OpenAI key; edit frames by hand or add a key.
- 'Describe this frame first.': the frame's 'What we see' box is empty.
- 'Describe at least one frame first.': no frame has a description, so Generate all frames has nothing to draw.
- A frame shows 'Failed. Try again.' and a toast 'Frame N: ...': click Regenerate on that frame or 'Retry failed'; check your key and credits.
- A sign-in box appears when drawing: add an OpenAI or MuAPI key / sign in.
- 'Could not save: browser storage is full or blocked. Export JSON instead.': allow site storage or use Export > JSON.
- 'Type a project name. Saved: ...' or 'No saved storyboard named "x".': enter an existing name to Load.
- 'Popup blocked. Please allow popups to export PDF.': allow popups for this site and export again.
- 'Nothing to export yet. Generate a storyboard first.': create frames first.
- 'That is plenty of frames. Delete some first.': you reached the 40-frame limit.
Troubleshooting steps:

chunks.title: Storyboard Studio — Problems and limits
chunks.text:
- issue: Frames come out inconsistent | steps: Fill 'Characters, setting and look' with names, clothes and place.; Open Generation settings and tick 'Use the previous frame as a reference'.; Regenerate the frames that drift.
- issue: Generate all frames stops partway | steps: Check the progress label for the failed count.; Click 'Retry failed'.; If it keeps failing, change the model or check your key and credits.
- issue: I lost my storyboard | steps: Open the 'Saved storyboards' list or type the project name and click Load.; Use Undo (Ctrl+Z) for recent edits.; In future use Save and Export JSON.
- issue: Animate button does nothing useful | steps: Generate the frame image first.; Click '▶ Animate' again.; Allow browser storage if you see 'Could not pass the frame along'.
Common problems:
- problem: Only some frames have images | whyItHappens: 'Also generate frame images' was unticked, no image key was available, or some frames failed. | howToFix: Click 'Generate all frames' or 'Retry failed'.
- problem: Aspect ratio changed when I changed the model | whyItHappens: The new model does not support the current ratio. | howToFix: Choose the ratio again after changing the model.
- problem: Seed or steps not visible in Generation settings | whyItHappens: The selected model does not expose them. | howToFix: Choose a MuAPI model that does.

chunks.title: Storyboard Studio — Problems and limits
chunks.text:
- problem: Brief disappeared after generating | whyItHappens: The board stage shows a one-line summary of the brief. | howToFix: Click 'Edit brief' or 'New storyboard'.
Limitations:
- Planning yields 3 to 12 frames; you can add more by hand up to 40.
- Without an OpenAI key the story is a generic template, not a custom plan.
- Saved projects live in your browser's storage and may drop large images.
- Each image times out after 180 seconds and failed frames are retried up to 3 times.
- Seed, guidance and steps are used only with MuAPI models that expose them.
- Storyboard frames are still images; video comes from Animate, Video Studio or Cinema Templates.
Limit details:
- limitation: Browser-only saving | impact: Clearing site data or using another browser loses saved projects. | workaround: Export JSON or PDF regularly.
- limitation: Template story without an OpenAI key | impact: Frames follow a generic arc. | workaround: Add an OpenAI key in Settings or edit frames by hand.
- limitation: Consistency between frames | impact: Characters can still drift. | workaround: Fill 'Characters, setting and look' and tick 'Use the previous frame as a reference'.
FAQs:
- question: How many frames can I have? | answer: The planner makes 3 to 12 frames. You can add more with '+ Add frame', up to 40 in total.

chunks.title: Storyboard Studio — Problems and limits
chunks.text:
- question: Do I need an OpenAI key? | answer: Not required. Without one the studio plans from a built-in story-arc template and shows a message saying so. With one, the story is AI-written and frames are drawn by OpenAI. You still need either an OpenAI or MuAPI key to draw images.
- question: Does it make video? | answer: No, it makes still frames. Use '▶ Animate' on a frame or 'Send to video studio ▸' to continue in video tools.
- question: How do I keep characters the same? | answer: Describe them in 'Characters, setting and look' and tick 'Use the previous frame as a reference'.
- question: How do I export? | answer: Open the Export menu: PDF shot sheet, CSV shot list or JSON.
- question: Where is my project saved? | answer: In your browser's storage after you press Save or Load a named project. Export to keep a copy.
- question: What are the shot and camera choices? | answer: Shots: Wide Shot, Medium Shot, Close-Up, Extreme Close-Up, POV, Overhead, Low Angle. Camera: Static, Pan Left, Pan Right, Tilt Up, Tilt Down, Dolly In, Dolly Out, Tracking, Handheld, Crane / Drone, Zoom In, Orbit.
- question: Can I undo? | answer: Yes: Undo / Redo buttons or Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Shift+Z (not while typing in a text field).
- question: Can I start from scratch without AI planning? | answer: Yes. Click 'or build the frames by hand'.

chunks.title: Storyboard Studio — Glossary

chunks.title: Templates — Overview
chunks.text:
Templates (#/templates). Overview.
Description:
Templates is a browsable library of ready-made image and video templates. Pick one, add your media, and generate. It has 292 templates in total: 52 standard templates in 8 categories and 240 industry (niche) video templates.
Summary:
Ready-made templates: pick one, add your media, generate.
About:
Templates (route #/templates) shows the line "Ready-to-use templates. Pick one, add your media, and generate." Under it are a "Search templates..." box, filter chips (All, Standard, the template categories, then a divider and the industry/niche names), a short how-to strip, and sections of template cards. Each card has a thumbnail, an icon, the template name, a one-line description and a small "Video" or "Image" tag. Clicking a card opens it in the Template Studio at #/template/<template id> (the side-menu highlight stays on Templates). The library currently holds 292 templates (counted from the code): 52 standard templates (Social Media, Style Transfer, Entertainment, Commercial, VFX & Action, Portrait & Creator, Decade & Era, Camera & Cinematic) and 240 industry templates across 12 industries. The studio has Media Sources, AI Enhancer, Advanced controls, Generate, Download and Regenerate.
Best for:

chunks.title: Templates — Overview
chunks.text:
Getting a polished look or format fast without writing a long prompt: social videos and thumbnails, style conversions, product shots, VFX moments, and promo videos for local businesses.
When to use it:
- You have a photo and want a specific effect (anime, Ghibli, explosion, 1980s style).
- You want a ready-made social format (TikTok, Reel, thumbnail, banner).
- You run a local business (restaurant, salon, dental office, real estate and so on) and want a promo or brand film.
When to use another studio:
- For free-form images from a text prompt, use Image Studio (#/image).
- For free-form videos, use Video Studio (#/video).
- For cinematic shots with camera/lens controls, use Cinema Studio (#/cinema) or Cinema Templates (#/cinema-template).
- For inspiration first, use Explore (#/explore).

chunks.title: Templates — How to use
chunks.text:
Templates (#/templates). How to use.
How to use:
1. Open Templates from the left side menu. 2. Search with "Search templates..." or click a filter chip (All, Standard, a category, or an industry after the divider). 3. Click a template card to open it in the Template Studio. 4. Fill in the inputs the template shows (for example "Upload your photo" and a description) and, for video templates, add Media Sources if you want. 5. Leave AI Enhancer on (default) or turn it off. 6. Optionally open Advanced controls. 7. Press Generate. 8. When it finishes, use Download, Publish to Social or Regenerate. Results are also saved in Library.
Steps:
- Open Templates from the left side menu.
- Search or filter and click a template card.
- Upload your photo or enter the description/inputs shown.
- Check the Model picker and AI Enhancer toggle.
- Press Generate and wait; press Cancel during generation if you need to stop.
- Download, Regenerate or find the result in Library.
Getting started:
- Try "Anime Converter" or "TikTok Video Creator" for a quick first result: upload a photo, add a short description, press Generate.
- Save your MuAPI key first; without it a key prompt appears when you press Generate.
Tips:
- Use the search box: it matches name, description, category, output type and niche.
- Describe subject, setting and mood in one or two sentences.
Best practices:

chunks.title: Templates — How to use
chunks.text: - Upload a clear, well-lit photo for image-based templates.

chunks.title: Templates — Problems and limits
chunks.text:
Templates (#/templates). Problems and limits.
Troubleshooting:
- "Please upload an image before generating.": add a photo in the template input.
- "Please upload a video before generating.": you chose the video-to-video route; attach a source video or remove it.
- "Please enter a prompt or description before generating.": fill the description field.
- "Please enter a longer prompt": add more words.
- "No output URL returned" or placeholder warning: try again; if repeated, change the model.
Troubleshooting steps:
- issue: Generate does nothing / asks for a key | steps: Add your Muapi API Key in Settings (labelled "Muapi API Key").; Press Generate again.
Limitations:
- Needs your own MuAPI key.
- Image-based templates require an upload.
- Extend is Seedance 2.0 only.
- Some industry category chips can show an empty list.
Limit details:
