chunks.title: Timeline Editor — Overview
chunks.text:
Timeline Editor (#/timeline). Overview.
Description:
A multi-track video editor in your browser with a project manager, media pool, source and timeline viewers, trim tools, AI generation tools (Fill Gap, Extend, Music, Mask) and an Export tab. The header shows the product name TIMELINE STUDIO EDITOR.
Summary:
Multi-track timeline for editing and rendering your videos, with built-in AI tools.
About:
Timeline Editor (#/timeline) is the full non-linear editor. It opens on a Project Manager where you create or open a project, then shows a workspace with the top tabs Elements, Spaces, Director, Edit, LLM, Export and Leads. The Edit tab is the editor itself: a media pool, a source viewer and timeline viewer, a tool sidebar (Selection, Blade, Ripple Trim, Roll Trim, Slip, Slide, Music, Fill Gap, Extend, Mask), multiple tracks with mute, solo and lock, clip properties (transform, effects, transitions, zoom, captions), keyframes, markers, snapping and multiple timeline tabs. The Export tab renders the timeline to MP4 at Draft 720p, Standard 1080p or High Quality 4K, at 24, 30 or 60 fps, and can also export an FCPXML file for Final Cut Pro, Premiere and DaVinci Resolve. A classic, older version of the editor is still reachable at #/timeline-classic and has its own AI Assistant chat with Ask, Search, Cut and Timeline modes.
Best for:

chunks.title: Timeline Editor — Overview
chunks.text:
Creators and marketers who want to assemble clips, music, voice-over and AI-generated footage on a real multi-track timeline, trim precisely, and export a finished MP4 without leaving the browser.
When to use it:
- You have several clips, images, music or voice-over and want to arrange them on tracks in order.
- You need precise trimming (ripple, roll, slip, slide) or want to split a clip at the playhead with the Blade tool.
- You want to bridge a gap between two clips with AI footage (Fill Gap) or lengthen a clip (Extend).
- You want AI-made background music that fits your video (Music Tool).
- You want to mask or isolate an object in a clip (Mask Tool).
- You want to finish with a rendered MP4 at 720p, 1080p or 4K, or hand the edit to Final Cut Pro, Premiere or DaVinci Resolve as FCPXML.
When to use another studio:
- Use Video Render (#/render) when you already have a finished generated video and only want to re-export it, make a trailer cut, social resize or shorts, without building a timeline.
- Use Video Tools (#/videotools) for quick one-off video operations rather than a full edit.
- Use Director (#/director) or Video (#/video) when you want to generate the clips first from prompts, then bring them here to edit.
- Use Personalizer (#/personalizer) when you want to build a personalized page or asset set for each contact rather than edit a video.

chunks.title: Timeline Editor — Overview
chunks.text: - Use Audio (#/audio) to create voice-overs or music as separate files before importing them.

chunks.title: Timeline Editor — How to use
chunks.text:
Timeline Editor (#/timeline). How to use.
How to use:
1. Open Timeline Editor from the side menu or go to #/timeline. 2. In the Project Manager, click New project, type a name in the Project name... box and open it. 3. Open the Edit tab. 4. Import or generate media into the media pool and drag clips onto tracks in the timeline. 5. Press Space to play and pause; use Left and Right arrows to step one frame. 6. Pick a tool from the sidebar (for example Blade Tool, B) to split clips, or use trim tools to adjust them. 7. Click a clip to change its properties, or right-click it for the clip menu. 8. Optionally use Fill Gap, Extend, Music Tool or Mask Tool for AI help. 9. Open the Export tab, choose a Preset, Frame Rate and Aspect ratio. 10. Click Render and wait for the progress to finish, then download the MP4. 11. Optionally click Export FCPXML to continue in another editor.
Steps:
- Open #/timeline and create a project with New project.
- Switch to the Edit tab.
- Add media to the media pool and drag it to tracks.
- Trim and split clips using the sidebar tools or shortcuts.
- Add music, effects, transitions or AI-generated fills where needed.
- Open Export, choose Preset, Frame Rate and Aspect ratio, then click Render.
Getting started:
- Create a project from the Project Manager, then go to the Edit tab.

chunks.title: Timeline Editor — How to use
chunks.text:
- Learn three shortcuts first: Space (play/pause), B (Blade) and V (Selection).
- Add a couple of clips, split one with the Blade, and press Render on the Export tab to see the whole path once.
- If you want the AI chat, add your OpenAI key in Settings first.
Tips:
- Turn Snap on to avoid tiny accidental gaps.
- Use markers to note beats or places to fix.
- Use Draft preset for test exports and High Quality only for the final.
- Rename timeline tabs so you remember which cut is which.
- Use the proxy toggle on large projects.
Best practices:
- Lock tracks you are finished with.
- Keep music, voice and effects on separate audio tracks.
- Check the aspect ratio and fit before exporting vertical or square videos.
- Enable the post-export check to catch black frames or silence.

chunks.title: Timeline Editor — Features
chunks.text:
Timeline Editor (#/timeline). Features.
Key features:
- Project Manager home screen with New project and Project name... field
- Top tabs: Elements, Spaces, Director, Edit, LLM, Export, Leads (plus Settings)
- Multi-track timeline with Add Track, track Mute / Solo / Lock buttons
- Tool sidebar: Selection (V), Blade (B), Ripple Trim (R), Roll Trim (N), Slip (Y), Slide (U), Music, Fill Gap, Extend (E), Mask (X)
- Source viewer and Timeline viewer with playback and frame stepping
- Snap toggle (S) and Add Marker (M) in the timeline tab bar
- Multiple timeline tabs inside one project (New Timeline, Close timeline)
- Fill Gap and Extend AI generation modals
- Music generation popup and a sound effects library
- Voice-over recording at the playhead
- Audio sync and batch sync, plus a proxy toggle for smoother playback on big projects
- Link / unlink audio from video (Ctrl or Cmd + L)
- Frame Chat on the clip under the playhead (Ctrl or Cmd + Shift + Space)
- Undo and redo (Ctrl or Cmd + Z, add Shift to redo)
- Export tab with preset, frame rate, aspect ratio, fit, bitrate, master quality and optional post-export check
- FCPXML export for Final Cut Pro, Premiere and DaVinci Resolve
- Leads tab to publish an interactive version and collect leads
Feature details:

chunks.title: Timeline Editor — Features
chunks.text:
- feature: Project Manager | explanation: When you open #/timeline you land on a Project Manager titled TIMELINE STUDIO EDITOR. You create a project with the New project button, type a name in the Project name... box, and open it. The open project is remembered in the page address (a project parameter), and a Back to Projects button in the top bar returns you to the list. | whyToUse: Keeps each edit separate so you can come back to it later. | inputRequired: A project name. | restrictions: Projects from the earlier build are imported once automatically. The List view, Export and Import buttons at the bottom of the Project Manager are disabled in the code.
- feature: Edit tab - media pool and viewers | explanation: The Edit tab has a collapsible media pool on the left for your imported or generated media, a source viewer for scrubbing a single clip, and a timeline viewer that plays the whole edit. You drag media from the pool onto tracks. | whyToUse: This is where you actually build the cut. | inputRequired: Imported or generated media (video, image, audio). | restrictions: Preview quality depends on your computer; use the proxy toggle (tooltips: Using proxy files for playback / Using original files for playback) if playback stutters.

chunks.title: Timeline Editor — Features
chunks.text: - feature: Tool sidebar and shortcuts | explanation: The sidebar offers Selection Tool (V), Blade Tool (B), Ripple Trim (R), Roll Trim (N), Slip (Y), Slide (U), Music Tool (M label), Fill Gap Tool, Extend Tool (E) and Mask Tool (X). The A key switches to a track-forward selection tool. Hovering a tool shows its name and shortcut as a tooltip. | whyToUse: Different tools make different edits fast: Blade cuts, Ripple closes gaps while trimming, Roll moves the cut point between two clips, Slip changes which part of a clip shows without moving it, Slide moves a clip between its neighbours. | inputRequired: A clip on the timeline. | restrictions: Shortcuts do not fire while you are typing in a text box, number field or dropdown. In the code, the M label on the Music Tool is shown but the keyboard handler for M is used for Add Marker; click the Music Tool icon to be sure. Fill Gap has no shortcut label in the sidebar, although the G key selects it.

chunks.title: Timeline Editor — Features
chunks.text:
- feature: Tracks | explanation: Each track row has a header with Lock/Unlock, Mute/Unmute and Solo/Unsolo buttons and a name you can rename. Add Track at the bottom bar adds a track; buttons Fit tracks to view and Fit timeline to view adjust zoom. The video and audio areas can be resized, and double-clicking the divider resets the split to half and half. | whyToUse: Layer b-roll over main footage, keep music and voice on separate audio tracks, and lock tracks you do not want to disturb. | inputRequired: None. | restrictions: There is also a Delete empty tracks action in the editor code; exact menu wording is not confirmed.
- feature: Clip right-click menu and linking audio | explanation: Right-clicking a clip shows a menu with cut, copy and paste (shown as X, C, V shortcuts), link or unlink audio (Ctrl or Cmd + L), a Delete action (Backspace), and Send Frame to Spaces. You can also select several clips with Shift or Cmd/Ctrl click. | whyToUse: Quick editing without hunting through panels; linking audio keeps a video clip and its sound moving together. | inputRequired: One or more selected clips. | restrictions: Ctrl or Cmd + L only works when the selection can be linked or unlinked.

chunks.title: Timeline Editor — Features
chunks.text:
- feature: Clip properties panel | explanation: Selecting a clip opens a properties panel with sections for transform (position, scale and similar sliders), layout, effects, transitions, zoom, captions, multicam, analyze and fade In / Out. Opacity and volume can be keyframed on a keyframe track per clip. | whyToUse: Fine control over how each clip looks and sounds. | inputRequired: A selected clip. | restrictions: Which sections appear depends on the clip type (video, image, audio, captions).
- feature: Snap and Markers | explanation: The bar above the tracks has a Snap button (tooltip Snap ON or Snap OFF with shortcut S) and a Marker button (Add Marker, shortcut M). Snap pulls clips to neighbouring edges and the playhead. | whyToUse: Keeps clips aligned with no accidental gaps; markers flag beats or notes. | inputRequired: None. | restrictions: None confirmed.
- feature: Multiple timelines | explanation: Timeline tabs above the tracks let you keep several edits of one project. Click the plus button (New Timeline) to add one (named Timeline 2, Timeline 3, and so on), rename by editing the tab name, and close with the Close timeline button. | whyToUse: Try alternative cuts, a short version and a long version, without duplicating the project. | inputRequired: None. | restrictions: Each tab is its own timeline; export always renders the active timeline.

chunks.title: Timeline Editor — Features
chunks.text:
- feature: Fill Gap | explanation: Fill Gap asks AI to generate footage that bridges a gap between two clips, using the surrounding frames for context. You type a prompt describing what should happen in the gap and generate. Ctrl or Cmd + Enter submits, Escape closes. | whyToUse: Smooth a jump cut or cover a missing moment without re-shooting. | inputRequired: A gap between two clips and a prompt. | restrictions: If the prompt is empty you see 'Enter a prompt describing what should happen in this gap'. The README says it uses Kling 3.0; a provider key may be needed in Settings.
- feature: Extend | explanation: Extend lengthens a clip before or after using an AI video model, taking a reference frame from the source clip. You describe what the extension should show. | whyToUse: Make a shot a little longer to cover narration or a transition. | inputRequired: A clip and a prompt. | restrictions: Empty prompt gives 'Enter a prompt describing what the extension should show'. If no frame can be read you see 'Could not extract reference frame from source clip. Try scrubbing the clip first.' The README says it supports 9 video models.

chunks.title: Timeline Editor — Features
chunks.text:
- feature: Music Tool and sound effects | explanation: The Music Tool opens a music generation popup with genre, mood, style and tempo presets and an instrumental option (per the project README). The sidebar also has a Sound effects library button and a voice-over recorder button (Record voice-over / Stop recording) that records at the playhead. | whyToUse: Add a soundtrack, effects or narration without leaving the editor. | inputRequired: Optional: a prompt or preset choices. | restrictions: Microphone permission is needed for voice-over. AI music needs a configured provider.
- feature: Mask Tool | explanation: The Mask Tool (X) opens the source viewer mask tool, which can segment an object with text, click or box prompts and preview as red overlay, white-on-black or cutout (per the README). | whyToUse: Isolate a subject for effects or replacement. | inputRequired: A clip and a prompt, click or box. | restrictions: Needs an AI segmentation provider; availability is not confirmed from the page code.

chunks.title: Timeline Editor — Features
chunks.text: - feature: Frame Chat | explanation: Pressing Ctrl or Cmd + Shift + Space opens Frame Chat on the video or image clip under the playhead. If nothing editable is under the playhead it falls back to chat-only. A separate shortcut on the same keys is also registered by the workspace for Voice Director. | whyToUse: Ask questions about, or edit, a single frame. | inputRequired: A playhead over a video or image clip (optional). | restrictions: Two handlers listen to the same key combination in the code; which one you see first is not confirmed.

chunks.title: Timeline Editor — Features
chunks.text:
- feature: Export tab | explanation: Export (subtitle: Render your timeline as an MP4 video) has: Preset (Draft 720p, Standard 1080p, High Quality 4K), Frame Rate (24, 30 or 60 fps, default 30), Aspect ratio, a Contain (whole picture) or Cover (fill frame) fit, Video bitrate (Auto, Compact (smaller file), Recommended, High (larger file), Custom...), a Master quality (higher default bitrate) checkbox, and a checkbox to check the finished export (duration, size, black / frozen frames, silence, peak level). Click Render to start. Progress is checked every 2 seconds. | whyToUse: Produces the final deliverable. | inputRequired: At least one clip on the timeline. | restrictions: Render is disabled with the tooltip 'Add clips to the timeline first' and the hint 'Add clips to the timeline in the Edit tab before exporting.' when the timeline is empty. Default preset is Standard and default frame rate 30.
- feature: Export FCPXML | explanation: The Export FCPXML button downloads the active timeline as an .fcpxml file for Final Cut Pro, Premiere and DaVinci Resolve. | whyToUse: Finish the edit in a desktop editor. | inputRequired: A timeline with clips. | restrictions: The page says: Relink the media after import.

chunks.title: Timeline Editor — Features
chunks.text: - feature: Leads tab | explanation: The Leads tab (Publish & collect leads) lets you publish an interactive version of the video with forms and buttons and collect leads from it. The Export tab links to it. | whyToUse: Turn a video into a lead capture page. | inputRequired: A finished timeline. | restrictions: Detailed Leads steps were not reviewed in depth.

chunks.title: Timeline Editor — Features
chunks.text:
- feature: Classic editor AI Assistant chat | explanation: The classic editor at #/timeline-classic has an AI Assistant panel with four modes: Ask (questions about the project), Search (find quotes and moments; answers include clickable timestamp buttons that move the playhead), Cut (rough cut or selects shown as a table with an Apply as new timeline tab button) and Timeline (pacing and edit suggestions, each with a Do it with AI Agent button). You can @mention a clip, use skill chips (Shot List, Rough Cut, Remove Dead Space, Selects & Highlights, B-Roll Planner, Prompt Writer, Editorial Brief, Delivery Prep), press Enter to send and Shift+Enter for a new line. A token counter is shown. | whyToUse: Get editing ideas and rough cuts from the footage's own transcript and tags. | inputRequired: A message; an OpenAI key. | restrictions: Uses your own OpenAI key. Without it you see: 'This uses your own OpenAI key. Add it in Settings -> API keys (OpenAI API Key).' If you are signed out you may see 'Sign in to use the AI assistant.'
Modes:
- Fill Gap
- Extend
- Music Tool
- Mask Tool
Mode details:
- mode: Selection Tool (V) | description: Select, move and arrange clips. | useCase: Everyday arranging.
- mode: Blade Tool (B) | description: Cut a clip at the cursor. | useCase: Remove a mistake or split a long shot.

chunks.title: Timeline Editor — Features
chunks.text:
- mode: Ripple Trim (R) | description: Trim a clip edge and shift later clips to close the gap. | useCase: Shorten a clip without leaving a hole.
- mode: Roll Trim (N) | description: Move the cut point between two neighbouring clips. | useCase: Adjust where one shot hands over to the next without changing total length.
- mode: Slip (Y) | description: Change which part of a clip is shown without moving the clip. | useCase: Find a better moment inside the same slot.
- mode: Slide (U) | description: Move a clip while its neighbours adjust. | useCase: Reorder timing between two clips.
- mode: Fill Gap | description: AI creates footage to bridge a gap. | useCase: Hide a jump or missing moment.
- mode: Extend (E) | description: AI adds footage before or after a clip. | useCase: Make a shot longer.
- mode: Mask (X) | description: Segment an object with prompts. | useCase: Isolate a subject.
- mode: Classic chat: Ask / Search / Cut / Timeline | description: Four modes of the AI Assistant in #/timeline-classic. | useCase: Q and A, finding moments, rough cuts, pacing advice.
Models:

chunks.title: Timeline Editor — Features
chunks.text: From the README (not verified at runtime): Fill Gap uses Kling 3.0; Extend supports 9 video models; the Spaces tab lists 50+ image, video and audio models. The classic AI chat runs on the OpenAI Responses API through /api/timeline-llm with your own OpenAI key and strict JSON output; the default model name is set on the server and can be overridden by environment variables. Speed adjustment is listed as 0.1x to 2x in the README.

Input details:
- name: Project name | description: Name typed into the Project name... box when creating a project. | required: true | whenToUse: Once at the start of each project. | restrictions: None stated in the code.
- name: Media (video, image, audio) | description: Files or generated assets placed in the media pool and dragged onto tracks. | required: true | whenToUse: Whenever you build a cut. | restrictions: Supported file types are not listed in the reviewed files.
- name: Fill Gap / Extend prompt | description: A text description of what the generated footage should show. | required: false | whenToUse: When using the AI generation tools. | restrictions: Cannot be empty when you generate.
- name: Export Preset | description: Draft (720p), Standard (1080p) or High Quality (4K). | required: false | whenToUse: Every export. | restrictions: Default is Standard.

chunks.title: Timeline Editor — Inputs and outputs
chunks.text:
- name: Frame Rate | description: 24 fps, 30 fps or 60 fps. | required: false | whenToUse: Every export. | restrictions: Default is 30 fps.
- name: Aspect ratio and fit | description: The frame shape of the project, with Contain (whole picture) or Cover (fill frame). The README lists 16:9, 4:3, 21:9, 1:1 and 9:16. | required: false | whenToUse: When making vertical or square videos. | restrictions: Exact list shown in the dropdown comes from the code's aspect list; the output size is displayed next to it.

chunks.title: Timeline Editor — Problems and limits
chunks.text:
Timeline Editor (#/timeline). Problems and limits.
Troubleshooting:
- Render button is greyed out: add clips to the timeline in the Edit tab first.
- Fill Gap says to enter a prompt: type a description of what should happen in the gap, then generate.
- Extend says it could not extract a reference frame: scrub the source clip first, then try again.
- AI chat says it uses your own OpenAI key: add the OpenAI API Key in Settings -> API keys.
- AI chat says Sign in to use the AI assistant: sign in to your account and try again.
- A keyboard shortcut does nothing: click on an empty part of the page, because shortcuts are ignored while a text box or dropdown has focus.
- Playback stutters: switch on the proxy toggle so the editor plays lightweight copies.
- Exported file looks cropped or has bars: change the Contain / Cover fit and the Aspect ratio before rendering.
Troubleshooting steps:
- issue: Cannot start an export | steps: Go to the Edit tab and confirm there is at least one clip on a track.; Return to Export and click Render.; If it still fails, check the progress card for an error message.
- issue: AI generation (Fill Gap, Extend, Music) fails | steps: Open Settings and check that the provider or account used by the tool is connected.; Make sure the prompt is not empty.; Try again; if a clip frame could not be read, scrub the clip first.

chunks.title: Timeline Editor — Problems and limits
chunks.text:
- issue: AI chat in the classic editor does not answer | steps: Open Settings -> API keys and add the OpenAI API Key.; Sign in if asked.; Try a shorter question; very large projects are truncated to fit.
Common problems:
- problem: Shortcut M does not select the Music Tool | whyItHappens: M is used for Add Marker in the timeline. | howToFix: Click the Music Tool in the sidebar.
- problem: Render finished but I cannot find the file | whyItHappens: The finished job appears in the Export tab progress area. | howToFix: Open the Export tab and use the download link on the latest job.
- problem: Cmd or Ctrl + L does nothing | whyItHappens: No linkable or unlinkable audio is selected. | howToFix: Select a video clip and its audio together, or right-click for the menu.
- problem: Edit disappeared after leaving the page | whyItHappens: You may be in a different project or timeline tab. | howToFix: Go back via Back to Projects, reopen the project, and check the timeline tabs.
Limitations:
- Export requires at least one clip on the timeline.
- AI tools need configured provider keys or accounts.
- The classic AI chat needs your own OpenAI key.
- FCPXML export requires relinking media in the other editor.
- Keyboard shortcuts are ignored while typing in input boxes.
Limit details:

chunks.title: Timeline Editor — Problems and limits
chunks.text:
- limitation: Empty timeline cannot be rendered | impact: The Render button is disabled. | workaround: Add at least one clip in the Edit tab first.
- limitation: AI chat needs an OpenAI key | impact: Chat returns an error asking for the key. | workaround: Add the OpenAI API Key in Settings -> API keys.
- limitation: Heavy projects may play back slowly | impact: Stuttering preview. | workaround: Turn on the proxy toggle for playback.
- limitation: FCPXML does not carry media | impact: Media appears offline in the other editor. | workaround: Relink the media after import.
FAQs:
- question: What quality can I export? | answer: Draft is 720p, Standard is 1080p and High Quality is 4K, at 24, 30 or 60 frames per second. The defaults are Standard and 30 fps.
- question: What format does it export? | answer: The Export tab renders an MP4 video. You can also export an FCPXML file.
- question: What are the keyboard shortcuts? | answer: Space plays or pauses, Left and Right arrows step one frame, V Selection, A track-forward select, B Blade, R Ripple Trim, N Roll Trim, Y Slip, U Slide, G Fill Gap, E Extend, X Mask, S Snap, M Add Marker, Delete or Backspace removes selected clips, Ctrl or Cmd + Z undo, add Shift for redo, Ctrl or Cmd + L link or unlink audio.

chunks.title: Timeline Editor — Problems and limits
chunks.text:
- question: Do I need my own key for the AI chat? | answer: Yes. The AI Assistant in the classic editor uses your own OpenAI key, added in Settings -> API keys as OpenAI API Key.
- question: Where is the older editor? | answer: At #/timeline-classic. It has the AI Assistant chat with Ask, Search, Cut and Timeline modes, Insert and Overwrite modes and a Snap button.
- question: Can I undo? | answer: Yes, press Ctrl or Cmd + Z. Add Shift to redo.
- question: Can I work on several edits in one project? | answer: Yes, use the plus button (New Timeline) in the timeline tab bar.

chunks.title: Timeline Editor — Workflows and use cases
chunks.text:
Timeline Editor (#/timeline). Workflows and use cases.
Example workflows:
- title: Quick social cut | steps: Create a project and open the Edit tab.; Drop two or three clips on a video track.; Press B and click to cut off unwanted parts, then delete them.; Add a music track from the Music Tool.; In Export, set Aspect ratio to 9:16, Preset to Standard, Frame Rate to 30.; Click Render and download the MP4.
- title: Bridge a jump cut with AI | steps: Place two clips with a small gap between them.; Choose the Fill Gap Tool.; Describe what should happen in the gap and generate.; Play through the join and keep or undo with Ctrl or Cmd + Z.
- title: Hand off to a desktop editor | steps: Finish the rough cut in the Edit tab.; Open Export and click Export FCPXML.; Import the file into Final Cut Pro, Premiere or DaVinci Resolve.; Relink the media files.
- title: Rough cut with the classic AI chat | steps: Open #/timeline-classic with a transcribed project.; Switch the chat to Cut mode.; Ask for a 30 second highlight cut.; Click Apply as new timeline tab and review the result.
Use cases:
- title: Promo video assembly | description: Combine product footage, voice-over and music. | steps: Import footage.; Arrange on tracks.; Record voice-over at the playhead.; Export 1080p. | expectedOutput: A finished MP4.

chunks.title: Timeline Editor — Workflows and use cases
chunks.text:
- title: Alternative versions | description: Make a short and long cut in one project. | steps: Build the long cut.; Click New Timeline.; Copy clips into it and trim.; Export each timeline separately. | expectedOutput: Two MP4 files.
Related studios:
- studio: render | relationship: Finishing and re-export of existing videos | whenToMove: You have one finished video and only need a trailer cut, social resize or format variants. | why: Render does not need a timeline.
- studio: video | relationship: Source of clips | whenToMove: You need new clips generated from prompts. | why: Generate there, then edit here.
- studio: audio | relationship: Source of voice and music | whenToMove: You want a standalone voice-over or track. | why: Create it, then import.
- studio: library | relationship: Where your assets live | whenToMove: You want to find saved videos to edit. | why: Library lists your generated media.

chunks.title: Timeline Editor — Glossary
chunks.text: Glossary: Timeline: The strip where clips are arranged in time, left to right. | Track: A horizontal lane that holds clips; there are video and audio tracks. | Clip: A piece of media placed on a track. | Playhead: The marker showing the current moment in the edit. | Blade: A tool that cuts a clip in two. | Ripple: A trim that also shifts later clips to close or open gaps. | Roll: A trim that moves the cut between two neighbouring clips. | Slip: Changes which part of a clip is visible without moving it. | Slide: Moves a clip between its neighbours. | Proxy: A light copy of media used for smoother playback. | FCPXML: An exchange file that other editors can open. | Keyframe: A saved value at a point in time, used to animate opacity or volume. | Bitrate: How much data per second the video uses; higher is bigger and sharper.

chunks.title: Upscale Suite — Overview
chunks.text:
Upscale Suite (#/upscale). Overview.
Description:
Upscale Suite makes a low-resolution or soft image larger and sharper with AI. You upload an image, pick one of three upscale methods, click Upscale Image and download the bigger result.
Summary:
Enlarge and sharpen images with AI (AI Upscaler, Topaz, Seed Upscale).
About:
Upscale Suite is a small, single-purpose studio. At the top you choose a method with a button that defaults to 'AI Upscaler'; the method list has three entries: AI Upscaler (general-purpose, with a 2x or 4x scale factor), Topaz Upscale (premium Topaz-quality enhancement) and Seed Upscale (SeedVR2 high-fidelity upscaling). You upload an image (or pick a Pexels stock photo), click 'Upscale Image', and the enlarged image appears below with a Download link and a Publish to Social button. The header reads 'Upscale and enhance images up to 4x with AI'. The studio upscales still images; the three methods are image-upscale models.
Best for:
Anyone with a good picture that is too small, blurry or low resolution for print, a website banner or a presentation: old photos, AI images generated at a small size, screenshots, product photos.
When to use it:
- A picture is too small or pixelated for where you want to use it.
- You generated an image in Image Studio at a low resolution and want a bigger version.
- You want a quick, one-click enlargement without writing a prompt.

chunks.title: Upscale Suite — Overview
chunks.text:
- You want to try a premium method (Topaz Upscale) or a high-fidelity method (Seed Upscale) on the same image.
When to use another studio:
- Use Edit Studio (#/edit) when you want to change the content of a photo (remove objects or background, effects, face swap). Its Upscale tool also lists the same three upscalers with each model's own settings.
- Use Image Studio (#/image) when you want to generate or restyle an image rather than just enlarge it.
- Use Video Studio (#/video), Video Tools (#/videotools) or AI VFX (#/ai-vfx) when your media is a video clip.
- Use Library (#/library) to find an earlier generation you want to upscale.

chunks.title: Upscale Suite — How to use
chunks.text:
Upscale Suite (#/upscale). How to use.
How to use:
1. Open Upscale Suite from the side menu (Upscale). 2. Click the method button at the top (it shows 'AI Upscaler') and choose AI Upscaler, Topaz Upscale or Seed Upscale. 3. Click the upload button at the left of the form and add your image (or click the Pexels button to choose a stock photo). 4. If you chose AI Upscaler, click Advanced and pick 2x or 4x under Scale Factor. 5. Click 'Upscale Image'. 6. Wait while the button says 'Upscaling...'. 7. When the result card appears, click Download to save the larger image, or Publish to Social to share it.
Steps:
- Choose a method with the method button.
- Upload the image (or pick one from Pexels).
- For AI Upscaler, open Advanced and choose 2x or 4x.
- Click Upscale Image.
- Download or Publish to Social from the result card.
Getting started:
- Keep AI Upscaler and 2x for your first try; it is the default.
- Compare the result by opening the original and the download side by side.
- If you want a different look, run the same image with Topaz Upscale or Seed Upscale.
Tips:
- Start from the best original you have.
- Try 2x before 4x; bigger is not always cleaner.
- Run the same image through two methods and compare.
- Upscale as the last step, after editing and generating.
Best practices:
- Keep a copy of the original.

chunks.title: Upscale Suite — How to use
chunks.text:
- Download the upscaled result right away; only the latest one is shown on the page.
- Use Edit Studio's Upscale tool when you need Topaz 4x/8x or SeedVR2 resolution control or a Before/After slider.

chunks.title: Upscale Suite — Features
chunks.text:
Upscale Suite (#/upscale). Features.
Key features:
- Three upscale methods in a provider-style picker: AI Upscaler (MuAPI), Topaz Upscale (Topaz) and Seed Upscale (ByteDance).
- Scale Factor choice of 2x or 4x for AI Upscaler (default 2x), found in the Advanced panel.
- Upload an image with the picker button, or browse stock photos with the Pexels button.
- 'Upscale Image' button that shows 'Upscaling...' while it works.
- Result card with the enlarged image, a Download link and a Publish to Social button.
- Thumbnail button to generate a custom studio thumbnail.
- Tools menu (three dots) with Recipes, Monetize and Prompts.
- Every upscale is added to your generation history so you can find it in the Library.
Feature details:
- feature: Method picker | explanation: The button at the top shows the current method (default 'AI Upscaler') with a provider logo. Click it to open a list with AI Upscaler ('General-purpose AI upscaling with 2x/4x factor'), Topaz Upscale ('Premium Topaz-quality enhancement') and Seed Upscale ('SeedVR2 high-fidelity upscaling'). | whyToUse: Different methods give different looks; try more than one on important images. | inputRequired: None. | restrictions: Choosing a method resets the scale factor: AI Upscaler goes back to 2x; Topaz and Seed Upscale have no factor button.

chunks.title: Upscale Suite — Features
chunks.text:
- feature: Scale Factor | explanation: Click the Advanced button (it changes to Less) to open the panel. For AI Upscaler it shows a 'Scale Factor' label with 2x and 4x buttons. | whyToUse: 2x doubles width and height; 4x makes the image four times wider and taller. | inputRequired: None (default 2x). | restrictions: Only AI Upscaler shows a factor here. For Topaz Upscale and Seed Upscale the studio sends no factor, so the model's own default is used. If you need to choose a Topaz factor (1, 2, 4 or 8) or a Seed resolution (2k, 4k or 8k), use the Upscale tool in Edit Studio.
- feature: Upload and Pexels | explanation: The round picker button at the left of the form opens the upload panel (upload a file, choose from your upload history, paste, or use a URL). The compass-style button titled 'Browse stock photos from Pexels' lets you pick a free stock photo. The hint text next to them says 'Upload image or video to upscale'. | whyToUse: Get your source image in. | inputRequired: One image. | restrictions: Images up to 10MB (picker limit). The picker also lists video and document types, but the three methods are image upscalers, so use images. Pexels images show an attribution chip.

chunks.title: Upscale Suite — Features
chunks.text:
- feature: Upscale Image | explanation: Starts the job. The button becomes 'Upscaling...' and returns to 'Upscale Image' when done. The finished image appears in a result card. | whyToUse: Run the upscale. | inputRequired: An uploaded image; a signed-in account with access; an API key. | restrictions: If no image is loaded you get an alert: 'Upload an image first'. Errors appear as an alert 'Error: <message>'.
- feature: Result card: Download and Publish to Social | explanation: Download saves the enlarged image. Publish to Social opens the social publishing dialog with the image. | whyToUse: Save or share the result. | inputRequired: A finished upscale. | restrictions: Only the latest result is shown on the page.
- feature: Thumbnail, Tools menu and attachments | explanation: Thumbnail opens a generator for a custom studio thumbnail. The three-dots menu has Recipes, Monetize and Prompts. An attachment toolbar in the form lets you add reference images or videos. | whyToUse: Optional extras shared with other studios. | inputRequired: None. | restrictions: These do not change how the upscale looks in a way confirmed by the code; reference files are passed along with the request but the effect on an upscaler is not confirmed.
Modes:
- Image upscale (AI Upscaler, 2x or 4x)
- Image upscale (Topaz Upscale)
- Image upscale (Seed Upscale / SeedVR2)
Mode details:

chunks.title: Upscale Suite — Features
chunks.text:
- mode: AI Upscaler | description: General-purpose AI upscaling with a 2x or 4x factor. Catalog description: 'AI-powered image upscaling and resolution enhancement.' | useCase: Everyday enlargement; the default.
- mode: Topaz Upscale | description: Premium Topaz-quality enhancement. Catalog description: 'Topaz Labs AI image upscaling and detail enhancement.' In Edit Studio the same model offers factors 1, 2, 4 and 8 (default 2). | useCase: When you want pro-grade detail recovery.
- mode: Seed Upscale | description: SeedVR2 high-fidelity upscaling. Catalog description: 'ByteDance SeedVR2 AI image upscaling and restoration.' In Edit Studio the same model offers resolution 2k, 4k or 8k (default 4k). | useCase: Restoring and enlarging images to a target resolution.
Models:

chunks.title: Upscale Suite — Features
chunks.text: Upscale Suite offers exactly three methods, each tied to one model id: AI Upscaler = ai-image-upscaler (MuAPI; 'general-purpose AI upscaling with 2x/4x factor'), Topaz Upscale = topaz-image-upscale (Topaz; 'premium Topaz-quality enhancement'), Seed Upscale = seedvr2-image-upscale (ByteDance SeedVR2; 'high-fidelity upscaling'). The public model catalog also lists other upscalers (Topaz Upscale Image Creative, Generative and Precision) but they are not offered in this studio. Edit Studio's note for the same models: AI Image Upscaler is a 'quick, clean upscale, good everyday default'; Topaz Image Upscale is 'pro-grade enlargement (choose 2x, 4x or 8x) that recovers fine detail'; Seedvr2 Image Upscale 'upscales to a resolution you choose, up to 4K' (the model schema lists 2k, 4k and 8k). No price, speed or quality scores for these three models are stated in the code or in the model comparison data, so none are given here.

chunks.title: Upscale Suite — Inputs and outputs
chunks.text:
Upscale Suite (#/upscale). Inputs and outputs.
Inputs:
- Method
- Image to upscale
- Scale Factor (AI Upscaler only)
- Optional attachments (reference images/videos)

Required inputs:

Optional inputs:

- Scale Factor (default 2x)

Input details:
- name: Image to upscale | description: The picture you want enlarged. Add it with the picker button or the Pexels button. | required: true | whenToUse: Always. | restrictions: Up to 10MB per image in the picker. Use a clean, well-exposed original; AI upscaling cannot invent perfect detail from a very tiny or heavily compressed image.
- name: Method | description: AI Upscaler, Topaz Upscale or Seed Upscale. | required: true | whenToUse: Pick by look and fidelity; all three are image upscalers. | restrictions: Default is AI Upscaler.
- name: Scale Factor | description: 2x or 4x, shown as buttons in the Advanced panel. | required: false | whenToUse: Use 2x for most images; 4x for very small ones. | restrictions: Shown only for AI Upscaler. The other two methods show no factor.

chunks.title: Upscale Suite — Inputs and outputs
chunks.text:
- name: Attachments | description: Optional reference images or videos added through the attachment toolbar. | required: false | whenToUse: Normally not needed for upscaling. | restrictions: Start frame, end frame and audio attachments are turned off in this studio.
Outputs:

- A Download link for the image
- A history entry (type upscale) available in the Library

chunks.title: Upscale Suite — Problems and limits
chunks.text:
Upscale Suite (#/upscale). Problems and limits.
Troubleshooting:
- Alert 'Upload an image first': you clicked Upscale Image with nothing loaded. Upload an image and try again.
- Alert 'Error: ...': the upscale failed. Read the message, try again, or switch to another method.
- An upgrade prompt appears when you click Upscale Image: your account does not have full access. Upgrade or sign in, then try again.
- A sign-in / API key dialog opens: complete it; the upscale restarts automatically afterwards.
- I cannot find a 4x option: it only exists for AI Upscaler, inside the Advanced panel (click Advanced).
- The Advanced panel is empty or says 'No advanced options for this model.': Topaz Upscale and Seed Upscale have no factor control on this page.
- 'Reference uploaded' toast appeared but nothing changed: attachments are optional extras and do not change the main result in a way the code confirms.
- My uploaded file will not load: images must be 10MB or smaller. Compress or resize and retry.
- The result still looks soft: the source may be too low quality. Try Topaz Upscale or Seed Upscale, or start from a better original.
Troubleshooting steps:

chunks.title: Upscale Suite — Problems and limits
chunks.text:
- issue: Upscale Image button seems stuck | steps: Wait for the label 'Upscaling...' to finish; large images take longer.; If an alert 'Error: ...' appears, close it and click Upscale Image again.; Try a different method or a smaller source image.
- issue: Need a larger output than 2x | steps: With AI Upscaler selected, click Advanced and choose 4x.; Or upscale the result again (download it, upload it and run another 2x).; Or use Edit Studio's Upscale tool with Topaz (up to 8x) or Seedvr2 (up to 8k).
- issue: Nothing happens when I click Upscale Image | steps: Check an image has been loaded through the picker or the Pexels button.; Look for an upgrade or sign-in dialog and finish it.; Click Upscale Image again.
Common problems:
- problem: Result looks over-sharpened or plastic | whyItHappens: AI upscalers add detail that was not in the original. | howToFix: Try another method (Seed Upscale for restoration, Topaz for detail) or use 2x instead of 4x.
- problem: Factor buttons missing | whyItHappens: Only AI Upscaler has them, and they sit in Advanced. | howToFix: Choose AI Upscaler and click Advanced.
- problem: Cannot upload a big file | whyItHappens: Image uploads are capped at 10MB. | howToFix: Reduce the file size first.
Limitations:
- Image upscaling only; there is no video upscaling method in this studio.

chunks.title: Upscale Suite — Problems and limits
chunks.text:
- The scale factor choice (2x/4x) exists only for AI Upscaler in this studio.
- No before/after comparison slider on this page.
- No batch upscaling; one image at a time.
- No denoise, face-enhancement or color-correction options.
- Only the latest result is displayed; earlier ones are in the Library.
- You need an account with access and an API key; image uploads are limited to 10MB.
Limit details:
- limitation: No video upscale | impact: Uploading a video will not give you an upscaled video. | workaround: Use Video Tools (#/videotools) or another video studio for video.
- limitation: No factor control for Topaz and Seed Upscale here | impact: You cannot choose 4x or 8k on this page for those two methods. | workaround: Open Edit Studio (#/edit), choose the Upscale tool, pick the model and use its own setting (Topaz factor or SeedVR2 resolution).
- limitation: No comparison view | impact: You judge the result by eye. | workaround: Edit Studio's Upscale tool has a Before / After slider.
FAQs:
- question: How much bigger will my image be? | answer: With AI Upscaler you choose 2x or 4x (default 2x). For Topaz Upscale and Seed Upscale this page does not let you choose; use Edit Studio's Upscale tool for Topaz factors 1/2/4/8 or SeedVR2 resolutions 2k/4k/8k.

chunks.title: Upscale Suite — Problems and limits
chunks.text:
- question: Can I upscale a video here? | answer: No. The three methods are image upscalers and the upload asks for an image. Use Video Tools or a video studio for clips.
- question: Which method is best? | answer: The code does not rank them. AI Upscaler is the quick everyday default, Topaz Upscale is described as premium, and Seed Upscale as high-fidelity. Try them on your own image.
- question: Where do my upscaled images go? | answer: The latest one is shown on the page with a Download link, and every upscale is registered in your generation history (Library).
- question: Is there a prompt box? | answer: No. Upscaling needs only the image and, for AI Upscaler, a factor.
- question: How big can the source file be? | answer: Up to 10MB for an image.
- question: Does it change what is in my picture? | answer: It aims to keep the content and add resolution, but AI upscalers can add or alter fine detail. Check the result before using it.

chunks.title: Video Agent — Overview
chunks.text:
Video Agent (#/video-agent). Overview.
Description:
Video Agent turns a plain-language description into a motion-graphics animation. An AI writes the animation code, you preview it live, tweak it by chatting, and then render it to an MP4 in your browser.
Summary:
Describe an animation and the agent writes, previews and renders it as an MP4.
About:
Video Agent is a prompt-to-motion-graphics studio (a port of Remotion's prompt-to-motion-graphics template). You describe an animation such as animated text, a bar chart, chat bubbles or a logo intro. The agent first checks that your prompt really describes a visual animation, then writes Remotion code, and the result plays immediately in a live preview player. You keep chatting to change it (colors, text, timing), you can also edit the code directly, and when you are happy you click Render & Download to render an MP4 inside your own browser tab. The finished MP4 is also uploaded and saved to your library. It runs on your own OpenAI API key, so you need to add that key in Settings before it can generate. It makes designed motion graphics from code; it does not edit your footage and does not generate photorealistic AI video.
Best for:

chunks.title: Video Agent — Overview
chunks.text:
Creators and marketers who want animated titles, kinetic typography, simple data charts, chat or UI mockup animations, logo intros and social motion graphics from a text description, and who already have (or are willing to add) an OpenAI API key.
When to use it:
- You want animated text, kinetic typography or a typewriter effect from a description.
- You want an animated bar chart, counters or other data visualization and you can put the numbers directly in the prompt.
- You want a chat or messaging UI animation (for example WhatsApp or iMessage style bubbles).
- You want a logo or brand intro, a social story/reel graphic or an abstract motion background built from code.
- You want to keep refining an animation with follow-up messages instead of starting over each time.
- You want an MP4 rendered in your browser without any server render queue.
When to use another studio:
- Use Video (#/video) when you want AI-generated live-action or cinematic video clips from a prompt or image instead of coded motion graphics.
- Use Motion Director (#/motion-director) when you want a promo film planned from your website, with real page captures and shot recipes.
- Use Workbench (#/workbench) when you already have clips, images or audio and want to arrange them on a multi-track timeline with motion cards and sound.

chunks.title: Video Agent — Overview
chunks.text:
- Use Timeline (#/timeline) when you want a full multi-track editor to cut and export footage.
- Use Director (#/director) when you want AI agents to analyse or edit an existing video (subtitles, highlights, dubbing).
- Use Cinema (#/cinema) or Animate (#/animate) when you want to bring a photo or scene to life as AI video.

chunks.title: Video Agent — How to use
chunks.text:
Video Agent (#/video-agent). How to use.
How to use:
1. Open Video Agent from the Agents section of the side menu (#/video-agent). 2. Make sure your OpenAI key is saved in SmartVideo Settings, API keys (OpenAI API Key). 3. On 'What do you want to create?' type a description in the box, or click one of the Prompt Examples chips (Typewriter text, Chat messages, Metric counters, Bar chart, Doge screensaver) to fill it in. 4. Optionally pick a model from the drop-down (default GPT-5.2 (Low Reasoning)) and attach up to 4 reference images with the paperclip. 5. Press Enter or click the arrow button. 6. Watch the code stream in and the animation appear in the preview player. 7. Use the chat sidebar ('Tune your animation...') to ask for changes, or edit the code directly. 8. Open Settings to change Duration (frames) and FPS if needed. 9. Click Render & Download and wait for 'Rendering...' to finish. 10. Click Download video. The MP4 is also saved to your library.
Steps:
- Open Video Agent from the Agents group in the side menu.
- Add your OpenAI API key in Settings, API keys (OpenAI API Key) if you have not already.
- Type a specific description of the animation, or click a Prompt Examples chip.
- Choose a model (default GPT-5.2 (Low Reasoning)) and optionally attach reference images.
- Submit with Enter or the arrow button and wait for the preview.

chunks.title: Video Agent — How to use
chunks.text:
- Refine with follow-up messages in the chat sidebar.
- Adjust Duration (frames) and FPS in Settings.
- Click Render & Download, then Download video.
Getting started:
- Save your OpenAI key first: Video Agent will not generate without it.
- Start with a Prompt Examples chip to see how a good prompt looks, then edit the wording.
- Put exact colors, text and numbers in your prompt for best results.
- Keep the first animation short and simple, then add detail with follow-up messages.
Tips:
- Be specific about colors, timing and layout, for example 'green sent bubbles on the right, gray received on the left'.
- Put your data directly in the prompt for charts.
- Describe the feel: 'bouncy spring entrance', 'smooth fade', 'staggered timing'.
- Use a higher reasoning model for 3D or very detailed scenes.
- Use the current-frame button to show the agent exactly what to fix.
Best practices:
- Start simple, then layer detail with follow-up messages.
- Reference images by URL in the prompt when you need them inside the animation.
- Set Duration and FPS before you render.
- Keep the tab open during Render & Download.
- Keep a copy of code you like using the copy button.

chunks.title: Video Agent — Features
chunks.text:
Video Agent (#/video-agent). Features.
Key features:
- Prompt-to-animation: type what you want and the agent writes the animation code.
- Prompt check: before generating, a lightweight classifier rejects prompts that are not about visual motion graphics (questions, essays, chat, non-visual tasks).
- Skill detection: the agent picks relevant guidance (charts, typography, messaging, transitions, sequencing, spring physics, social media formats, 3D) for each request.
- Live preview player with the animation playing as soon as code is ready.
- Follow-up chat edits: small changes are applied as targeted edits to the code; big changes can replace the whole code.
- Model picker: seven GPT-5.2 reasoning variants (see modelCapabilities).
- Reference images: attach up to 4 images (10 MB each) as visual reference, paste or drop them, or use the current preview frame as an image in chat.
- Prompt Examples chips for a quick start (Typewriter text, Chat messages, Metric counters, Bar chart, Doge screensaver).
- Editable code view with a copy button.
- Settings dialog for Duration (frames) and FPS.
- Render & Download: renders an MP4 in the browser and lets you download it.
- Automatic save: the rendered MP4 is uploaded and saved to your library.
Feature details:

chunks.title: Video Agent — Features
chunks.text: - feature: Describe your animation | explanation: The first screen asks 'What do you want to create?'. You type a description in the box (placeholder 'Describe your animation... (paste or drop images)') and press Enter or the arrow button. Shift+Enter makes a new line. | whyToUse: It is the fastest way to get a first animation without writing code. | inputRequired: A text prompt describing visual motion graphics. Your OpenAI key must be saved in Settings. | restrictions: The prompt must describe animation or visual content. Questions, requests for written text (poems, essays), conversations and non-visual tasks are rejected with 'No valid motion graphics prompt. Please describe an animation or visual content you'd like to create.'

chunks.title: Video Agent — Features
chunks.text: - feature: Model picker | explanation: A drop-down next to the input lets you choose how much the model thinks before writing code. The default is 'GPT-5.2 (Low Reasoning)'. | whyToUse: Use a higher reasoning level for complex animations (3D, many elements, tricky timing). Use No Reasoning or Low for quick simple ones. | inputRequired: None, it has a default. | restrictions: Options are fixed to: GPT-5.2 (No Reasoning), GPT-5.2 (Low Reasoning), GPT-5.2 (Medium Reasoning), GPT-5.2 (High Reasoning), GPT-5.2 Pro (Medium), GPT-5.2 Pro (High), GPT-5.2 Pro (XHigh). If your OpenAI account has no access to the chosen model you get 'Your OpenAI account doesn't have access to this model. Pick another model and try again.'

chunks.title: Video Agent — Features
chunks.text: - feature: Attach reference images | explanation: Use the paperclip button (title 'Attach images'), paste an image, or drag and drop it. The agent can look at the images to understand what you mean. | whyToUse: To show a layout, color palette or style you want the animation to resemble. | inputRequired: Image files. | restrictions: Maximum 4 images, each at most 10 MB. Too-large files show 'File too large (max 10MB): <name>'. The app states 'Images for reference only, they cannot be embedded in the animation'. If you want a picture shown inside the animation, put its public web URL in the prompt instead; the generated code can use it with Remotion's Img component. The whole request is limited to about 6 MB, otherwise you see 'Request too large. Attach fewer or smaller images.'

chunks.title: Video Agent — Features
chunks.text:
- feature: Follow-up chat (Tune your animation) | explanation: After the first generation, a chat sidebar lets you ask for changes (placeholder 'Tune your animation... (paste or drop images)'). The agent chooses between targeted edits to the code (for small changes such as colors, text, numbers, timing) and a full rewrite (for major restructuring or when you ask to start fresh). It keeps manual edits you made to the code unless you ask to change them. | whyToUse: Iterating is cheaper and faster than regenerating from scratch. | inputRequired: A text instruction. | restrictions: A targeted edit can fail if the agent cannot find the exact text to change ('Edit N failed: Could not find the specified text') or finds more than one match ('Found N matches. The edit target is ambiguous.'). Rephrase more specifically or ask for a full rewrite.
- feature: Use current frame as image | explanation: A button in the chat input (title 'Use current frame of Preview as image in chat') captures the frame currently shown in the preview and attaches it to your next message. | whyToUse: Point at exactly what looks wrong, for example 'make the title in this frame bigger'. | inputRequired: A playing or paused preview. | restrictions: Counts toward the 4 image limit.

chunks.title: Video Agent — Features
chunks.text:
- feature: Settings (Duration and FPS) | explanation: The Settings button above the player opens a dialog titled 'Settings' ('Configure your animation settings.') with Duration (frames) and FPS, and shows the resulting video length, for example 'Video length: 5.00s (150 frames / 30 FPS)'. Close with the Close button. | whyToUse: Set how long the animation runs and how smooth it is before rendering. | inputRequired: Numbers. | restrictions: Duration (frames) accepts 1 to 1000. FPS accepts 1 to 60. Video length in seconds = frames divided by FPS.
- feature: Render & Download | explanation: The render button reads 'Render & Download'. While it works it shows 'Rendering...' with a progress bar, and when done it becomes 'Download video' with the file size. Rendering happens in your own browser using Remotion's web renderer and produces an MP4. | whyToUse: Turn the live animation into a file you can post or edit further. | inputRequired: A generated animation. | restrictions: Needs a browser that supports in-browser MP4 rendering; if it does not, an error is shown instead of rendering. Keep the tab open while rendering. Long durations and high FPS take longer.

chunks.title: Video Agent — Features
chunks.text:
- feature: Auto-save to library | explanation: When a render finishes, the Video Agent page uploads the MP4 and saves it as a video generation in your library. The status text beside the toolbar reads 'Saving video to your library...' and then 'Saved to your library'. | whyToUse: Your result is kept even if you close the tab. | inputRequired: Being signed in. | restrictions: If upload fails you see 'Downloaded - couldn't save to library (<reason>)'. The file still downloaded to your computer.
Modes:
- Generate from prompt
- Follow-up edit (targeted)
- Follow-up rewrite (full)
- Auto-correction
Mode details:
- mode: Generate from prompt | description: First message: the prompt is validated, relevant skills are detected, and the model writes a complete animation component. | useCase: Starting a new animation.
- mode: Follow-up edit (targeted) | description: The agent returns exact find-and-replace edits to your existing code, applied in order. | useCase: Changing colors, text, numbers or timing, or adding or removing a single element.
- mode: Follow-up rewrite (full) | description: The agent returns replacement code for the whole animation. | useCase: Completely different style, major restructure, or when you say 'start fresh'.

chunks.title: Video Agent — Features
chunks.text:
- mode: Auto-correction | description: If the generated code fails to compile, the app can automatically ask the agent to fix the compile error, up to a limited number of attempts. | useCase: Happens automatically; you may see a retry rather than a broken preview.
Models:
The generation endpoint uses OpenAI models through your own OpenAI key. The picker offers GPT-5.2 at No, Low, Medium and High reasoning, and GPT-5.2 Pro at Medium, High and XHigh reasoning (ids gpt-5.2:none, gpt-5.2:low, gpt-5.2:medium, gpt-5.2:high, gpt-5.2-pro:medium, gpt-5.2-pro:high, gpt-5.2-pro:xhigh). The default selected is gpt-5.2:low. The server default model can be overridden by the environment variable VIDEO_AGENT_MODEL and the prompt-check model by VIDEO_AGENT_CLASSIFIER_MODEL, so the exact model that answers may differ on a deployment. Higher reasoning levels generally spend more time thinking and suit complex animations. The animation itself is code (React with Remotion, optionally Remotion shapes, transitions and Three.js) rendered in your browser; no video-generation model is used.

chunks.title: Video Agent — Inputs and outputs
chunks.text:
Video Agent (#/video-agent). Inputs and outputs.
Inputs:
- Prompt
- Model
- Reference images
- Follow-up message
- Duration (frames)
- FPS
- Code edits
Required inputs:
- Prompt
- OpenAI API key (saved in Settings)
Optional inputs:
- Model
- Reference images
- Follow-up message
- Duration (frames)
- FPS
- Code edits
Input details:
- name: Prompt | description: A text description of the motion graphics you want, including colors, layout, timing feel and any data. | required: true | whenToUse: Always, for the first generation. | restrictions: Must describe visual animation content. Non-visual requests are rejected by the prompt check.
- name: OpenAI API key | description: Your own OpenAI key. SmartVideo sends it with each generation request; nothing is billed by SmartVideo for this feature in the code that was reviewed, your OpenAI account pays for the usage. | required: true | whenToUse: Add it once in Settings, API keys (OpenAI API Key). | restrictions: Error if missing: 'The Video Agent uses your own OpenAI key. Add it in SmartVid -> Settings -> API keys (OpenAI API Key).' The key must look like a standard OpenAI key (starts with sk-). A rejected key gives 'OpenAI rejected your API key. Check it in SmartVid -> Settings -> API keys.'

chunks.title: Video Agent — Inputs and outputs
chunks.text:
- name: Model | description: Reasoning level of the GPT-5.2 model used to write the code. | required: false | whenToUse: Raise it for complex scenes; lower it for speed. | restrictions: Seven fixed choices.
- name: Reference images | description: Images used only as visual reference for the AI. | required: false | whenToUse: When describing a look in words is hard. | restrictions: Max 4 images, 10 MB each. They cannot be embedded in the animation. Use a URL in the prompt to show a picture inside the animation.
- name: Duration (frames) and FPS | description: Length and frame rate of the animation, edited in the Settings dialog. | required: false | whenToUse: Before rendering. | restrictions: Duration 1 to 1000 frames; FPS 1 to 60.
Outputs:
- A live-playing animation preview
- Editable Remotion (React) animation code
- An MP4 file rendered in your browser (Download video)
- A saved video entry in your library

chunks.title: Video Agent — Problems and limits
chunks.text:
Video Agent (#/video-agent). Problems and limits.
Troubleshooting:
- Message 'The Video Agent uses your own OpenAI key...': add your OpenAI key in Settings, API keys (OpenAI API Key), wait a few seconds and resend.
- Message 'OpenAI rejected your API key': the saved key is wrong or revoked; paste a fresh key in Settings.
- Message 'Your OpenAI account is rate-limited or out of credit': check your OpenAI billing and usage limits, then try again.
- Message 'Your OpenAI account doesn't have access to this model': pick a different model in the drop-down, for example a GPT-5.2 option.
- Message 'No valid motion graphics prompt...': your text was not an animation request. Describe something visual, for example colors, text and motion.
- Message 'Request too large. Attach fewer or smaller images.': remove some reference images or use smaller ones.
- Nothing loads or the page stays blank: reload the page; the Video Agent is an embedded app that must finish loading before it can talk to SmartVideo.
- 'Edit N failed' errors after a follow-up: the agent could not find or uniquely match the code to change; ask again with the exact text, or ask for a full rewrite.
- Render & Download shows an error: use a current Chrome-based browser and try a shorter Duration or lower FPS.

chunks.title: Video Agent — Problems and limits
chunks.text:
- Status says 'Downloaded - couldn't save to library': the MP4 downloaded but the upload failed; check your connection and sign-in, and keep the downloaded file.
Troubleshooting steps:
- issue: Generation will not start (key problem) | steps: Open SmartVideo Settings and find API keys.; Paste your OpenAI key into OpenAI API Key and save.; Return to Video Agent, wait up to about 15 seconds or click back into the window, then submit again.; If it says OpenAI rejected the key, create a new key in your OpenAI account and replace it.
- issue: My prompt was rejected | steps: Read the message: it means the prompt did not describe visual motion graphics.; Rewrite it as a description of what should appear and move, with colors, text and timing.; Try a Prompt Examples chip and adapt it.
- issue: The preview looks wrong or an error appears in the code | steps: Wait a moment: the app may auto-correct compile errors by itself.; Send a follow-up describing what is wrong, or attach the current frame with the 'Use current frame of Preview as image in chat' button.; If it stays broken, ask the agent to start fresh with a simpler version.

chunks.title: Video Agent — Problems and limits
chunks.text:
- issue: Rendering fails or the MP4 is not saved | steps: Keep the tab open and in front while 'Rendering...' runs.; Lower Duration (frames) or FPS in Settings and try again.; If the status says it could not save to your library, use Download video to keep the file and check your connection.
Common problems:
- problem: The image I attached does not appear in the animation | whyItHappens: Attached images are reference only for the AI. | howToFix: Include a public image URL in the prompt so the code can load it.
- problem: A follow-up change was not applied | whyItHappens: A targeted edit could not match the code text exactly or matched several places. | howToFix: Be more specific, mention the exact text or element, or ask for a full rewrite.
- problem: My animation is too short or too long | whyItHappens: Length is set by Duration (frames) and FPS, not only by the prompt. | howToFix: Open Settings and change Duration (frames) and FPS. Length in seconds = frames divided by FPS.
- problem: The chart shows wrong numbers | whyItHappens: The agent invents data when you do not supply it. | howToFix: Type the exact data values directly in the prompt.
Limitations:
- Requires your own OpenAI API key; there is no fallback platform key.
- Only motion graphics and animation prompts are accepted.
- Reference images cannot be embedded in the animation, only used as visual reference.

chunks.title: Video Agent — Problems and limits
chunks.text:
- Maximum 4 reference images, 10 MB each.
- Duration is limited to 1 to 1000 frames and FPS to 1 to 60 in Settings.
- Rendering is done in your browser tab, so it depends on your device and browser.
- Output is coded motion graphics, not live-action or photoreal AI video.
- Direct image uploads into the animation are not supported; images must be referenced by URL.
Limit details:
- limitation: Needs your own OpenAI key | impact: Without it nothing generates and you see the message about adding your OpenAI key in Settings. | workaround: Add the key under Settings, API keys (OpenAI API Key), then try again. The studio re-sends the key about every 15 seconds and when the window regains focus, so a new key should work shortly after you save it.
- limitation: Only visual motion graphics prompts | impact: Questions or text-writing requests are rejected. | workaround: Rephrase as a visual: 'Animated title that says Hello with a bounce' instead of 'What is a bounce?'.
- limitation: Reference images are not embedded | impact: A logo you attach will not appear in the video. | workaround: Host the image online and include its URL in the prompt, for example 'a DVD screensaver animation of this image https://example.com/logo.png'.

chunks.title: Video Agent — Problems and limits
chunks.text:
- limitation: Browser rendering | impact: Render & Download can fail on browsers that cannot render MP4 on the web, and takes longer for long clips. | workaround: Use a current Chrome-based browser, keep the tab open and lower Duration or FPS.
FAQs:
- question: Do I need an API key? | answer: Yes. Video Agent runs on your own OpenAI key. Add it in Settings, API keys (OpenAI API Key). If it is missing you see: The Video Agent uses your own OpenAI key.
- question: Where does the video get rendered? | answer: In your own browser tab using Remotion's web renderer. You get an MP4 and it is also uploaded to your library.
- question: Can I upload my own logo or image into the animation? | answer: Not as a direct upload. Attached images are reference only. To show a picture inside the animation, put its public URL in the prompt.
- question: How many images can I attach? | answer: Up to 4, each up to 10 MB.
- question: How long can the animation be? | answer: Settings accepts Duration from 1 to 1000 frames and FPS from 1 to 60. At 30 FPS, 1000 frames is about 33 seconds.
- question: Can I edit the code? | answer: Yes, the code is editable and has a copy button. Your manual edits are preserved by follow-up requests unless you ask to change them.

chunks.title: Video Agent — Problems and limits
chunks.text:
- question: Why was my prompt rejected? | answer: A quick check rejects prompts that are not about visual motion graphics, such as questions or requests for written text. Describe something that can be seen and animated.
- question: Is this the same as the Timeline editor's AI agent? | answer: No. The Timeline editor has its own separate AI agent for editing a timeline. Video Agent here writes animation code from a prompt.

chunks.title: Video Agent — Workflows and use cases
chunks.text:
Video Agent (#/video-agent). Workflows and use cases.
Example workflows:
- title: Animated bar chart for a social post | steps: Open Video Agent and click the Bar chart Prompt Examples chip.; Replace the sample data with your own numbers and label colors.; Submit and wait for the preview.; Ask 'make the bars appear one after another with a bouncy spring'.; Open Settings and set Duration (frames) and FPS for the length you need.; Click Render & Download, then Download video.
- title: Logo intro with a hosted logo | steps: Upload your logo somewhere public and copy its URL.; Type: 'A 5 second logo intro on a dark background, the logo fades and scales in, using this image <URL>'.; Submit, review, and ask for tweaks such as a tagline appearing below.; Render & Download.
Use cases:
- title: Kinetic typography title | description: Animated words for a video opening. | steps: Describe the text, font feel, colors and effect (for example typewriter or word carousel).; Generate and preview.; Refine with follow-ups, then render. | expectedOutput: An MP4 of the animated text.

chunks.title: Video Agent — Workflows and use cases
chunks.text:
- title: Chat conversation mockup | description: Animated message bubbles for a story or explainer. | steps: Describe who speaks, the messages and bubble colors (for example green sent bubbles on the right and gray received bubbles on the left).; Generate, then adjust timing between messages.; Render. | expectedOutput: An MP4 showing staggered chat bubbles.
- title: Metric counters and charts | description: Animated numbers or charts for a report video. | steps: Paste the real data into the prompt.; Generate and check the labels.; Render and download. | expectedOutput: An MP4 with animated counters or bars.
Related studios:
- studio: workbench | relationship: Video Agent exports are saved to your library; Workbench is where you combine media on a timeline. | whenToMove: After you have the MP4 and want to add other clips, text cards or sound. | why: Workbench edits and combines media; Video Agent only creates the animation. Note: Video Agent results themselves are not offered the 'Edit in Workbench' hand-off in the code reviewed, so open Workbench and use Add your generations.
- studio: motion-director | relationship: Both create motion films, but Motion Director plans from your website and uses a library of shot recipes. | whenToMove: When you want a promo film built from your real site pages. | why: It captures your pages and outputs an editable multi-shot film.

chunks.title: Video Agent — Workflows and use cases
chunks.text: - studio: video | relationship: Video generates AI video clips; Video Agent generates coded motion graphics. | whenToMove: When you need realistic or cinematic footage rather than graphics. | why: Video Agent cannot create live-action looking footage.

chunks.title: Video Agent — Glossary
chunks.text: Glossary: Motion graphics: Animated graphics such as moving text, charts and shapes, as opposed to filmed footage. | Remotion: A tool that builds videos from React code. Video Agent writes this code for you. | FPS: Frames per second: how many pictures per second the video plays. | Frames: Single images that make up the animation. Length in seconds = frames divided by FPS. | Reasoning level: How much extra thinking the AI does before answering. Higher is slower but usually better for complex requests. | Targeted edit: A small find-and-replace change to existing code instead of rewriting everything. | BYOK: Bring your own key: you supply your own OpenAI API key and pay OpenAI directly for usage.

chunks.title: Video Agent — What you can ask or do here
phrases: make a video just by describing it
create an animated explainer from a prompt
make motion graphics with text and shapes
preview my video then download an mp4
make a promo with animated text
