chunks.text: Video Agent (#/video-agent). People use this when they want to: make a video just by describing it; create an animated explainer from a prompt; make motion graphics with text and shapes; preview my video then download an mp4; make a promo with animated text; make an animated intro or title video. Describe an animation and the agent writes, previews and renders it as an MP4.

chunks.title: Video Studio — Overview
chunks.text:
Video Studio (#/video). Overview.
Description:
Video Studio makes AI videos from a text prompt, from a still image you upload, or from a video you upload (edit, extend, motion transfer, watermark removal and similar tools). It is the one studio behind the #/video route and the aliases #/text-to-video, #/image-to-video, #/video-to-video and #/video-watermark.
Summary:
Create AI videos from text, images or existing videos with a large catalog of models.
About:

chunks.title: Video Studio — Overview
chunks.text:
Video Studio is a prompt bar with a model picker. If you only type a prompt it runs a text-to-video model. If you attach a start-frame image it switches to an image-to-video model and animates your picture. If you attach a video it switches to a video-to-video tool (the default tool for an uploaded video is the AI Video Watermark Remover; you can pick others such as editing, extending, motion transfer, upscaling). Controls for aspect ratio, duration, resolution and quality appear and change depending on which model is selected, so not every control is available for every model. After a run you get a result screen with Regenerate, Download, Extend (when the model supports it), Open in Render, Publish to Social and Add AI Captions, and a History strip of your earlier results. The routes #/text-to-video, #/image-to-video, #/video-to-video and #/video-watermark are explanatory landing pages whose buttons send you into this same studio.
Best for:
Beginners and creators who want to turn a prompt or a single picture into a short clip, try different video models side by side, extend a clip, or clean up an existing video (for example remove a watermark) without leaving one screen.
When to use it:
- You want a short AI video clip from a text description (text-to-video).
- You have a photo, product shot, character or illustration and want it to move (image-to-video, 'Animate image').

chunks.title: Video Studio — Overview
chunks.text:
- You have a start image and an end image and want the AI to fill the motion between them ('Keyframes (start + end)').
- You have an existing video and want to edit it, extend it, transfer motion onto a character image, remove a watermark, or run another video-to-video tool.
- You want to compare several video model families (Seedance, Kling, Veo, Wan, Pixverse, Hunyuan, Runway, Sora, MiniMax Hailuo, Vidu, LTX and others) using the same prompt.
- You want to extend a Seedance 2.0 result or upscale a result to 4K when the continuation model is available.
When to use another studio:
- Use Cinema Studio (#/cinema) when you want camera body, lens, focal length, aperture, camera movement and film look controls built into the prompt.
- Use Cinema Templates (#/cinema-template) when you want a ready-made cinematic template (trailer, brand film, ad film, and so on) that asks you simple questions and writes the prompt for you.
- Use Storyboard Studio (#/storyboard) when you first want to plan a multi-shot story as still frames, then animate frames later.
- Use Animate (#/animate) when your only goal is to animate a single image.
- Use Video Tools (#/videotools) or Upscale (#/upscale) for dedicated clean-up or upscaling workflows.
- Use Lipsync (#/lipsync) or Avatar (#/avatar) when you need a talking person or lip-synced speech.

chunks.title: Video Studio — How to use
chunks.text:
Video Studio (#/video). How to use.
How to use:
1. Open Video Studio from the side menu (#/video). 2. Type what you want in the prompt box ('Describe the video you want to create'), or attach a start-frame image, or attach a video. 3. Optionally open the workflow menu and pick 'Text to video', 'Animate image', 'Keyframes (start + end)', 'References', 'Edit video', 'Extend uploaded video' or 'Motion transfer'. 4. Click the model button (tooltip 'Select AI video model') and pick a model. 5. Set the aspect ratio, duration, resolution and quality buttons that the model offers. 6. Optionally open Advanced (Native Audio, Character Lock, extra controls) or Motion & Style (Camera Speed, Guidance Scale, Style Preset). 7. Click Generate. A progress overlay with a cancel option appears while the clip renders. 8. When the result appears use Regenerate, Download, Extend, Open in Render, Publish to Social or Add AI Captions, or click + New to start another.
Steps:
- Open Video Studio (#/video) from the side menu.
- Type your prompt in 'Describe the video you want to create', or attach media first.
- Pick a workflow and model if you do not want the default.
- Set aspect ratio, duration, resolution and quality for the chosen model.
- Press Generate and wait for the progress overlay to finish.
- Review the result, then download, extend, send to Render, caption or publish it.
Getting started:

chunks.title: Video Studio — How to use
chunks.text:
- Start with a simple, single-action prompt such as 'A slow dolly in on a steaming coffee cup on a wooden table, morning light'.
- Leave the default model and the default aspect ratio on your first run to see how it behaves.
- If you want predictable output, upload a clear start-frame image and add a short motion description.
- You need to be signed in with credits: if no API key is available an AuthModal appears, and an error 'Please sign in and add api credits.' can be shown.
Tips:
- Keep prompts to one subject and one action.
- Name the camera move in words, for example 'slow dolly in' or 'static shot'.
- Use image-to-video when you need the subject to look exactly like your picture.
- Test a cheaper or faster model first, then switch to a higher-quality one for the final.
- Match aspect ratio to where the video will be posted before you generate.
- Use Regenerate to get a new take with the same settings.
Best practices:
- Change one setting at a time when comparing models.
- Write what you want to see, not what you do not want, unless the model has a negative prompt field.
- Download results you like; do not rely only on the History strip.
- Use Add AI Captions before Publish to Social for silent autoplay feeds.

chunks.title: Video Studio — Features
chunks.text:
Video Studio (#/video). Features.
Key features:
- Three automatic modes: text-to-video (prompt only), image-to-video (an image is attached) and video-to-video (a video is attached). The studio switches model lists for you when you attach or clear media.
- A workflow menu with these exact options: 'Text to video', 'Animate image', 'Keyframes (start + end)', 'References', 'Edit video', 'Extend uploaded video', 'Motion transfer'.
- A catalog model picker (button labelled with the current model name, tooltip 'Select AI video model') with a large list of text-to-video, image-to-video and video-to-video models.
- Per-model controls: aspect ratio, duration (shown like '5s'), resolution (default label '720p' if the model gives none) and quality (default label 'basic'). Only the values the selected model supports are offered.
- Attachment buttons for start frame, end frame, image, video; a button to browse stock photos for the reference image, one to browse stock videos for video-to-video, and a button that pulls the last frame out of a video file for image-to-video.
- Advanced panel with 'Native Audio' and 'Character Lock' toggles plus extra model-specific controls such as negative prompt and seed when the model supports them.
- Motion & Style panel with 'Camera Speed', 'Guidance Scale' and a Style Preset row (None, Cinematic, Anime, Realistic, Watercolor, Noir).

chunks.title: Video Studio — Features
chunks.text:
- Prompt helpers in a three-dot menu: GTM Boost, Recipes, Monetize, Prompts. Also a Personalize button and a Thumbnail button.
- Result screen: Regenerate, Download, Extend (or Upscale to 4K), Open in Render, + New, Publish to Social, Add AI Captions, a scrubber and a History strip.
- Interrupted jobs are recovered: if a generation finished while you were away, a toast says 'Recovered a generation that finished while you were away'.
Feature details:
- feature: Text to video | explanation: Type a description in the prompt box (placeholder 'Describe the video you want to create') and press Generate. The studio runs the selected text-to-video model. | whyToUse: Fastest way to get a clip when you have no source picture. | inputRequired: A prompt. Without one you see 'Please enter a prompt to generate a video.' | restrictions: Available aspect ratios, durations and resolutions depend on the selected model.

chunks.title: Video Studio — Features
chunks.text:
- feature: Animate image (image-to-video) | explanation: Attach a start frame image. The studio switches to the first image-to-video model and the prompt box placeholder becomes 'Describe the motion or effect (optional)'. | whyToUse: Gives more predictable results because the first frame is your own picture. The built-in help tips also suggest starting with image-to-video for more predictable results. | inputRequired: An image. Without one you see 'Please upload a start frame image first.' The prompt is optional. | restrictions: Shared upload limits in the app code are 10MB for images and 50MB for videos.
- feature: Keyframes (start + end) | explanation: Workflow option that selects the model 'seedance-2-first-last-frame' so the clip starts on your start frame and ends on your end frame. The end frame can be added with the end frame button (tooltip 'Upload end frame image for I2V'); click it again to clear the end frame. | whyToUse: Use for transformations or controlled transitions between two pictures. | inputRequired: A start frame and an end frame image. | restrictions: Only models that have an end-frame input use the end frame.

chunks.title: Video Studio — Features
chunks.text:
- feature: References | explanation: Workflow option that selects the model 'seedance-2-omni-reference' so you can guide the result with reference media. | whyToUse: Use when you want the output to follow the look of reference images. | inputRequired: Reference media attached with the attachment buttons. | restrictions: Exact reference counts and types are defined by the model and not confirmed here.
- feature: Edit video / Extend uploaded video / Motion transfer | explanation: Three video-to-video workflows. 'Edit video' selects wan2.2-edit-video and needs a prompt describing the change. 'Extend uploaded video' selects wan2.7-video-extend. 'Motion transfer' selects wan2.2-animate and needs both a source video and a character image. | whyToUse: Change, lengthen or re-animate footage you already have. | inputRequired: An uploaded video. Motion transfer also needs the character image ('Please add the character image to animate.'). Edit needs a prompt ('Please describe the change you want.'). | restrictions: When a video is attached the prompt can be disabled for tools that do not use text (for example watermark removal shows 'Video ready - click Generate to remove watermark').

chunks.title: Video Studio — Features
chunks.text: - feature: Video watermark removal | explanation: Attach a video with the video button (tooltip 'Upload video to remove watermark'). The studio switches to the video-to-video list whose first model is 'AI Video Watermark Remover' (id video-watermark-remover, described as removing watermarks, logos, captions and unwanted text). The prompt box is disabled and says 'Video ready - click Generate to remove watermark'. | whyToUse: Clean a clip of overlays without writing a prompt. | inputRequired: A video file. | restrictions: Upload limit for video is 50MB in the shared limits.

chunks.title: Video Studio — Features
chunks.text:
- feature: Extend / Upscale to 4K | explanation: After a result appears, an Extend button shows when a compatible continuation model exists for the model you used. With one target it is labelled for that target (for example 'Upscale to 4K' or 'Extend (Seedance 2.0)'); with several it reads 'Extend / 4K' and opens a small menu. For Seedance 2.0 a banner reads 'Extending previous Seedance 2.0 generation - add an optional prompt to guide the continuation'. | whyToUse: Make a clip longer or higher resolution without starting over. | inputRequired: A finished generation from a supported model. Otherwise: 'No Seedance 2.0 generation found to extend. Generate a video first.' | restrictions: Not every model has a continuation model. If the continuation model is missing from the catalog you get 'Extend model not found in catalog'.
- feature: Advanced: Native Audio and Character Lock | explanation: Open the Advanced button to reveal two toggles. Native Audio asks audio-capable models to produce sound. Character Lock reuses a stored character reference so the same character carries across clips. | whyToUse: Keep a character consistent or ask for generated sound. | inputRequired: None, just switch them on. | restrictions: Only has an effect on models that support the matching input; which models do is not confirmed here.

chunks.title: Video Studio — Features
chunks.text:
- feature: Motion & Style panel | explanation: Opens with Camera Speed (1-10, default 5), Guidance Scale (1-20, step 0.5, default 7.5) and Style Preset buttons (None, Cinematic, Anime, Realistic, Watercolor, Noir). A chosen style adds text like 'cinematic style' to your prompt for text and image runs. | whyToUse: Quick style nudge without rewriting the prompt. | inputRequired: None. | restrictions: The style is appended to the prompt text, so it is a suggestion to the model, not a guarantee.
- feature: Result actions | explanation: Regenerate re-runs, Download saves the file, Open in Render saves the video as an asset and opens Render, + New returns to the prompt bar, Publish to Social opens the social publish dialog, Add AI Captions adds captions and updates the preview ('Preview updated with captions'). | whyToUse: Finish, share or continue editing your clip. | inputRequired: A completed result. | restrictions: Open in Render can fail with 'Could not open in Render: ...' followed by the reason.
Modes:
- Text to video
- Animate image
- Keyframes (start + end)
- References
- Edit video
- Extend uploaded video
- Motion transfer
- Video-to-video tools (watermark removal, upscale, face swap, captions, and others from the catalog)
Mode details:

chunks.title: Video Studio — Features
chunks.text:
- mode: Text-to-video | description: Prompt only. Uses a text-to-video model. Default model is the first in the catalog list (Seedance Lite). | useCase: Concept clips, b-roll, ideas without source art.
- mode: Image-to-video | description: A start-frame image is attached. Uses an image-to-video model; the studio picks the first one in the list until you choose another. | useCase: Animate product shots, portraits, illustrations.
- mode: Video-to-video | description: A video is attached. The studio switches to the video-to-video list; the first entry is AI Video Watermark Remover. | useCase: Edit, extend, motion transfer, remove watermark, upscale.
- mode: Extend | description: Continues a previous result using a continuation model (for Seedance 2.0 it uses the stored request id of your last generation). | useCase: Make a clip longer or upscale to 4K.
Models:

chunks.title: Video Studio — Features
chunks.text: The catalog (public/api/model-catalog.json) lists 115 text-to-video, 188 image-to-video and 74 video-to-video entries. Main families by name: Seedance (ByteDance; Lite, Pro, Pro Fast, v1.5 Pro, v2.0, 2.5, plus Seedance 2.0 Extend and first/last-frame and reference variants), Kling (v2.1 Master, v2.5 Turbo Pro, v2.6 Pro, O1 Pro, v3.0 Pro and Standard, plus motion-control and edit tools), Google Veo (Veo 3, Veo 3 Fast, Veo 3.1, Veo 3.1 Fast, Veo 4), OpenAI Sora (Sora 2, Sora 2 Pro), Wan (2.1, 2.2, 2.5, 2.6 and Fast variants, Wan 2.2 Animate, Wan 2.2 Edit Video, Wan 2.7 Extend), Hunyuan, Runway (Gen-3, Aleph, Act Two), Pixverse (v4.5, v5, v5.5), MiniMax Hailuo, Vidu, LTX 2, OVI, Grok Imagine, Midjourney v7 image-to-video, and Flux 3 video models. Video-to-video entries include AI Video Watermark Remover, Video Background Remover, AI Video Upscaler / Topaz upscalers, AI Captions, AI Video Face Swap, Remix Video, MMAudio v2, Luma Flash Reframe and several Kling O1 / Happy Horse / Seedance 2.5 edit and extend tools. The in-app model descriptions are short one-liners, for example Seedance 2.0 is 'ByteDance Seedance 2.0 latest text-to-video generation', Kling V3.0 Pro is 'cinematic text-to-video generation', Kling O1 is 'high-resolution', Veo 3.1 is 'Google Veo 3.1 text-to-video generation', Wan 2.2 5B Fast is 'fast'. The comparison table in the app uses relative numbers (price, speed

chunks.title: Video Studio — Features
chunks.text: 1-6, quality 1-5 scale; not real currency) for a few video models, for example Wan 2.5 price 2 speed 3 quality 4, Seedance 2.0 price 3 speed 4 quality 5, Kling V3.0 Pro, Sora 2 and Veo 3 each price 5 speed 6 quality 5. These are relative guides, not exact prices or timings. Which models are active on your account is not confirmed.

chunks.title: Video Studio — Inputs and outputs
chunks.text:
Video Studio (#/video). Inputs and outputs.
Inputs:
- Prompt
- Start frame image
- End frame image
- Reference image
- Source video
- Model
- Aspect ratio
- Duration
- Resolution
- Quality
- Native Audio
- Character Lock
- Camera Speed
- Guidance Scale
- Style Preset
- Negative prompt and seed (model dependent)
Required inputs:
- Prompt (text-to-video and prompt-required edits)
- Start frame image (image-to-video)
- Source video (video-to-video modes)
- Character image (Motion transfer)
Optional inputs:
- Prompt for image-to-video
- End frame image
- Native Audio
- Character Lock
- Style Preset
- Camera Speed
- Guidance Scale
- Negative prompt
- Seed
Input details:
- name: Prompt | description: Text description of the scene and motion. Placeholder changes by mode. | required: true | whenToUse: Always for text-to-video; optional when you attach an image. | restrictions: Disabled when a tool that does not use text (like watermark removal) is active.
- name: Start frame image | description: Image that becomes the first frame. Uploaded from your computer, from a URL or stock photo browser, or taken from the last frame of a video. | required: false | whenToUse: To animate a picture. | restrictions: Shared upload limit 10MB for images.

chunks.title: Video Studio — Inputs and outputs
chunks.text:
- name: End frame image | description: Optional last frame for models with an end-frame input. | required: false | whenToUse: Keyframes (start + end). | restrictions: Click the button again to clear it.
- name: Source video | description: A video you upload for video-to-video tools. | required: false | whenToUse: Edit, extend, motion transfer, watermark removal, upscale and similar. | restrictions: Shared upload limit 50MB for videos.
- name: Aspect ratio | description: Shape of the video (for example 16:9). Default comes from the model, otherwise 16:9. | required: false | whenToUse: Match the destination platform. | restrictions: Only values supported by the selected model are listed.
- name: Duration | description: Clip length in seconds, shown like 5s. Default comes from the model, otherwise 5. | required: false | whenToUse: Longer clips for slow actions. | restrictions: Model dependent.
- name: Resolution | description: Output resolution; button label falls back to 720p if the model lists none. | required: false | whenToUse: Higher for final output. | restrictions: Model dependent; higher usually costs more and takes longer.
- name: Quality | description: Quality tier where a model has one; label falls back to 'basic'. | required: false | whenToUse: When the model offers quality levels. | restrictions: Model dependent.

chunks.title: Video Studio — Inputs and outputs
chunks.text:
- name: Style Preset | description: None, Cinematic, Anime, Realistic, Watercolor or Noir. Adds a style phrase to the prompt. | required: false | whenToUse: Quick look change. | restrictions: Not applied to Extend or video-to-video runs.
Outputs:
- A generated video clip shown on the result screen
- Downloadable video file
- History entry (kept in the History strip)
- Optional captioned preview
- Optional saved asset in Render

chunks.title: Video Studio — Problems and limits
chunks.text:
Video Studio (#/video). Problems and limits.
Troubleshooting:
- Nothing happens on Generate and a sign-in box appears: sign in and make sure you have API credits ('Please sign in and add api credits.').
- 'Please enter a prompt to generate a video.': type a prompt, or attach an image if you want image-to-video.
- 'Please upload a start frame image first.': you are in image mode (an image workflow is selected); attach a start frame or switch the workflow to 'Text to video'.
- 'Please upload a video first.': a video-to-video model is selected; upload a video with the video button, or switch back to a text or image workflow.
- 'Please add the character image to animate.': Motion transfer needs both a motion video and a character image.
- 'Please describe the change you want.': Edit video needs a prompt describing the edit.
- 'No Seedance 2.0 generation found to extend. Generate a video first.': generate a Seedance 2.0 clip in this session, then use Extend.
- 'Too many requests. Wait a moment and retry.': you hit a rate limit; wait and try again.
- 'Network error. Check your connection and retry.': check your internet connection and retry.
- 'Service temporarily unavailable. Try again shortly.': the model provider is busy or returned no video; try again or pick a different model.

chunks.title: Video Studio — Problems and limits
chunks.text:
- The aspect ratio or duration you want is missing: the selected model does not support it; choose another model.
- Frame extraction failed ('Failed to extract last frame: ...'): use a different video file or take a screenshot of the last frame and upload it as an image.
Troubleshooting steps:
- issue: Generate does nothing or asks me to sign in | steps: Check that you are signed in.; Confirm your account has credits.; Click Generate again after the sign-in box closes.
- issue: I see 'Service temporarily unavailable. Try again shortly.' | steps: Wait a minute.; Click Generate again.; If it repeats, choose a different model from the model picker.
- issue: My uploaded video or image will not attach | steps: Check the file size (images up to 10MB, videos up to 50MB in the shared limits).; Try a common format such as JPG, PNG, WebP or MP4.; Read the toast: it begins with 'Attachment upload failed:' or 'Video upload failed:' and gives the reason.
- issue: Extend button missing | steps: Make sure the result came from a model that has a continuation model.; Try a Seedance 2.0 generation.; Otherwise download the clip and use the 'Extend uploaded video' workflow.
- issue: The result is not what I described | steps: Shorten the prompt to one subject and one action.; Try image-to-video with a clear start image.; Switch models and compare.
Common problems:

chunks.title: Video Studio — Problems and limits
chunks.text:
- problem: Prompt box is greyed out | whyItHappens: A video is attached and the selected tool does not use text (for example watermark removal). | howToFix: Clear the video (click the video button again) to type a prompt, or just click Generate to run the tool.
- problem: Model changed by itself | whyItHappens: Attaching an image switches to the first image-to-video model, attaching a video switches to the first video-to-video model, and clearing media switches back to the first text-to-video model. | howToFix: Pick your model again after attaching or clearing media.
- problem: Style looks different than expected | whyItHappens: The Style Preset adds a phrase to the prompt and the model may interpret it loosely. | howToFix: Set Style Preset to None and describe the style in your own words.
- problem: Open in Render failed | whyItHappens: Saving the clip to the asset store failed. | howToFix: Use Download and import the file manually.
Limitations:
- Controls depend on the selected model; not every model has quality, resolution, end frame, audio or seed options.
- Shared upload limits in code: images 10MB, videos 50MB.
- Extend only appears when a continuation model exists for the model you used.
- Prompt-less tools (like watermark removal) disable the prompt box.
- You need an API key / credits; otherwise sign-in is requested.
- Generation time and cost vary by model.

chunks.title: Video Studio — Problems and limits
chunks.text:
Limit details:
- limitation: Model-specific controls | impact: A button you expect (for example Quality) may show only one value or nothing useful. | workaround: Switch to a model that lists more options, or accept the default.
- limitation: 50MB video upload limit | impact: Large source videos may be rejected. | workaround: Trim or compress the clip before uploading.
- limitation: Extend availability | impact: No Extend button on some results. | workaround: Use 'Extend uploaded video' in the workflow menu with the downloaded clip, or choose a model with a continuation model.
- limitation: Credits required | impact: Generation will not start without an API key and credits. | workaround: Sign in and add credits when prompted.
FAQs:
- question: What is the difference between text-to-video and image-to-video? | answer: Text-to-video builds a clip from words only. Image-to-video starts from a picture you attach and animates it; the prompt then only describes the motion.
- question: Where did Text to Video, Image to Video, Video to Video and Video Watermark go? | answer: #/text-to-video, #/image-to-video, #/video-to-video and #/video-watermark are landing pages that explain each mode. Their buttons (for example 'Start Creating Videos', 'Get Started Free') take you into Video Studio, where all of those modes live.

chunks.title: Video Studio — Problems and limits
chunks.text:
- question: Which model should I pick? | answer: The studio does not rank models for you. The in-app descriptions call Kling V3.0 Pro cinematic, Kling O1 high-resolution and Wan 2.2 5B Fast fast. The comparison table gives relative scores only. Try the same prompt in two models and compare.
- question: How long can my video be? | answer: Duration options come from the selected model (the button shows values like 5s). The default is the model's default or 5 seconds. The built-in help text mentions about 3 to 10 seconds, but the actual list depends on the model.
- question: Can I add sound? | answer: Open Advanced and switch on Native Audio. It only has an effect on models that can produce audio. You can also use the Audio studio separately.
- question: How do I keep the same character across videos? | answer: Switch on Character Lock under Advanced. It reuses a stored character reference.
- question: How do I extend a video? | answer: On the result screen click Extend (or Extend / 4K). For your own file use the 'Extend uploaded video' workflow.
- question: Can I send the video to editing? | answer: Yes. Click Open in Render on the result screen to save it as an asset and open Render. You can also Download it or add captions.

chunks.title: Video Studio — Problems and limits
chunks.text: - question: Does Video Studio keep my past videos? | answer: A History strip on the page lists your results; completed generations are also saved to your generation history. Jobs that finish while you are away are recovered when you come back.

chunks.title: Video Studio — Workflows and use cases
chunks.text:
Video Studio (#/video). Workflows and use cases.
Example workflows:
- title: Animate a product photo | steps: Open Video Studio.; Attach your product photo as the start frame.; Type 'Slow orbit around the product, soft studio light' (optional).; Pick an image-to-video model and a 9:16 or 16:9 aspect ratio.; Click Generate, then Download.
- title: Text-to-video concept clip | steps: Leave the workflow on 'Text to video'.; Type a one-action prompt.; Choose a model and duration.; Click Generate and review; use Regenerate for another take.
- title: Remove a watermark from a clip | steps: Click the video button and choose your file.; Check the model shows 'AI Video Watermark Remover'.; Click Generate when the prompt box says 'Video ready - click Generate to remove watermark'.; Download the cleaned video.
- title: Make a longer Seedance clip | steps: Generate a clip with a Seedance 2.0 model.; Click Extend / 4K (or Extend) on the result.; Optionally type how the clip should continue ('Optional: describe how to continue the video...').; Click Generate.
Use cases:
- title: Social media short | description: Create a vertical clip for a reel. | steps: Choose 9:16.; Write a short action prompt.; Generate, then Add AI Captions, then Publish to Social. | expectedOutput: A captioned vertical video ready to post.

chunks.title: Video Studio — Workflows and use cases
chunks.text:
- title: Bring artwork to life | description: Animate an illustration or a portrait. | steps: Attach the artwork.; Describe subtle motion.; Generate. | expectedOutput: A short animated clip starting from your artwork.
- title: Clean up footage | description: Remove logos or overlay text. | steps: Upload the video.; Run the watermark remover.; Download. | expectedOutput: A cleaned copy of the video.
Related studios:
- studio: cinema | relationship: Cinema Studio builds camera, lens and film-look into a video prompt. | whenToMove: When you want real cinematography controls. | why: It writes the camera language for you.
- studio: cinema-template | relationship: Cinema Templates are guided, ready-made cinematic formats. | whenToMove: When you want a trailer, brand film or ad structure with simple form fields. | why: You answer a few questions instead of writing a long prompt.
- studio: storyboard | relationship: Storyboard Studio plans still frames for a story. | whenToMove: Before generating video, to plan shots. | why: Frames can be animated afterwards.
- studio: render | relationship: Render is where clips are assembled and exported. | whenToMove: After a clip is ready. | why: Use Open in Render to continue.

chunks.title: Video Studio — Glossary
chunks.text: Glossary: Text-to-video: An AI model that makes a video from a text description. | Image-to-video: An AI model that animates a still picture you provide. | Video-to-video: A tool or model that takes an existing video and edits, extends or transforms it. | Start frame / End frame: The first and last pictures of a clip. Some models accept both. | Keyframes: Fixed pictures at points in time that the AI fills in between. | Aspect ratio: The shape of the video, like 16:9 wide or 9:16 tall. | Resolution: How many pixels the video has, such as 720p. | Native Audio: Sound the video model creates together with the picture. | Character Lock: Reusing the same stored character look across generations. | Guidance Scale: How strongly the model follows your prompt. | Seed: A number that makes a result repeatable; -1 means random in the app's other studios. | Motion transfer: Making a character image copy the movement from another video.

chunks.title: Video Tools — Overview
chunks.text:
Video Tools (#/videotools). Overview.
Description:
Video Tools is a page for working on videos you already have. It has three tabs: Tools (upscale, edit, reframe, clip, remix, translate, remove watermarks, caption), Recast (drive a character image with the motion from a video) and Motion control (rebuild a performance video with new characters while keeping its motion).
Summary:
Upscale, extend, translate, clean up and enhance videos, plus Recast and Motion control.
About:

chunks.title: Video Tools — Overview
chunks.text:
Video Tools opens on the Tools tab. You choose a tool from the model button at the top (13 tools such as AI Video Upscaler, AI Video Upscaler Pro, Topaz Video Upscale, WAN 2.2 Edit Video, WAN 2.2 Animate, Luma Flash Reframe, Luma Modify Video, AI Clipping, Remix Video, HeyGen Video Translate, Seedance Watermark Remover, Wan 3.0 Upscale and AI Captions (Vadoo)), upload a Source Video (or pick a stock clip from Pexels), fill in the prompt or options if that tool offers them, and press Process Video. The result plays in the page with Download Video, Publish to Social and, for video files, Add AI Captions buttons. The Recast tab takes a Motion video and a Character image and makes the character perform that motion. The Motion control tab takes a Motion video and one or more Character images and rebuilds the scene with the new characters, either as Motion transfer or Objects swap. You can jump straight to a tab using ?mode=recast or ?mode=control in the URL.
Best for:
Creators who already have a video and want to improve, change, translate, reframe, caption or re-cast it, rather than generate a brand new clip from an image or text.
When to use it:
- You want to upscale or enhance a video (AI Video Upscaler, AI Video Upscaler Pro, Topaz Video Upscale).
- You want to edit or restyle an existing video with a text prompt (WAN 2.2 Edit Video, Luma Modify Video).

chunks.title: Video Tools — Overview
chunks.text:
- You want to reframe a video to another shape (Luma Flash Reframe) or cut a long video into short segments (AI Clipping).
- You want to translate a video into another language (HeyGen Video Translate).
- You want to remove a Seedance watermark (Seedance Watermark Remover).
- You want animated captions (AI Captions (Vadoo)).
- You want a character image to copy the movement from a video (Recast) or want to rebuild a performance video with new characters and assets (Motion control).
When to use another studio:
- Use Video Studio (#/video) to generate a video from text or an image, or to extend or edit videos with its own tool list.
- Use Animate Studio (#/animate) to turn a still image into a video with a motion prompt.
- Use Effects Studio (#/effects) or AI VFX Studio (#/ai-vfx) for one-click preset effects on a photo.
- Use Lip Sync Studio (#/lipsync) to make lips match new audio, or Avatar Studio (#/avatar) for talking avatars.
- Use Upscale Studio (#/upscale) for upscaling still images.
- Use Timeline (#/timeline) to cut, arrange and export videos manually.
- Use Audio Studio (#/audio) for voice-over, music or sound effects.

chunks.title: Video Tools — How to use
chunks.text:
Video Tools (#/videotools). How to use.
How to use:
1. Open Video Tools from the side menu (#/videotools). The page opens on the Tools tab. 2. Click the model button at the top and choose a tool, for example AI Video Upscaler. 3. Under Source Video, upload your video (hint: Upload a video or pick a stock clip) or use the stock video button. 4. If the Prompt (optional) box appears, describe what you want (placeholder: Describe the transformation you want...). If a Native Audio switch appears, turn it on to keep or create audio. 5. Optional: open Advanced for extra options, or use Thumbnail and Personalize. 6. Press Process Video. The button shows Processing... while it works. 7. When the result appears, press Download Video, Publish to Social or Add AI Captions. 8. For Recast: switch the top toggle to Recast, upload a Motion video and a Character image, choose the model, set Orientation, then press Generate. 9. For Motion control: switch to Motion control, choose Motion transfer or Objects swap, upload a Motion video and Character images, choose model, Aspect, duration, Quality, Bitrate and Audio, and press Generate.
Steps:
- Open #/videotools and stay on Tools, or pick Recast or Motion control from the top toggle.
- Tools tab: choose a tool, upload a Source Video, add a prompt if shown, press Process Video.

chunks.title: Video Tools — How to use
chunks.text:
- Recast tab: add a Motion video and Character image, choose a model, press Generate.
- Motion control tab: add a Motion video and Character images, choose mode and model, set options, press Generate.
- Download or publish the result.
Getting started:
- Use a short clip for your first try; shorter clips process faster.
- Keep video files at 50 MB or less (MuAPI video limit).
- Make sure your MuAPI key is saved in settings and your account has full access.
- Start with AI Video Upscaler to see the flow, then try Recast with a clear character picture.
Tips:
- Use steady footage with one clear subject for Recast and Motion control.
- Use the shortest clip that does the job to save time.
- For Recast, try both Orientation options if the character faces the wrong way.
- In Motion control add several reference images for a better character match (up to the model limit).
Best practices:
- Keep source videos at 50 MB or less and use common formats like MP4.
- Run one tool at a time and download each result before the next step.
- Upscale last, after edits and captions are done, to avoid repeating work.

chunks.title: Video Tools — Features
chunks.text:
Video Tools (#/videotools). Features.
Key features:
- Three tabs: Tools, Recast, Motion control (top toggle; ?mode=recast or ?mode=control).
- 13 tools in the Tools tab chosen with a model selector dropdown.
- Source Video upload with a stock clip button (Browse stock videos from Pexels).
- Prompt (optional) box that appears only for tools that take a prompt.
- Native Audio switch that appears only for tools that support it.
- Advanced panel, Thumbnail button and Personalize button on the Tools tab.
- Result actions: Download Video, Publish to Social, Add AI Captions.
- Recast: three models with orientation control and optional prompt.
- Motion control: two modes (Motion transfer, Objects swap), four Seedance models, duration, quality, bitrate and audio options.
- Recast and Motion control keep the last 30 results in this browser.
Feature details:
- feature: Tool selector (Tools tab) | explanation: The button at the top shows the selected tool and its provider. Click it to open the list and choose one. The form below adapts: the Prompt box and the Native Audio switch only appear if the tool supports them. Default tool is AI Video Upscaler. | whyToUse: Pick the job you want to do to your video. | inputRequired: A selected tool and a Source Video. | restrictions: Only the 13 listed tools are available on this page.

chunks.title: Video Tools — Features
chunks.text:
- feature: AI Video Upscaler, AI Video Upscaler Pro, Topaz Video Upscale, Wan 3.0 Upscale | explanation: Upscaling tools. In the code AI Video Upscaler is described as basic AI video upscaling, AI Video Upscaler Pro as professional AI video upscaling and Topaz Video Upscale as Topaz-quality video enhancement. Wan 3.0 Upscale is the one tool with a Native Audio switch. | whyToUse: Make low resolution or soft footage sharper and larger. | inputRequired: A Source Video. | restrictions: Output resolution and scale options are not exposed in this page for the first three tools; they run with the tool defaults.
- feature: WAN 2.2 Edit Video and Luma Modify Video | explanation: Prompt-based video editing. WAN 2.2 Edit Video is described as text-based video editing; Luma Modify Video as style transformation for videos. Both show the Prompt (optional) box with the placeholder Describe the transformation you want... | whyToUse: Change style, look or elements of an existing clip with words. | inputRequired: A Source Video and a prompt (the page marks it optional, but a prompt gives the tool something to do). | restrictions: Results depend on clip length, resolution and prompt clarity.

chunks.text:

No prompt box on this page. | whyToUse: Animate or replace characters in a clip. | inputRequired: A Source Video. A character image is not requested on the Tools tab; use the Recast tab, which lists Wan2.2 Animate with an image slot, when you need to supply a character. | restrictions: Use the Recast tab for character replacement.

- feature: AI Clipping | explanation: Auto-clips long videos into short segments. | whyToUse: Pull highlights from a long recording. | inputRequired: A Source Video. | restrictions: The page shows a single result player; how multiple clips are returned is not documented here.

- feature: AI Captions (Vadoo) | explanation: AI-generated animated captions with viral themes such as the Hormozi style. | whyToUse: Add burned-in animated subtitles for social video. | inputRequired: A Source Video with speech. | restrictions: Caption style choices are not shown on this page.

chunks.title: Video Tools — Features
chunks.text: - feature: Recast tab | explanation: Drive a character image with the motion from a video. Upload a Motion video and one Character image, choose a model (Kling 3.0 Pro Motion Control, Runway Act Two or Wan2.2 Animate), optionally an aspect ratio (Runway Act Two only: 16:9, 9:16, 1:1, 4:3, 3:4, 21:9) and Orientation: video (Follow the video) or Orientation: image (Follow the image), then press Generate. | whyToUse: Make a still character perform a real performance or dance. | inputRequired: Motion video and Character image. | restrictions: Only one character image. The prompt box works only for models that take a prompt (Kling 3.0 Pro Motion Control and Wan2.2 Animate); for Runway Act Two it is disabled and reads: This model does not take a prompt.

chunks.title: Video Tools — Features
chunks.text:
- feature: Motion control tab | explanation: Rebuild a performance video with new characters and assets while keeping its motion. Choose Motion transfer (extract motion and rebuild the scene with your characters) or Objects swap (keep the scene as filmed and swap characters, products or clothes with your reference images). Upload a Motion video and one or more Character images, pick a model, aspect ratio, duration and options, and press Generate. | whyToUse: Replace people or products in a clip, or recreate a dance with new characters. | inputRequired: Motion video and at least one Character image. | restrictions: Models differ: Seedance 2.5 Motion Control and its Intl and Spicy variants allow 4 to 30 seconds and up to 30 images with audio and bitrate options; Seedance 2.0 Motion Control allows 4 to 15 seconds and up to 9 images with quality (High or Basic) and audio options. Default duration is 5 seconds and default aspect ratio is 16:9.
Modes:

- Recast
- Motion control (Motion transfer)
- Motion control (Objects swap)
Mode details:
- mode: Tools | description: Choose one of 13 tools and process an existing video. | useCase: Upscale, edit, reframe, clip, remix, translate, remove watermark, caption.
- mode: Recast | description: A character image performs the motion from your video. | useCase: Animate a mascot or portrait with a real performance.

Models:

chunks.text: Tools tab (13 tools): AI Video Upscaler (MuAPI, basic upscaling), AI Video Upscaler Pro (MuAPI, professional upscaling), Topaz Video Upscale (Topaz, Topaz-quality enhancement), WAN 2.2 Edit Video (Wan, text-based editing, takes a prompt), WAN 2.2 Animate (Wan, character animation from video), Luma Flash Reframe (Luma, reframing and resizing), Luma Modify Video (Luma, style transformation, takes a prompt), AI Clipping (MuAPI, auto-clips long videos), Remix Video (MuAPI, transform and resize), HeyGen Video Translate (HeyGen, translate to multiple languages), Seedance Watermark Remover (ByteDance, removes watermarks), Wan 3.0 Upscale (upscaling, has a Native Audio switch) and AI Captions (Vadoo, animated captions with viral themes). Motion control models: Seedance 2.5 Motion Control (up to 30 s, up to 30 reference assets, adaptive aspect ratio and audio), Seedance 2.0 Motion Control (up to 15 s, 9 assets), Seedance 2.5 Intl Motion Control (international region version) and Seedance 2.5 Spicy Motion Control (described as a bolder creative treatment). No

Video Tools (#/videotools). Inputs and outputs.
Inputs:
- Source Video

Input details:
- name: Source Video | description: The video to process on the Tools tab. Without it you see an alert: Upload a source video first. | required: true | whenToUse: Always on the Tools tab. | restrictions: MuAPI upload limit for videos is 50 MB (images 10 MB). The upload picker accepts MP4, WebM, MOV, MKV, AVI and M4V files. Stock videos from Pexels can be used instead.
- name: Prompt (optional) | description: Text instruction for tools that support it (WAN 2.2 Edit Video, Luma Modify Video). | required: false | whenToUse: Edit or modify tools. | restrictions: Hidden for tools that do not use a prompt.
- name: Native Audio | description: Switch shown only for tools that support it (Wan 3.0 Upscale in the current list). | required: false | whenToUse: When you want audio handled by the tool. | restrictions: Off by default.

chunks.title: Video Tools — Inputs and outputs
chunks.text:
- name: Motion video | description: Slot in Recast and Motion control. Without it: Please upload a motion video first. | required: true | whenToUse: Always on those tabs. | restrictions: Upload failures show: Upload failed: followed by the reason.
- name: Character image(s) | description: Slot named Character image (Recast, one image) or Character images (Motion control, several). | required: true | whenToUse: Always on those tabs. | restrictions: Recast without an image shows: Please upload a character image first. Motion control without images shows: Please add at least one character image. Max images per model: 30 for Seedance 2.5 variants, 9 for Seedance 2.0.
- name: Model (Recast / Motion control) | description: Chosen from the model pill. Recast default: Kling 3.0 Pro Motion Control. Motion control default: Seedance 2.5 Motion Control. | required: false | whenToUse: Choose based on duration, image count and prompt support. | restrictions: Options shown depend on the model (for example aspect ratio is hidden if a model has none).
- name: Duration (Motion control) | description: Pill showing seconds; choices step by 1 second up to 9 and then by 5 seconds up to the model maximum. | required: false | whenToUse: To control length. | restrictions: Minimum 4 seconds; maximum 15 (Seedance 2.0) or 30 (Seedance 2.5). Default 5.

chunks.text:
- name: Quality, Bitrate, Audio (Motion control) | description: Quality pill (High or Basic) for Seedance 2.0; Bitrate: normal or high for Seedance 2.5 variants; Audio: off or on for all four. | required: false | whenToUse: Final renders or when sound is needed. | restrictions: Pills appear only when the selected model supports them. Defaults: High, normal bitrate, audio off.
Outputs:
- An upgraded, edited, reframed, translated, clipped, captioned or watermark-free video from the Tools tab, shown in a player with Download Video.
- A recast video where your character performs the motion (Recast tab).
- A rebuilt performance video with new characters or swapped objects (Motion control tab), up to 30 seconds depending on the model.
- Recast and Motion control results are kept in a gallery (last 30 in this browser).

chunks.title: Video Tools — Problems and limits
chunks.text:
Video Tools (#/videotools). Problems and limits.
Troubleshooting:
- Alert says Upload a source video first: upload a video or pick a Pexels stock video on the Tools tab, then press Process Video.
- Alert says Error: followed by a message after Process Video: read the message; typical causes are a missing MuAPI key, an unsupported file or a service problem. Fix the cause and press Process Video again.
- A settings window opens when you press Process Video: save your MuAPI key, then press the button again.
- An upgrade prompt appears: your account needs full access to process videos.
- File is too large message: videos must be 50 MB or less. Compress or trim the clip.
- The Prompt box is missing: the selected tool does not take a prompt. Choose WAN 2.2 Edit Video or Luma Modify Video if you need one.
- Recast shows Please upload a motion video first. or Please upload a character image first.: add both before pressing Generate.
- Motion control shows Please add at least one character image.: add one or more Character images.
- Recast prompt box is greyed out with This model does not take a prompt: you selected Runway Act Two; pick Kling 3.0 Pro Motion Control or Wan2.2 Animate to use a prompt.

chunks.title: Video Tools — Problems and limits
chunks.text:
- Motion control options are missing (no Quality, Bitrate or Audio pill): those pills only appear for models that support them. Seedance 2.0 shows Quality; Seedance 2.5 models show Bitrate; all four show Audio.
- No video URL returned by API: the service finished without a video. Retry or try a shorter clip.
- Add AI Captions button is missing on the result: it appears only when the result link looks like a video file.
Troubleshooting steps:
- issue: Process Video fails | steps: Confirm the Source Video preview or file name appears.; Check the file is 50 MB or less and a common format (MP4, WebM, MOV).; Make sure your MuAPI key is saved and your account has full access.; Try a shorter clip or a different tool.
- issue: Recast or Motion control result does not follow the motion | steps: Use a motion video with one clear subject and steady camera.; Use a clear, full-body character image if the motion is full body.; In Recast try the other Orientation (Follow the video vs Follow the image).; Try another model.
- issue: Upload fails in Recast or Motion control | steps: Look for the toast Upload failed: with the reason.; Check file size and type (video for Motion video, image for characters).; Retry the upload.
Common problems:

chunks.title: Video Tools — Problems and limits
chunks.text:
- problem: Output looks the same as the input | whyItHappens: Some tools (like AI Video Upscaler) change quality, not content, and the page has no strength controls. | howToFix: Compare at full size, or try Topaz Video Upscale or AI Video Upscaler Pro.
- problem: Character does not match the reference image | whyItHappens: Low quality or cropped character images make the match weaker. | howToFix: Use a sharp, well lit, uncropped image; add more images in Motion control.
- problem: Result is longer or shorter than expected | whyItHappens: Motion control clamps duration to the model range (4 to 15 or 4 to 30 seconds). | howToFix: Pick the model and duration that fit your clip.
- problem: Tab opens on the wrong mode | whyItHappens: The URL contains ?mode=recast or ?mode=control. | howToFix: Use the Tools button in the top toggle.
Limitations:
- Only the 13 listed tools are offered on the Tools tab.
- Upload limits come from MuAPI: 50 MB for videos and 10 MB for images.
- Most tools have no visible settings on this page, so you cannot choose target resolution, language or caption style here.
- Recast takes only one Character image; Motion control takes up to 9 or 30 depending on the model.
- Motion control duration is 4 to 15 seconds (Seedance 2.0) or 4 to 30 seconds (Seedance 2.5).
- Processing may take several minutes for long or high resolution videos.

chunks.title: Video Tools — Problems and limits
chunks.text:
- The Video Tools page does not generate new clips from text or images; use Video Studio or Animate for that.
Limit details:
- limitation: Large video files | impact: Files over 50 MB are rejected with: This file is too large for MuAPI (images 10 MB, videos 50 MB, other 10 MB). | workaround: Trim or compress the video before uploading.
- limitation: Few visible options per tool | impact: For example, upscalers run with their defaults and translate has no language selector visible in the code read. | workaround: Try the other upscale tool, or use Video Studio, which has its own tool options such as target resolution.
- limitation: Prompt only on some tools | impact: The Prompt (optional) box is hidden for most tools. | workaround: Choose WAN 2.2 Edit Video or Luma Modify Video when you need a text instruction.
FAQs:
- question: What can I do in Video Tools? | answer: On the Tools tab you can upscale, edit, reframe, clip, remix, translate, remove a Seedance watermark or add AI captions, using one of 13 tools. The Recast and Motion control tabs transfer motion from a video onto characters.

chunks.title: Video Tools — Problems and limits
chunks.text:
- question: What is the difference between Recast and Motion control? | answer: Recast drives one character image with the motion from a video using Kling 3.0 Pro Motion Control, Runway Act Two or Wan2.2 Animate. Motion control rebuilds the whole scene with one or more new characters and assets using Seedance models, with Motion transfer and Objects swap modes.
- question: How big can my video be? | answer: MuAPI allows videos up to 50 MB and images up to 10 MB.
- question: Can I open Recast or Motion control directly? | answer: Yes. Add ?mode=recast or ?mode=control to the Video Tools address, or use the top toggle.
- question: How long can a Motion control video be? | answer: From 4 seconds up to 15 seconds with Seedance 2.0 Motion Control, or up to 30 seconds with the Seedance 2.5 models. The default is 5 seconds.
- question: Does Recast need a prompt? | answer: No. It is optional, and the prompt box is disabled for Runway Act Two, which does not take a prompt.
- question: Where are my results saved? | answer: Tools results are registered in your generation history and shown on the page with Download Video. Recast and Motion control keep your last 30 results in a gallery in this browser.
- question: Can I add captions to the result? | answer: Yes, press Add AI Captions under the result on the Tools tab (shown for video results), or use the AI Captions (Vadoo) tool.

chunks.title: Video Tools — Workflows and use cases
chunks.text:
Video Tools (#/videotools). Workflows and use cases.
Example workflows:
- title: Upscale a low resolution clip | steps: Open Video Tools and choose AI Video Upscaler.; Upload a clip under 50 MB.; Press Process Video.; Press Download Video, or Add AI Captions if you need subtitles.
- title: Make a mascot dance (Recast) | steps: Switch to the Recast tab.; Upload a dance clip as Motion video.; Upload the mascot as Character image.; Keep Kling 3.0 Pro Motion Control, set Orientation to Follow the video, and describe the performance if you like.; Press Generate and review the result.
- title: Swap a product in existing footage (Motion control) | steps: Switch to Motion control and select Objects swap.; Upload the original clip as Motion video.; Add product reference images as Character images.; Choose Seedance 2.5 Motion Control and a duration that fits.; Press Generate.
- title: Restyle a clip with a prompt | steps: Choose WAN 2.2 Edit Video or Luma Modify Video.; Upload the clip.; Write a prompt such as make it look like a watercolor painting.; Press Process Video.
Use cases:
- title: Clean up a social clip | description: Upscale and caption a short vertical video. | steps: Process with AI Video Upscaler.; Press Add AI Captions on the result.; Download. | expectedOutput: A sharper video with captions.

chunks.title: Video Tools — Workflows and use cases
chunks.text:
- title: Recreate a performance with a new character | description: Use a real person's performance to drive a brand character. | steps: Use Recast or Motion control.; Upload motion video and character images.; Generate. | expectedOutput: A video of the character repeating the performance.
- title: Cut highlights from a long video | description: Use AI Clipping to get short segments. | steps: Select AI Clipping.; Upload the video.; Press Process Video. | expectedOutput: Short clips from the source (how they are delivered is not documented in the page).
Related studios:
- studio: video | relationship: Video generation plus its own list of video tools such as extend and edit. | whenToMove: When you need text-to-video, image-to-video or longer continuations. | why: Video Tools only processes existing videos.
- studio: lipsync | relationship: Syncs lips to new audio. | whenToMove: When the speech or dubbing is the goal. | why: Video Tools translation is a separate, simpler tool.

chunks.title: Video Tools — Glossary
chunks.text: Glossary: Upscale: Increase a video's resolution and apparent sharpness. | Reframe: Change the shape (aspect ratio) of a video while keeping the subject in view. | Recast: Make a different character perform the motion from a video. | Motion transfer: Copy motion from a reference video and rebuild the scene with new characters. | Objects swap: Keep the scene as filmed but replace characters, products or clothes with reference images. | Native Audio: Audio produced or kept by the tool itself. | Bitrate: Amount of data per second of video; high bitrate usually looks cleaner but makes bigger files. | Orientation (Recast): Whether the character follows the pose direction of the video or of the image. | Seedance: ByteDance's video model family used for Motion control.

chunks.title: Smart Video Viral — Overview
chunks.text:
Smart Video Viral (#/viral). Overview.
Description:
Smart Video Viral is a browsable feed of trending AI image and video prompts collected from X (Twitter), with preview media and source links. You copy a prompt, or send it straight to a creation studio, to make your own version.
Summary:
Continuously refreshed feed of trending AI prompts from X - copy any prompt into your studio and create.
About:
Smart Video Viral does not generate media itself. It is a prompt-inspiration library. It loads a feed of prompts from several sources (an upstream visual prompt feed on GitHub, a bundled Seedance prompt list and a bundled overflow list), shows each one as a card with a preview image or video, tags, a recommended model and a link to the original post, and lets you search, filter and sort. At the top you see counts of prompts, videos, images and providers and a carousel preview; below the controls are horizontal rails for Trending, Categories and Providers. On any card you can copy the prompt, open it in a creation studio with the prompt prefilled (Create This Style), personalize the demo for a business (Personalize This Demo), or open the original post (Source). The feed refreshes itself every 5 minutes and you can refresh it manually or export the filtered list as JSON.
Best for:

chunks.title: Smart Video Viral — Overview
chunks.text:
Anyone who wants prompt ideas that are already working for other creators: beginners who do not know what to write, marketers looking for ad and product prompt styles, and creators who want to recreate a trending look.
When to use it:
- You do not know what prompt to write and want proven examples.
- You want to see which AI image and video styles are trending and which model they were made with.
- You want to start from a prompt and open it directly in Image Studio, Video Studio or another studio.
- You want to collect or export prompts for a category such as product ads, cinematic or character.
- You want to personalize a viral-style demo for a specific business.
When to use another studio:
- Use Image Studio (#/image) when you already have a prompt and want to generate an image.
- Use Video Studio (#/video) when you want to generate a video from a prompt.
- Use Cinema Studio (#/cinema) for cinematic style shots.
- Use Character Studio (#/character) for consistent characters.
- Use Commercial Studio (#/commercial) for product ads.
- Use Personalizer (#/personalizer) for personalized video at scale.
- Use Templates (#/templates) or Explore (#/explore) for ready-made starting points that are not from X.

chunks.title: Smart Video Viral — How to use
chunks.text:
Smart Video Viral (#/viral). How to use.
How to use:
1. Open Smart Video Viral from the side menu (#/viral). 2. Look at the hero numbers and the Trending, Categories and Providers rails for ideas. 3. Use the search box ('Search prompts, tags, or authors… (press /)') to find a subject. 4. Narrow results with All / Images / Videos, All Categories, All Models and the sort list (Newest First, Most Popular, Most Likes). 5. Leave 'Exclude Chinese' on, or click it to switch to 'Include Chinese'. 6. Click a card to see it; use 'View Full Prompt ›' for long prompts. 7. Click 'Copy Prompt' to copy it, or click 'Create This Style' to open the right studio with the prompt filled in. 8. In that studio click Generate. 9. Optionally click 'Personalize This Demo' to adapt a demo for a business, or 'Source' to see the original post. 10. Click the refresh button to reload the feed or the export button to download the filtered list as JSON.
Steps:
- Browse or search the feed.
- Filter by media type, category, model and sort order.
- Open a card and read the full prompt.
- Copy the prompt or click Create This Style.
- Generate in the studio that opens.
- Optional: Personalize This Demo, view the Source, or export JSON.
Getting started:
- Scroll the feed and click Videos or Images to pick what you want to make.
- Pick a category such as Product Ads or Cinematic.

chunks.title: Smart Video Viral — How to use
chunks.text:
- Click Create This Style on a card you like and press Generate in the studio that opens.
Tips:
- Sort by Most Popular to see what has the most engagement.
- Use the same recommended model first, then try others.
- Change names, products and details in the prompt to make it your own.
- Click View Full Prompt before copying a long prompt so you know what is in it.
Best practices:
- Credit the original author when you share a recreated style.
- Test a prompt on the recommended model first.
- Keep a JSON export of your favorite category for later.

chunks.title: Smart Video Viral — Features
chunks.text:
Smart Video Viral (#/viral). Features.
Key features:
- Feed of trending AI image and video prompts with preview media.
- Hero stats: prompts, videos, images and providers counts, plus a trending preview carousel.
- Search box: 'Search prompts, tags, or authors… (press /)'.
- Media filter buttons: All, Images, Videos.
- Category dropdown (All Categories) with 15 categories.
- Model dropdown (All Models), built from the models seen in the feed.
- Sort options: Newest First, Most Popular, Most Likes.
- Exclude Chinese / Include Chinese toggle (Chinese-language prompts are excluded by default).
- Horizontal rails: Trending, Categories, Providers.
- Card buttons: Copy Prompt, Personalize This Demo, Create This Style, Source, and 'View Full Prompt ›' for long prompts.
- Refresh button, 'Updated ...' timestamp and automatic refresh every 5 minutes.
- Export of the currently filtered prompts as a JSON file.
- Infinite scroll in pages of 30 cards.
- Keyboard shortcuts: / search, r refresh, c toggle Chinese, ? help.
- On small screens a Filters button opens a bottom sheet with the same controls and an Apply Filters button.
Feature details:

chunks.title: Smart Video Viral — Features
chunks.text:
- feature: Search | explanation: Type in the search box to match prompt titles, prompt text, tags and authors. Press / to jump to the box (when you are not typing in another field). Searching waits a moment after you stop typing. | whyToUse: Find prompts about a subject such as 'sneaker' or 'rain'. | inputRequired: Any text. | restrictions: Matches only the loaded feed.
- feature: Filters and sorting | explanation: Use All / Images / Videos, the Category list, the Model list and the Sort list together. Sort offers Newest First, Most Popular and Most Likes. | whyToUse: Narrow thousands of prompts to the few you need. | inputRequired: None. | restrictions: If nothing matches you see 'No prompts match your filters.' with a 'Reset All Filters' button.
- feature: Categories | explanation: The 15 categories are: Animation, Architecture, Camera Moves, Character, Cinematic, Food & Drink, Illustration 3D, Nature, Photography, Poster Design, Product Ads, Product Brand, Travel, UGC and UI Graphic. You can also click a category pill in the Categories rail. | whyToUse: Browse by type of content. | inputRequired: None. | restrictions: A prompt can belong to more than one category.

chunks.title: Smart Video Viral — Features
chunks.text:
- feature: Exclude Chinese toggle | explanation: Hides prompts marked as Chinese language. It is ON by default. The button reads 'Exclude Chinese' when on and 'Include Chinese' when off. The count line shows how many were excluded. | whyToUse: Keep the feed in a language you can read, or include them for more ideas. | inputRequired: None. | restrictions: Only affects items the feed marks as Chinese.
- feature: Copy Prompt | explanation: Copies the full prompt text to your clipboard and shows the toast 'Prompt copied to clipboard!'. | whyToUse: Paste it into any studio. | inputRequired: None. | restrictions: If the browser blocks copying you see 'Failed to copy'.
- feature: Create This Style | explanation: Opens a creation studio and passes the prompt (and, when available, a mapped model, aspect ratio, duration and audio setting). Video prompts open Video Studio and image prompts open Image Studio; for items without a clear type, categories decide (cinematic -> Cinema, character -> Character, product ads/brand -> Commercial, UGC/animation -> Video). | whyToUse: Go from inspiration to your own generation in one click. | inputRequired: None. | restrictions: You still click Generate in the studio you land in, and you need credits there.

chunks.title: Smart Video Viral — Features
chunks.text:
- feature: Personalize This Demo | explanation: Opens a personalization dialog for that viral demo so you can adapt it for a business. | whyToUse: Turn a trending style into a customized sales or outreach demo. | inputRequired: Details you enter in the dialog. | restrictions: The dialog's own steps are not documented in this studio's code.
- feature: Source and View Full Prompt | explanation: 'Source' opens the original post on X in a new tab. 'View Full Prompt ›' opens a detail viewer for long prompts. | whyToUse: Credit the author and read the whole prompt. | inputRequired: None. | restrictions: Some items may lack a source link.
- feature: Video preview | explanation: Video cards have a play toggle on the preview. If no video is available you see 'No video source available'. | whyToUse: Watch what the prompt produced. | inputRequired: None. | restrictions: Depends on the media host being reachable.

chunks.title: Smart Video Viral — Features
chunks.text:
- feature: Refresh and Export | explanation: The refresh button (tooltip 'Refresh feed from upstream') reloads the feed; it also reloads automatically every 5 minutes. The export button (tooltip 'Export filtered prompts as JSON') downloads viral-prompts-YYYY-MM-DD.json with title, prompt, media type, categories, model, author and source URL, and shows 'Exported N prompts'. | whyToUse: Keep a local copy of prompts for a category. | inputRequired: None. | restrictions: Export contains only what is currently filtered, as JSON.
Models:
Smart Video Viral does not run models. Each card shows a 'recommended model' label from the prompt's source data, and the Model filter and Providers rail list these labels. Colors are defined in the code for gptimage, nanobanana, seedance, kling, minimax, ideogram and flux. When you click Create This Style the studio maps some labels to a studio model id: seedance -> seedance-v2.0-t2v, nanobanana or nano-banana -> nano-banana-2, gptimage or gpt-image -> nano-banana-2, kling -> kling, minimax -> minimax; other labels are passed through as written. Video items open Video Studio, image items open Image Studio. No prices, speeds or quality scores are available for these labels in the code.

chunks.title: Smart Video Viral — Problems and limits
chunks.text:
Smart Video Viral (#/viral). Problems and limits.
Troubleshooting:
- 'Failed to load the prompt feed' with a Retry button: click Retry or the refresh button; check your connection.
- 'No prompts match your filters.': click 'Reset All Filters' or widen the search.
- Toast 'No video source available': that card has no playable video; use the image preview or the Source link.
- Toast 'Failed to copy': your browser blocked clipboard access; allow clipboard permission or select and copy the text from the full prompt viewer.
- Video does not play: the media host may block it or be slow; open the Source link to watch it on X.
- Fewer prompts than expected: 'Exclude Chinese' is on by default; click it to include them.
- Feed looks old: click the refresh button; the studio also refreshes every 5 minutes and shows 'Updated ...' with the time.
- Cards load slowly: they load in pages of 30; keep scrolling to load more.
- Keyboard shortcut does nothing: shortcuts do not work while you are typing in a box; click outside it first.
Troubleshooting steps:
- issue: Feed does not load | steps: Check your internet connection.; Click Retry (or the refresh button).; Reload the page if it still fails.
- issue: Cannot find a good prompt | steps: Click Reset All Filters.; Pick a category from the Categories rail.; Sort by Most Popular.; Switch Include Chinese on for more results.

chunks.title: Smart Video Viral — Problems and limits
chunks.text:
- issue: Create This Style opened an empty-looking studio | steps: Check the prompt box in the studio; the prompt should be filled in.; If not, go back and use Copy Prompt, then paste it.; Choose the recommended model manually.
Common problems:
- problem: I expected to generate here | whyItHappens: Smart Video Viral is a prompt library, not a generator. | howToFix: Click Create This Style to open a studio and generate there.
- problem: The count says fewer prompts than the hero number | whyItHappens: Your filters and the Chinese exclusion reduce the list; the count line shows 'N prompts loaded of Total'. | howToFix: Reset filters or toggle Include Chinese.
- problem: Prompt is cut off on the card | whyItHappens: Long prompts are shortened on the card. | howToFix: Click 'View Full Prompt ›'.
Limitations:
- It only shows prompts; it does not generate images or videos itself.
- Content depends on external sources (a GitHub-hosted feed, a bundled Seedance list and a bundled overflow list) and on media hosts being reachable.
- Export is JSON only.
- Prompts were written for specific models; results can differ when run in another model.
- The feed shows 30 cards at a time and loads more as you scroll.
Limit details:

chunks.title: Smart Video Viral — Problems and limits
chunks.text:
- limitation: Feed can fail to load | impact: You may see 'Failed to load the prompt feed' with a Retry button. | workaround: Click Retry or the refresh button. If the remote feed stays unavailable, the studio falls back to its bundled overflow prompts when available.
- limitation: Different model, different result | impact: A prompt that looked great on one model may look different on another. | workaround: Use the card's recommended model in the studio, or adjust the prompt.
- limitation: Chinese prompts hidden by default | impact: Fewer results than the total. | workaround: Click 'Exclude Chinese' to switch to 'Include Chinese'.
FAQs:
- question: Where do the prompts come from? | answer: They are collected from posts on X and shown with author and source link. The feed combines an upstream GitHub-hosted prompt feed, a bundled Seedance prompt list and a bundled overflow list.
- question: Does it cost credits to browse? | answer: Browsing, copying and exporting prompts does not generate anything. Generating in a studio uses that studio's credits.
- question: How often does the feed update? | answer: Automatically every 5 minutes while the page is open, or when you click the refresh button.

chunks.title: Smart Video Viral — Problems and limits
chunks.text:
- question: Can I use the prompt in any studio? | answer: Yes. Copy it and paste it into any studio, or click Create This Style to send it to Image Studio or Video Studio (or another studio chosen by category).
- question: What are the keyboard shortcuts? | answer: / focuses search, r refreshes, c toggles Chinese content, and ? shows a reminder. They do not work while typing in a box.
- question: Can I export prompts? | answer: Yes, as a JSON file of the currently filtered list using the export button.

chunks.title: Website Builder — Overview
chunks.text:
Website Builder (#/website-builder). Overview.
Description:
Website Builder (branded Smart Website Builder) lets you describe a website in plain language and have an AI agent write the code, preview it live in your browser and deploy it to a public address. You bring your own AI provider key.
Summary:
Build and publish a full website from a prompt using your own AI key.
About:
Website Builder is an embedded app (the OpenThorn builder, shown as Smart Website Builder) inside SmartVideo. You sign in with your normal SmartVideo account, land on the builder Dashboard, type what you want in the prompt box ('What do you want to build?'), choose an AI model from a provider you have a key for, and the agent writes the site, previews it live in the browser and lets you keep chatting to change it. When you are happy you click Deploy to publish it to a public address (Cloudflare Pages), or download the code as a ZIP. Both free and paid SmartVideo accounts can use it. The builder manages its own provider keys inside the studio (Settings, Providers), so you pay your AI provider directly at their normal rates; it does not use SmartVideo credits for the AI. It builds websites, not videos.
Best for:

chunks.title: Website Builder — Overview
chunks.text:
Founders, creators and small businesses who want a landing page, portfolio or small website built by AI quickly, are comfortable bringing their own AI provider API key, and want to download or publish the result.
When to use it:
- You want a landing page, portfolio or small website generated from a description.
- You want a live preview in the browser and to keep changing it by chatting.
- You want a one-click public address for the site.
- You want the full source code to download and own.
- You want to choose your own AI provider and pay them directly.
When to use another studio:
- Use Video Agent (#/video-agent) when you want an animated video or motion graphics instead of a website.
- Use Motion Director (#/motion-director) when you want a promo film made from your existing website.
- Use Brand (#/brand) or Find My Brand (#/find-my-brand) when you want to define or discover your brand look first.
- Use Image (#/image) or Video (#/video) when you need pictures or clips to place on the site.
- Use Commercial (#/commercial) or Viral (#/viral) when you want an ad or social video for your product.

chunks.title: Website Builder — How to use
chunks.text:
Website Builder (#/website-builder). How to use.
How to use:
1. Open Website Builder from the Agents group in the side menu (#/website-builder). 2. If you see 'Sign in to use Smart Website Builder', click Sign in with your SmartVideo account. 3. On the Dashboard, open Settings, then Providers, and add an API key for the AI provider you want to use. 4. Back on the Dashboard, type your idea into the box labelled 'Describe your website idea' under 'What do you want to build?'. 5. Choose a model in the model selector (otherwise you get 'Please select a model first.'), optionally set the agent thinking level and attach files. 6. Send it and watch the agent write the site and show a live preview. 7. Keep chatting to change things. 8. Click Deploy to publish and open the public address, or download the code as a ZIP.
Steps:
- Open Website Builder; sign in if asked.
- Add your AI provider key in Settings, Providers.
- Describe your website in the prompt box and pick a model.
- Send and review the live preview.
- Refine by chatting with the agent.
- Click Deploy for a public address, or download the ZIP.
Getting started:
- Have an API key from an AI provider ready (a free tier works for trying it).
- Write what the site is for, who it is for, the sections you want and the style.
- Start with a small site and add pages later.
- Check the preview before you deploy.
Tips:

chunks.title: Website Builder — How to use
chunks.text:
- Be concrete about sections, tone and colors in your first prompt.
- Try a provider free tier first.
- Preview thoroughly before deploying.
- Download the ZIP as a backup.
Best practices:
- Keep your provider key private and rotate it if exposed.
- Change one thing per follow-up message.
- Check on a phone-size window in the preview.
- Use Starred projects to keep your best builds handy.

chunks.title: Website Builder — Features
chunks.text:
Website Builder (#/website-builder). Features.
Key features:
- Prompt-to-website AI agent that writes the code and plans the work.
- Live in-browser preview with no build wait.
- Follow-up chat to change the site.
- Model selector: you choose a provider and model you have a key for.
- Agent thinking level control in the prompt box.
- Attach files to the prompt (Upload files).
- Deploy button that publishes the site (Cloudflare Pages, per the app documentation).
- Download code as a ZIP.
- Dashboard with your projects, search and sort (Recent, Starred).
- Templates page and Community publishing ('Publish to Community').
- Settings with Account, Providers (API Keys and Model Providers), Knowledge and Danger Zone, including deleting your builder data.
- Multiple AI providers with automatic fallback to another provider on rate limits (per the app documentation).
- Signs in automatically with your SmartVideo account; works on free and paid accounts.

Website Builder (#/website-builder). Problems and limits.
Troubleshooting:
- Stuck on 'Loading Website Builder...': reload the page; check your connection.
- 'Sign in to use Smart Website Builder': click Sign in and use your SmartVideo account.
- 'Please select a model first.': pick a model in the model selector; if none appear add a provider key in Settings, Providers.
- The agent does not respond or errors: check the provider key is valid, has credit and is not rate limited; try another provider or model.
- Blank iframe or content fails to load: reload; if you are on a local development setup the builder runs on a separate dev server.
- Deploy failed: open the 'Deploy project' dialog message, retry, and make sure the preview works first.
- Download does nothing: allow downloads in your browser; the embedded builder permits downloads.
- A popup blocked the live site: allow popups for SmartVideo so the deployed link can open in a new tab.
Troubleshooting steps:
- issue: I cannot send my prompt | steps: Check that a model is selected.; Open Settings, Providers and make sure a key is saved for that provider.; Try another provider if one is rate limited.; Send again.
- issue: The site will not deploy | steps: Make sure the preview loads without errors.; Click Deploy and read the 'Deploy project' dialog.; Retry; if it keeps failing download the ZIP and host it yourself.

- problem: Costs are higher than expected | whyItHappens: Your provider bills per use and long sessions use many tokens. | howToFix: Use a cheaper model or a free tier, keep prompts focused, and review the provider's usage dashboard.
- problem: No models are listed | whyItHappens: No provider key has been added yet. | howToFix: Add a key under Settings, Providers.

- A model must be selected before sending.
